en: ŚŚS 1.1.1: We shall explain the sacrifice. ŚŚS 1.1.2: It belongs to the three castes. ŚŚS 1.1.3: To the Brāhmaṇa, the Kṣatriya, and the Vaiśya.
ŚŚS 1.1.4: That which is prescribed without being specifically connected is common [to all].
ŚŚS 1.1.5: Through specific connection, it becomes restricted.
ŚŚS 1.1.6: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (yajñopavītī), one performs rites for the gods.
ŚŚS 1.1.7: For rites pertaining to the ancestors, he should wear the sacred thread over the right shoulder (prācīnāvītī).
ŚŚS 1.1.8: From the act of sipping water (ācamana) onwards, he should not turn away from whatever ritual procedure he has engaged in.
ŚŚS 1.1.9: Nor should he allow anything to intervene between himself and that procedure.
Thus ends the definition of the *āvṛtā*.
[Section 1.1.11] The enumeration.
[Section 1.1.12] The procedure from the north.

ŚŚS 1.1.13: Rituals for the gods follow the rule of facing east. ŚŚS 1.1.14: Rituals for the ancestors follow the rule of facing south. ŚŚS 1.1.15: The ritual of the Bahvṛcas follows the rule of sitting.
ŚŚS 1.1.16: The place [of recitation] is determined by the specific instruction.
ŚŚS 1.1.17: And the Hotṛ shall perform that which has not been specifically prescribed.
ŚŚS 1.1.18: In groups of three or more ṛcs, the first and the last are each recited three times, except in the case of silent recitations (japa).

ŚŚS 1.1.19: After the final vowel of the *chandomāna* [meter] and before its initial consonant, the syllable *oṃ* is substituted; it is protracted (*pluta*), consisting of three morae (*trimātra*), and pure (*śuddha*).
ŚŚS 1.1.20: Or, it may end with the letter *m*.
ŚŚS 1.1.21: They call that the *praṇava*.

ŚŚS 1.1.22: At the pause [of the recitation], there is an *m*-sound at the end in all groups of *ṛc*s that include a *puronuvākyā*. ŚŚS 1.1.23: Having joined the half-verse (*ardharca*) of the following [verse] with it, one pauses; or [having joined] the foot (*pāda*), that is called "continuous" (*saṃtata*). ŚŚS 1.1.24: This is the rule for all groups of *ṛc*s which are enjoined by connection with a ritual action.
ŚŚS 1.1.25: Even in the case of distant ritual acts, one desires a connection by means of a half-verse, provided there is no *prathamā* or *paridhānīyā*.
ŚŚS 1.1.26: And verses follow the principle of the half-verse (*ardharca*).
ŚŚS 1.1.27: There is an exception to this due to a specific scriptural statement (*vacana*).
ŚŚS 1.1.28: The Ṛgveda is characterized by the rule of high pitch.
ŚŚS 1.1.29: From a specific injunction, there is low-voiced recitation.
ŚŚS 1.1.30: And there is the rule of *saṃsvāra* for the sounds.
ŚŚS 1.1.31: And there is monotony of pitch (ekasvarya). ŚŚS 1.1.32: The *praṇava* is higher in pitch than the *puronuvākyā*.
ŚŚS 1.1.33: The *yājyā* is higher in pitch than the *praṇava*.
ŚŚS 1.1.34: The *vaṣaṭ*-call is higher in pitch. ŚŚS 1.1.35: Or it may be equal [in pitch].
ŚŚS 1.1.36: The *praṇava*, the *ye yajāmahe*, the *vaṣaṭ*-call, the *saṃpraiṣas*, and the *praiṣas* are uttered loudly; however, they are whispered (*upāṃśu*) in the case of oblations (*havirṣu*).
ŚŚS 1.1.37: And the name of the deity [is recited] in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) at the places where the *nigama* formulas are used.
ŚŚS 1.1.38: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ" is the muttered prayer (*japa*) preceding [the offering].
ŚŚS 1.1.39: "Ye yajāmahe," "Vauṣaṭ," "Ojaḥ sahaḥ saha ojaḥ svar"—these four [formulas] are [recited] after [the name of the deity] in all *yājyā* offerings.
ŚŚS 1.1.40: However, in the *anuyāja* offerings, there is no *ye yajāmahe*.
ŚŚS 1.1.41: And [it is absent] at the *anuvaṣaṭkāra* as well.
ŚŚS 1.1.42: The connection of the *vaṣaṭkāra* with the protracted (*pluta*) end of the *yājyā* verse [is prescribed].
ŚŚS 1.1.43: Or [the *praṇava*] may be unprotracted (*apluta*).
ŚŚS 1.1.44: That [rule] does not apply in the case of the *upāṃśuyāja*.
ŚŚS 1.2.1: One should protract the vowel *ā* in the invocation (*āvāhana*).
ŚŚS 1.2.2: The *ye-yajāmahe* formula, with its protracted vowel (*pluta*) and so forth, precedes the *yājyā* verses.
ŚŚS 1.2.3: The protraction (*pluti*) used by the ritualists consists of four morae (*mātrā*).
ŚŚS 1.2.6: All other syllables are pronounced according to their natural form (*prakṛti*).
ŚŚS 1.2.7: The vowels *e* and *o* are *pragṛhya*.
ŚŚS 1.2.8: [This applies] at the end of a *yājyā* verse.
ŚŚS 1.2.9: A *visarjanīya* followed by *r* (rephita) becomes the letter *r*.
ŚŚS 1.2.10: A non-aspirated consonant is elided. ŚŚS 1.2.11: The letter *m* becomes an *anusvāra*.
ŚŚS 1.2.12: Other consonants remain in their original form (*prakṛti*).
ŚŚS 1.2.13: In the *vaṣaṭ*-call, the vowel *o* has a duration of four morae.
ŚŚS 1.2.14: And the vowel *a* following the letter *ṣ*.
ŚŚS 1.2.15: Or both [the *o* and the *a*] may remain in their natural state.
ŚŚS 1.2.16: Or the former [syllable] remains in its original form.
ŚŚS 1.2.17: Jātūkarṇya says that the vowel *a* remains in its original form.
ŚŚS 1.2.18: One should utter the *vaṣaṭ* call in the Bārhatarāthaṃtara manner—with a long vowel at the beginning and a short vowel at the end.
ŚŚS 1.2.19: After the *ye yajāmaha* formula, there is the announcement of the deity together with the *puronuvākyā*.
ŚŚS 1.2.20: However, this does not occur when there is a *praiṣa* (a call for the Hotṛ).
ŚŚS 1.2.21: When it is said "he offers" (*juhoti*), clarified butter (*sarpiḥ*) should be used.

ŚŚS 1.2.22: The utterance of *svāhā* occurs at the end of the mantras for the oblations (*homa*). ŚŚS 1.2.23: And [it occurs] at the end of the mantras for the placing of the fuel-sticks (*samid-ādhāna*).
ŚŚS 1.2.24: From the distinctness of the mantras follows the distinctness of the ritual acts.

ŚŚS 1.2.25: The particle *iti* is placed at the end of a mantra. ŚŚS 1.2.26: When instruments are used with the end of a mantra, there is a conjunction of the action with that [mantra]. ŚŚS 1.2.27: Having been prompted, he recites after [the command].
ŚŚS 1.2.28: He sacrifices in that manner.
ŚŚS 1.2.29: This constitutes the ritual common to all sacrifices.
ŚŚS 1.3.1: Having fasted, he sacrifices with the full-moon oblation.
ŚŚS 1.3.2: Likewise with the New Moon sacrifice.
ŚŚS 1.3.3: There are two Full Moon sacrifices. ŚŚS 1.3.4: And [there are] two New Moon sacrifices.
ŚŚS 1.3.5: That day on which the moon sets after it has become full, and that day on which it rises after having set—these two are the *paurṇamāsī* (full-moon) days.
ŚŚS 1.3.6: That day on which one will not see [the moon] tomorrow, and that day on which it is not seen at all—these two are the *amāvāsye* (new-moon) days.
ŚŚS 1.3.7: Regarding the performance of the sacrifice (*ijyā*) on those days, one may act according to one’s desire.

ŚŚS 1.3.8: By the instruction "thus at the full moon" and "thus at the new moon," [the rites] are established as distinct. ŚŚS 1.3.9: And the words connected with that [instruction] are also [restricted]. ŚŚS 1.3.10: The rest is the same.
ŚŚS 1.3.11: In both cases, there is a cake (puroḷāśa) for Agni.
ŚŚS 1.3.12: There is a low-voiced sacrifice (upāṃśuyāja) for Agni-Soma.
ŚŚS 1.3.13: Or it may be for Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 1.3.15: For one who does not offer the *sāṃnāyya*, the second [offering] on the new moon day is dedicated to Indra and Agni.
ŚŚS 1.3.16: For one who offers the *sāṃnāyya*, the offering is dedicated to Indra.
ŚŚS 1.3.17: Or it may be dedicated to Mahendra.
ŚŚS 1.3.18: However, one who is not performing the *saṃnayya* sacrifice performs the *upāṃśuyāja* for Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 1.4.1: Having been addressed, the Hotṛ proceeds between the *utkara* and the *praṇītā* waters; he steps upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with the right forepart of his foot.
ŚŚS 1.4.2: His heel is aligned with the edge of the altar at the rear.
ŚŚS 1.4.3: Having stepped forward to his place. ŚŚS 1.4.4: Being addressed with the call, "To Agni being kindled."

Whom shall I take refuge in? Him I take refuge in. That *chandas* which is your refuge, O Prajāpati, that I take refuge in. As much as you know, O Viṣṇu, so much shall I perform for you. Impelled by the divine Savitṛ, I shall perform the office of the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*). Homage to Agni, the overseer; homage to Vāyu, the listener; homage to Āditya, the announcer. Today I shall speak speech pleasing to the gods, speech to be listened to by men, speech accompanied by *svadhā* for the ancestors, and a firm foundation for all beings. O Praśāstṛ, with my self, my offspring, and my cattle, I take refuge in Prajāpati. May there be safety for us. I shall recite the portion belonging to Prajāpati. "Speech shall perform the office of the officiating priest"—thus taking refuge in Speech, and having murmured "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ," [he proceeds].
ŚŚS 1.4.6: Having uttered the *him* sound three times;
ŚŚS 1.4.7: having joined [the next part] with the verse "pra vo vājā," in a medium tone of voice;
ŚŚS 1.4.8: [he recites] the two triplets beginning with "agna ā yāhi vītaye" and "īḷenya."
ŚŚS 1.4.9: "We choose Agni as the messenger"—this is one verse.
ŚŚS 1.4.10: "Being kindled, O sacrifice"—this is one verse.
ŚŚS 1.4.11: There are three [verses] in the seventeen-fold chant.
ŚŚS 1.4.12: That [is performed] on other occasions than the two seasonal sacrifices (sāyana) and the New and Full Moon sacrifices (darśapūrṇamāsa).

ŚŚS 1.4.13: "O Agni, kindled, invoked with oblations..."—these two verses. ŚŚS 1.4.14: Having joined [the last word of the second verse] with the syllable *praṇava* (oṃ), [he recites]: "O Agni, you are great, O Brāhmaṇa, descendant of Bharata."

ŚŚS 1.4.15: Having recited three ancestral lineages (*ārṣeya*) of the sacrificer from the most recent back to the oldest; ŚŚS 1.4.16: But six [lineages] for one who belongs to two *gotras*; ŚŚS 1.4.17: For a non-Brāhmaṇa, by means of the lineage of his domestic priest (*purohita*).
ŚŚS 1.4.18: [The *praṇava*] belongs to all [the verses] after the word *mānava*.

ŚŚS 1.4.19: Having paused after [the words]: "kindled by the gods, kindled by Manu, praised by the ṛṣis, rejoiced in by the sages, extolled by the poets, sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*), offered with clarified butter.
ŚŚS 1.4.20: Having paused after [the words]: "the leader of sacrifices, the charioteer of rituals, the unassailable Hotṛ, the swift carrier of oblations."

"Thou art the vessel of the gods, the ladle; thou art the cup from which the gods drink. Like the felly around the spokes, O Agni, thou encompassest the gods"—having paused thus, while about to conclude, he invokes the deities:
"Bring the gods for the sacrificer! (ŚŚS 1.4.21–22; 1.5.1).
ŚŚS 1.5.2: "Agni, bring hither; Soma, bring hither"—these are the two portions of clarified butter (ājyabhāgau).

ŚŚS 1.5.3: "Bring hither Agni; bring hither Agni and Soma; or [bring hither] Viṣṇu; bring hither Agni and Soma; bring hither Indra and Agni; bring hither Indra; or [bring hither] Mahendra. ŚŚS 1.5.4: "Bring hither the gods who drink the clarified butter."
"Bring Agni for the office of the Hotṛ;
bring him with his own majesty;
and bring them hither, O Jātavedas, and perform the sacrifice well"—having thus invoked [the deity].
Having sat down with his knees raised, touching the ground with his right forefinger, he recites:
"For this support, may I not be cut off; O Earth, Mother, do not harm me, do not injure me.

I shall conceive honey, I shall win honey, I shall produce honey. Today I shall speak honeyed speech to the gods and pleasant speech to men. With this fifteenfold thunderbolt, I strike down my evil rival."
Or with the *saptadaśa* [stoma].

ŚŚS 1.6.1: When "O Man! has been called out; ŚŚS 1.6.2: "O God Savitṛ, they choose thee here together with Vaiśvānara as father—O Indra, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati—speak forth and sacrifice forth! May we be in the bounty of the Vasus, in the favor of the Rudras."
"O Ādityas, O Ādityas, you who are free from blemish, when at the choosing of this Hotṛ-priest his sidelong glance flew away,
Agni Jātavedas, the far-seeing, brought that back again."
Having recited [the formula], he stands up;
having touched the right shoulder of the Adhvaryu with his right forefinger and the right shoulder of the Agnīdhra with his left, he recites:
"We take hold of Indra, the domestic priest, for the choosing of the Hotṛ."
By which these gods, the Aṅgirases, went to the highest light, to heaven;

by which the sacrificial post and the ninety-nine nooses were spread out between heaven and earth. I bind the simple one; I, the wise, approach. May both these, heaven and earth, be pleasant to me. Thus.
ŚŚS 1.6.4: Having released [the breath] with the words, "May the six expanses protect us from distress: heaven and earth, day and night, water and plants," ŚŚS 1.6.5:
Turning toward the right arm with the words, "I turn according to the turning of Indra; I turn following the turning of the Sun," ŚŚS 1.6.6:

Having torn a dry blade of grass from both ends with the words, "Parāvasu is cast out—he who hates us and whom we hate, along with him," he throws it away toward the south-western intermediate direction.
Having sipped water (ŚŚS 1.6.7),
having placed [the grass] that is not dry with its tip pointing north (ŚŚS 1.6.8),
and having sat down with the words, "Here I sit in the seat of Arvāvasu" (ŚŚS 1.6.9).
ŚŚS 1.6.10: Having placed his right hand over his left, and having extended his hands forward, he mutters:

ŚŚS 1.6.11: "Homage to Heaven and Earth, to the two Hotṛs, the first-born, the all-makers! You two are the protectors of my body; guard my body, do not harm me, and do not cause me distress," he says, looking at the Āhavanīya and the Gārhapatya fires. ŚŚS 1.6.12: While moving toward the north, he says: "This is your space."

ŚŚS 1.6.13: Having murmured, "O Viśvedevas, teach that today of speech; obeisance to the great ones. ŚŚS 1.6.14: Having paused after [murmuring], "May Agni know the office of the Hotṛ; may Agni know the Hotṛ's duty; may he fulfill the invocation; well for thee, O sacrificer, is the deity. ŚŚS 1.6.15:
[He murmurs] in a low voice, "He who has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ."

"O Adhvaryu, take up the butter-filled ladle that seeks the gods and contains all boons; let us praise the gods, we praise the others who are to be praised, we bow to those who are to be bowed to, and we sacrifice to those worthy of sacrifice. Having thus taken up the two spoons, he performs the five fore-sacrifices (*prayāja*).
ŚŚS 1.7.1: "May the fuel-sticks, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter"—this is the first. ŚŚS 1.7.2: "May [the fuel-sticks] partake of the clarified butter"—this is the second.

ŚŚS 1.7.3: "May Narāśaṃsa, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter"—this is the second [verse], for the Vasiṣṭhas, the Śunakas, the Atris, the Vadhryaśvas, the Kaṇvas, the Saṃkṛtis, for kṣatriyas, and for those desiring progeny.
ŚŚS 1.7.4: "May the Iḍās, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter"—this is the third.
ŚŚS 1.7.5: "May Barhis, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter"—this is the fourth.

ŚŚS 1.7.6: *svāhā* to Agni; *svāhā* to Soma; *svāhā* to Agni; *svāhā* to Agni and Soma, or to Viṣṇu; *svāhā* to Agni and Soma; *svāhā* to Indra and Agni, or to Indra or Mahendra; *svāhā* to the gods who drink the clarified butter (*ājyapāḥ*). "May they, being pleased, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter oblation"—these are the *yājyās* for the fore-offerings (*prayājas*). ŚŚS 1.8.1: "Agni [destroys] the Vṛtras" and "Thou, O Soma, art the lord of the virtuous"—these two *ājyabhāgas* at the full moon sacrifice are the *vārtraghnas*. ŚŚS 1.8.2: "Agni with the ancient [prayer]" and "O Soma, with songs"—these two at the new moon sacrifice are the *vṛdhanvants*.
ŚŚS 1.8.3: "May Agni, being pleased, accept the clarified butter as an oblation; may Soma, being pleased, accept the clarified butter as an oblation"—this is the *yājyā*.
ŚŚS 1.8.4: "Agni is the head"—this is the *puronuvākyā* for the offering to Agni.
ŚŚS 1.8.5: "Of the sacrifice, the lord of the world"—this is the *yājyā*.
"O Agni and Soma, this... is the *puronuvākyā* for the *upāṃśuyāja*.
"May Agni and Soma, being pleased, partake of the oblation of clarified butter... is the *yājyā*. "This [is] Viṣṇu... and "Vaṣaṭ to you, O Viṣṇu! are for the offering to Viṣṇu.

ŚŚS 1.8.9: Or [the verse] "juṣāṇo vā" (or enjoying). ŚŚS 1.8.10: "O Agni and Soma, you two who possess common knowledge, [accept] these... for the offering to Agni and Soma. ŚŚS 1.8.11: "O Indra and Agni, with your protection, come forth for the sake of the people... for the offering to Indra and Agni.

ŚŚS 1.8.12: "O Indra, [the one] who wins," and "Thou hast conquered"—these are for the *sāmnāyya*. ŚŚS 1.8.13: "Great is Indra by his might," and "Great is Indra, like a man"—these are for the *māhendra* offering.
ŚŚS 1.8.14: "Indra for you from all sides," and "Rejoice with thy two bay steeds"—these are for the *indra* offering which has no substitute.
"Delight the gods"—this is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.

He has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni and Soma, or of Viṣṇu; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni and Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra and Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra, or of Mahendra; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter (*ājyapāḥ*). May he sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; may he sacrifice to his own majesty; may they both offer the sacrifice.
"May he who knows all beings (Jātavedas) perform the worship; may he enjoy the oblations at the sacrifice. O Agni, whatever today of the people's sacrifice..."—this is the *yājyā* verse.
Having uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call, there is the touching [of the mouth].
While about to invoke the *iḍā*, he anoints the forefinger of his right hand.

On the best and the middle joint [of the finger], he applies the ointment first to the lower lip with the formula: "I eat of what has been offered by the Lord of Speech for the sake of food and the out-breath.
Then, to the upper lip, he applies the second [ointment] with the formula: "I eat of what has been offered by the Lord of Mind for the sake of strength and the up-breath."
Having sipped water,
holding the *uttara-iḷā* with his right hand,
with fingers neither extended nor clenched into a fist.
ŚŚS 1.10.6: Having taken up the *pañcama* [note] himself; ŚŚS 1.10.7:
Holding it level with his mouth or level with his heart; ŚŚS 1.11.1a:
"The *bṛhat* has been invoked together with heaven, together with the sun, together with sight; may the *bṛhat*, together with heaven, together with the sun, together with sight, invoke me!"

The Vāmadevya has been invoked together with the intermediate space, with Vāyu, and with the breath; may the Vāmadevya invoke me together with the intermediate space, with Vāyu, and with the breath. The Rathantara has been invoked together with the earth, with Agni, with speech, and with cattle; may the Rathantara invoke me together with the earth, with Agni, with speech, and with cattle. The stationary world has been invoked; may the stationary world invoke me.
Invited is the moving world; let the moving world invite me.
Invited is the companion, the portion to be consumed; let the companion, the portion to be consumed, invite me.
Invited are the seven officiating priests; let the seven officiating priests invite me.
The cows have been invited together with the milk-mixture; may the cows together with the milk-mixture invite me.
Speech has been invited together with the breath; may speech together with the breath invite me.
Speech has been invited together with the mind; may speech together with the mind invite me.

Having murmured, "Iḷā, the rain, has been invoked; may Iḷā, the rain, invoke me! Iḷā, the overcomer, has been invoked; may Iḷā, the overcomer, invoke me! O Iḷā, you are indeed invoked; be pleased with me, O Iḷā! he invokes Iḷā.
ŚŚS 1.12.1a: Iḍā is invoked; Iḍā is invoked. May Iḍā call upon us; may Iḍā be invoked. She is the daughter of Manu, whose foot is dripping with ghee, belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa.
ŚŚS 1.12.1b: The prayer fashioned by the gods is invoked.
The divine *adhvaryu*s are invoked; the human ones who protect this sacrifice are also invoked.
"And may they strengthen the lord of the sacrifice.
"The two ancient, law-abiding goddesses, Heaven and Earth, mothers of the gods, are invited.

"This sacrificer is invited to the subsequent worship of the gods; he is invited to the preparation of abundant oblations. May the gods enjoy this my oblation! Having thus invoked him with the words "He is invited," he invites him to that [portion].
ŚŚS 1.12.2: Having pounded [the grain]; ŚŚS 1.12.3: He breathes out four times while holding the *iḍā* between; ŚŚS 1.12.4: Or he does so four times at the end.
"Thou art *iḷā*, thou art pleasant, thou art the maker of pleasantness; as such, do thou establish us in good offspring and royal prosperity.

O beloved one, may I attain thy favor; O invited one, may I obtain thy invitation. For the splendor of the mouth and for the fragrance of the breath, I eat thee. Having thus eaten the northern *iḷā* portion, [the priests] and the sacrificer as the fifth eat the other [portion].
ŚŚS 1.12.7: Until the wiping [of the hands], there is restraint of speech.
ŚŚS 1.12.8: With the three verses beginning "idam āpaḥ," they perform the purification within the altar (antarvedi) where the strainers (pavitra) are present.
ŚŚS 1.12.9: Once the portion for the Brahman has been carried around, they bring the Anvāhārya mess of rice.

ŚŚS 1.12.10: This is the time for the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) for all *iṣṭi* sacrifices. ŚŚS 1.12.11: There is no *anvāhārya* rice in those sacrifices where a specific sacrificial fee has been prescribed.
ŚŚS 1.12.12: "This is your fuel-stick, O Agni; through it may you grow and may you swell."
"May we increase and may we swell.
Having thus consecrated the fuel-stick (*samidh*),
he performs three after-offerings (*anuyāja*).
May the divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*) partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.
May the divine Narāśaṃsa partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.

May the divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the possessor of beautiful riches, the delightful, the sage, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificer, the invoker, more skilled at sacrificing than any other invoker—partake [of the offering]. O Agni, having paused after reciting: "The gods whom you have sacrificed for, whom you have satisfied, who have rejoiced in your office as invoker..."

ŚŚS 1.13.4: "That Hotṛ-offering which has been performed, which goes to the gods—send this sacrifice up to the gods in heaven. And you, O Agni, being the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Hotṛ, [act] for the winning of wealth; at the utterance of 'Homage,' partake of the gift of wealth. These are the *yājyā* verses for the *anuyāja*s. ŚŚS 1.14.1: When addressed with "Recite the *sūktavāka*," ŚŚS 1.14.2:
[He recites: "O Heaven and Earth, this has become auspicious. We have accomplished the *sūktavāka* and the utterance of 'Homage. May we succeed in the recitation of the *sūkta*."

Having paused at "O Agni, you are the one who speaks the hymns," [he continues] with "May Heaven and Earth be favorable to us at this sacrifice, O sacrificer, being full of grace. Having paused, [he continues] with "The two who are auspicious, quick-giving, tireless, unfailing, wide-ranging, and providers of safety. Having paused, [he continues].

"May the rain-giving heaven and the flowing waters be auspicious and blissful; may they be full of vigor and full of milk, easy of access and good to dwell in; may we obtain their favor"—having paused at this point:
"Agni has enjoyed the oblation; he has increased it; he has made it greater and more glorious. "Soma has enjoyed the oblation; he has increased it; he has made it greater and more glorious."
Agni has enjoyed the oblation; he has grown strong; he has made it greater and more glorious.
Agni and Soma have enjoyed the oblation; they have grown strong; they have made it greater and more glorious.
Or Viṣṇu [has done so].
Agni and Soma have enjoyed the oblation; they have grown strong; they have achieved greatness and further excellence.

Indra and Agni have enjoyed the oblation; they have grown strong; they have achieved greatness and further excellence. Indra has enjoyed the oblation; he has grown strong; he has achieved greatness and further excellence.
Or [it is] Mahendra. ŚŚS 1.14.14:
The gods who drink the clarified butter (ājyapāḥ) have enjoyed the clarified butter; they have increased; they have made it great, even greater. ŚŚS 1.14.15:
Agni, through the office of the Hotṛ, has enjoyed the oblation; he has increased; he has made it great, even greater.
In this sacrifice, which is successful and leads to the gods, this sacrificer makes this aspiration.

Having pronounced the two names of the sacrificer, "So-and-so" and "So-and-so," he aspires for the subsequent worship of the gods; he aspires for the performance of further oblations; he aspires for long life; he aspires for good progeny; he aspires for the celestial abode.

Whatever he aspires for by means of this oblation—may he attain it, may he prosper in it, may the gods grant it to him, and may the god Agni favor it for the sake of the gods; and we, the humans, [attain it] from Agni.
"May what was sacrificed and what was offered be successful;
may both Heaven and Earth protect him from distress; may your path lead him here; this is homage to the gods.
Having placed his joined palms upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he mutters: "Homage, up... (ŚŚS 1.14.20).
ŚŚS 1.14.21: When told, "Recite the *śamyor*," he says "That *śamyor*" and, having uttered the *śamyor-vākya*, touches [water].
ŚŚS 1.14.22: From the taking up of the ladle (*srug-ādāpana*) until the end of the *yājyā-bhāga* [recited] in the low pitch (*mandra*).
ŚŚS 1.14.23: The subsequent [portion] with the middle pitch (*madhyamā*).
ŚŚS 1.14.24: [The offering] beginning with the after-offerings (*anuyāja*) is performed with the final verse.
ŚŚS 1.15.1: They perform the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings silently (*upāṃśu*) at the Gārhapatya fire.
ŚŚS 1.15.2: He sacrifices to Soma, Tvaṣṭṛ, the wives of the gods, and Agni Gṛhapati.
ŚŚS 1.15.3: For one desiring offspring, [the verses] for Rākā and Sinīvālī come first, followed by those for Gṛhapati.

ŚŚS 1.15.4: "Do thou swell" (*ā pyāyasva*); "May thy milks unite" (*sam te payāṃsi*); "May Tvaṣṭṛ here" (*iha tvaṣṭāram*); "That seed of ours" (*tan nas turīpam*); "The wives of the gods and the goddesses" (*devānām patnīr uta gnāḥ*); "May they enjoy" (*vyantu*); "I invoke Rākā" (*rākām aham*); "Those which are thine, O Rākā" (*yās te rāke*); "O Sinīvālī" (*sinīvāli*); "In whom the arm" (*yāsu bāhuḥ*); "Agni the Hotṛ, the master of the house" (*agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ*); "We indeed thee, O master of the house" (*vayam u tvā gṛhapate*). ŚŚS 1.15.5: Having murmured "As surely as that, O Vasus" (*yathā ha tyad vasavaḥ*), he invokes Iḷā.

ŚŚS 1.15.6: Or there is a modification [of the formula]: "This sacrificer's wife has been invoked. ŚŚS 1.15.7: The offerings to the wives end with the *iḍā* invocation. ŚŚS 1.15.8: Or they end with the *śamyu* formula.
ŚŚS 1.15.9: Having unfastened the *yoktra* with the mantra, "I release thee," [he releases] the *veda*.

ŚŚS 1.15.10: Having placed the *veda* and the unfastened *yoktra* into the joined palms of his wife, ŚŚS 1.15.11: While sprinkling water around the *veda* and the *yoktra*, he mutters [the following].
For the sake of desire: "Thou art the Veda; as thou, O Veda, becamest a Veda for the gods, so do thou become a Veda for us.

Thou art the Veda; thou art acquisition; may I acquire. Thou art action; thou art the instrument; thou art the performance. Thou art gain; thou art the winner; may I win. [He offers] the ghee-filled, nest-like, thousandfold increase of wealth.
"May the Veda grant a prize-winning horse.
With these words, he makes the wife recite over the Veda;
then, grasping blades of grass, it is placed between her thighs.

Reciting "Stretching the thread" (tantum tanvan), he spreads the sacrificial grass (barhis) to the north of the Gārhapatya fire. Having worshipped the remainder of the Veda with the formula, "Thou art full; thou art filling; fill me with offspring and cattle," he [proceeds] with this [verse]: "O Agni Jātavedas, by this prayer (brahman) thou hast sacrificed the sacrifice; sitting within, thou art the first among them."
"Winning the prize, release [the horse] with a good release; bestow wealth upon us, O Jātavedas!
Having thus paid homage to the Āhavanīya fire, he touches water and releases [the horse].

ŚŚS 1.16.1: The New and Full Moon sacrifices (darśapūrṇamāsa) have been explained; they are the archetype (prakṛti) for the Iṣṭis, the Animal Sacrifices (paśubandha), and the other rites. ŚŚS 1.16.2: It is called the "archetype" because of its underlying connection (anvaya). ŚŚS 1.16.3: That which is offered between the two Ājyabhāga offerings and the Sviṣṭakṛt offering is termed the "insertion" (āvāpa); that constitutes the principal part (pradhāna).
The others are its ancillaries (ŚŚS 1.16.4).
Their manifestation occurs when there is no separation in time (ŚŚS 1.16.5).
That is the definition of the *tantra* (ŚŚS 1.16.6).
ŚŚS 1.16.7: It is heard in the scriptures that the offering is connected with various high and low deities.

ŚŚS 1.16.8: In that case, when there is a modification of the deity, the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses belong to that specific deity. ŚŚS 1.16.9: And that deity is indicated in the places where the *nigama* formulas occur.

ŚŚS 1.16.10: At the final *prayāja*, in the *sviṣṭakṛt* *nigada*, and in the *sūktavāka*, the deities being sacrificed to enter [the formula]; therefore, these are the places for insertion (*nigama-sthāna*). ŚŚS 1.16.11: We shall explain the modifications (*vikāra*) as they occur in sequence.
ŚŚS 1.16.12: When it is said "a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice," one should understand the two *vārtraghna* verses.
ŚŚS 1.16.13: The two [stotras] containing the word *vṛdhant* are modifications of the new moon sacrifice (*amāvāsyā*).
ŚŚS 1.1.14: In the absence of a specific injunction, they serve as optional alternatives (*vikalpa*).
ŚŚS 1.16.15: [The deity is determined] from the name of the divinity.
ŚŚS 1.16.16: Or rather, it is because of the nature of the oblation.
ŚŚS 1.16.17: In the case of a combination, it is because of the nature of the oblation.
ŚŚS 1.16.18: There is a restrictive rule based on commonality.
ŚŚS 1.16.19: And there is a set of seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses.
ŚŚS 1.16.20: In the *iṣṭi*, animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*), and other rites, it is otherwise because of a specific scriptural injunction.
ŚŚS 1.16.21: In the optional sacrifices (*kāmyā-iṣṭis*), the oblation is to be offered in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).

And we shall explain them in their proper sequence. ŚŚS 1.17.1: In the section concerning injunctions (*codanā-prakaraṇa*), there is the citation of the opening words (*pratīka-grahaṇa*) of the *havis*-offerings, as well as the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses, provided there is no connection with another purpose. ŚŚS 1.17.2: In cases involving two or more [verses], they follow the order of the injunctions.
ŚŚS 1.17.3: By means of the deity; ŚŚS 1.17.4:
And by means of its characteristic mark;
ŚŚS 1.17.5: If, when the deities have been approached, he does not obtain [the desired result], he should satisfy them by means of that deity through its characteristic mark.
ŚŚS 1.17.6: But when [the deities] are approached [in sequence], they proceed [together].

ŚŚS 1.17.7: Since an oblation is frequently enjoined for each individual deity, one should recognize that in such cases, those *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses which are taught first apply everywhere. ŚŚS 1.17.8: Furthermore, it is not possible to enumerate the sacrifices (*iṣṭi*) individually.

ŚŚS 1.17.9: In that case, when the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses have not been specifically prescribed, one should seek out two verses for those deities in the *gāyatrī* and *triṣṭubh* meters. ŚŚS 1.17.10: Or, having omitted the *uṣṇih* and *bṛhatī* meters [from the search].
ŚŚS 1.17.11: However, the *yājyā* verse must be longer.
ŚŚS 1.17.12: Or they may be equal.
ŚŚS 1.17.13: Wherever any of these characteristics should be present; ŚŚS 1.17.14:
"I call," "we call," "hear us," "come hither," "sit down upon this sacrificial grass"—these are the characteristics of the *puronuvākyā* verses.
"‘Eat, drink, enjoy, rejoice, be impetuous, partake!’—these are the characteristics of the *yājyā* [offering verse].
ŚŚS 1.17.16: That which has its characteristic at the beginning is the *puronuvākyā*. ŚŚS 1.17.17: That which has its characteristic at the end is the *yājyā*."
ŚŚS 1.17.18: If he does not obtain that deity, he should sacrifice with the two [verses] addressed to Nara and Nārāśaṃsa.
ŚŚS 1.17.19: "Hear this our invocation as we call upon you with our songs;
sit down here upon this sacred grass of ours."

May you sit down in due order upon the strewn sacrificial grass; come here today, being entreated by us. Without an angry mind, take pleasure in this; partake of our oblation, which is presented and offered.
Thus one should reflect upon [the formulas] in the case of sacrifices to two deities or many deities.
Or rather, one should adapt them to the archetypal forms; or rather, one should adapt them to the archetypal forms.
In the spring, the establishment of the sacred fires (agnyādheya) is for a Brāhmaṇa.
ŚŚS 2.1.2: For a Kṣatriya, in the summer;
ŚŚS 2.1.3: For a Vaiśya, in the rainy season;
ŚŚS 2.1.4: Or in the autumn.
ŚŚS 2.1.5: The cool season (*śiśira*) is for all classes (*varṇa*).
ŚŚS 2.1.6: For one who intends to sacrifice with Soma, there is freedom of choice regarding the seasons.
ŚŚS 2.1.7: He should establish [the sacred fires] on either the new moon day or the full moon day.
ŚŚS 2.1.8: Or during the bright fortnight under an auspicious lunar mansion;
ŚŚS 2.1.9: namely, the three beginning with Kṛttikā and the three beginning with Phalgunī.
ŚŚS 2.2.1: Now, the times for the iṣṭi sacrifice.
ŚŚS 2.2.2: [The initiation] takes place immediately, or after twelve days, a month, a season, or a year.
ŚŚS 2.2.3: There is an *iṣṭi* sacrifice for Agni Pavamāna.
ŚŚS 2.2.4: It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice (*paurṇamāsī*).
ŚŚS 2.2.5: *agna āyūṃṣi*, *agne pavasva*.
ŚŚS 2.2.6: *tam hi śaśvanta īḷate*, *te syāma ye agnayaḥ*—these are for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 2.2.7: *agnaye ca pāvakāya*, *agnaye ca śucaye*—this is the second [verse].
ŚŚS 2.2.8: It is a modification of the Amāvāsyā [rite].
ŚŚS 2.2.9: *agne pāvaka sa naḥ pāvaka*. ŚŚS 2.2.10: *agniḥ śucivratatama ud agne śucayaḥ*.
ŚŚS 2.2.11: "Agni, Agni with oblations; by Agni is Aṅgiras kindled"—this is for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. ŚŚS 2.2.12: The third [verse] is for Aditi.
ŚŚS 2.2.13: "O Agni, thou who art far-reaching; O Soma, those which are thine"—these two Ājyabhāga portions contain the word *sád*.
And [the hymn]: "O Aditi, the Great One...
We invoke for protection the Great Mother of those who follow good vows, the consort of Ṛta;
the Aditi who possesses abundant dominion, who is undecaying, far-reaching, a provider of excellent shelter, and a wise leader.
ŚŚS 2.2.15: *pra iddho agne*, *imaṃ agne*—these two Virāj verses are for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
ŚŚS 2.2.16: They perform four [verses], making the first one for Agni.
ŚŚS 2.2.17: *agne dyumnena*, *upa tvā juhvaḥ*.

ŚŚS 2.2.18: "arcantas tvā agnim stomena" is the *sviṣṭakṛt* [verse]. ŚŚS 2.3.1: Or it may be performed at the first [offering] with a common ritual procedure (*samānatantre*). ŚŚS 2.3.2: Or at the middle [offering].
ŚŚS 2.3.3: Or it may consist of two oblations.
ŚŚS 2.3.4: For a Brāhmaṇa, the second [oblation] is dedicated to Aditi and Indra-Agni.
ŚŚS 2.3.5: Or it is dedicated to Agni-Soma.
ŚŚS 2.3.6: For a Kṣatriya, [the offering] is for Indra.
ŚŚS 2.3.7: For a Vaiśya, [the offering] is for the Viśvedevas.
ŚŚS 2.3.8: "O Viśvedevas, upon the strewn sacrificial grass..."
ŚŚS 2.3.9: Or, for two [offerings], the first may be dedicated to Agni.

ŚŚS 2.3.10: With clarified butter, one offers to the deities of the body before the *puroḍāśa*; and to Agni Pavamāna, Agni Pāvaka, and Agni Śuci after it. ŚŚS 2.3.11: "O Agni, with all the Agnis," and "O Agni, with all the Agnis"—these are the formulas for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 2.3.12: The second [offering] is for Aditi. ŚŚS 2.3.13:

It is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice (Amāvāsyā). ŚŚS 2.3.14: For three days, there is one oblation consisting of the Tākṣṇī verses with the Tanū-devatās; another day with the Vaiṣṇava verses as the second; another day with the Āditya verses as the third; and on the tenth day, the unmodified [verse] for Agni.
ŚŚS 2.3.15: In all [these offerings], the oblations are performed in a low voice (upāṃśu).
ŚŚS 2.3.16: And there is a fifteenfold number (pāñcadaśya) of the sāmidhenī verses. ŚŚS 2.3.17: In the offering to Āditya, there are seventeen [sāmidhenīs].
ŚŚS 2.3.18: There are twenty-four sacrificial fees.
ŚŚS 2.3.19: Or twelve. ŚŚS 2.3.20: Or six.
ŚŚS 2.3.21: A horse;
ŚŚS 2.3.22: A hundred-measure chariot, a garment, and goats;
ŚŚS 2.3.23: For twelve nights, he himself should perform the oblations.
ŚŚS 2.3.24: And speaking the truth;
ŚŚS 2.3.25: And giving to guests;

ŚŚS 2.3.26: One who has established the sacred fires shall not eat meat from an animal without having performed the *paśu* sacrifice, nor shall he eat the fruits of new herbs without having performed the *āgrayaṇa* sacrifice.
ŚŚS 2.4.1: Prior to the New and Full Moon sacrifices, there is the Anvārambhaṇīyā offering.
ŚŚS 2.4.2: [It consists of oblations] to Agni-Viṣṇu, to Sarasvatī, and to Sarasvant.
ŚŚS 2.4.3: O Agni and Viṣṇu, great is that majesty of yours; drink [the offering], for the secret names of ghee are yours.
In every house, this fair praise approaches you; let your tongue move toward the clarified butter.

O Agni and Viṣṇu, you enjoy your great and beloved domain; delighting in the secret [places] of the clarified butter, and bestowing the seven treasures in every house, let your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.
ŚŚS_2.4.4: "Purifying us, we invoke Sarasvatī with our ladle. ŚŚS_2.4.5:
"Desiring wives, he has grown great.
ŚŚS_2.4.6: Some [perform] an offering of five oblations to Agni Bhagina and Vratapati.
ŚŚS 2.4.7: O Agni, you are glory accompanied by heroic sons; you are Bhaga for us. ŚŚS 2.4.8:
O Agni, protector of vows, [recite] "that which we [have done] unto you. ŚŚS 2.4.9:
This is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice.
ŚŚS 2.4.10: And a milch cow is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 2.5.1: The optional re-establishment of the sacred fires (punarādheya) is for one who is ignorant [of the proper procedure].
ŚŚS 2.5.2: For one intending to move the fires, there is an offering to Agni and to Agni Vaiśvānara.
ŚŚS_2.5.3: May Vaiśvānara come from afar for our protection;
may Agni, who is praised in heaven, attend to our well-spoken hymns.
ŚŚS_2.5.4: The period for re-establishing the sacred fires (*punarādheya*) is during the middle of the rainy season.
ŚŚS_2.5.5: And the Punarvasu asterism; ŚŚS_2.5.6: Or the new moon following the latter Āṣāḍhī;
ŚŚS_2.5.7: And the time of midday.
ŚŚS 2.5.8: And there is an offering to Agni on five potsherds. ŚŚS 2.5.9: And there are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses.
ŚŚS 2.5.10: And in three of the *prayāja* offerings, the word "Agni" is modified.
ŚŚS_2.5.11: Tanūnapāt, Agni, Iḷas, with Agni; Barhis, Agni. ŚŚS_2.5.12:
The first Ājyabhāga [is dedicated] to Vṛtrahan. ŚŚS_2.5.13:
Or [the verse] "Awaken Agni with the hymn" (agnim stomena bodhaya) is for Agni the Awakened.
ŚŚS 2.5.14: "O Agni, [grant] lives" (*agna āyūṃṣi*) is for Agni Pavamāna. ŚŚS 2.5.15: "Come here, O Indra, I shall speak to you" (*ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi*) is for Indumat.
ŚŚS 2.5.16: Or else, "Agni is the head" (*agnir mūrdhā*) is for Retasvat.
ŚŚS 2.5.17: He performs the sacrifice as prescribed.
ŚŚS 2.5.18: "O Agni, him today..."—this is the first [verse]; at the third oblation, the second and fourth [verses] belong to the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 2.5.19: "The divine barhis for the winning of wealth from Agni; the divine Narāśaṃsa for the winning of wealth from Agni."
ŚŚS 2.5.20: They say that the case-endings [of the word] *agni* are used in the four preceding *prayāja*s and in the two *anuyāja*s. ŚŚS 2.5.21: And these [words] are whispered (*upāṃśu*).
ŚŚS 2.5.22: And so is the subsequent *ājyabhāga*.
ŚŚS 2.5.23: And the oblation.
ŚŚS 2.5.24: Or everything together with the two preceding after-offerings (anuyāja). ŚŚS 2.5.25: Or ending with the oblation.
ŚŚS 2.5.26: Or rather, the oblation itself.
ŚŚS 2.5.27: A worn-out garment that has been sewn back together, a repaired chariot, a draft-ox, or gold is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 2.5.28: The second [offering] is for Aditi.
ŚŚS 2.5.29: It is a modification of the new moon sacrifice (Amāvāsyā).
ŚŚS 2.5.30: Or it belongs to Agni and Varuṇa.
ŚŚS 2.5.31: [The verses] are "sa tvam no agne 'vamaḥ" and "tvam no agne varuṇasya vidvān."
ŚŚS 2.6.1: He performs the Agnihotra sacrifice both in the evening and in the morning.
ŚŚS 2.6.2: Before the shadows meet, he draws the Āhavanīya fire from the Gārhapatya fire.
ŚŚS 2.6.3: When the night is brightening.
ŚŚS 2.6.4: [The lighting of the fire] is the making manifest of that which is maintained perpetually.
ŚŚS 2.6.5: [Those who are to be honored are] a Brāhmaṇa who has heard the Vedas and one who has attained prosperity, a village headman, and a member of the royal class (Kṣatriya).
ŚŚS 2.6.6: While the fire is being lifted up, [one recites]: "Lift me up from the evil that I have done unknowingly and that which I have done knowingly."
"Whatever sin we have committed here during the day, protect us from all of that, O one who has been lifted up!
I offer an oblation of immortality into the immortal; I offer Agni upon the earth for the conquest of immortality.
By means of this, may I conquer the infinite world which Prajāpati first conquered. (ŚŚS 2.6.7)
ŚŚS 2.6.8: "Of the night"—this is the modification for the morning.

ŚŚS 2.6.9: Having swept around [the fire], when he is about to offer the oblation: ŚŚS 2.6.10: Having sprinkled water three times each around [the fire] with the formula, "I sprinkle thee, the Order, with Truth," and having offered the oblation.

ŚŚS 2.6.11: "With truth I sprinkle thee with the *ṛta*," thus [he says] in the morning. ŚŚS 2.6.12: "Thou art the continuity of the sacrifice; for the continuity of the sacrifice, I lead thee," thus [he says], pouring a continuous stream of water from the *gārhapatya* fire to the *āhavanīya* fire.
ŚŚS 2.6.13: "Stretching the thread," [he says] when a wild beast has passed between [the fires].
ŚŚS 2.7.1: He offers when the sun has first set;
ŚŚS 2.7.2: or while a constellation is still visible; ŚŚS 2.7.3: or at dawn, as the sun is rising.
ŚŚS 2.7.4: Or [it may be performed] when [the sun] has risen.
ŚŚS 2.7.5: But one should direct the mind toward it at the earlier time.
ŚŚS 2.7.6: For its failure, there is an expiation.
ŚŚS_2.7.7: Having drawn up [the milk], having sat until sunrise, having offered the oblation, and having granted a boon, he should consecrate it with the mantra "bhūḥ.
ŚŚS_2.7.8: Or, without having offered [the morning oblation], having carried away the Āhavanīya fire and having led forward another [fire], he should offer.
ŚŚS_2.7.9: Milk, barley-gruel, curd, and clarified butter are the oblations for the Agnihotra.
ŚŚS 2.7.10: He does not place curd over [the ghee]. ŚŚS 2.7.11: He does not pour water back into the ghee.
ŚŚS 2.7.12: Having thrown two young *kuśa* blades into it, he draws up the ghee.

ŚŚS 2.7.13: To the west of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, the sacrificer, standing facing it, worships the sun with the formula: "For the sake of truth and cosmic order (*ṛta*), I shall lead thee, the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*)," at evening. ŚŚS 2.7.14: "For the sake of cosmic order and truth, I shall lead thee, the sacrificial fee," he says [with this formula] to the *āhavanīya* fire at morning.
ŚŚS 2.7.15: To the north of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire is the path for the sacrificer's movement.
ŚŚS 2.7.16: To the south-west of the Āhavanīya fire is the seat. ŚŚS 2.7.17: Likewise, to the south-west of the Gārhapatya fire is the seat for the wife.
ŚŚS 2.7.18: "Thou art rain; cut off my evil. Thou art knowledge; drive away my evil"—with these words he sips water.
And he restrains his speech.
To the south, they release the Agnihotrī cow.
And they should not pass between [the fire and the cow].
ŚŚS 2.8.3: Nor should one have it milked by a *śūdra*.
ŚŚS 2.8.4: In the evening, he mutters: "Milk for Agni and for the gods.
ŚŚS 2.8.5: In the morning, [he mutters]: "Milk for Sūrya and for the gods."
ŚŚS 2.8.6: "Hunger and thirst [afflict] women; may women not afflict you two! With Agni as a protector, with a calf as a hero"—thus [he says] at evening and morning. ŚŚS 2.8.7:

"With the Anvāhāryapacana fire as a hero"—this is [the formula] when there is a female calf. ŚŚS 2.8.8: "O makers of prosperity, make prosperity for us!"—having removed the embers from the Gārhapatya fire toward the north using the *upaveṣa* (fire-stirring stick), he places the vessel upon it. "With hunger and thirst" [is used]; "with the Agnihotra-pot as a hero, with the Gārhapatya as a hero"—this is the modification.
ŚŚS 2.8.9: Having kindled a fuel-stick with the formula, "O Agni, look upon [this] with your eye," and having illuminated it;

ŚŚS 2.8.10: having poured back water with the dipping-spoon (sruva) while reciting, "Together with the sap of the waters and the plants"; ŚŚS 2.8.11: having heated it again and silently illuminated it once more.
Having moved the fire three times toward the north,
as if not cutting off [the continuity],
and having touched the embers from the south while saying, "Homage to the gods," [he proceeds].

ŚŚS 2.8.15: Having pushed back those [grains] that have been well-pushed-back with the formula "For Subhūti, va! ŚŚS 2.8.16: Having heated both the *sruva* and the *sruk* ladles, he pours [the ghee] up with the *sruk*; the modification is [made] with the verse beginning "Hunger and thirst," using the *sruk* and the *sruva* with the word "vīreṇa.
ŚŚS 2.8.17: Four or five times.

ŚŚS 2.8.18: For each ladleful [offered with] the *sruva* spoon, there is a mantra. ŚŚS 2.8.19: When [the oblation] has been poured out, he touches the *sruc* ladle. ŚŚS 2.8.20: In the evening, he murmurs: "In harmony with the gods who move in the evening."
ŚŚS 2.8.21: "In unison with the gods who travel at dawn"—thus [he offers] in the morning.

ŚŚS 2.8.22: Having placed the *sruk* ladle to the north of the *gārhapatya* fire, having taken a fuel-stick (*samidh*) of *palāśa* wood one span (*prādeśa*) long, and having carried the *sruk* across the middle [of the space], he places the *sruk* upon *kuśa* grass with tips pointing north behind the *āhavanīya* fire. He then places the fuel-stick upon it, using the mantra beginning with "from hunger and thirst," with the modification: "with the heroic *āhavanīya*. ŚŚS 2.8.23: Having carried the fuel-stick across by two finger-breadths, he makes an offering over it.
ŚŚS 2.9.1: "Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā"—thus at evening. ŚŚS 2.9.2: "Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā"—thus in the morning.
ŚŚS 2.9.3: Having bent the right knee during those [oblations] that do not have the *vaṣaṭ* call.
Having set it down, without letting [the ladle] touch the northern one, he silently pours more [milk] into the eastern ladle.
He should fill the ladle as full as possible.
Having touched the coals with the base of the ladle and having twice lifted the ladle toward the north, he sets it down.

"Breath has gone to the heavenly world; having conquered, I conquer; may there be safety for me from the state of being without a world, without a son, and without cattle," thus the sacrificer breathes out over the first oblation.

"Exhalation has come to the self; having conquered, I conquer; may there be safety for me from the state of being without a world, without a son, and without cattle," thus he breathes in over the second oblation.
"May that blessing which belongs to the successful sacrifice be fulfilled for me."
ŚŚS 2.9.10: After the two oblations have been offered, he wipes [the fire] twice toward the west in the evening.
ŚŚS 2.9.11: He wipes it upward toward the south in the morning.
ŚŚS 2.9.12: He mentally applies the first wiping to the kuśa grass blades, thinking, "I gratify the plants."

ŚŚS 2.9.13: He places his right hand, palm upward, to the north of the south [hand], mentally thinking, "I gratify the ancestors. ŚŚS 2.9.14: Having tasted [the food] twice with the forefinger, having turned toward the north while making a sound, having eaten with [the spoon] whose handle points eastward, having tilted it so its handle points eastward, having licked it clean, having washed it, having sipped water, and having splashed water toward the northeast, he directs [the offering] toward the northeast.
This is the ritual procedure for a single oblation (*ekahoma*).
However, when offering oblations in all [the fires], having placed the woolen ladle (*ūrṇāsruk*) to the north of the *gārhapatya* fire, [he recites]:
"May the Lord of Prosperity bestow prosperity here; may Prajāpati cause offspring to be born here."
Svāhā to Agni, the possessor of wealth, the possessor of cattle, the lord of nourishment!
Svāhā to Agni, the master of the house!
Svāhā to Agni!
Silently, the fourth [offering] is made at the Gārhapatya fire:
"That most excellent splendor of Savitṛ—*bhūr*, speech! May it become much, may it become more for me, svāhā!
We meditate upon the radiance of the god—*bhuvaḥ*, breath! May it become greater, may it become more for me, svāhā!"
"May he who impels our thoughts [bestow] the name 'Light' (Svar); may everything be mine, Svāhā!
To Agni, the eater of food, the lord of food, Svāhā!"—this is the fourth [offering] on the Anvāhāryapacana fire.
For one desiring spiritual luster (brahmavarcasa), there are three [offerings] with the Mahāvyāhṛtis.
ŚŚS 2.10.4: The fourth [portion] is unmodified.
ŚŚS 2.10.5: He divides the water in the *sruva*-ladle into three parts: he places one part in the *agnihotra* pot behind the *gārhapatya* fire, and another in the joined palms of his wife.
ŚŚS 2.10.6: With the words, "I unite thee with offspring and wealth," [he pours it] into her joined palms.
Having heated the *sruva* ladle, he sets it down.

To the south, the ritual procedure for the sacrificer (*yājamāna*) follows. He recites three times the first and the last of the six verses: "Approaching the sacrifice," "This Agni is thousandfold," "Both of you," "This is your womb," "This one here," and "His ancient [path]."

O Agni, you are the giver of life; give me life. O Agni, you are the giver of splendor; give me splendor. O Agni, you are the protector of the body; protect my body. O Agni, whatever is deficient in my body, fill that up for me.
Kindling you, may we enkindle you, the radiant one, for a hundred winters—being full of vigor, may we kindle you, the creator of vigor; being full of power, may we kindle you, the creator of power.
Having murmured, "O Agni, the subduer of rivals, you who are undeceived and invincible," he recites three times, "O thou of wondrous aid, may I reach thy end in safety."

"O Agni, you have come together with the splendor of the sun, together with the praise of the seers, together with the praise of the seers, together with your beloved abode. May I be united with long life, with splendor, with offspring, with my beloved abode, and with the increase of wealth—may I prosper.

Having sat down [with this], he says: "You are water; may I partake of your water. You are greatness; may I partake of your greatness. You are strength; may I partake of your strength. You are the increase of wealth; may I partake of your increase of wealth."

"O Revatī, rejoice in this womb, in this world, in this cow-pen, in this dwelling, in this blessing, in this foundation; remain right here, do not depart from this place"—with these words he approaches the cow. Having touched her forehead with the mantra, "Thou art the collection, O thou of all forms; enter me with vigor and the lordship of cattle," he [approaches] the Gārhapatya fire with the triplet beginning with "Upa tvā agne" and the two-footed verse "Agnē tvaṃ naḥ."

ŚŚS 2.12.3: With the words, "O *iḷā*, come! O *aditi*, come! O *sūnṛtā*, come! he approaches the cow. ŚŚS 2.12.5: With the triplet beginning with "The pressing-stone for Soma," he [addresses] the *anvāhāryapacana* fire from the north.
ŚŚS 2.12.6: Having murmured the *māhitra* formula between the *gārhapatya* and *āhavanīya* fires, he worships the *āhavanīya*.
He recites this verse three times: "That excellent splendor of Savitṛ," "Never art thou ungenerous," and "Thou art difficult to deceive.
While offering oblations with all the *mahāvyāhṛtis*, he places three fuel-sticks each time upon the Āhavanīya fire; indeed, one who performs a single oblation (*ekahāvī*) does so for each.
Having touched the embers to the south of the Āhavanīya fire, he says: "Thou art the divine thread; I grasp thee; may I not be severed from thee."

ŚŚS 2.12.10: "Thou art the thread; do thou extend me with offspring, with cattle, with the increase of wealth, with good progeny, and with heroic vigor. Thou art the human thread; do thou hold fast to me; mayest thou not be cut off from me, O [Name]!"—having thus pronounced the name of his eldest son, or as many sons as he has who have not yet been born. ŚŚS 2.12.11: [This applies] to one who himself has no son yet born. ŚŚS 2.12.12: Having sipped water with the formula, "By truth I descend to the final bath (avabhṛtha); in the waters is my vow," he releases his speech.

ŚŚS 2.13.1: Then, in the morning; ŚŚS 2.13.2: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through my children, rich in nourishment through my possessions, and rich in heroes through my men. Fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us! With my mind I pay homage to you. I go to the world and to heaven"—with these words [he worships] the Āhavanīya fire;
ŚŚS 2.13.3: Standing right there, he worships the other two fires.
"May there be safety for you; may there be safety for us. With my speech I attend upon you; I approach offspring and cattle"—with these words he attends upon the *gārhapatya* fire.
"May there be safety for you; may there be safety for us. With my breath I attend upon you; I approach the out-breath and life"—with these words he attends upon the *anvāhāryapacana* fire.
"May there be safety for you; may there be safety for us. With desire I attend upon you; I approach acquisition and prosperity"—with these words he attends upon all [the fires].
ŚŚS 2.13.7: [The procedure] is the same from the *samidh* onwards until the dismissal of the vow (*vratavisarjana*).
ŚŚS 2.13.8: Or, one may perform it with this very [formula] both in the evening and in the morning.
ŚŚS 2.13.9: Or, there is no formal attendance (*anupasthāna*) in the morning.
ŚŚS 2.14.1: When about to depart on a journey, he looks at the fires, saying: "Fearlessness for you; let there be fearlessness for us. ŚŚS 2.14.2:

[He says] to the Gārhapatya fire: "O manly one, protect my offspring; protect me from human fear. ŚŚS 2.14.3: To the Anvāhāryapacana fire, he says: "O steadfast one, protect my food; protect me from the fear of the ancestors."
Having gone to the north of it, he addresses the Āhavanīya fire with the words: "O Praśaṃsya, protect my cattle; protect me from fear of the gods.
(ŚŚS 2.14.4) Having lifted up three steps with the words "Food! Food!", he restrains his speech from its vicinity.
(ŚŚS 2.14.7) For the reason [for this] has not departed. (ŚŚS 2.14.8)

ŚŚS 2.14.9: At the two junctions [of day and night], having sipped water (ācamya) and restrained his speech, and having sipped water again, he should perform the dismissal (visarga) with the Mahāvyāhṛtis.
ŚŚS 2.14.10: He should restrain his speech within the range of sight of the fires. Upon returning from a journey, ŚŚS 2.15.1: And likewise, he should gaze [at them] in that same manner.
"O Agni, sovereign ruler, we have come to you, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra and the best finder of wealth for us. Bestow upon us splendor and power!

You have protected my cattle, O one worthy of praise; protect them for me! You have protected them even from fear of the gods; protect me from that [fear] as well!"—thus he says regarding the Āhavanīya fire.
ŚŚS 2.15.3: The removal of grass and the placing of fuel-sticks are performed in all [rites].
ŚŚS 2.15.4: "This Agni Purīṣya is possessed of wealth and increases prosperity.
O Agni Purīṣya, bestow upon us splendor and power."

"O Aryaman, you have not spared me from the fear of my father; protect me from that very paternal fear! You have not spared me from that; therefore, protect me!"—thus [he says] regarding the Anvāhāryapacana fire. "This Agni is the lord of the house, the best winner of wealth for offspring from the Gārhapatya.
O Agni, lord of the house, bestow upon us splendor and power!"
"O noble one, you have protected my offspring; protect that for me. Do not protect me from human fear; protect me from that. Thus [he addresses] the Gārhapatya fire.
He departs on a journey having separated from the fires;
and by that very [separation], he is released from them.
ŚŚS 2.16.1: When the first half of the ten-night period has passed during the *dhruva* sacrifice dedicated to Vāstoṣpati;

ŚŚS 2.16.2: Having unyoked the horse standing at the southern fire-altar and spread out a garment, he recites the invitatory verse, "O Vāstoṣpati, acknowledge [us]," and then offers the oblation with the offering verse, "O Vāstoṣpati, for our welfare. ŚŚS 2.16.3: Once the oblation has been offered, he should discard what was not placed [on the fire].
While ascending, having warmed his hands over the *gārhapatya* fire, he touches his vital breaths (*prāṇa*) with the mantra: "Come, ascend to my vital breaths.
He does this once each time with the mantra, twice each time silently.
Then, with the mantra "This is your womb," he warms the *vāraṇī* (the wooden support for the ladle).
ŚŚS 2.17.4: [He takes] once each with the mantra, twice each silently.
ŚŚS 2.17.5: In this same manner, [he takes from] the Āhavanīya fire.
ŚŚS 2.17.6: When [the fire] is not one that is constantly maintained, [he takes] from another [fire].
ŚŚS_2.17.7: And the churning [of the fire] takes place before sunset.
ŚŚS_2.17.8: Descend again, O Jātavedas; knowing our way, carry the oblation to the gods for us.
Bestow upon us long life, progeny, and wealth; shine unharmed within our home.
Thus, having caused the fire to descend from the two kindling woods (*araṇī*) into either a common fire or a non-common fire,
[the churning takes place]. When the Full Moon sacrifice has been completed, there is an offering to Indra Vimṛdh.
ŚŚS 3.1.2: It is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice.
ŚŚS 3.1.3: "The dominion of Indra; like a formidable wild beast... ŚŚS 3.1.4: "Pleasing, the friend of the house; O Agni, be bold"—these are for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
ŚŚS 3.1.5: For Aditi, on the new moon day, when [the sacrifice] has been completed;
3.1.6: It is a modification of the full moon sacrifice; 3.1.7: Those [verses] which belong to the Vaimṛdha [offering] are for the Sviṣṭakṛt [offering].
ŚŚS 3.1.8: And for as long as one lives;
ŚŚS 3.1.9: until the end of the performance.
ŚŚS 3.2.1: When the new moon day has arrived before the [scheduled] festival day, the Abhyuditeṣṭi sacrifice is performed.

ŚŚS 3.2.2: [He offers] to Agni the Giver, to Indra the Bestower, and to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa. ŚŚS 3.2.3: When [the grain] has been poured out, knowing them [to be the portions], he should divide them accordingly.
ŚŚS 3.2.4: [With the verses] "O Agni, giving," and "O Agni, of the great."
ŚŚS 3.2.5: "O thou who art a thousandfold, bring [the wealth] by the hundreds.
ŚŚS 3.2.6: This is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice (Amāvāsyā).
ŚŚS 3.2.7: And a bow is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) for the three [days].
ŚŚS 3.2.8: And the new-moon sacrifice is performed at the proper time. ŚŚS 3.2.9: There is no repetition of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.
ŚŚS 3.3.1: When the new-moon day has passed and the full-moon day has begun, the Abhyudṛṣṭeṣṭi is performed.
To Agni Pathikṛt, to Indra Vṛtrahan, and to Vaiśvānara;
for you, O Ordainer, know the gods,
for the slaying of Vṛtra along with Dānu.
We pray to the one who abides in Truth, Vaiśvānara, the lord of the light of Truth,
the eternal radiance—
the navel of sacrifices.
ŚŚS 3.3.6: It is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice.
ŚŚS 3.3.7: A staff and sandals are the sacrificial fee.
ŚŚS 3.3.8: And when it has been completed, the ritual of the New Moon sacrifice [is performed].

ŚŚS 3.3.9: There is no repetition of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña. ŚŚS 3.4.1: [The offering is made] to Agni Anvāhita, when the fire has been taken out from the fire. ŚŚS 3.4.2: [It is offered] on a path, between the two sacrificial fires, on a wheeled vehicle, on a circular path, and when there is a lapse of the fixed time.
ŚŚS 3.4.3: For the sake of dispersal, [the fire] is used when [the grasses] are mixed together;
ŚŚS 3.4.4: For the sake of separation, with a domestic [fire]; ŚŚS 3.4.5: For the sake of gathering, with a forest fire.
To the Pure One, with the flesh-eating [oblation];
to the One Possessing Waters, with the lightning [oblation];
to Rudra, the one who causes the spreading of disease.
ŚŚS 3.4.9: When about to travel on a journey, [one offers] to Pūṣan, the maker of the path.
ŚŚS 3.4.10: For the fulfillment of all desires, [one offers] to Agni Kāma.
ŚŚS 3.4.11: To Vratapati, after having stayed away from home at the time for breaking a vow, or after having performed an act forbidden by the vow.
ŚŚS 3.4.12: [One should offer] to Vratabhṛt after shedding tears; ŚŚS 3.4.13: to Kṣāmavat in the event of a house fire;
ŚŚS 3.4.14: to the Maruts when twins are born.
ŚŚS 3.5.1: Agni, Agni is kindled by oblations; through Agni, Agni is kindled. ŚŚS 3.5.2: O Agni, come hither for the feast, you who [serve] Agni for the divine feast. ŚŚS 3.5.3:
With what [splendor], O Agni, do you shine upon us? O Agni, the human [prayers] [approach] you.
ŚŚS_3.5.4: Will you not indeed be with us? Do not abandon us in this great contest for wealth.
ŚŚS_3.5.5: O Agni, you are the great one within the vast waters.
ŚŚS_3.5.6: What may we offer to Rudra so that he may be gracious to us?
ŚŚS 3.5.7: O Lord of the path, we [choose] you from among all paths. ŚŚS 3.5.8: Agni, in the highest abodes, is the desire for what has been and what is to be;
as the sole sovereign, he shines forth. May we attain him.

O Agni, you are the bearer of vows, the pure one; O Agni, bring the gods here to our sacrifice and to our oblation. Upholding the sacred laws, O guardian of vows, inviolable, become for us an envoy, ageless and a source of noble heroes.
The very gracious Agni has held fast the treasures; O Jātavedas, protect us that we may live.
Black dust clings to your feet, O many-faced Hotṛ, in whom all riches abide.
O Maruts, you who are like blazing flames, come hither like twins.

"White, with golden girths, the Maruts, whose brilliance is like the wind, for the sake of glory," or so it is said. ŚŚS 3.6.1: Kinsmen who are not in agreement should perform an offering to many deities.
May Agni, the first, protect us along with the Vasus; may Soma guard us by his own self with the Rudras.
May Indra, together with the Maruts, act according to the seasons, and may Varuṇa, with the Ādityas, grant us protection.
May Agni protect us fully with the Vasus, and may Soma [protect us] with the bodies of the Rudras.

"May Indra, to whom oblations are offered, be united with the Maruts; may Varuṇa, the knower of all, be united with the Ādityas. And they should mutter the *Saṃjñāna* hymn, as prescribed for the *Mitravindā* sacrifice.
ŚŚS 3.7.2: There are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses. ŚŚS 3.7.3: "With Agni [we gain] wealth, O increaser of the household" (*agninā rayim gayasphāna*)—these are the two *ājyabhāga* offerings.
ŚŚS 3.7.4: Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ—who is the possessor of a thousand.
May Pūṣan with his aids and Sarasvatī with her cattle, and Tvaṣṭṛ, adorn us with forms through sacrifices.
May Tvaṣṭṛ bestowing forms, Sarasvatī, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Savitṛ grant me [fortune].
May Bṛhaspati grant it, and Indra strength to me; may Mitra, Varuṇa, Soma, and Agni grant me sovereign power (*kṣatra*).
ŚŚS 3.7.5: "Now grant us [wealth] thousandfold; and do thou, O Brahman, protect us"—this is for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 3.7.6: The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) consists of a thousand.
ŚŚS 3.7.7: In the ritual recitations (*nigama*), the deities follow the same sequence as in the *puronuvākyā* verses.
ŚŚS 3.7.8: [The procedure is] like that of the *yājyā* when there is an instruction (*ādeśa*). ŚŚS 3.7.9: Or [it is] according to the specific direction (*sampreṣita*).
ŚŚS 3.8.1: On the full moon day of Phālguna, in the performance of those who do not undergo initiation for the *ayana* sacrifices.
ŚŚS 3.8.2: [The interval for] the Vasiṣṭha-sacrifice and the Sākamprasthāyya is on the new moon day.
ŚŚS 3.8.3: Fifteen years is the interval for the Dākṣāyaṇa-sacrifice. ŚŚS 3.8.4: Or, for all [these sacrifices], it is one year each.
For one who does not perform [the Dākṣāyaṇayajña], the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices (darśapūrṇamāsa) continue to be obligatory.
Regarding the Dākṣāyaṇayajña:
the rites belonging to the full-moon sacrifice are performed on the day before [the full moon].
ŚŚS 3.8.8: Or [the victim] belongs to Agni and Soma.

ŚŚS 3.8.9: On the full moon day, there is an offering to Agni and the *sāṃnāyya* (milk-offering) for Indra. ŚŚS 3.8.10: During the dark fortnight, one who is under the vow of initiation gives [food] to guests.
ŚŚS 3.8.11: Or he is one whose vow is truth.
ŚŚS 3.8.12: He does not wear garments washed with the fat of sheep.
ŚŚS 3.8.13: He eats only the remnants of the sacrificial oblation.
ŚŚS 3.8.14: He should not eat to satiety. ŚŚS 3.8.15: Meditating in his mind with the thought, "I consume King Soma, the Moon," he eats.
ŚŚS 3.8.16: [This applies] to the rites of the new moon on the preceding day.
ŚŚS 3.8.17: Or [the offering] belongs to Indra and Agni. ŚŚS 3.8.18:
On the new moon day, there is a curd-offering (payasyā) dedicated to Agni and one to Mitra and Varuṇa. ŚŚS 3.8.19:
"By Truth, that which is yours among the people... (Ṛgveda 2.41.6).
ŚŚS 3.8.20: He sacrifices to the Vājins either before the utterance of the *śamyu* formula or after it, without having invoked them [previously].
ŚŚS 3.8.21: They are included in the final *prayāja* offering and, as appropriate, in the *sūktavāka*.
ŚŚS 3.8.22: "The divine Vājins will enjoy the oblation; they will cause it to increase; they will make it greater and more glorious."
ŚŚS 3.8.23: With the formula, "May the prize-winners be auspicious to us in every contest," he offers the sacrifice while standing with knees raised and without pausing.
ŚŚS 3.8.24: "O Agni, partake of the prize-winner"—this is the *anuvashaṭkāra*.
ŚŚS 3.8.25: Having invited one another, the sacrificer, the Brahman, the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, and the Āgnīdhra consume [the remains].
ŚŚS 3.8.26: The first and the last [verses] belong to the sacrificer.
ŚŚS 3.8.27: "That seed of mine which flows away, or which, once poured, is lost—I maintain that through King Soma within us."
"Thou art vigor; thou art vigorous; bestow vigor upon me"—this is the mantra for the consumption [of the oblation].

However, the [offerings] of the new moon are performed first;

ŚŚS 3.12.7: "This [is] for you two," and "Of this [sacrifice], the pure one now... ŚŚS 3.12.8: "Come hither, those who are well-performing their rites, the bright-shining ones..."

With the *sainānīka* [verse];

ŚŚS 3.16.9: [This applies] when there is no continuity and the *praṇava* is distinct.
ŚŚS 3.16.10: "Those who have thirsted," and "O Agni, being invoked," [are for] Agni Kavyavāhana.

He sacrifices to these deities;

with the exception of the verse addressed to the ancestors (*pitṛmat*).

With the three-verse hymn beginning "We call the mind hither" (mano nv ā huvāmahe), [they worship] the Dakṣiṇāgni fire. They should recite "May the mind come back to us again" (ā ma etu manaḥ punar).
With the three-verse hymn beginning "I honor that Agni" (agnim tam manye) and the two-footed verse "O Agni, you for us" (agne tvam naḥ), [they worship] the Gārhapatya fire.

ŚŚS 3.19.15: If a firebrand is not available, one should touch the two kindling woods with ashes and perform an *iṣṭi* sacrifice to Agni Tapasvat, Janadvat, and Pāvakavat. ŚŚS 3.19.16: "Come with heat among the people, O Agni, as the purifier with your flame;
come to this my well-spoken hymn."
"Come to us with heat among the people, O Agni, the purifier, shining brightly;
place our offerings among the gods.

(ŚŚS 3.20.11) If the oblation has not been offered to the deity or is spoiled, there is no repetition of the *hautra* (the Hotṛ’s duties); having prepared another oblation, he should offer it to the deity.
(ŚŚS 3.20.12) If the defect occurs after the offering has been made, there is no repetition; the *sviṣṭakṛt*, the *iḍā*, and the portions for consumption are omitted. (ŚŚS 3.20.13)
ŚŚS 3.20.14: [The offering] with clarified butter is supreme.
ŚŚS 3.20.15: When other deities have been worshipped, or when there is a defect, the offering is repeated while the ritual procedure (*tantra*) still has a remainder.
ŚŚS 3.20.16: The entire sacrifice is performed when nothing remains.

ŚŚS 3.20.17: There is no repetition of what has already been performed when a secondary element (*guṇa*) is omitted, because the primary factor (*pradhāna*) is the immediate conjunction (*samnipāta*).
ŚŚS 3.20.18: One should not repeat the mantra after [the teacher].
ŚŚS 3.20.19: Jātūkarṇya says that one should indeed repeat it.

ŚŚS 3.20.20: If [the oblation] has been taken from other [vessels], or if it has been offered into other [fires], one should give it to those [fires] that have been commanded; having invoked [the deity] with clarified butter (ājya), one should sacrifice. ŚŚS 3.21.1: In the case of the *iṣṭi* sacrifices, the animal sacrifices (*paśubandha*), and the Soma sacrifice, the Brahman priest performs the expiation (*prāyaścitta*). ŚŚS 3.21.2: If there should be a fault in the Ṛgveda, he offers into the Gārhapatya fire with the formula: "bhūḥ svāhā."
If [the offering] is from the Yajurveda, one says "bhuvaḥ svāhā" over the Anvāhāryapacana fire;
if it is in the Soma sacrifice, however, [one says it] over the Āgnīdhrīya fire; if it is from the Sāmaveda, one says "svaḥ svāhā" over the Āhavanīya fire.
ŚŚS 3.21.6: If there is no instruction [to depart], one should offer with "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā.

ŚŚS 3.21.8: If one has already performed the attendance and there is no sudden departure, it is as if one had gone abroad.
ŚŚS 3.21.9: Having placed [the fires] together, one should perform the churning during a period free from calamity.
ŚŚS 3.21.10: There is no formal worship (upasthāna) of the two fire-sticks (araṇi). ŚŚS 3.21.11: One should not abandon the sacred fires without an oblation or without a sacrifice.
ŚŚS 3.21.12: Having performed the penance, however, one should substitute for the past rites; one should substitute. ŚŚS 4.1.1: The wife and the sacrificer [observe] the vow-food.
ŚŚS 4.1.2: They should eat before the driving away of the calf.
ŚŚS 4.1.3: Whatever else [is required], except for meat, salt, the pair [of sesame and rice], and beans, as well as whatever substance one intends to sacrifice with;

ŚŚS 4.2.4: with the middle [verse], in the dakṣiṇa fire;

ŚŚS 4.2.12: The Paiṅgya [is recited] with the Mahāvyāhṛtis.

ŚŚS 4.3.2: Having placed the winnowing basket, the cooking pot, the wooden sword (sphya), the vessel, and the mortar and pestle to the east of the southern fire;
ŚŚS 4.3.3: Having placed the wooden sword upon the kuśa grass to the south of the Gārhapatya fire;
ŚŚS 4.3.4: [He places] the rice grains above in the vessel.
ŚŚS 4.3.5: [He places] the pot in front on the winnowing basket.
ŚŚS 4.3.6: Bending his left knee and with a low fist, he takes up the rice grains while meditating upon the ancestors.

ŚŚS 4.3.8: Just as he would be [seated] facing downward toward a hole, having cooked on the *dakṣiṇa-agni* the grains once-threshed by his wife, having sprinkled them with clarified butter, having removed them from the fire toward the west, having swept around the area below, having strewn grass, and having sprinkled water, he bends his right knee, wears the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder (*yajñopavītī*), sits facing east, and offers the oblation with a stirring-spoon (*mekṣaṇa*).
ŚŚS 4.4.1: "To Agni Kavyavāhana, svāhā! To Soma Pitṛmat, svāhā! To Yama Aṅgirasvat Pitṛmat, svāhā! Thus he says.

Having thrown the stirring-stick (mekṣaṇa) into the fire, he should wipe the southern corner of the southern fire-altar with the wooden sword (sphyá), saying: "The Asuras and Rakṣas who sit upon the altar have been struck down," and then sprinkle it with water.
[He recites: "Those Asuras who, assuming various forms, move about with their own power (svadhā);
those who carry away the *parāpur* and *nipur*—may Agni drive them away from this world."

ŚŚS 4.4.2b: Having thus wiped the firebrand and placed it in the southern half [of the site], and having placed once-cut kuśa grass at the base upon that which was wiped, he pours water on the kuśa grass with his hand turned downwards, pronouncing the name of the father, saying: "O [Name], pour water for yourself and for those who follow you here. ŚŚS 4.4.3: In the same manner, [he performs this] for the grandfather to the south. ŚŚS 4.4.4: And likewise for the great-grandfather.
ŚŚS 4.4.5: Having placed the rice-balls (piṇḍas) according to the order in which they were moistened, [reciting] "O N.N., this is for you, and for those who follow you here.
ŚŚS 4.4.6: Both [offerings] are made at a single spot when there is a division among the ancestors.
ŚŚS 4.4.7: There is no [offering] for one whose father is living.
ŚŚS 4.4.8: Not [to one] separated by a living being.
ŚŚS 4.4.9: Or rather, [the rule applies] from father to those [sons], or from sons to those [fathers].
ŚŚS 4.4.10: Or until the end of the *homa* offering.
ŚŚS 4.4.11: "O Fathers, rejoice here; O Fathers, come hither according to your respective portions.
ŚŚS 4.4.12: Having turned toward the north.

ŚŚS 4.4.14: Having turned back, [he recites] "The fathers have rejoiced; they have refreshed themselves according to their portion. ŚŚS 4.4.15:
In the same manner, having performed the *avanejana* (sprinkling) rite, [he recites] ŚŚS 4.5.1a:
"Homage to you, O fathers, for life; homage to you, O fathers, for growth."
Homage to you, O Fathers, for your terrible power; homage to you, O Fathers, for your essence.
Homage to you, O Fathers, for your strength; homage to you, O Fathers, for your death.
Homage to you, O Fathers, for your wrath; homage to you, O Fathers, for your *svadhā*.
Homage to you, O fathers; O fathers, homage to you!
O fathers who are here, may you be the most excellent among them. O fathers who are here as humans, may we be the most excellent among them.
"O Pitṛs who are here, let that which is yours be *svadhā*; O Pitṛs who are there, let that which is ours prosper.
O Pitṛs, grant us houses."

ŚŚS 4.5.2: Having laid down three threads with the formula, "O Pitṛs, this is your garment; put it on, O Pitṛs. ŚŚS 4.5.3: Having poured out the remainder of the water with the formula, "Carrying strength, carrying nectar, ghee, milk, kīlāla, and parisrut—you are the svadhā; satisfy our Pitṛs."
Having smelled the rice-balls (piṇḍas),
he should either place them down and eat them,
or give them to a Brāhmaṇa.

"O Fathers, bestow upon us a child, a boy adorned with a lotus garland."
"Just as a man here might be non-existent.
Having placed a firebrand into the fire,
he throws it in after having cut off a single portion.

ŚŚS 4.5.11: The Agnihotra is performed with barley gruel alone, both in the evening and in the morning. ŚŚS 4.5.12: And the oblation is offered by oneself on the festival days (parvan). And there is witness-bearing for all ritual acts.
In those rites accompanied by mantras, there is restraint of speech.
In all courses of action, they proceed as they go, and otherwise they return from that.

ŚŚS 4.6.13: When the fire is being led forward, he follows after it. ŚŚS 4.6.14: He sits down together with the fuel-sticks. ŚŚS 4.6.15: At the establishment of the sacred fires, a horse belongs to the Brahman priest.
ŚŚS 4.6.16: Or [the permission] may be given for all [the priests].
ŚŚS 4.6.17: For the commencement of the ritual action, having been addressed, he says "Oṃ" and then gives the impulse (prasauti) according to the specific rite.
ŚŚS 4.7.1: At the time of the *praṇītā* water, there is the restraint of speech (*vāgyamana*).
ŚŚS 4.7.2: The dismissal by the *haviṣkṛt* formula. ŚŚS 4.7.3: And after the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering has been performed, there is the dismissal by the impulse for the *anuyāja*s.
ŚŚS 4.7.4: Having looked at the *prāśitra* portion with the words, "I gaze upon thee with the eye of Mitra."

Having accepted it with the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I accept thee," he places it on the sacrificial mound with its handle pointing eastward, saying, "I set thee on the navel of the earth, in the lap of Aditi. Then, taking a portion for the *prāśitra* with the ring finger and the thumb...
Having eaten [the food] with the formula, "I eat thee with the mouth of Agni," he should not chew it;
having sipped water with the formula, "Thou art peace," he touches his vital breaths.
"Thou art the protector of the breath; protect my breath," [he says] over the two nostrils and the mouth.
"Thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye," [he says] over the two eyes. "Thou art the protector of the ear; protect my ear," [he says] over the two ears.
With the mantra, "I seat you in the belly of Indra," [he places it] on the navel.
With the mantra, "You are the protector of hearing; protect my hearing," [he places it] on the two ears. With the mantra, "I seat you in the belly of Indra," [he places it] on the navel.
"Who gave? To whom did he give? Desire gave; to desire did he give.

Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver; O Desire, this is for you"—having thus accepted the *anvāhārya* rice, [the Adhvaryu], being addressed with the words, "O Brahman, I shall set forth," [proceeds].

ŚŚS 4.7.17: Having murmured, “O divine Savitṛ, they have proclaimed this sacrifice of yours to Bṛhaspati the Brahman; protect the sacrifice with that, protect the lord of the sacrifice with that, and protect me with that, impelled by the divine Savitṛ,” he gives the impulse with, “Om, be established!
ŚŚS 4.7.18: When the *praṇītā* waters have been released, there is the dismissal of the Brahman.
ŚŚS 4.7.19: There is the consumption of the Brahman’s portion.

ŚŚS 4.8.1: "With unerring vision I gaze upon you for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for heroic vigor; you are the tongue of Agni, a good invoker for the gods; for every station, be mine for the sake of the *yajus*, for every *yajus*.
