With these words, the wife gazes at the clarified butter (*ājya*). ŚŚS 4.8.2: "You are splendor; you are brilliance; you are immortality; you belong to all the gods. With these words, the sacrificer gazes at the oblations placed on the *vedī*. ŚŚS 4.8.3a: "The firm ones have settled in the womb of Truth, in the world of well-done deeds; protect them, O Viṣṇu! Protect the sacrifice! Protect the lord of the sacrifice! Having touched the oblations thus placed, [he recites this].

"Protect me, who am engaged in sacrifice," [he says] regarding himself. Having sipped water [with the words], "Thou art rain; cut away my evil! Thou art knowledge; know my evil away!", [he says], "O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow; may I be able to do it; may it be successful for me."
Having placed a fuel-stick on the Āhavanīya fire while saying, "Here I come from untruth to truth," he restrains his speech;
or he may do so with whatever desire he might have. [If the desire is: "May I obtain imperishable food," [he should restrain his speech] toward the sky or the ocean.
"May this great power of Indra bestow [strength] upon us; may the liberal lords attend to our wealth. May our blessings be realized; may our blessings be fulfilled.
Thus [he recites] while the *iḷā* is being invoked.

"O Bradhna, overflow! Protect my breath; protect my progeny; protect my cattle; milk for me the *brahman*; milk for me the *kṣatra*; milk for me the subjects. You are the ordainer of the quarters; may the quarters be favorable to me; may the quarters be favorable to me. When they have been ordained, may I prosper therein. O fathers, rejoice here! O fathers, satisfy yourselves according to your respective portions. Having touched the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) placed upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he says:
"The fathers have rejoiced; they have satisfied themselves according to their respective portions," and having set it down again.

"Thou art the portion of Prajāpati; full of vigor, full of milk; thou art imperishable; mayest thou not perish for me there, in yonder world, and here. Having thus touched the *anvāhārya* rice, [he proceeds].

When the *anuyāja* offerings have been performed, having moved the two offering-ladles (*sruk*) apart, he [the Adhvaryu] moves the *juhū* eastward with his right hand held upward, saying: "May I win after Agni's and Agni-Soma's winning; by the impulse of strength (*vāja*), I push it forward. Then, with his left hand held downward, he moves the *upabhṛt* westward, saying: "May Agni, Agni-Soma, and [the other deities] drive away him who hates us and whom we hate; by the impulse of strength, I push him away. (ŚŚS 4.9.6) In other cases, [he proceeds] according to the respective deity. (ŚŚS 4.9.7) If the master of the house has not yet offered, he offers into the *gārhapatya* fire using the *sruva* ladle.
O you two of a hundred powers, that portion of strength which the gods ordained for you both—that I satisfy you with this; may you be satiated by it. *Ahāhā*, *Ahuḥū*, *svāhā*!
To the Gandharvas Nariṣṭā, *Ahāhā*, and *Ahuḥū*, *svāhā*!

"O Agni, lord of the earth; O Vāyu, lord of the intermediate space; O Savitṛ, lord of instigations; O Sūrya, lord of the constellations; O Soma, lord of the plants; O Tvaṣṭṛ, lord of the forms of fuel-sticks; O Mitra, lord of the truthful; O Varuṇa, lord of the laws; O Indra, lord of the preeminent; O Prajāpati, lord of creatures—O gods, exert your prowess among the gods!
Exert your prowess, the first ones, among the second ones!"—in this manner, one by one, up to eleven.

ŚŚS 4.10.3: "O Viśvedevas, thirty-three in number, thrice eleven, you whose paths are ever higher, whose beings are ever higher, you who belong to all men, you who belong to Vaiśvānara, you who possess universal greatness—protect me here! In this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this dominion (*kṣatra*), in this rite (*karman*), in this blessing (*āśis*), in this foundation (*pratiṣṭhā*), in this invocation of the gods (*devahūti*)! May this desire of mine be fulfilled, svāhā!"—thus [he says] according to whatever desire he may have.
ŚŚS 4.10.4: "O Prajāpati," is the fourth [offering]. ŚŚS 4.11.1: "May the *dhruvā* ladle swell with the oblation of ghee, for every sacrifice, toward those who are devoted to the gods."
"O Sūryā, from the udder of Aditi, from the lap of the Earth, flow wide-streaming at this sacrifice.
With these words, he causes the *dhruvā* ladle to swell;
he then touches the *sam-iṣṭayajus* oblation as it is being offered.

"May you be present in my assembly; you are everything, may you be everything for me; you are full, may you be full for me; you are imperishable, may you not perish for me, both there in yonder world and here. Having touched the full vessel with these words, he sprinkles water toward the quarters:
"May the gods and the officiating priests purify themselves along with the eastern quarter.
May the months and the ancestors purify themselves along with the southern quarter."
"May the houses together with the eastern direction purify themselves;
may the sacrifice, the year, and the lord of the sacrifice together with the upward direction purify themselves"—
with this mantra he does so once each time, and twice each time silently.
Having touched [the water] with the three verses beginning with *āpo hi ṣṭha*, he pours it out toward the east or the north with the verse *acchāyam vo yayor ojasā*.
[He says: "I send you forth to the ocean; go to your own source."
"May our heroes be unharmed; let not our wealth flow away.
Having consecrated [the water] with this, he should touch his chest with the four verses beginning with *śaṃ no devīr*.

O Indra, unite us with vital breath, with luster, with milk, and with our bodies; may we be united with a gracious mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us; may he restore whatever in our bodies is impaired.
Having thus wiped his mouth,
he strides the Viṣṇu-steps from the southern buttock of the altar toward the Āhavanīya fire.
"Viṣṇu strode out in the sky with the Jāgata metre; I have strode out after him. Excluded from that is he who hates us and whom we hate. Having lifted his right foot, [he places] the left one lower.
(ŚŚS 4.12.2) "Viṣṇu strode out in the intermediate space with the Triṣṭubh metre"—thus a second time.
(ŚŚS 4.12.3) "Viṣṇu strode out on the earth with the Gāyatrī metre"—thus a third time. (ŚŚS 4.12.4)
"Viṣṇu strode through the quarters with the Anuṣṭubh metre," [saying this] he strides transversely. The conclusion is the same.
"We have gone to heaven," [saying this] he looks toward the east.
"May we be united with light," [he says] regarding the Āhavanīya fire.

"May I be united with offspring, may offspring be united with me; may I be united with the increase of wealth, may the increase of wealth be united with me; the sacrifice is a Vasu; may I become more prosperous. Thus he breathes out.

"Thou art self-existent, the best ray; thou art the giver of life, give me life. Thou art the giver of splendor, give me splendor. Thou art the protector of the body, protect my body. From these quarters, from this heaven, from this atmosphere, from this food-eating world, from this foundation, I banish my hateful rival. The hateful rival is banished. Having thus worshipped the sun, he turns his right arm following the turn of Indra and the turn of the sun, saying: "I turn following the turn of Indra; I turn following the turn of the sun."
Having returned to the Gārhapatya fire by way of the left, [he says]:
"O Agni, lord of the house, may I be a master of the house together with you, O Agni, lord of the house; may you be a good master of the house together with me, O Agni, lord of the house.
May our household duties not be performed with a single cow."
"May a hundred winters be mine from such-and-such [a person]," having thus uttered the names of his sons;
then, touching a coal with the words, "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, unite me with desire," he recites:
"The sacrifice has come into being; it has come into existence; it was born; and it has grown again."
"May he become the lord of the gods; may he make us lords.
Having muttered this, he sips water in the same manner as before.

"O Agni, Lord of Vows, I have performed the vow; I was able to do it; through it I have succeeded. Whatever I am, that indeed I am. Having thus spoken, he places a fuel-stick on the Āhavanīya fire and releases his speech:
"O Agni, whoever hates us from afar, whoever hates us from near, the kinsman or even the stranger... (ŚŚS 4.13.1a).
"May not even a trace of it remain, as if of a faggot being consumed.
Having thus thrown the embers of the Āhavanīya fire together, he mutters the three-verse hymn beginning with "O Agni, rich in cattle. (ŚŚS 4.13.1b)

"May we rise up; may that eye of thine, which is thy manifestation, not cut me off; may I not be deprived of that fervor of thine"—having thus worshipped the sun, and having turned back in the same manner, he sits down, turning to the left.
May this oblation be for me a source of progeny, possessing ten heroes and a full assembly of kinsmen, for my well-being. May it grant me self, offspring, fearlessness, cattle, and the world.
May Agni make my progeny abundant; bestow upon us food, milk, and seed.
Thus, one desiring offspring consumes milk. Or, one wishing to become powerful consumes curd with the mantra, "I have performed [the praise] of Dadhikrāvan.
With the mantra, "May the lord of the sacrifice [be united] with his blessing," he consumes the sacrificer's portion.

ŚŚS 4.13.4: He performs the *samiṣṭayajus* offering together with [the sacrificer] when departing on a journey. ŚŚS 4.14.1: The rites are for one who is living. ŚŚS 4.14.2: If he should die before the rite is completed, there is no completion of it in the case of *ekāha* sacrifices; [the rite ends] with death.
ŚŚS 4.14.3: Having cast all the oblations into the Āhavanīya fire;
ŚŚS 4.14.4: having removed the hair and nails of the deceased;
ŚŚS 4.14.5: having bathed and adorned [the body].
ŚŚS 4.14.6: In the southern direction, on ground sloping toward the south, or sloping toward the southeast (or east).
ŚŚS 4.14.7: Having swept [the site] with a branch of the *palāśa* tree while reciting "Go away, depart!
ŚŚS 4.14.8: Having scraped it with the wooden sword (*sphya*) and sprinkled water over it.
Having constructed the altar-hearth (citī) facing the east-southeast;
having placed the Āhavanīya fire in front and the Gārhapatya fire behind it, and the Dakṣiṇa fire to the south;
and having carried [the materials] between the Gārhapatya and the Dakṣiṇa fires.
Having laid her supine upon the funeral pyre,
he should push toward the south a cow intended for the funeral rite, or a red goat, facing southward; then,
having extracted the two kidneys from the living animal or from one that has been slaughtered, [he should place them] behind her.

Having made the two [pieces of meat] warm over the *anvāhāryapacana* fire and having placed them in his hands with the two verses beginning "ati drava," and having placed pieces of gold on the seats of the vital breaths (*prāṇa-āyatana*),
he covers the face with the omentum while reciting "agner varma."
ŚŚS 4.14.18: [He places] the *juhū* in his right hand;
ŚŚS 4.14.19: the *upabhṛt* in his left;
ŚŚS 4.14.20: the *dhruvā* on his chest.
ŚŚS 4.14.21: [He places] the *agnihotra-havaṇī* ladle on the neck; ŚŚS 4.14.22: the two *sruva* ladles on the nostrils; ŚŚS 4.14.23:
the *prāśitra-haraṇa* vessel on the right ear.
ŚŚS 4.14.24: The carrying forward of the *praṇītā* waters is on the left side.
ŚŚS 4.14.25: The skull-bones are on the head. ŚŚS 4.14.26: The pressing-stones are in the waters.
ŚŚS 4.14.27: [He places] the vessel for the cuttings on the belly; ŚŚS 4.14.28: two bowls on the two sides;
ŚŚS 4.14.29: the wooden sword (sphya) on the right side.
ŚŚS 4.14.30: A black antelope skin on the left [thigh]. ŚŚS 4.14.31: The two fire-sticks (araṇī) in the lap.
ŚŚS 4.14.32: The mortar and pestle upon the thighs and the knees.
At the two feet: a winnowing basket and a cart.
At the two ankles: the Agnihotra vessels.
Having filled those with clarified butter and speckled ghee.
"Truly, this one is from you; you are from this one. This is your source; you are his source.
O Jātavedas, carry him to that world where the doers of good deeds dwell.
Truly, this one begot you; may he be born again from you, [O Agni], svāhā!"—with these words they place [the fire] together with the fires.
ŚŚS 4.15.1: Having recited "Mā enam agne" ten times while the fire is blazing, they proceed toward the northeast, turning to the left and not looking back.
ŚŚS 4.15.2: He consecrates [the water] with the two verses beginning with "mṛtyoḥ padam.
ŚŚS 4.15.3: With the two hymns "āpo hi ṣṭhā" and "sanā ca soma," they touch the water, neither bending down nor immersing themselves, and without running.
Having offered one handful of water with the formula,
"This is for you," having stepped out with the formula, "O Waters,
[protect] us," and having put on an unwashed garment.
Having performed the worship of the sun with the mantra beginning "That eye," they return led by the youngest.

Having placed dūrvā grass, barley, and mustard seeds into a water-vessel and set it upon fresh cow-dung, they touch the anointed stone, the fire, and the water-vessel while reciting the verse "aśmanvatī."

ŚŚS 4.15.6: Sleeping on the ground, eating sacrificial food (haviṣya), and the suspension of ritual activities—with the exception of those pertaining to the sacred fires—these observances are to be maintained for one night, three nights, or nine nights until the collection of the bones (saṃcayana). ŚŚS 4.15.7: "They should not prolong the days of impurity," so said Kauṣītaki.
ŚŚS 4.15.8a: Having performed the collection of the bones during the dark fortnight, [the rites are performed] on the odd-numbered nights.

Having extinguished the bones with water mixed with milk while reciting the two verses beginning with "O Agni, that which you... (yam tvam agne), and having placed the remains in an old jar, he covers it with a clod of earth while reciting "I prop up your [stake]... (ut te stabhnāmi).
Having dug a hole, he says, "Rise up, O swelling one!
Having placed [the object] in a measured space, he says, "Swelling forth!
They bury it in the forest.
ŚŚS 4.15.9: When the bodies are no longer visible, there are three hundred and sixty palāśa stalks. ŚŚS 4.15.10: This is the place for their insertion. ŚŚS 4.15.11: Forty are placed on the head.
ŚŚS 4.15.12: Ten [strokes] on the neck. ŚŚS 4.15.13: One hundred on the shoulders, the spine, and the two arms. ŚŚS 4.15.14: Thirty on the chest.
There are twenty in the belly;
six in the two testicles;
four in the penis.
One hundred [strokes] on the thighs;
thirty on the knees, the shanks, and the kneecaps;
twenty on the toes of the feet.
Thus, there are three hundred and sixty [stanzas].
Having fashioned a human form, having wrapped it with woolen threads, having smeared it with barley flour, and having anointed it with clarified butter, they cremate it with fires.
If one desires to take another wife after his previous wife has died, he should cremate her with the sacred fires, or else perform the *sāṃtapana* rite, and then establish the fires again.
ŚŚS 4.16.1: The ritual for the enclosing sticks at the conclusion of the vow.

ŚŚS 4.16.2: Having spread out to the west of the fire a fresh red bull's hide with its neck pointing north or east and the hair side up, or else *kuśa* grass with the tips pointing in that same direction, they sit down upon it.
ŚŚS 4.16.3: Having placed an anointed stone between the fire and these [sitters].
Having made the *śamyā* sticks the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*),
he offers with fuel of *śamī* wood or *palāśa* wood,
using either a ladle (*sruva*) made of *vāraṇa* wood or one of bell-metal (*kāṃsya*).
ŚŚS 4.16.4: [The verse] "upasthākṛtaḥ" is recited while they have taken hold of one another.
ŚŚS 4.16.5: "imam jīvebhyaḥ.
May death pass away; may immortality come to me. May Vaivasvata grant us fearlessness.
"May wealth fall upon us like a leaf from a tree; may the Lord of Power attend us—
those ten [fingers] which are placed along the ruddy [horse]," so it is said.
Having offered twelve oblations,
he looks at the right shoulder with the two verses beginning "yathā ahāni," and having mixed the ointment with clarified butter.
He anoints the eyes of the women with *kuśa* grass, reciting the mantra "Come hither, O women... once for each eye, and twice silently.
With the two verses beginning "Arise, O Brahmanaspati," he consecrates the sacrificer as he stands up, while the sacrificer touches his right arm.
ŚŚS 4.16.8: Or [the gift] is the tail of an ox.
ŚŚS 4.16.9: An ox, a new garment, and a bronze vessel are the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 4.16.10: With the hymn beginning "Turn back the wealth from the right," the Pratyenās circumambulates [the fire] three times from left to right.
ŚŚS 4.16.11: The ritual concerning the enclosing-sticks for the Pratyenasī.
ŚŚS 4.17.1: One sacrifices with a cow to Rudra for the sake of well-being.
ŚŚS 4.17.2: They call it the "spit-ox" sacrifice.
Having fasted during the bright fortnight under the Puṣya asterism, in the north-easterly direction, he should churn the fire,
carry it forward facing east,
and plant a Palāśa branch with its leaves in front of it.
Having stationed the animal to the north of it:
"I dedicate you, acceptable to Rudra. "I sprinkle you, acceptable to Rudra."
"O Rudra, I bind you, who are dear to him," [he says].
They lead the animal, around which fire has been carried, toward the north.
They cause it to be quieted with its head to the east and feet to the north, or with its head to the west and feet to the north, while it remains silent.
"Whatever cry the animal has uttered, or [the sound] it makes when struck by feet or chest— may Agni Jātavedas release me from that sin,
svāhā! Thus he offers while [the animal] is crying out.

Having extracted the omentum, washed it, cooked it over the eastern fire, sprinkled clarified butter over it, and removed it from the heat, he sprinkles water around the fire three times, saying "May it be auspicious, may it be auspicious," and offers oblations of clarified butter.
"Her who does not fall sideways, but goes straight, saying 'I am the supporter'—her I yoke with a stream of ghee; may I prosper her. Svāhā! (ŚŚS 4.18.1)
"We invoke him to whom all this belongs;
may he, the Lord of Desires, grant my desires. Svāhā!"—this is the second [offering].
"O Agni, lord of the earth," with these words he offers the third oblation;
"O Prajāpati," with these words the fourth.
Having joined together three middle palāśa leaves and having spread them out as an underlayer...
Having placed the omentum and having sprinkled it with clarified butter:
"As many as I am lord over, as many as my attendants are—to them I honor you, O God; O God, be gracious to them for us."
"I know your father, I know your mother; heaven is your father, earth is your mother.
To that god Bhava, to Śarva, to Paśupati, to Ugra, to the great god, to Rudra, to Īśāna, to Aśani—svāhā! Having thus offered the omentum, he throws the *palāśa* leaves after it.
And [he places] the two omentum-cooking spits.
Having offered the northern oblation of clarified butter with the formula, "To the looker-on for thee, to the counter-looker-on, svāhā!", he sprinkles water around the fire in the same manner.
In the western fire, he cooks the pot-offering.
ŚŚS 4.18.9: To the north, the portions for cutting off (avadāna).

ŚŚS 4.18.10: Having poured together the cooked rice from the pot, the broth, the meat, and the clarified butter, and having sprinkled water around [the fire] three times with the formula "For each *śamī* branch," he offers the oblation.
ŚŚS 4.19.1: "To Bhava, svāhā! To Śarva, svāhā! To Rudra, svāhā! To Īśāna, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā! Thus [he says].
ŚŚS 4.19.2: Having sprinkled water around in the same manner;
ŚŚS 4.19.3: having gathered those very [embers] together;
ŚŚS 4.19.4: [placing them] in the western fire.
"Oṃ bhavānyai svāhā, oṃ śarvāṇyai svāhā, oṃ rudrāṇyai svāhā, oṃ īśānānyai svāhā, oṃ agnāyyai svāhā. Thus [he offers].
The sprinkling around [the fire] is the same.
Having placed six palāśa leaves from the cutting edge toward the northeast, [he proceeds].
Having placed the omentum mixed with blood among them, he assigns it to the armies of Rudra:
"The sounding ones, the echoing ones, the clamorous ones, the searching ones, the snorting ones, the flesh-eaters—this is your portion; enjoy it, svāhā! (ŚŚS 4.19.8).
And the sacrificer worships:

"O Lord of the earth, Lord of the atmosphere, Lord of the world, Lord of beings, Lord of creatures, Lord of the great being—be gracious to us, to our bipeds and our quadrupeds; be gracious to our bipeds and our quadrupeds. He who hates us and whom we hate—you are difficult to overcome, O Shadow, by name (or by pride)."
Your bow is the heart, your arrows are the mind, and your discharge is the eye; I know you thus. Homage be to you! May Soma protect you; do not harm me.
To the two who are lords of the forest, like wolves with gaping jaws—to Bhava and Śarva, the sons of the Great God, be homage!
ŚŚS 4.20.2: The hymns "kad rudrāya," "imā rudrāya," "ā te pitar," "imā rudrāya," and "sthiradhanvane" [are recited].
ŚŚS 4.20.3: A boon is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).

ŚŚS 4.20.4: The rites of the animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*) consist of the introductory ritual (*upākaraṇa*), the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*), and the carrying of fire around the victim (*paryagnikaraṇa*).

ŚŚS 4.20.5: For other animals, [the portions] for the deity are from a *palāśa* branch; [the portions] for the deity are the omentum (*vapā*) and the sacrificial oblation (*havis*), and for the *sviṣṭakṛt* [deity] as well.

ŚŚS 4.20.6: The two *ājyabhāga* portions belong to Agni and Soma; [the portions] for the deity are the omentum and the sacrificial oblation; and for the *sviṣṭakṛt*, there is an oblation of clarified butter (*ājya-āhuti*). For the *sthālīpāka* offerings, there is an oblation for Anumati. ŚŚS 4.21.1: There are six persons worthy of the *arghya* reception: the teacher (*ācārya*), the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*), the father-in-law (*śvaśura*), the king (*rājan*), the graduate (*snātaka*), and a friend (*priya*).

Facing either north or east, he sits upon or steps over the ritual grass-bundle (*kūrca*), reciting: "I, the height among those like me, like the sun among lightnings, step upon this man who seeks to harm us.
Thus he sits upon or steps over the *kūrca*.

ŚŚS 4.21.3: Having accepted the water for the feet with the formula, "Thou art the milking of Virāj; may I obtain the milking of Virāj; [may] the milking of Virāj be in me for the sake of the earth," ŚŚS 4.21.4:

When addressed with the words, "The water of honor (*arghya*)," he accepts the water. ŚŚS 4.21.5: When addressed with the words, "The water for sipping (*ācamanīya*)," he sips water once with each of the three verses beginning with *āpo hi ṣṭha*.
When addressed with "The honey-mixture," he looks toward it just as he did the *prāśitra* portion;
he receives it in the same manner, with the modification:
"For glory, for spiritual luster."

Having received [the vessel] and placed it in his left hand, taking a portion from the eastern half with the thumb and the ring finger, he smears it on the eastern half of the bronze vessel, saying: "May the Vasus, whose king is Agni, consume you.

(ŚŚS 4.21.8) Taking a portion from the southern half, he smears it on the southern half, saying: "May the Pitṛs, whose king is Yama, consume you. (ŚŚS 4.21.9) Taking a portion from the western half, he smears it on the western half, saying: "May the Ādityas, whose king is Varuṇa, consume you. (ŚŚS 4.21.10)
"May the Rudras, with Indra as their king, consume thee"—with this [formula], he [takes] from the northern half to the northern half.
"May the Viśve Devas, with Prajāpati as their king, consume thee"—with this [formula], he takes from the middle upwards.
He does so once each time with the mantra, and twice each time silently.
Having consumed [the food] with each of the three Mahāvyāhṛtis one by one, he consumes the fourth without water. He gives the remains to a Brāhmaṇa.
ŚŚS 4.21.17: Or [he may drink] all [the remaining Soma].
ŚŚS 4.21.18: He pours water down [into his mouth].
ŚŚS 4.21.19: Having touched his chest with the four verses beginning with "śaṃ no devīr," [he concludes the rite].
The touching of the breath is the same;
so too is the wiping of the mouth.
[He remains] silent until the lowing of the cow.
When it is said, "The cow," one should respond, "Om.
Having recited the mantra, "She is the mother of the Rudras," one should say, "Release her! Let her eat grass!

One should announce, "A seat, water for the feet, the respectful offering (arghya), water for sipping (ācamanīya), the honey-mixture (madhuparka), and the cow"—one should announce this, one should announce it.

ŚŚS 5.1.1: One who is about to perform the Soma sacrifice chooses as officiating priests (ṛtvij) those who are of noble lineage, young, and learned in the Vedas. ŚŚS 5.1.2: He chooses four, or all [of them].
ŚŚS 5.1.3: He chooses with a low voice, saying, "The Moon is my divine Brahman priest," and aloud, saying, "You are my human [Brahman priest]."
ŚŚS 5.1.4: Thus for all [the priests].
ŚŚS 5.1.5: Āditya is my divine Udgātṛ; you are the human one. ŚŚS 5.1.6: Agni is my divine Hotṛ; you are the human one.
Vāyu is my divine Adhvaryu; you are the human one. Prajāpati is my divine Sadasya; you are the human one.
The Seasons are my divine Hotrāśaṃsins; you are the human ones.

ŚŚS 5.1.10: Having been chosen, he should mutter: "Speak for my splendor; speak for my welfare; speak for my prosperity; speak for my fortune; speak for my glory; may splendor be in me, may welfare be in me, may prosperity be in me, may fortune be in me, may glory be in me. Then, having asked, "Is this not one of those who has performed an *ahīna* sacrifice, or who has been appointed as an officiating priest (*ārtvijya*), or from whom the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) has already been received?"—if he accepts [the invitation], he should respond accordingly, or he may decline it. ŚŚS 5.2.1: The place for the sacrifice to the gods (*devayajana*) should have a slope toward the east.
ŚŚS 5.2.2: For one desiring a sacrifice, [the ground] should slope toward the east and the north.

ŚŚS 5.2.3: Wherever the Hotṛ, while reciting, can see the Āhavanīya fire, the sun, and water, that is for one desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). ŚŚS 5.2.4: The initiation (*dīkṣā*) should take place during the bright fortnight under an auspicious lunar mansion, and the conclusion likewise.
ŚŚS 5.3.1: In the afternoon, there is the *dīkṣaṇīyā* offering dedicated to Agni and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 5.3.2: It is a modification (*vikāra*) of the Full Moon sacrifice.
ŚŚS 5.3.3: It has fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses.
ŚŚS 5.3.4: The oblation is performed in a whisper.
ŚŚS 5.3.5: There are two *virāj* verses for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 5.3.6: Or [one may use] the regular [verses].

ŚŚS 5.3.7: "This sacrificer has been invited; may I attain the conclusion of the *āgura* of this sacrifice"—thus he prays. "This sacrificer has been invited; may I attain the conclusion of the *āgura* of this sacrifice"—thus he prays. This is the place for blessings (*āśis*) in the *iḍā* and the *sūktavāka*, prior to the *iḍā* of the *puroḍāśa* belonging to the third pressing.
ŚŚS 5.3.8: In the *sūktavāka*, he does not utter the name of the sacrificer prior to the *savanīya* [offering].
ŚŚS 5.3.9: And [the ritual] ends with the *patnīsaṃyāja*.

ŚŚS 5.4.1: Having taken hold of the sacrificer from behind while the Adhvaryu offers the *udagrabhaṇa* oblations, [the sacrificer recites]: "May my mind be consecrated by the mind; may my speech be consecrated by speech; may my breath be consecrated by breath; may my sight be consecrated by sight; may my hearing be consecrated by hearing. ŚŚS 5.4.2: Or he may offer the oblations. ŚŚS 5.4.3: And there is the ritual attendance (*upasthāna*) for one who has undergone a single consecration (*ekadīkṣa*).
"Into the initiation of the mind I enter," he says regarding the Āhavanīya fire; "Into the initiation of speech I enter," regarding the Gārhapatya fire;
"Into the initiation of breath I enter," regarding the Dakṣiṇa fire.
ŚŚS 5.4.7: There are unlimited consecrations; at their conclusion is the Prāyaṇīyā offering.

ŚŚS 5.5.1: [One offers] to Pathyā Svasti, Agni, Soma, and Savitṛ with clarified butter, and to Aditi with a *caru* of rice. ŚŚS 5.5.2: "May there be well-being for us on our paths; may there indeed be well-being."
O Agni, lead us; O Agni, do you carry us across.
O Soma, you are wise; [fulfill] those domains of yours with oblation.
That most excellent [glory] of Savitṛ, [belongs to him] who [created] all these beings.
"Suṭrāmāṇam mahīm ū ṣu.
(ŚŚS 5.5.3): There are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses;
(ŚŚS 5.5.4): the oblation is performed in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
ŚŚS 5.5.5: The two *ājyabhāga* offerings do not take place.
ŚŚS 5.5.6: The verses for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering are "tvām citraśravastama" and "yad vāhiṣṭham.
ŚŚS 5.5.7: And [the ritual] ends with the *śamyu*.
ŚŚS 5.6.1: Having purchased the King (Soma) and placed him upon a cart, [the Adhvaryu] is addressed with the words, "For Soma being carried around.
ŚŚS 5.6.2: "From good go forth to better; let Bṛhaspati be your leader.
Now, choosing the best place on earth, drive your enemies far away, you who are possessed of all heroes."
Standing between the two tracks, he recites:
"This prayer of one who strives," "In the woods," "O Soma, you who traverse the atmosphere"—these four verses while moving along between the two tracks.
Having stationed the cart in front of the hall, they cause the King (Soma) to descend.
He should follow along whichever way they go.
Having entered with the verse, "Those abodes of yours which [are reached] by oblation," he stands to the south in front of the Āhavanīya fire and concludes with the verse, "The god has come."
Having touched water, he releases [the vow].
From this point forward, until the carrying forth of the Āgnīṣoma fires, the purpose of water is served by the *madantī* (boiling) waters.
The guest-offering (*ātithyā*) is dedicated to Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 5.7.2: It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice.
ŚŚS 5.7.3: "Viṣṇoḥ nu kam" and "Pra tad viṣṇuḥ.
ŚŚS 5.7.4: "Hotāram citra-ratham" and "Yaḥ tvā sva-aśva" are for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
ŚŚS 5.7.5: And the fire-drills [are used] when the oblation is near.
ŚŚS 5.7.6: The oblation is performed in a low voice (upāṃśu). ŚŚS 5.7.7: It ends with the *iḍā* invocation.

Having touched water, all [the priests] together touch the *tānūnaptra*—the clarified butter from the *dhruvā* ladle containing gold, placed in a vessel upon the sacrificial grass—with the formula: "Thou art unassailable, unassailable; the vigor of the gods, a protector against curses, not to be cursed. May I straightway attain truth; place me in prosperity."
Having touched water and having gone around the front of the Āhavanīya fire while touching the stalks, they cause King Soma to swell:
"O divine Soma, may each stalk of thine swell for Indra, the winner of the single prize;
may Indra swell for thee, and may thou swell for Indra."
"Make us, your friends, swell with gain and wisdom; may it be well with you!
O divine Soma, may I attain the completion of the pressing.
(ŚŚS 5.8.4) "That stalk which the Ādityas cause to swell, which the imperishable ones drink as their imperishable portion..."
"May King Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, and the guardians of the world cause us to swell.

Having touched their chests with this [formula] and having sipped water, they place their right hands, palms upward, upon the sacrificial grass (prastara); in the afternoon, they conceal them by placing their left hands, palms upward, over them.
"Desired riches for the impulse, for fortune; truth for those who speak truth; homage to Heaven and Earth.
(ŚŚS 5.8.6) From the rite of swelling [the milk] until the Upasad, when the Upasad has been completed:
the first sacrifice is without the Pravargya. (ŚŚS 5.9.1)
ŚŚS 5.9.2: There is an option for the one learned in the Vedas (śrotriya).
ŚŚS 5.9.3: To the north of the Gārhapatya fire.
ŚŚS 5.9.4: While the Mahāvīra vessels are being set down, having entered the hall by the eastern door.
Having gone to the north of the Āhavanīya fire to the two mounds and the vessels,
and having sat down behind them, he is addressed: "O Hotṛ, recite the invitatory verses."
Without taking breath, he recites each verse individually, accompanied by the *praṇava*:
"The Brahman was born first in the east; from the navel [of the world], Vena has revealed the radiant ones.
His foundations, his highest stations, the womb of the existent and the non-existent—he has disclosed them. (RV 10.72.3–4) ŚŚS 5.9.5.
ŚŚS 5.9.6: This royal power has come to the father first for the sake of the first birth; he was the bestower of the earth.
For him they prepare this bright, well-sounding draught, the *gharma*, as the first portion of the drink.
ŚŚS 5.9.7: Toward that god Savitṛ, the source of the two worlds, whose will is that of a seer, [I turn].
I worship the one of true impulsion, the bestower of jewels, the beloved thought, the sage,
from whom the upward-shining light has flashed forth during the act of impelling;
he of golden hands and skillful wisdom has measured out the heaven with his form, which is a source of well-being.
ŚŚS 5.9.8: [The verse] "They anoint him" (*añjanti yam*) is recited when the ghee is being poured into the cavity.
ŚŚS 5.9.9: [The verse] "Sit down together" (*saṃsīdasva*) is recited when [the fire] is being settled.

ŚŚS 5.9.10: [The verses] "Be well-disposed toward us, O Agni" (*bhavā no agne sumanāḥ*), "Burn away, O Agni" (*tapo ṣv agne*), and "He who is our kinsman" (*yo naḥ sanutyaḥ*) are recited while the embers are being pushed back.
ŚŚS 5.9.11: "kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ" and the following five [verses].
ŚŚS 5.9.12: "pari tvā girvaṇaḥ" and the two [verses] following it.
ŚŚS 5.9.13: "śukraṃ te arhan bibharṣi."

ŚŚS 5.9.14: The two hymns beginning with *pataṅgam aktam srakve drapsasya*. ŚŚS 5.9.15: The two verses beginning with *pavitram ta āre*. ŚŚS 5.9.16: [The verse] beginning with *vi yat pavitram dhiṣaṇā atanvata gharmam śocantaṃ praṇaveṣu bibhrataḥ*.
In the ocean, they discerned the three names of the sun throughout the day.
Having extracted the hymn beginning with "This Vena," [and] "The fair-winged bird on the vault of heaven," [one recites] the hymn beginning with "Thee,
the leader of the hosts."
ŚŚS 5.9.19: With the words "May we speak loudly at the assembly, possessing brave sons," one should meditate upon a hero for a woman desiring a hero.
ŚŚS 5.9.20: There are nine [verses] beginning with "Who shall grant? (kā rādhad...). ŚŚS 5.9.21: There are three [verses] beginning with "With all your aids, come to us" (ā no viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ).
ŚŚS 5.9.22: "prātar.yāvāṇaḥ" is the hymn for the forenoon; ŚŚS 5.9.23:
"ā bhāti" is for the afternoon; ŚŚS 5.9.24:
having uttered the entire *dyāvīya* [section], one should cease speaking.
ŚŚS 5.9.25: Having set aside the final [verse], when it is said, "The Gharma has shone forth according to his will," he recites the hymn, "He has shone forth" (arūrucat).
ŚŚS 5.9.26: He concludes with the final verse.
ŚŚS 5.9.27: Having touched water and stood up, having worshipped the Mahāvīra with the Anuvāka of the openings (avakāśa), and having touched water again, he sits down.
ŚŚS 5.10.1: [The verse] "Upahvaya" is [recited] when the cow is being summoned. ŚŚS 5.10.2:
[The verse] "Himkṛṇvatī" is [recited] as she approaches.
ŚŚS 5.10.3: [The verse] "Abhi tvā deva savitar" is [recited] while she is being addressed.
ŚŚS 5.10.4: [The verse] "samī vatsam" (like unto the calf) is [recited] when the cow is being approached by the calf; ŚŚS 5.10.5:
"yas te stanaḥ" (that breast of yours) is [recited] when the calf has taken hold of the udder; ŚŚS 5.10.6:
"gaur amīmet" (the cow has lowed) is [recited] while she is being milked.
"Sit down with reverence, being in agreement," with these words he sits down.
"They milk the cow with a milking-vessel, with seventeen [verses] containing the word *ātman*.
'Agni is kindled, O Aśvins; the *gharma* is heated for you; come hither!'"
"The cows are milked here; the bulls are milch-cows; O doers of marvels, the poets rejoice. This [verse] is for when the cow is being milked.
"He has milked; arise, O Brahmanaspati"—with this, he rises.
Run hither with milk, O milker of cows;
sprinkle me with the heat of the milk of the ruddy cow.
Savitṛ, the friend of the house, has looked upon the vault of heaven, following heaven and earth, O excellent leader.

When the two milks are being brought forward, [he recites] *ā sute siñcata śriyam ā nūnam aśvinoḥ ṛṣiḥ*. When they are being poured out, [he recites] *ud u sya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā*. When it is being lifted up, [he recites] *ud u sya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā*.
ŚŚS 5.10.13: In the case of a reversal of ritual actions, it is according to the action.
ŚŚS 5.10.14: "May Brahmanaspati go forth"—this [is recited] when they are departing. ŚŚS 5.10.15: "The eagle upon the vault of heaven"—this [is recited] while following along.
Having sat down on the Hotṛ’s seat, [the Adhvaryu],
being addressed with the call, "Recite the offering prayer for the Gharma," recites:
"Drink both."

"The heated cauldron reaches you; your own Hotṛ-priest approaches. The Adhvaryu moves forward for you, bearing the sacrificial food. O Aśvins, partake of the milked honey for the sake of progeny; drink of the milk of the ruddy cow.
Having uttered *vaṣaṭ* with these two verses recited together.
"O Agni, partake of the Gharma"—with these words he performs the *anuvaṣaṭkāra* in the forenoon.
Now, in the afternoon:
"Drink of this."
"That which is offered in the cows as ghee and milk—this, O Aśvins, is your portion; come hither!
O lovers of sweetness, upholders of the assembly, lords of the virtuous, drink the heated *gharma* in the light of heaven!
Having uttered *vaṣaṭ* with these two verses taken together.
In the same manner, having uttered the *anuvaṣaṭ* call:

"The Gharma, consecrated with *svāhā*, pure among the gods, which is the cup of the Aśvins, the drink of the gods— may all the immortals, taking pleasure in it, lick it as they have drawn it back from the Gandharva."
Having thus praised,
[the verse] "O friend, [greet] the friend" is recited as he approaches;
[the verse] "The *gardharva* thus" is recited as he is being seated.
He shall repeat the *pragātha* verse beginning with "tam gha īm itthā" before the offering;
[he shall repeat] "haviḥ haviṣmat" prior to the oblation;
the Hotṛ's portion is to be consumed as a breath-sacrifice (*prāṇabhakṣa*).
ŚŚS 5.10.29: It is directly perceived by the sacrificer.
ŚŚS 5.10.30: And also in the case of the *dadhigharma*.

ŚŚS 5.10.31: "The oblation has been offered into the most Indra-like fire; O divine Gharma, may we partake of thee who art honeyed, full of vigor, and full of nourishment"—this is the mantra for the consumption.
While the great heroic vessels are being set down—
those upon which the seven Vasus ascend as ancient plants—
the Ṛṣi of far-reaching fame is indeed Indra’s guest, the one who is most worthy of praise.
Having thus offered praise,
and having concluded with the verse "sūyavasa-," and having touched water, he releases [the vow].
ŚŚS 5.10.35: On the day of the Soma-pressing, the *pravargya* rite is performed at the *āgnīdhrīya* fire during the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant and also at the midday pressing.

ŚŚS 5.10.36: Having removed [the *pravargya* implements] from the *prastara* grass-bundle, they perform the *upasad* rites; if the *pravargya* has been performed, they do so after concluding the *pravargya*. ŚŚS 5.11.1: For the *upasad*, in the forenoon, he recites three *sāmidhenī* verses without taking breath, repeating each one three times with the *praṇava* (*oṃ*) at the end.
ŚŚS 5.11.2: "O Agni, this fuel for me..."—with these three verses, he performs [the rite] in the afternoon.
ŚŚS 5.11.3: Having joined the latter verse with the third word of the former, he concludes.
ŚŚS 5.11.4: Having joined [them] with the *praṇava* (the syllable Om), [he recites]: "Bring Agni; bring Soma; bring Viṣṇu."
ŚŚS 5.11.5: Having caused [the sacrificer] to take up the two *sruva*-ladles by means of the *srug-ādāpana* formula;
ŚŚS 5.11.6: He performs the sacrifice in a whisper (*upāṃśu*);
ŚŚS 5.11.7: "Agni, who [is like] a fierce one, [slays] the Vṛtras..."
"O Soma, you who with your mental powers are invincible in battles—him, the ancient one, do you, O praisers, [extol].
(ŚŚS 5.11.8): One should perform as much as has been prescribed.
ŚŚS 5.11.9: There is a reversal of the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses in the afternoon.

ŚŚS 5.11.10: On the second day, in the forenoon, there are three *sāmidhenī* verses beginning with "This fuel of mine, O Agni" (*imām me agne samidham*). ŚŚS 5.11.11: In the afternoon, [the verses begin] with "To the one worthy of attendance" (*upasadyāya*).
As it was in the first [day], so it is in the third.
However, their respective times should be extended;
or else, there is a reversal day by day.
ŚŚS 5.11.15: On the day of preparation (upavasatha), in the morning, having brought both ritual sessions to a conclusion;
ŚŚS 5.12.1: The carrying forward of the fire (agnipraṇayana) takes place when the Pravargya rite is not performed;
ŚŚS 5.12.2: The removal of the Mahāvīra vessel takes place when the Pravargya rite is performed.
ŚŚS 5.12.3: Therein, the *prastotṛ* chants the *sāman*. ŚŚS 5.12.4: Therein, the method for the *hotṛ*'s *nidhana* [is as follows].
ŚŚS 5.12.5: The carrying forward of the fire (*agnipraṇayana*) has been explained.
ŚŚS 5.13.1: He is addressed [with a mantra] for the purpose of setting the two *havirdhāna* carts in motion.

ŚŚS 5.13.2: Standing between the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and the southern track of the northern one, he is addressed with the words, "While the two *havirdhāna* carts are being set in motion...
ŚŚS 5.13.3: "...O Vṛtra-slayer, away with the danger from one's own kin and away with that from strangers."
"Having cast away the hair with his right forefoot, saying, 'The wheels have turned back,' and while standing,
having recited, 'May they go forth of the sacrifice,'" ŚŚS 5.13.4.

ŚŚS 5.13.5: While moving along, leaning toward the northern track of the southern [fire], he recites, "O Heaven and Earth, for us... and "Of these two, indeed, the one rich in ghee, like Yama... ŚŚS 5.13.6:
He recites, "Over the two," when the roof-covering is being placed. ŚŚS 5.13.7:
He recites, "All forms indeed," while the two [fires] are being encircled by the enclosing stones.
ŚŚS 5.13.8: [The verse] "ā vām upastham" is for the two [verses] situated at the navel. ŚŚS 5.13.9: In the case of a reversal of the ritual action, it is according to the action.
ŚŚS 5.13.10: Having performed the ritual covering with [the verse] "pari tvā girvaṇaḥ."
ŚŚS 5.13.11: Standing where he first uttered [the call], he releases [the victim] while remaining there.

ŚŚS 5.14.1: When the sacrificial sheds have been measured out, they lead forward Agni and Soma. ŚŚS 5.14.2: From that point until the conclusion of the Anubandhyā sacrifice, the path between the *cātvāla* and the *utkara* is the *tīrtha*.
Having entered by that [door],
having gone past the Āgnīdhrīya hearth and the Sadas to the north,
and having passed the two Adhvaryus and the sacrificial vessels to the north, he enters the hall by the eastern door.

Having sat down behind the *śālāmukhīya* fire, [the Adhvaryu], being addressed with the words, "To Agni and Soma as they are being led forth," recites: "O God, impel [the sacrifice] for the first father; bestow height upon him, bestow breadth upon him."
"Then, O Savitṛ, impel for us in our complete prosperity day by day abundant cattle"—having recited this while seated, [he says]:
"Arise, O Brahmanaspati! (ŚŚS 5.14.9).
"May Brahmanaspati come forward" (ŚŚS 5.14.10);
"The divine Hotṛ [has come]"; "O Agni, come hither"—these two triplets (ŚŚS 5.14.14).
For one desiring a child, he should meditate upon a child with the verse, "He has placed the germ of beings," while walking along behind the northern part of the *sadas*.

They place the fire on the Āgnīdhrīya hearth while the oblation is being offered with the verse, "O Agni, be pleased. Following this, they walk around the fire to the north, reciting the three verses beginning with, "Soma goes forth."
ŚŚS 5.14.16: [He recites] "upa priyam" when the oblation is being offered into the Āhavanīya fire.
ŚŚS 5.14.17: [He recites] "tam asya rājā" while he is being led forward.
ŚŚS 5.14.18: [He recites] "antaś ca prāg ā" after having followed him in.

ŚŚS 5.14.19: When the King [Soma] has been settled in the southern *havirdhāna* cart, standing to the north of it facing south, he recites: "Like a falcon, you have settled in your womb; you have propped up the sky for the multitudes. ŚŚS 5.14.20: Having concluded with "Thus do you praise," ŚŚS 5.14.21: Turning to the left, he sits down at the eastern door of the two *havirdhāna* carts.
When [the sacrificer] is being led out by the western door, the Hotṛ follows him.
The recitation is the same.
Having turned to the right and exited by the western door, having turned to the left and gone north of the two *havirdhāna* carts, he sits down right there.
ŚŚS 5.15.1: On the day of preparation (*upavasatha*), he sacrifices with the animal victim dedicated to Agni and Soma.

ŚŚS 5.15.2: When addressed with the call, "Bring the clarified butter for the sacrificial post (*yūpa*)," he recites [the verse], "They anoint you" (*añjanti tvām*). ŚŚS 5.15.3: When addressed with the call, "For the one being raised," he recites: "Be raised up, O Lord of the Forest (*vanaspate*)"; "Being placed in front of the kindled fire"; "Born, he is born upright"; and "Upright for us, may he stand upright for us."

When [the Adhvaryu] says, "For him who is being girded," [the Hotṛ], having put on a fresh garment with the verse, "Young and well-clad," stands and recites the verses for kindling the fire by friction (*agnimanthanīyāḥ*).
Having put on [the garment] with the verse, "By sacrifice, sacrifice," he recites the *sāmidhenī* verses.
Having invoked the deity of the animal sacrifice, he subsequently invokes Vanaspati.
Having touched the two *adhvaryus*, he stands still.
With the formula, "By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the directors, I give you over for the safety of the sacrifice," the sacrificer hands the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
Having accepted it with that same mantra as required, the Hotṛ, turning to the right, proceeds first to the south of the Hotṛ.

Having gone between the two *havirdhāna* sheds to the south of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, having entered the *sadas* by the eastern door, and having sat down behind his own hearth, he performs the eleven *prayāja* offerings.
(ŚŚS 5.16.1) The *praiṣas* belong to the Maitrāvaruṇa;
(ŚŚS 5.16.2) and the *puronuvākyās* accompany the *praiṣas*.
ŚŚS 5.16.3: Likewise with the recitations.

ŚŚS 5.16.4: While standing during the abandonment [of the grass-bundle], having stepped forward with the staff, and being addressed with "Command for the fuel-sticks," the Hotṛ issues the command: "Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni with the fuel-stick.
ŚŚS 5.16.5: The Āprī verses are the *yājyās* for the fore-sacrifices (*prayāja*), according to the lineage of the sacrificer.
ŚŚS 5.16.6: Or, for all [the prayājas], he recites "samiddho adya manuṣaḥ" (kindled today by man).
ŚŚS 5.16.7: But the Nārāśaṃsī verse belongs to that [third] prayāja.

ŚŚS 5.16.8: Having performed with ten [verses], when the call "paryagnayaḥ" (around the fires) is given, he recites the three verses beginning with "agnir hotā no adhvaraḥ" (Agni is our priest at the sacrifice).

ŚŚS 5.16.9: Having been addressed with "Upapreṣya hotar" (Prompt the Hotṛ), he recites the *upapraiṣa* formula: "Agni has won. ŚŚS 5.16.10: Once the *upapraiṣa* has been recited, the Hotṛ recites the *adhrigu* formula.
ŚŚS 5.17.1: "O divine immolators and also you human ones, take hold! Bring forward the sacrificial doors, desiring the sacrifice for the two lords of the sacrifice."

ŚŚS 5.17.2: Bring fire for him; spread the sacrificial grass. Let his mother give her consent, let his father give his consent, let his brother born of the same womb give his consent, and let his companion from the same herd give his consent.

ŚŚS 5.17.3: Place his feet turned toward the north. Make his eye go to the sun, release his breath to the wind, his life-spirit to the intermediate space, his hearing to the quarters, and his body to the earth.
ŚŚS 5.17.4: Flay off his skin in one piece before reaching the navel. Extract the omentum without cutting it into shreds. Hold back the internal heat as if it were between you.

ŚŚS 5.17.5: Make his breast like a hawk; his arms with the *praśas* knife, his forearms with the *śalā*; his shoulders like those of Kaśyapa; his hips without holes; his thighs like *kavaṣa* reeds; and his knee-bones like *srekaparṇa* leaves.
ŚŚS 5.17.6: There are twenty-six ribs in him; pull them out one by one from the sides; make every limb of his free from deficiency. ŚŚS 5.17.7:
Dig out the raw entrails and the cow-dung for fuel.
ŚŚS 5.17.8: "Do not let the Rakṣas mingle with the entrails.

ŚŚS 5.17.9: "Do not tear out his rectum, thinking it to be the liver; do not let there be a cry for you regarding your offspring and descendants, O preparers!"—this is the ninth section in the *adhrigu* formula.
ŚŚS 5.17.10: Having recited three times, "O *adhrigu*, prepare! Prepare well! Prepare, O *adhrigu*!", he should mutter in a low voice: "Both [the gods] are free from evil... etc.
ŚŚS 5.17.11: One should not look at the animal while it is being slaughtered.
ŚŚS 5.17.12: Looking at the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) is the expiation.
ŚŚS 5.17.13: Or one should mutter a verse addressed to Viṣṇu.
When addressed with "To the drops," he recites the hymn beginning with "Be pleased with this most extensive sacrifice of ours.
When addressed with "To the Svāhā-offerings," the Hotṛ issues the direction: "Let him sacrifice to Agni; Svāhā to the clarified butter!
The final verse of the Āprī-hymns serves as the offering prayer (yājyā).
ŚŚS 5.18.4: Between the final fore-offering (*prayāja*) and the omentum offering, there is the restraint of speech.
ŚŚS 5.18.5: He does not offer the two *ājyabhāga* portions.
ŚŚS 5.18.6: Or [he offers] the two [portions] accompanied by the word *vṛdh*.
The *nigamas* belonging to the New and Full Moon sacrifices (*darśapūrṇamāsa*) are to be applied to those [formulas] in which they occur;
however, not in the case of the *praiṣas*.
"O Agni and Soma, this... is the *puronuvākyā* for the omentum (*vapā*).
ŚŚS 5.18.10: "The Hotṛ shall sacrifice to Agni and Soma"—this is the *praiṣa* (direction).
ŚŚS 5.18.11: "You two [have taken] these"—this is the *yājyā* (offering verse).
ŚŚS 5.18.12: Having gone out by the way they entered, and having touched the *cātvāla* pit with the three-verse hymn beginning "O Waters, this," they are released from their vows.

ŚŚS 5.19.1: Having been summoned for the animal-cake (paśu-puroḍāśa), the two [the Hotṛ and the Āgnīdhra] go past the north of the Āgnīdhrīya fire and the Hotṛ’s hearth, and each sits down at his own hearth (dhiṣṇya).
ŚŚS 5.19.2: By virtue of their capacity, they accomplish the purposes intended for the animal sacrifice.
ŚŚS 5.19.3: This applies even when there is a combination with the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the cake.
ŚŚS 5.19.4: [The verses] for those that are unequal [are to be used] without modification.
ŚŚS 5.19.5: There are no *nigamas* (concluding formulas) for those being enjoined in the animal sacrifice ritual (*paśutantre*).
ŚŚS 5.19.6: "O Agni and Soma, he who today... is the *puronuvākyā* for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*).
ŚŚS 5.19.7: "Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni and Soma"—this is the *praisha* (direction).
ŚŚS 5.19.8: "O Agni and Soma, satisfy [the gods]"—this is the *yājyā* (offering verse).
ŚŚS 5.19.9: "O Agni, [bring] the *iḍā*"—this is the *puronuvākyā* for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 5.19.10: "The Hotṛ shall sacrifice to Agni of the puroḍāśa"—this is the *praisha* (direction).
ŚŚS 5.19.11: "To Agni, the well-shining one"—this is the *yājyā* (offering verse).
ŚŚS 5.19.12: Having invoked *iḷā*, they proceed with the animal sacrifice.
ŚŚS 5.19.13: When [the Adhvaryu] has said, "For the Manotā, for the oblation," he recites the Manotā hymn beginning with, "For you, O Agni, are the first Manotā.
ŚŚS 5.19.14: "O Agni and Soma, who [are invoked] when the offering is made"—this is the puronuvākyā for the animal sacrifice.
ŚŚS 5.19.15: "Let the Hotṛ worship Agni and Soma"—this is the *praiṣa* (direction).
ŚŚS 5.19.16: At the half-verse of the *yājyā* beginning with "O Agni and Soma, of the oblation," he pauses before the *vasā-homa*.
ŚŚS 5.19.17: Once it has been offered, he utters the *vaṣaṭ* call.
ŚŚS 5.19.18: "To the gods, O Vanaspati"—this is the *puronuvākyā* for Vanaspati.
ŚŚS 5.19.19: "The Hotṛ shall sacrifice to Vanaspati"—this is the *praiṣa* (direction).
ŚŚS 5.19.20: "O Vanaspati, with the cord..."—this is the *yājyā* (offering verse).
ŚŚS 5.19.21: "Delight the gods..."—this is the *puronuvākyā* for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
"Let the Hotṛ worship Agni Sviṣṭakṛt"—this is the *praisha*.
The *yājyā* is without the *nigada*.
Having invoked the *iḷā*, he performs eleven *anuyāja* offerings.
ŚŚS 5.20.1: He issues the direction without pausing: "O divine *barhis*, well-divine, with the gods...
ŚŚS 5.20.2: He performs the sacrifice in the same manner as in the Cāturmāsya offerings.
ŚŚS 5.20.3: The two additional [verses] are inserted between the eighth and ninth [verses].
"May the divine Vanaspati partake of the gift of wealth for the winning of wealth.
May the divine Barhis of the waters partake of the gift of wealth for the winning of wealth.
(ŚŚS 5.20.4) Having been addressed with "Recite the hymn; give the command," he recites the *sūktavāka-praiṣa* (the call for the hymn-recitation): "Agni today as the Hotṛ... (ŚŚS 5.20.5).
ŚŚS 5.20.6: [The procedure] for the *savanīya* [offering] is that of the Soma sacrifice.
ŚŚS 5.20.7: When the two *śamyu* verses have been recited, the Maitrāvaruṇa priest steps out as he has entered and is released from his duties.
ŚŚS 5.20.8: The Hotṛ, having gone to the hall, concludes the night rite with the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings; he concludes it, he concludes it.

ŚŚS 6.1.1: The animal sacrifice dedicated to Agni and Soma has been explained; it is the archetype (*prakṛti*) of all animal sacrifices. ŚŚS 6.1.2: The Vedic tradition (*ārṣam āmnānam*) of the mantras belongs to the archetype.

ŚŚS 6.1.3: Since the modification of meaning does not arise in its formal manifestation during the subsequent performance (*tatau*) according to the specific purpose, they call the modification of the word-text "ūha."
In the *ṛc* verses, no modification occurs.
[The forms] are *yajamānābhyām*, *yajamānebhyaḥ*;
*medhapataye*, *medhapatibhyaḥ*.
May they be wise; may they bestow wisdom;
may they eat; may they cause [all] to eat.
"They have eaten," "they have devoured," or "they have eaten"—thus [it is said].
Like two very powerful ones, as it were; like two very powerful ones, as it were.
They have seized; they have seized. They have grown strong; they have grown strong.
They have attained.
*ṛdhyāsuḥ*,
*acīkametām*, *acīkamanta*:
thus, due to a difference in meaning, there is a modification of the word.

ŚŚS 6.1.6: [The names] *barhis*, *cakṣus*, *śrotra*, *prāṇa*, *asu*, *tvac*, *nābhi*, *ūṣman*, *jñāti*, *nāman*, *śyena*, *śalā*, *kaśyapa*, *kavaṣa*, *sreka*, *parṇa*, *ūvadhya*, *goḥ*, and *asna*—[these are used] according to their traditional recitation (yathā-samāmnātam).
ŚŚS 6.1.7: And [the same applies] in case of doubt regarding an injunction (*codanā*).
ŚŚS 6.1.8: Those which have become subordinate (*śeṣabhūta*) are "new" (*apūrva*).
ŚŚS 6.1.9: And the *āyanigadas*. ŚŚS 6.1.10: Or, by way of summary: "One by one, twenty-six, twenty-six.
ŚŚS 6.1.11: This is the rule for the enumeration.
ŚŚS 6.1.12: And [the dual ending] is used in the plural for [a compound consisting of] a single deity and two deities.
ŚŚS 6.1.13: In the case of a pair [of male and female deities], when [the names] are identical, [the masculine form] is used as in the masculine. ŚŚS 6.1.14: Or optionally, even otherwise.
ŚŚS 6.1.15: With the syllable *eva*, there is a conjunction of the name of the deity beginning with a vowel when it belongs to a dual divinity.
ŚŚS 6.1.16: When there is a distinction between the sacrificial animals (*paśu*), one binds [the formula] once.
ŚŚS 6.1.17: And [they are] well-established.
ŚŚS 6.1.18: At the beginning and end of the northern course of the sun, there is the Nirūḍhapaśubandha sacrifice dedicated to Indra and Agni.
ŚŚS 6.1.19: Or it may be performed annually.
ŚŚS 6.1.20: There are many optional (kāmya) forms of this sacrifice.

ŚŚS 6.1.21: The animal sacrifices, beginning with the leading forward of the fire (agni-praṇayana) and ending with the heart-spit (hṛdaya-śūla), are performed, excluding the Agniṣomīya and the Savanīya. ŚŚS 6.1.22: And for one who is about to sacrifice, there is the offering to Agni and Viṣṇu. ŚŚS 6.1.23: And the formal utterance of the benediction (nirvacanam ca āśiṣam).
ŚŚS 6.1.24: And except for the Agniṣomīya [offering], there is no mention of names in the *sūktavāka*.
ŚŚS 6.1.25: From the *prātar-anuvāka* onwards, the hymns (*sūktas*) are prescribed for the recitation of the *śastras* and the *anuvacanas*.
ŚŚS 6.1.26: One should follow a single [hymn] elsewhere.
At the end of the night, having been summoned for the morning recitation (prātar-anuvāka), standing in front of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth, he mutters the *prapada* formulas.

ŚŚS 6.2.2: I take refuge in *bhūḥ*; I take refuge in *bhuvaḥ*; I take refuge in *svaḥ*; I take refuge in *bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*. I take refuge in *om*; I take refuge in speech; I take refuge in the *ṛc*; I take refuge in the mind; I take refuge in the *yajus*; I take refuge in the *sāman*; I take refuge in breath; I take refuge in sight; I take refuge in hearing. Homage to the gods; homage to the deities; homage to the Great God; homage to the *gandharvas* and *apsarases*; homage to the serpent-deities; homage to the past; homage to the future; homage to the ancestors; and homage also to you who respond to salutations. ŚŚS 6.2.3: He worships the quarters according to their respective forms.

ŚŚS 6.3.1: "In this eastern direction of mine, the Sun and the Moon are the lords; may the Sun and the Moon protect me from this direction. May he who seeks to harm us from here encounter the Sun and the Moon along with their deities"—thus [he addresses] the east. ŚŚS 6.3.2: "In this southern direction of mine, Yama and Death are the lords; may Yama and Death protect me from this direction. May he who seeks to harm us from here encounter Yama and Death along with their deities"—thus [he addresses] the south.

"In this western direction of mine, Mitra and Varuṇa are the overlords; may Mitra and Varuṇa protect me from this direction. May he among the gods who seeks to harm us from here reach Mitra and Varuṇa"—thus [he addresses] the west.

"In this northern direction of mine, Soma and Rudra are the overlords; may Soma and Rudra protect me from this direction. May he among the gods who seeks to harm us from here reach Soma and Rudra"—thus, turning to the left, [he addresses] the north.

ŚŚS 6.3.5: "In this upward direction, Bṛhaspati and Indra are the two overlords; may Bṛhaspati and Indra protect me from this direction; may he among the gods who seeks after Bṛhaspati and Indra reach him who assails us from here"—thus [he looks] toward the upward direction. ŚŚS 6.3.6: "In this intermediate space, Vāyu and Vṛṣṭi are the two overlords; may Vāyu and Vṛṣṭi protect me from this direction; may he among the gods who seeks after Vāyu and Vṛṣṭi reach him who assails us from here"—thus [he looks] toward the intermediate space.

"On this earth, Agni and food are the two lords; may Agni and food protect me from this quarter. May he among the gods who seeks after Agni and food reach him who assails us here"—thus [he addresses] the earth.

Having murmured, "The *bṛhat* and *rathantara* are my thighs, the *vāmadevya* is my self, the *yajñāyajñīya* is my foundation; *bhūḥ* am I, *bhuvaḥ* am I, *svar* am I, the stone am I, the stone-cutter am I; [and] 'Sutrāmāṇam' (SV 2.1207)," and having offered an oblation with the *sruva*-ladle while turning to the right at the *āgnīdhrīya* fire with the formula, "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! To Agni svāhā! To Uṣas svāhā! To the Aśvins svāhā! To the Aśvins svāhā! To Sarasvatī svāhā! May the great ones, enjoying the libations, partake of the clarified butter svāhā!", he then turns to the left and sits at the eastern door of the two *havirdhāna* carts.

ŚŚS 6.3.9: Having been addressed with the words, "To the gods who go early in the morning," and having uttered the sound *him*, he recites the *prātar-anuvāka* (morning litany) in a medium tone of voice.

ŚŚS 6.3.10: He should pause after combining three *padās* (metrical feet) of the *paṅkti* verses; he should utter the *praṇava* (*oṃ*) after two [feet]. ŚŚS 6.3.11: Having recited the *revatī* verses beginning with "āpo revatīḥ," he recites the *āgneya* hymn in the *gāyatrī* meter, which is the *kratu*.
Ceasing the sacrifice,
I praise Agni, the domestic priest;
we choose Agni as our messenger.
"Aśvam na tvā" consists of ten [verses]. "Juṣasva saprathastamam" and "Abhi tvā gotamā girā."
Agni is the Hotṛ, the one placed in front;
he is your messenger. O Agni, have mercy!
Singing hymns to you, we approach Agni with a chant for the sake of service.
These [verses] belong to the Brahmin:
"With fuel for Agni" (ŚŚS 6.4.1c); "May they impel Agni."
"O Agni, [I offer] speech.
"Thou, O Agni, of sacrifices..."—these are twenty-six [verses].
Next is the *ānuṣṭubha* [section].
"Te te agne" is one verse; "Hotā ajaniṣṭa" and "Tvaṃ hi kṣaitavad" are nine verses.
"O Agni, when will it be for you in succession?"—these five verses;
then the *traiṣṭubha* [section]:
"When of the grass..."—these five verses.
"yo martyeṣu" consists of three [verses];
"pra vo devam" consists of five hymns;
and "agne bṛhan" consists of seven [verses].
"aganma mahā. Now follows the Bārhata [stotra]: "enā vaḥ" and "pra vo yahvam."
"O Agni, Vivasvat," twelve [verses];
"O friends, you," eight;
"It has been seen," four.
The three verses beginning with "samiddhaś cit" [are recited]. Then follows "ayam agniḥ suvīryasya," which is in the *auṣṇīha* meter. (ŚŚS 6.4.8)
ŚŚS 6.4.9: "O Agni, the wise ones [praise] you; do thou indeed come hither; [they praise] thee many times. ŚŚS 6.4.10:
Now follows the Jāgata [meter].
"Seated upon the altar," etc., seven [verses].
"Come hither, O Hotṛ!
"Grow through the sacrifice! [These are the verses.]
The guardian of the people. ŚŚS 6.4.12:
Now follows the *pāṅkta* [hymn]. ŚŚS 6.4.13:
"I think of that Agni..."
Now follows the *uṣasya* hymn in the *gāyatrī* meter:
the three verses beginning with "Who [has praised] thee, O Dawn? and "Toward her, the noble lady... (RV 7.81.1–3).
ŚŚS 6.5.3: Now, [the hymn] in the *anuṣṭubh* meter; ŚŚS 6.5.4:
"O Dawn, with your auspicious [chariots]";
ŚŚS 6.5.5: Now, [the hymn] in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
ŚŚS 6.5.6: "upo ruruca" consists of four [verses].
ŚŚS 6.5.7: Now follows the Bārhata [section].
ŚŚS 6.5.8: "praty u adarśi."
With the *vāmā* [verse].
ŚŚS 6.5.9: Now follows the *auṣṇiha* [section].
ŚŚS 6.5.10: The three verses beginning with "uṣas taccitram" [are recited].
ŚŚS 6.5.11: Now follows the Jāgata [meter].
ŚŚS 6.5.12: "etā u tyā" and so forth, four verses.
ŚŚS 6.5.13: Now follows the Pāṅkta [meter].
ŚŚS 6.5.14: *mahe naḥ*. ŚŚS 6.6.1: Now follows the *āśvina* [stotra] in the *gāyatrī* meter. ŚŚS 6.6.2: The three verses beginning with *aśvinā yajvarīriṣaḥ*.
The four [verses] beginning with *prātar yujā*;
the three [verses] beginning with *āśvināv aśvavatī*;
and this [verse], *eṣo uṣāḥ*.
"Go maduṣu" consists of two [verses].
"Dūrād iha iva" consists of thirty-six [verses]. "Ud īrāthām" and "Ā me havam."
Now follows the Ānuṣṭubh [section]: the two hymns beginning with "With all your aids,
come to us" (RV 8.60.1) and "If today you are in the far distance" (RV 8.60.20).
Now follows the *traiṣṭubha*:
the hymn beginning with "ā bhāti" (ŚŚS 6.6.6a),
and the three [verses] beginning with "nāsatyābhyām" (ŚŚS 6.6.6b).
The three verses beginning with "O Vasus and Rudras," and the hymn beginning with "Your realms," [are recited] like the pressing-stones.
The hymns "Dhenuḥ pratnasya" and "Ka u śravat," and from the hymn "Stuṣe naraḥ," excluding the five-footed verse.
"Your chariot, encompassing the two worlds..."—these are five hymns. ŚŚS 6.6.7:
Now follows the Bārhata [section]. ŚŚS 6.6.8: "These offerings of yours in heaven... [etc.]
"ayam vām madhumattamaḥ"—this is the first, third, and fifth [verses].
Next is the auṣṇiha:
"yuvor u ṣu ratham"—these five [verses].
Now follows the *jāgata* [meter]: "triścin no adya" and "īḷe dyāvīyam."
And [the verse] "Ghoṣā with her sons.
Now follows the Pāṅkta [section]:
"Prati priyatamam" (To the most beloved).
Having donned [the garment] with the *uttama* verse and having released his speech,
he proceeds either immediately after the *chandas* or with the *pratipad*, the *samārohaṇīya* verses, and this recited collection (*samāmnāya*), which consists of three hundred and sixty [verses].
Or, beyond a hundred, he may proceed according to his desire.
ŚŚS 6.6.19: One should not omit the *pāṅkta* verses.
ŚŚS 6.6.20: "They shall offer the *upāṃśu* [oblation] before sunrise"—this is the time for the *paridhāna* (the concluding rite).
ŚŚS 6.6.21: The restraint of speech continues until the *antaryāma* [offering].
ŚŚS 6.7.1: Having been addressed with "O Hotṛ, invite [the gods]," he recites the verse beginning with *pra devatrā*, omitting the twelfth.
ŚŚS 6.7.2: Having recited nine verses, he recites the eleventh while the oblation is being poured into the waters.
ŚŚS 6.7.3: When those [waters] have been turned back, he recites the tenth verse.
ŚŚS 6.7.4: [He recites] *prati yad āpaḥ* when the waters are being seen;
ŚŚS 6.7.5: [He recites] *sam anyāḥ* when they are flowing together;
ŚŚS 6.7.6: [He recites] *āpo na devīḥ* while the waters are being poured into the Hotṛ’s cup.
ŚŚS 6.7.7: Having recited the entire [hymn] beginning with "The cows have come" (*ā dhenavaḥ*) while the [verses] are being brought forward, he pauses with the *praṇava*.
ŚŚS 6.7.8: He asks the Adhvaryu, "O Adhvaryu, have you found water? (*adhvaryo 'veṣīr apaḥ*). ŚŚS 6.7.9: He replies, "Indeed, they have bowed down" (*uta iva namnamuḥ*).

Having been addressed, he recites the *nigada*: "O Adhvaryu, run hither for Indra the Soma—full of vigor, full of greatness, bestowing thirst-quenching strength, accompanied by the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, the Vājins, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods;
drinking which, Indra, in his exhilaration, struck down the Vṛtras.
May you further us across the hostilities."

Having recited the first one-and-a-half verses beginning with "ambayaḥ," and having stood up and turned toward the Adhvaryu, he recites the next one-and-a-half verses and the penultimate verse of the hymn.
Having put on the upper garment with the *uttamā* verse and having turned around, he sits down.
As the *upāṃśu* cup is being offered, he breathes in after it, saying: "Protect my breath; quicken my breath; svāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya. (ŚŚS 6.8.1)
"Protect my out-breath; quicken my out-breath. Svāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya"—with these words he follows the Antaryāma cup.
Then, having sat down to the south, the Brahman and the Maitrāvaruṇa say:
"O Brahman, we shall chant the Stotra; O Praśāstṛ, give the command. Thus they are addressed.
Having murmured, "O long-lived ṛc-verses, do not depart; protect our bodies; praise the Sāman; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ," [he says]: "Om, praise! ŚŚS 6.8.7.
Having murmured, "O long-lived ṛc-verses, do not depart; protect our bodies; praise the Sāman; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ," [he says]:
"Om, praise! ŚŚS 6.8.7. "Om, praise! ŚŚS 6.8.7.

ŚŚS 6.8.8: The *prasava* (impulse) belongs to all the *stotras*. ŚŚS 6.8.9: "Lead me from non-existence to existence; lead me from darkness to light; lead me from the end to the infinite; lead me from death to immortality"—thus the sacrificer [recites] when about to approach the *pavamāna* chants.

ŚŚS 6.8.10: "You are a falcon, a winged one, with the *gāyatrī* metre; I take hold of you; carry me safely across to the conclusion of this sacrifice"—[this he says] when the *bahiṣpavamāna* has been chanted.

"Thou art the fair-winged bird, the Triṣṭubh metre," [he says] at the midday pressing; "Thou art the friend, the winged bird, the Jagatī metre," [he says] at the third pressing. The conclusion is the same for both.

ŚŚS 6.8.14: "The gods have been invited to partake of this Soma, the purifying and far-seeing one. May the gods invite me to partake of this Soma, the purifying and far-seeing one. With my mind I partake of you; with my speech I partake of you; with my breath I partake of you; with my sight I partake of you; with my hearing I partake of you. Thus [he says] when the *bahiṣpavamāna* has been chanted. ŚŚS 6.9.1: The animal victim for the *savana* belongs to Agni. ŚŚS 6.9.2: Or it belongs to Indra and Agni.
ŚŚS 6.9.3: Or [the ritual] may be performed with eleven victims.
ŚŚS 6.9.6: When there are eleven victims tied to a single sacrificial post, the verse for the girding of the ropes is repeated three times each, because the ropes are distinct.
ŚŚS 6.9.7: Between the eleventh victim and the verse for the girding of the ropes, he recites the *pragātha* and the remainder of the hymn beginning with "yān vo naraḥ."
ŚŚS 6.9.8: He consecrates the sacrificial animal lying near with the last [verse].
ŚŚS 6.9.9: On the previous day, when the stakes have been raised but the ropes have not yet been fastened around them, he should enclose [the altar] with the first [of the two verses].
ŚŚS 6.9.10: Or, for the sake of continuity, he may wait until the half-verse alone [is completed].
ŚŚS 6.9.11: One should follow with those of the same class.
ŚŚS 6.9.12: Just as in the last [verse], so too by means of modification (*ūha*).
ŚŚS 6.9.13: Having invoked the deity of the animal sacrifice and Vanaspati.

"Bring Indra accompanied by the Vasus; bring Indra accompanied by the Rudras; bring Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, the Vājas, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods. These are the deities of the libations (*savana-devatās*).
They do not appear in other places of recitation (*nigama-sthāna*), or [only] in the *sūktavāka*.
ŚŚS 6.9.16: Having touched [the two fires] together with the Adhvaryu, he offers the two Pravara-offerings in the prescribed order.
ŚŚS 6.9.17: "May I be beloved of speech; may I be beloved of Vācaspati. O divine Speech, bestow upon us today that which is the sweetest part of your speech."
With the formula "Svāhā to Sarasvatī," he offers the first oblation;
silently, the second.

With the verses beginning "O Agni, lead us" (RV 1.189.1), "Of the sacrifice... (RV 2.1.1), and "Forward for the bright one... (RV 8.43.1) and "O singers... (RV 8.43.2), [he offers] the three oblations belonging to Agni.

ŚŚS 6.10.2: “From the great heaven, from the mountain, may we, seeking the gods, [invoke] Sarasvatī; O Sarasvatī, may the radiant maiden come toward us with her flood; these [oblations] are being offered. This is for the sacrifice to Sarasvatī. ŚŚS 6.10.3: “O Soma, you are wise; you [know] these plants; Soma [is] the cow; those divine abodes of yours; [you are] victorious in battles; those abodes of yours; this is the oblation. This is for the sacrifice to Soma. ŚŚS 6.10.4: “Pūṣan [protects] these regions; on the path of paths; the path of paths; bright is your [light]; those [paths] of yours, O Pūṣan; Pūṣan is a good kinsman. This is for the sacrifice to Pūṣan.

ŚŚS 6.10.5: “To the divine ordainer, Bṛhaspati has won him, for he is pure; with the well-praised [hymn], with the one containing ṛks; may he come to our womb”—this is the [introductory verse] for the offering to Bṛhaspati. ŚŚS 6.10.6: “O Viśve Devas, O Maruts, today, all you who provide aid; O gods, whomsoever among you gods you favor; O Viśve Devas, praise those who are on earth; for they are the ones worthy of sacrifice at the rites, the helpers; upon the strewn sacrificial grass”—this is the [introductory verse] for the Vaiśvadeva offering.
ŚŚS 6.10.7: “Indra the men, Indra the king; Indra, the wide dominion; come to us with all your aids, being of one mind; your vigor, O bull”—this is the [introductory verse] for the offering to Indra.

ŚŚS 6.10.8: "O men, [be] like one possessing cattle and horses; O pure ones, you are like spokes; that which is your protection, may you [grant it] to us"—this is for the Maruts. ŚŚS 6.10.9: "Both of you, O slayers of Vṛtra, fight; the wise man with his songs [praises] the pure one among the peoples"—this is for Indra and Agni.

ŚŚS 6.10.10: "May the god Savitṛ come to our aid; may the god Savitṛ come with his restraints; may he grant us what is desirable today; those paths of yours, [grant] that from heaven to us"—this is for Savitṛ.
"astabhnād dyām," "tat tvā yāmi," "ava te heḷaḥ," "eva ā vandasva," "imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasya," "ud uttamaṃ varuṇa"—these are for the [sacrifice] to Varuṇa.
Thus [are the verses] for the eleven [animal sacrifices].
And those animals which have such deities [follow this rule].

ŚŚS 6.11.1: "indrā nu pūṣaṇā" is for the offering to Indra and Pūṣan; ŚŚS 6.11.2: "somāpūṣaṇā" is for the offering to Soma and Pūṣan; ŚŚS 6.11.3: "saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā" is for the offering to Indra and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 6.11.4: "To the two Nāsatyas"—this is for the [offering] to the Aśvins.
ŚŚS 6.11.5: "Viṣṇo nu kam"—this is for the [offering] to Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 6.11.6: "Rātrī"—this is for the Night.
"Extensive indeed," [is the first verse] of the hymn addressed to Dyāvāpṛthivī. "Desiring wives," [are] the three [verses] beginning with "He has grown strong, the celestial bird.
"Whose law all cattle follow, whose law the waters attend."
"In whose ordinance the Lord of Prosperity is seated, him, Sarasvant, we invoke for protection"—
this is the [verse] for Sarasvant.
Having omitted the fourth verse of the Vaiśvakarman hymn, beginning with "He who [created] all these worlds."
ŚŚS 6.11.10: "ā te pitar" is for the [oblation] dedicated to Rudra; ŚŚS 6.11.11: "ahaṃ rudrebhiḥ" is for the one whose deity is Vāc;

ŚŚS 6.11.12: Three each of the former [verses] are the invitatory verses (*puronuvākyā*) for the omentum, the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and the animal victim; three each of the latter [verses] are the offering verses (*yājyā*).
ŚŚS 6.11.13: Some do not [perform] the animal-cake offering for the *savanīya* sacrifice.
ŚŚS 6.11.14: But the ritual procedure is the logical rule.
ŚŚS 6.11.15: The offerings to Savitṛ and Vāgdevatā are performed in a whisper (*upāṃśu*).
The *manotā* hymn is repeated for the herd of animals.

Having performed the ritual actions for the animal sacrifice at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), beginning with the encircling of the sacrificial post and ending with the omentum (*vapā*), he goes out, touches water in the same manner as before, and [touches] the *cātvāla* pit.
Having paid homage to the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, they proceed to the *sadas*.
Standing in front of the two *havirdhāna* sheds and looking at each of them [in turn], he [addresses] the Āhavanīya fire with:
“Thou art the sovereign, O *kṛśānu*; protect me with thy Rudra-like aspect, O Agni; satisfy me; let there be homage to thee; do not harm me.
The beginning contains the word *raudra* and the conclusion contains the word *udarka*.
ŚŚS 6.12.5: Or [the fire] is without subsequent result.
ŚŚS 6.12.6: Having churned [the fire] with the mantra, "Thou art born from friction, worthy of worship," it is cast into the fire.
ŚŚS 6.12.7: With the mantra, "Thou art the one to be honored in the assembly, O Pavamāna," the stotra is performed.
"Thou art swift-moving, thou art the wind," [with these words] he addresses the *cātvāla* pit;
"Thou art the sage, the preparer of oblations," [with these words] the *śāmitra* fire;
"Thou art the gatherer, the sustainer of all," [with these words] the *utkara* heap.

ŚŚS 6.12.11: Turning to the right, [he recites] "Thou art the pervasive one, the carrier," and approaches the Āgnīdhra fire. ŚŚS 6.12.12: Those about to enter the Sadas touch it from above, saying, "Thou art the back of heaven; do not burn me. ŚŚS 6.12.13: Having touched the two door-posts, they say, "Thou art the two doors of Order; do not burn me."
They go north of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth, those who pass by the hearths from west to east.
[The Adhvaryu addresses] the seat of the Acchāvāka with: "Thou art the swallower, O Sagara.
[He addresses] the hearth of the Hotṛ with: "Thou art the carrier, O bearer of oblations."
"Thou art the protector, thou art the wise one"—this is for the Maitrāvaruṇa. "Thou art Tutha, the all-knowing"—this is for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
"Thou art Uśij, thou art the sage"—this is for the Potṛ.
"Thou art seeking help, thou art the worshipper," [this is] for the Neṣṭṛ;
"Thou art the remover of distress, thou art the remover of poverty," [this is] for the Acchāvāka;
"Thou art pure," [this is for the Agnīdh].
Having looked at the *mārjālīya* with the words, "Thou art the Mārjālīya";
[he looks] at the seat of the Brahman with the words, "Thou art pure, O approachable one";
[and he looks] at the Audumbarī post with the words, "Thou art the abode of Truth, the light of heaven."
"Thou art the ocean, all-pervading," with these words he looks toward the *sadas*.
"Thou art the one-footed goat," with these words [he looks] at the *śālāmukhīyā* fire. "Thou art the serpent of the deep," with these words [he looks] at the *prājahita* fire.
ŚŚS 6.12.27: "Thou art food, the lord of food"—with these words, he performs the cooking for the vow-food.

ŚŚS 6.13.1: [He addresses] all the fires with: "O fires, you are the Sagaras; by your name Sagara, with your fierce aspect, protect me, O fires! Fulfill me! Homage be to you! Do not harm me! ŚŚS 6.13.2:

Having worshipped the sun with: "Thou art the lord of the paths; may it stand well with us today on the path traveled by the gods," the Maitrāvaruṇa and the others, moving northward and excluding the Acchāvāka, enter the Sadas through the eastern door.

ŚŚS 6.13.3: Reciting, "O All-Gods, follow me; O Indra, [grant] the threefold refuge," and "From whatever we fear, O Indra," and "The Lord of the Assembly, the wonderful one," they proceed in front of and to the north of all the *dhiṣṇya* hearths.
ŚŚS 6.13.4: Each [priest] goes first to his own southern *dhiṣṇya* and sits down behind his respective *dhiṣṇya*.
ŚŚS 6.13.5: Having gone to the north of the *sadas*, the *brahmán* enters the *sadas* by the rear door, goes to the south of the *maitrāvaruṇa*’s seat, and sits according to his place.
ŚŚS 6.13.6: They do not exit by the rear door while the *savana* has not yet concluded.
ŚŚS 6.13.7: [They pass] between the *dhiṣṇya* hearths of the Hotṛ and the Maitrāvaruṇa.
Moving in a disordered manner:
6.13.8: To the north of their respective hearths for those who have hearths; 6.13.9:
To the west of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth, facing north.
