ŚŚS 6.13.10: Or [the sacrificial fee] is given to the south of the Mārjālīya fire.
ŚŚS 6.13.11: And they return without turning back.
ŚŚS 6.13.13: The worship of the Sun (ādityopasthāna) does not occur during the night rounds nor during the Āśvina [laud]; it does not occur, it does not occur.
ŚŚS 7.1.1: Having moved forward, they proceed with the *puroḍāśa* cakes belonging to the *savana*s. ŚŚS 7.1.2: "The one accompanied by parched grains" (*dhānāvantaṃ*) is the *puronuvākyā*.
ŚŚS 7.1.3: "Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the lord of the bay horses" (*hotā yakṣad indraṃ harivān*); this is the *praiṣa* for each *savana*, as it has been handed down in the tradition.
ŚŚS 7.1.4: He distributes [the portions] according to the pressing (savana).
ŚŚS 7.1.5: Having extracted [the portion], the Hotṛ sacrifices with that very same [verse], omitting the words "O Hotṛ, sacrifice" (*hotar yaja*).
ŚŚS 7.1.6: "O Agni, enjoy our oblation" (*agne juṣasva no haviḥ*) is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
ŚŚS 7.1.7: At each pressing, [the Adhvaryu] gives the *praisha* calls, beginning with "Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni of the *puroḍāśa*s.
ŚŚS 7.1.8: And the *yājyā* is "O Agni, enjoy the oblation.
ŚŚS 7.2.1: The cups for Indra-Vāyu, Mitra-Varuṇa, and the Aśvins are those dedicated to two deities (*dvidevatya*).
ŚŚS 7.2.2: *vāyav ā yāhi darśata indravāyū ime* (O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one; Indra and Vāyu, these... are the two invitatory verses (*puronuvākyā*) for the cup belonging to Indra and Vāyu.

ŚŚS 7.2.3: *hotā yakṣad vāyum*, *hotā yakṣad indravāyū* (Let the Hotṛ worship Vāyu; let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Vāyu) are the two directions for the offering (*praiṣa*). ŚŚS 7.2.4: *agram piba śatena naḥ* (Drink the first portion with a hundred [blessings] for us) is the offering verse (*yājyā*).
"O Mitra and Varuṇa, this [is for you]" is the *puronuvākyā* for the offering to Mitra and Varuṇa; "The Hotṛ shall worship Mitra and Varuṇa" is the *praiṣa*;
"Being praised by Jamadagni" is the *yājyā*.
ŚŚS 7.2.8: "prātar.yujaḥ" is the puronuvākyā for the offering to the Aśvins;
ŚŚS 7.2.9: "hotā yakṣad aśvinā" is the *praisha*;
ŚŚS 7.2.10: "vāvṛdhānā" is the yājyā.
ŚŚS 7.2.11: He recites the invitatory verses (*puronuvākyā*) and the calls for the offering (*praisha*) for the two-deity cups without taking breath.
ŚŚS 7.2.12: Likewise, he performs the sacrifice.
ŚŚS 7.2.13: For the cup dedicated to Indra and Vāyu, there are two invitatory verses with separate *praṇava* syllables.

ŚŚS 7.2.14: When there is a separate *vaṣaṭ*-call for the *yājyā*, [the following applies]. ŚŚS 7.2.15: The silent recitation (*japa*) of the *ye yajāmahe* formula and the subsequent consecration (*anumantraṇa*) are performed once at the beginning.

ŚŚS 7.3.1: Having received the cup for Indra and Vāyu with the mantra "May the Vasu, the possessor of much wealth, come," and having placed it on the broad right [side], one should neither cover it nor look at it until the remnants of the cups for the dual deities have been poured out.

ŚŚS 7.3.2: Having received the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa with the formula, "May the Wealth-bringer come; may the Wealth-finder [come]," and having carried it to the south past the cup for Indra and Vāyu, he places it to the south-west.

ŚŚS 7.3.3: Having received the cup for the Aśvins with the formula, "May the Wealth-bringer come; may the Wealth-uniter [come]," and having carried it to the south past the two preceding cups, he places it to the north-west.

ŚŚS 7.3.4: At all *soma*-offering *yajyā* verses, excluding the dual-deity offerings and the seasonal offerings (*ṛtuyāja*), the *anuvashatkāra* is performed with the formula, "O Agni, enjoy the *soma*," as well as for the cup for Āditya, the cup for Savitṛ, and the cup for the Patnīvats.
ŚŚS 7.3.5: The offering for the Pātnīvata [cup] is performed in a whisper.
ŚŚS 7.4.1: When the call "For those being lifted" has been made, [the Hotṛ recites] "May the bay horses bring you hither" (ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ) as the hymn for the cups being lifted.
ŚŚS 7.4.2: "Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra for the morning pressing"—this is the formal command (praiṣa).
ŚŚS 7.4.3: He offers with the mantra, "This sweet Soma is for thee.

ŚŚS 7.4.4: Having looked at the *hotṛ*’s cup with the words, "Thee, who beholdest men, I, who behold men, gaze upon," and having received it with the words, "Thee, who bestowest vigor, I, who bestow vigor, receive," he touches his chest and [the cups] of the two deities (*dvidevatya*).
ŚŚS 7.4.5: The *hotraka*s offer the cups that have been refilled.
"Mitram vayam" is for the Maitrāvaruṇa;
"Indra tvā vṛṣabham" is for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin;
"Maruto yasya" is for the Potṛ.
ŚŚS 7.4.9: The Neṣṭṛ [recites] "agne patnīḥ.
ŚŚS 7.4.10: The Āgnīdhra [recites] "ukṣann annāya.
ŚŚS 7.4.11: When [the Adhvaryu] says "ayāḷ agnīd," the Āgnīdhra responds "ayāḷ."
ŚŚS 7.4.12: "May he who will cause us to drink Soma do what is auspicious," says the Hotṛ.
ŚŚS 7.4.13: Those about to consume the Soma, desiring permission from one another, invite each other with the words, "O performer of the sacrifice, grant me your invitation by name.
ŚŚS 7.4.14: The one who utters the *vaṣaṭ* first consumes [the Soma].

ŚŚS 7.4.15: He pours the remnant of the cups for the dual deities that has been tasted, as well as the remnants of the Nārāśaṃsa cups, into the *hotṛ*’s goblet with the formula: "Having been offered and tasted, I pour thee in—full of vigor for the gods, full of life for myself.

ŚŚS 7.4.16: There is a double pouring of the remnant of the cup for Indra and Vāyu; there the mantra is repeated. ŚŚS 7.4.17: And there is no release [of the goblet] for the cups for the dual deities until the pouring out of the remnant.

ŚŚS 7.5.1: Having taken up the cup for Indra and Vāyu with the mantra, "Here is wealth, O Purūvasu," and having recited, "Vāyu and Indra have invited me together with breath and together with luster; I am invited by them together with breath and together with luster," he consumes it. Then, having taken it up again with the mantra used for taking up, he consumes it again with the mantra used for consuming.
ŚŚS 7.5.2: Having taken up the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa with the mantra, "Here is wealth, O Vidadvasu."

Having consumed [the draught] with the formula: "Mitra and Varuṇa are invited together with sight, together with splendor; of those two, I am invited together with sight, together with splendor," he should carry the cup of the Aśvins around his head from left to right, look at it, carry it back around, look at it again, and then hold up the cup of the Aśvins with the formula: "Here is wealth, the gatherer of wealth. (ŚŚS 7.5.3–5)

ŚŚS 7.5.6: Having consumed [the draught] with the formula, "The two divine Aśvins have been invited together with hearing and together with luster; may I be invited of them together with hearing and together with luster," he touches water.
ŚŚS 7.5.7: Having touched water, he invokes the *iḍā*.
ŚŚS 7.5.8: They lift up the cups.
ŚŚS 7.5.9: He takes hold of the *hotṛ*'s cup.
ŚŚS 7.5.10: In all cases, there is no physical contact with the Soma due to the coating of clarified butter.
ŚŚS 7.5.11: Having invoked one another, they consume the portions that have been set forth.
"May I consume thee for splendor and for Vedic luster," is the mantra for consumption at the morning pressing;
"May I consume thee for vigor and for sensory power," is [the mantra] at the midday pressing;
"May I consume thee for progeny and for nourishment," is [the mantra] at the third pressing.
Having consumed [the portion] with the formula "Be auspicious for our heart," he touches his chest.
Having placed the cups in his left hand, they cause them to swell with the right hand using the swelling formula, "Swell up;
may [the drops] gather," at the morning pressing.
ŚŚS 7.5.18: With the verse "sam te payāṃsi," they cause the two [cups] following [the first] to swell. ŚŚS 7.5.19: They cause the [cups] that have been set forth to swell.
ŚŚS 7.5.20: [This applies] also to the clarified butter and the Marutvatīya cup.
ŚŚS 7.5.21: [The Nārāśaṃsa cups are consumed] at the Ājya and Prauga [śastras], at the Niṣkevalya and Marutvatīya [śastras], and at the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].

ŚŚS 7.5.22: "Thou art the divine Narāśaṃsa; that which is thy sacrificial essence, the light of heaven—of that which has been consumed by the *ūma* fathers, and of which thou hast been invited, I, being invited, partake. This is the mantra for consuming the Nārāśaṃsa cups at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*).
ŚŚS 7.5.23: At the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), "by the *ūrva*s" is the modification.
ŚŚS 7.5.24: [The recitation] with the *kāvyas* occurs at the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*). ŚŚS 7.6.1:

Addressed with the words "O Acchāvāka, sit down," the Acchāvāka sits down to the east of the *sadas* and to the north of the path (*sruti*). Having taken up the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and being addressed with the words "O Acchāvāka, speak! he recites three verses beginning with "Toward Agni for your protection" (*acchā vo agnim avase*). ŚŚS 7.6.2: [He recites] the *nigada* containing the *praṇava*.

"O Sacrificer, Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Agnīdh, Brahman, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Upavaktṛ: impel for food, conquer for strength! Let your kinsmen bow down, let those who are not your kinsmen bow down; let your rivals be defeated on the march; you shall conquer.

You shall conquer the non-attacking and the attacking. May Indra hear you, may Agni hear you! Having set forth, speak of the Soma to Indra and Agni. O Brāhmaṇas, call us Brāhmaṇas hither! Thus [he says].
ŚŚS 7.6.4: "This Brahmin desires an invitation," says the Adhvaryu, or "the Acchāvāka. [The other replies: "O Hotṛ, invite him! ŚŚS 7.6.5:

The Hotṛ invites him. ŚŚS 7.6.6: "One of you two has responded; the sacrificer, pressing the Soma, has grasped the hymn. And the Upavaktṛ has established himself. And our cows have been invited. And [I] am invited"—thus [he speaks] while about to be invited.
ŚŚS 7.6.7: Or [he recites] "And may our cows be summoned" (*uta no gāva upahūtāḥ*), at which point he who was not previously invited [should respond].
ŚŚS 7.6.8: The Acchāvāka, though uninvited, should run after [the Hotṛ] as far as he is able, saying "Turn back! (*nivartadhvam*) at the end of the hymn (*sūkta*). ŚŚS 7.6.9:
Or the Hotṛ, having invited the Acchāvāka in return, [recites the response].
When [the Adhvaryu] says, "For him who is being led up," the Acchāvāka responds with "To him who desires to drink" and recites the *sūktavāka*.
He performs the offering with the verse beginning, "With those who come at dawn.

Having consumed [his portion] and handed over the cup, which has been replenished, to the Adhvaryu, he turns to the right, enters the *sadas* by the western door, sits down behind his own *dhiṣṇya* hearth, and eats the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*).

ŚŚS 7.7.4: If he has already crept forward, he should perform the *acchāvākīyā* verse; having gone out by his own irregular path of movement, performed the *bahiṣkarma* for the *acchāvāka*, he performs his own ritual duty.
ŚŚS 7.7.5: But the Hotṛ [performs it] at his own *dhiṣṇya*. ŚŚS 7.7.6: There is an option regarding the *yājyā* verses of the *hotraka*s.
ŚŚS 7.7.7: Having recited [the invitatory verses] at the morning pressing, they sacrifice either verse by half-verse.
ŚŚS 7.7.8: Here they consume the fast-milk (vrata).
ŚŚS 7.7.9: And [they do so] after the ritual attendances (upāsana).
ŚŚS 7.8.1: Then they proceed with the offerings pertaining to the seasons (ṛtujāya).
ŚŚS 7.8.2: "The Hotṛ shall worship Indra from the office of the Hotṛ"—with these *ṛtupraiṣas*, he issues the calls without pausing.
ŚŚS 7.8.3: He performs the sacrifice in that same manner.
ŚŚS 7.8.4: That [verse] with which he gives the *praisha* is the *yājyā*; having extracted it, the Hotṛ says, "Let such-and-such sacrifice.
ŚŚS 7.8.5: Or [he may say], "O Indra, drink the Soma with the *ṛtu* according to Medhātithi.
ŚŚS 7.8.6: Whichever [name] is heard at the end of the *praisha*, that very one sacrifices.
"O Hotṛ, sacrifice this," says the Adhvaryu; "and the Gṛhapati [sacrifice this]," he says;
he sacrifices for those two.
ŚŚS 7.8.10: They consume [the portion] according to the *vaṣaṭ* call. ŚŚS 7.8.11: At the end, the Hotṛ consumes twice.
ŚŚS 7.8.12: He should, as it were, touch [it] and smell it; this applies also in the case of offerings to dual deities.

ŚŚS 7.9.1: When about to recite the *ājya* [śastra], having muttered, “May Father Mātariśvan recite; may the flawless Uśij recite; may Soma, the knower of ways, lead us through the ways; may Bṛhaspati recite the hymns and songs of praise,” he utters the call, “*śoṃsāvo*,” at the beginning of the *śastra* during the morning libation (*prātaḥsavana*). Having called thus, he recites the *śastra* in a low voice and silently. ŚŚS 7.9.2:

Having paused after “Agni is light, light is Agni,” and having paused after “Indra is light, light is Indra,” and having paused after “Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya,” he pauses after each half-verse while reciting the *puroruc*.
Agni is kindled by the gods; Agni is kindled by Manu;
he is the charioteer of the sacrifices.
The invincible Hotṛ;
the swift bearer of oblations;
may the god bring the gods hither.
"May Agni the god sacrifice to the gods; may he, Jātavedas, perform the rites. "To the god... and so forth is the *ājya* [laud].
Of that, the first half-verse is recited foot by foot.
And [this applies] to the Marutvatīya and Vaiśvadeva [śastras].

Having recited the remainder of the hymn (*sūkta-śeṣa*), having called [the Agnīdh], and having performed the concluding verse (*paridhāna*) with the final [verse], he mutters the *uktha-vīrya*: "Bhā vibhā uṣāḥ svar jyotiḥ; for the sake of fame, the *uktha* has been spoken to you.
At all the *śastra-yājyās*, the Adhvaryu says: "O reciter of the *uktha* (*ukthaśas*)."
He performs the *yajñā* with the verse beginning "agna indraś ca.
When the *ājya* chant has concluded, they chant the *stotra*.
Having called out after the final *pratīhāra* of the *śastra*s that possess a *stotra*, he says, "This is for those who have *stotras*," and they recite the *śastra*s.
ŚŚS 7.10.3: Between the *prauga* and the *mādhucchandasa* triads, they insert verses; these are called *puroruc*s. ŚŚS 7.10.4: Before them, there is the *āhāva*.
ŚŚS 7.10.5: And [the *āhāva* is also placed] before the *paridhānīyā*.
The Vaiśvadeva [section] consists of six feet. In it, one pauses after every two [feet] and chants the *praṇava* after the next two. Regarding the Sārasvata [section], there is an option.
One may recite it or not;
however, the *āhāva* is obligatory.
ŚŚS 7.10.9: "Vāyu, who goes at the head, the delighter of the sacrifice, has come together with the mind to the sacrifice."
"May Śiva [come] with auspicious thousands.
Having recited this once, he recites three times the first of the three verses beginning with "O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one," and [the verse]:
"O golden-pathed heroes, O divine lords, for our protection."
"Vāyu and Indra, the two of excellent sacrifice.
"O Indra and Vāyu, these..."—these three [verses]. "In the assemblies of the two sages, through the power of wisdom in the house of skill... ŚŚS 7.10.11.
"O you two who destroy enemies, come to the place of assembly; we invoke Mitra"—these are three verses.
"O two divine Adhvaryus, come on a chariot with a sun-bright skin."
"Anoint the sacrifice with honey,
O Aśvins, [and bestow] nourishing foods upon the sacrificer"— these are the three [verses].
"Indra is most gladdened by hymns, the lord of spoils and of strength."
"Harivān, the friend of the sons," "O Indra, come, O you of brilliant luster"— these three [verses];
"We invoke all the gods, being of one accord at this sacrifice."
"Then the divine gods came to this sacrifice with their divine thought—
those who are the makers of the body of the sacrifice, all for the drinking of Soma; 'the protectors, the sustainers of the people'— these three [verses]."
"Of all voices, I [choose] the goddess Vāc, the well-adorned one, at this sacrifice;
we invoke Sarasvatī.
Having performed the concluding rite (*paridhāna*) with the last of these three verses beginning with "May the purifying Sarasvatī [be ours]," he mutters the *ukthavīrya*: "Quicken my speech."
Satisfy my breath; protect my sight;
favor my hearing.
Bestow color upon me;
protect my body;
grant me glory.
"A hymn has been recited for you, O Ghoṣa"—thus [the Adhvaryu says].
"With all [the gods], [I offer] the Soma-mead"—with these words he performs the *yajyā*.
The *stotriya* and *anurūpa* stanzas consist of triplets, excluding the *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 7.11.2: *ā no mitrā varuṇā gantam* and *naḥ* [are] the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 7.11.3: *pra vo mitrāya* is the opening of the *uktha*.
ŚŚS 7.11.4: Having concluded with the last of the nine verses beginning with *pra mitrayoḥ*, he performs the *yajyā* with *upa naḥ sutam ā gatam*.

ŚŚS 7.12.1: "ā yāhi suṣuma" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. ŚŚS 7.12.2: The remainder of the hymn constitutes the *ukthamukha*, excluding the final verse. ŚŚS 7.12.3: "indra tvā vṛṣabham."
Having concluded with the last of the three verses beginning with *ud gha it abhi*, he performs the offering with the verse *indra kratuvidam*.
For the Acchāvāka, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* are the two verses beginning with *indra agnī ā gatam sutam*.
The remainder of the hymn constitutes the *ukthamukha*.
ŚŚS 7.13.3: "O Indra and Agni, I invoke you here"—these five [verses]. ŚŚS 7.13.4:
Having concluded with the last of the nine verses beginning with "This prayer of yours," he performs the *yajñayājyā* with "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [soma].
ŚŚS 7.14.1: For the *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha* [stotra], the *stotriya* verses are "We [praise] Mitra," "Indra indeed," "The singers," and "O Indra and Agni."

ŚŚS 7.14.2: The Acchāvāka performs the *stotriya* and the *anurūpa* [verses] belonging to the *rāthantara* [sāman]. ŚŚS 7.14.3: The *anurūpa* serves as the opening of the *śastra*. ŚŚS 7.14.4: The *hotraka*s have four calls for the *āhāva*.
ŚŚS 7.14.5: And the Hotṛ [recites] during the additional hymns (atiriktoktha).

ŚŚS 7.14.6: [He recites] for the Stotriya and the Anurūpa, and that which follows after the Anurūpa up to the Paridhānīyā. ŚŚS 7.14.7: The Pragātha immediately following the Anurūpa; after that, at the midday pressing, is the fifth [laud].
ŚŚS 7.14.8: [The procedure] for all [the priests] at night begins from the opening of the *uktha*.
ŚŚS 7.14.9: When the *adhvaryu* says, "O *praśāstṛ*, give the command," the *praśāstṛ* replies, "Om, creep forth!
ŚŚS 7.14.10: Turning to the right, they creep out through the western door; the *brahmā* [creeps out] to the north of the *udumbara* post and to the south [of the others].
ŚŚS 7.14.11: [They go] northward in front of the hall.

ŚŚS 7.14.12: Having crept forward for the midday pressing according to the manner of their exit, they sit down according to their respective seats. ŚŚS 7.15.1: At the beginning of the midday pressing, they press the King (Soma).

ŚŚS 7.15.2: Having entered the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door as the *grāvastut*, standing to the south in front of the southern wheel of the northern *havirdhāna*, and having wrapped the mouth [of the soma-vessel] with the *soma-upanahana*, he—upon hearing the sound of the pressing-stones (*grāva-ghoṣa*)—recites the hymn even though not formally directed to do so, either in half-verses without interruption or without pausing. ŚŚS 7.15.3: "O God Savitṛ, toward you... (RV 6.71.1); "They yoke the mind and they yoke the insights" (RV 5.81.1); "Hither to us, O Indra, [bring] that which is rich in food"; "Bring it hither with your right hand"; "Come near, bring it hither."
ŚŚS 7.15.4: Having praised the first of the three verses beginning with *ā pyāyasva sametu te*—which have been used for the swelling [of the Soma]—one praises two verses of the *Arbuda*.
ŚŚS 7.15.5: Having praised the second [verse], one praises two verses of the *Arbuda*.
ŚŚS 7.15.6: Having praised the third [verse], one praises one verse of the *Arbuda*.

Having recited the verses beginning with "The ten fingers cleanse you" (ŚŚS 7.15.7) and "The ten fingers cleanse this very one," which contain the word *mṛj* (to cleanse), he praises the Soma as it has been cleansed.

Having recited the verses containing the word *kalaśa* (jar), beginning with "The jars have shouted aloud" (ŚŚS 7.15.8) and "O Soma, your juice flows around" (ŚŚS 7.15.9), the second pressing (*sava*) is likewise performed, starting from the verse "It has swelled" (*āpyāyitavatī*). Thus is the second pressing distributed.
The five days beginning with the sixth belong to the Arbuda.
Thus the third pressing is distributed;
the three days beginning with the eleventh belong to the Arbuda.
ŚŚS 7.15.11: On whichever day they should make the sound "bṛhat," saying "the Bṛhat-sāman is being chanted," there [the following applies].
ŚŚS 7.15.12: On the first [day], the sixth [verse is used].
ŚŚS 7.15.13: "When the two strainers are spread out" and "The strainer for you"—these two; and "As the strainer goes apart"—this one.

When the streams are flowing, [he recites] *prāsya dhārāḥ*, *pra dhārā asya*, and *pra te dhārāḥ*. While the cups are being drawn, whichever [verse] he might desire, he restrains with the three verses beginning with *indrāyendo marutvate*.
When the final *graha* has been drawn, having recited the final verse of the *Arbuda*, and having taken the turban, it is discarded.
However, for *satras* and *ahīnas*, this occurs on the final day;
or one may recite the pure *Arbuda* [at that time].
ŚŚS 7.16.1: When the Pavamāna-stotra has been chanted at the midday pressing, they proceed with the Dadhigharma offering, provided that the Pravargya rite has been performed.
ŚŚS 7.16.2: When [the Adhvaryu] says, "O Hotṛ, speak," he recites the first verse of the hymn, beginning with, "Arise, look down!
ŚŚS 7.16.3: When [the Adhvaryu] says, "The oblation is cooked," he recites the second verse of the hymn.

When addressed with the call, "Recite the offering prayer for the curd-milk (dadhigharma)," he recites with the third [verse]. He chants each verse individually without pausing, accompanied by the *praṇava*. He likewise offers the oblation in that same manner.
"O Agni, partake of the curd-mixture (dadhigharma)!"—this is the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*.
"In me be that great sensory power; in me be skill, in me be resolve. May the three-pointed Gharma shine forth together with intention and the mind."
"May we obtain the milking of that [Virāj] together with the light.
This is the mantra for the consumption.
Having performed the ritual with the animal-cake (paśu-puroḍāśa), they proceed from there with the Savanīya cakes.

"Of the midday pressing"—this is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*). "At the midday pressing"—this is for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering. "The god has been pressed"—this is the hymn for the soma being ladled out.
ŚŚS 7.17.4: "Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra for the midday pressing"—this is the *praisha* (direction).
ŚŚS 7.17.5: He recites the offering verse: "Drink the Soma, O fierce one, for whom...
ŚŚS 7.17.6: The second [verse] belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 7.17.7: The third [stotra] belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
ŚŚS 7.17.8: "Come hither" (arvān ehi) is for the Potṛ. ŚŚS 7.17.9: "This Soma is yours" (tava ayaṃ somaḥ) is for the Neṣṭṛ.
ŚŚS 7.17.10: "For Indra, the Somas, known from of old... is for the Acchāvāka. ŚŚS 7.17.11:
"Full is this [cup]... is for the Āgnīdhra. ŚŚS 7.17.12:
There are no dual-deity offerings nor seasonal sacrifices (*ṛtuyāja*) in the two later pressings (*savana*).
ŚŚS 7.17.13: There is no external ritual act for the Acchāvāka.
ŚŚS 7.17.14: Everything else is the same as at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*).
ŚŚS 7.17.15: Having invoked the *iḷā* and having consumed the portions set forth, [the ritual proceeds].
ŚŚS 7.17.16: This is the time for the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 7.17.17: One should give one hundred and twelve cows. ŚŚS 7.17.18: Or, beginning with twenty-one, as many as are available.
"May Varuna give you to me for Agni; may I attain immortality.
Be a giver of life to the donor, and a source of joy to me who receives. With these words, he accepts the gold.
"May Varuna give you to me for Rudra; may I attain immortality."
"O cow, be a giver of joy to me, O acceptor!"—thus [he addresses] the cows.
"May Varuṇa give thee to me for Bṛhaspati; may I attain immortality.
O skin, be a giver of joy to me, O acceptor!"—thus [he addresses] the garment.
"May Varuṇa give you to me for Yama; may I attain immortality.
Be a horse to the giver, a joy to me who receives"—with these words [he addresses] the single-hoofed animal.
"May Varuṇa give you to me for Prajāpati; may I attain immortality."
"O giver, be breath for me; be joy for me who receives," [he says] regarding one thing;
or he says "Om" regarding everything.
He follows with the mantra over a living being: "Who gave? To whom did [he] give? ŚŚS 7.18.6–7.
He touches the other [hand].
Having given [the gift] with the formula, "O you who are rich in honey, given by us, go to the gods; enter the giver," he mutters:
"To Indra accompanied by the Maruts," when so addressed.
ŚŚS 7.19.2: *indra marutvaḥ* is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*).
ŚŚS 7.19.3: *hotā yakṣad indraṃ marutvantam* is the direction for the offering (*praiṣa*).
ŚŚS 7.19.4: He recites the offering verse (*yajati*) with *sajoṣā indra sagaṇa*.
Having consumed that [cup], he recites the Marutvatīya śastra.
At the beginning of the śastra at the midday pressing, the call is "O Adhvaryu, śoṃśāvo!
The call at the morning pressing occurs within the śastra.
Having recited the triplet beginning with *ā tvā rathaṃ yathā ūtaye*, he calls for the response;
having recited the triplet following it, *idaṃ vaso sutaṃ andhaḥ*, he calls for the response;
having recited the *indra-nihava* *pragātha*, *indra nedīya ed ihi*, he calls for the response.

Having recited the *pragātha* addressed to Brahmaṇaspati, beginning with "Now indeed, Brahmaṇaspati" (pra nūnaṃ brahmaṇaspatiḥ), he calls for the response. Having recited one verse, "Agni is the leader" (agnir netā), he calls for the response.
Having recited one verse, "O Soma, with thy mental powers" (tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ), he calls for the response.
Having recited the single verse beginning with *pinvanty apaḥ*, he calls for the response.
Having recited the six verses beginning with *janiṣṭhā ugraḥ*, he calls for the *nivid*.
In this [recitation], the first response (*pratigara*) contains the word *mad*.
ŚŚS 7.19.17: Having recited one [verse] from among those verses that are unequal in number; ŚŚS 7.19.18: [Having recited one] from among those with equal numbers of verses, in the middle;
ŚŚS 7.19.19: Having recited one [verse] from among the triplets.

ŚŚS 7.19.20: At the end of the *sūktavivṛddhi*, [the *āhāva* occurs]. ŚŚS 7.19.21: But at the first [of these], there is the *āhāva*. ŚŚS 7.19.22: Having omitted the last [verses] at the third *savana*.
ŚŚS 7.19.23: He recites the *nivid* verses line by line (*pacchas*).
ŚŚS 7.19.24: At the final word, he utters the *praṇava*.

ŚŚS 7.19.25: Having recited the remainder of the hymn, having called for the response, and having performed the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) with the last [verse], he mutters the *ukthavīrya* formula and performs the *yajati* offering with the verse beginning "ye tvāhihatya."
The *rathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* of the *niṣkevalya-śastra*;
or the *bṛhat*.
For the *rathantara*, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* are the two *pragāthas*: "abhi tvā śūra" and "abhi tvā pūrvapītaye."
"Tvām iddhi havāmahe, tvam hy ehi ceravaḥ"—these are the *bṛhat* verses;
"yad vāvāna" is the *dhāyyā*;
"pibā sutasya rasinaḥ" is the *pragātha* of the *rathantara*.
"May he hear both," [is the verse] for the Bṛhat[-sāman];
"Now, indeed, the heroic deeds of Indra," [is the verse] when the Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha;
"Praise him, indeed," [is the verse] when the Bṛhat is the Pṛṣṭha.
ŚŚS 7.20.10: He should recite the *paridhānīyā* (concluding verse) repeatedly.
ŚŚS 7.20.11: Having murmured the *ukthavīrya*, he performs the *yajyā* with the verse: "Drink the Soma, O Indra; let it exhilarate you. ŚŚS 7.21.1: [This applies] when both *sāmans* are used.
ŚŚS 7.21.2: In the Rathantara-pṛṣṭha [rite], having extracted that Pragātha which precedes the hymn, he recites the source (yoni) of the Bṛhat.
ŚŚS 7.21.3: In the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha [rite], [he recites] the source of the Rathantara.
ŚŚS 7.21.4: In the other concluding rites, [he recites it] after the Sāman-Pragātha.
"This is called the recitation according to the *yoni*.
Kauṣītaki used to say, "One should recite only the *Bṛhat* and the *Rathantara* [verses].
Since the original *Agniṣṭoma* has a limited number of recitations, he therefore extracts a *pragātha*.
The call (āhāva) is for the *stotriya*, for the *anurūpa*, for the *dhāyyā*, for the *pragātha*, for the *sūkta*, for the *nivid*, and for the *paridhānīyā*.
The *nivid* is either "aśvo" or "varo varaḥ.
The *vāmadevya* [sāman] belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 7.22.2: *kayā naś citraḥ* and *kayā tvam na ūtyā* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 7.22.3: *kas tam indra* is the *sāmapragātha*.
ŚŚS 7.22.4: *sadyo ha jātaḥ*.
ŚŚS 7.22.5: "Thus, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, [be] here. ŚŚS 7.22.22:
He performs the *yajati* offering with the verse beginning "Desiring now indeed for us...
ŚŚS 7.23.1: The *naudhasa* [sāman] is for the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*, when the *rathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra].
Śyaita and Bṛhat are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras].
For the *naudhasa* [sāman], the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas* are "tam vo dasmam" and "tat tvā yāmi suvīryam.
For the *śyaita* [sāman], they are "abhi pra vaḥ" and "pra su śrutam."
"ud u tye madhumattamāḥ" is the *sāmapragātha*;
"indraḥ pūrbhit" belongs to the *naudhasa* [sāman];
"asāvi somaḥ puruhūta" belongs to the *śyaita*.
"Ud u brahmāṇi"—this is the same [as before].
"Ṛjīṣī vajrī"—with these words he performs the sacrifice.
The *kāleya* hymn belongs to the Acchāvāka.
ŚŚS 7.24.2: "tarobhir vas taraṇir it siṣāsati"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 7.24.3: "ud inv asya ricyate"—this is the *sāmapragātha*. ŚŚS 7.24.4: "bhūya id vāvṛdhe."
ŚŚS 7.24.5: [He recites] "imām ū ṣu"; ŚŚS 7.24.6: he performs the *yajati* offering with "pibā vardhasva"; ŚŚS 7.25.1:
[This applies] during the *śastra* recitations.
ŚŚS 7.25.2: Generally, it is not as it has been handed down in the traditional recitation.
ŚŚS 7.25.3: When a *bṛhatī* verse precedes and a *kakubh* or *sato-bṛhatī* follows, they call that a *pragātha*.
ŚŚS 7.25.4: In the case of a *bārhata* [pragātha], it consists of a *bṛhatī* as the first verse.
ŚŚS 7.25.5: [The *kākubha* occurs] in the *kakubh* [meter]. ŚŚS 7.25.6:

Having recited the *bṛhatī*, having taken up the last foot of it, having paused with the first [foot] of the following [verse], having chanted forth with the second, having taken up that [second foot], having paused with the third, he chants forth with the last [foot].
ŚŚS 7.25.7: These become three verses: the first is a *bṛhatī*, and the two following are *kakubhs*.
ŚŚS 7.25.8: [The rule applies] to the *bṛhat* and *rathaṃtara* [sāmans].
ŚŚS 7.25.9: And [it applies] to the *hotṛ*-priests wherever these two form the *pṛṣṭha* stotras based on *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 7.25.10: Everywhere [the rule applies] to the *yajñāyajñīya* [sāman].
ŚŚS 7.25.11: And [this applies] to the *indra-nihava* and *brāhmaṇaspatya* verses. ŚŚS 7.25.12: In other cases, [it applies] to the *bārhata* verses.

ŚŚS 7.25.13: Having recited the *bṛhatī*, having twice resumed the last foot and paused, having pronounced the *praṇava* with the first half-verse of the next [verse], having twice resumed the second foot and paused, he pronounces the *praṇava* with the final half-verse.
Those three are *bṛhatīs*.
He takes up the last [verse] as a *kakubh*. He takes up the second [verse] as a *sato bṛhatī*.
Those three are *kakubh* verses,
either because they serve as the *stotriya* or because they serve as the *anurūpa*. The *pragāthas* obtain this characteristic.
The *indra-nihava* verses are the *astotriya*; and the verses addressed to Brāhmaṇaspati as well.
Having paused after two [verses], and having paused after two [more], he chants the *praṇava* with one [verse] of the *paṅkti* type.
[This applies] to *apcchas*, *triṣṭubh*, *jagatī*, *akṣarapaṅkti*, and *dvipadā* verses.
(ŚŚS 7.26.4) The second and the fourth [pādas] are accompanied by the *praṇava*.

(ŚŚS 7.26.5) However, those which consist of five pādas—whether in a *triṣṭubh*-predominant or *jagatī*-predominant [verse], or where there may be an additional pāda—one should combine them there; for there is no separation of one pāda from another pāda. (ŚŚS 7.26.6)

ŚŚS 7.26.7: [The *uttamā* verses are] at the *apunaḥpada* [stage]. ŚŚS 7.26.8: Having paused after two [verses], having paused after two, he chants the *praṇava* after two [verses] for the six *punar-pada* verses. ŚŚS 7.26.9: Having paused after two [verses], he chants the *praṇava* after one [verse] for the *apunar-pada* verses; having paused after one, [he chants the *praṇava* after the next].
The eight-syllable [verse] is to be chanted with the *praṇava*. Having made a pause after one [foot], he chants the *praṇava* over seven feet; having made a pause after two, he chants it over two.
In the first rounds of the night, they repeat the first quarters of the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses in the *gāyatrī* meter.
In the middle-middle [stomas], [the verses are recited] by half-verses; in the highest-highest [stomas], [they are recited] by whole verses;
or the morning pressing may be performed by half-verses.
ŚŚS 7.26.16: Having omitted the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 7.27.1: The three-footed *gāyatrī*. ŚŚS 7.27.2: The *uṣṇih*.
ŚŚS 7.27.3: Pura-uṣṇih;
ŚŚS 7.27.4: Kakubh; ŚŚS 7.27.5: Virāj with the [Kakubh] preceding.
ŚŚS 7.27.6: Virāj with four syllables in the second foot;
ŚŚS 7.27.7: Bṛhatī; ŚŚS 7.27.8: Sato-bṛhatī.
Jagatī; Anuṣṭubh; and Triṣṭubh.
ŚŚS 7.27.12: [The *pañcapaṅkti* has five feet.
ŚŚS 7.27.13: [The *ṣaṭpadā* and *saptapadā* are types of] *aticchandas*.
ŚŚS 7.27.14: "sa hi śardho na mārutam" consists of eight [syllables].
ŚŚS 7.27.15: There are two [syllables] for each of the two-footed [verses].
ŚŚS 7.27.16: These generally consist of eight syllables.
ŚŚS 7.27.17: That of the Jagatī consists of twelve syllables.
And the third [verse] consists of an uṣṇih and a bṛhatī;
the first and third [verses] consist of a sato-bṛhatī;
and the middle [verse] consists of a kakubh.
ŚŚS 7.27.21: The first [verse] is a purauṣṇih.
ŚŚS 7.27.22: Eleven syllables belong to the triṣṭubh and virāj meters.
ŚŚS 7.27.27: Of the subsequent [verse], there are ten syllables.
They also call that the *akṣarapaṅkti*. A *padapaṅkti* consists of five feet of five syllables each.
There are also six [syllables] of eight syllables belonging to the *jagatī*.
ŚŚS 7.27.27: When there is a deficiency of one or two [syllables], it is *nicṛt*. ŚŚS 7.27.28: When there is an excess, it is *bhurik*.
ŚŚS 7.27.29: Having completed [the verse] by means of a quarter-part of the *āhārya* verse, they are equalized; they are perfected by that quarter-part.
Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī—this is the sequence of the meters, beginning with twenty-four syllables and increasing by four syllables each. ŚŚS 8.1.1:
Just as [they proceed] for the midday pressing, so do they proceed after the midday pressing.
ŚŚS 8.1.2: At the beginning of the third pressing, they perform the rite with the Āditya cup.
ŚŚS 8.1.3: "To the Ādityas," thus it is said.
ŚŚS 8.1.4: "With the favor of the Ādityas," is the *puronuvākyā*.
ŚŚS 8.1.5: "Let the Hotṛ worship the Ādityas," is the *praiṣa* (direction).
ŚŚS 8.1.6: He performs the sacrifice with the formula, "The Ādityas are Aditi.
ŚŚS 8.1.7: He does not look at the oblation, nor does he consume it.
ŚŚS 8.1.8: And [this applies] also to the Sāvitra cup.

When the Pavamāna has been chanted with the Ārbhava [Sūkta], having performed the rites for the animal sacrifice (pauśakarma) ending with the *iḍā* from the *manotā* onwards, they proceed with the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) belonging to the third pressing.
ŚŚS 8.2.1: "O Agni, at the third pressing... is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*).
ŚŚS 8.2.2: "O Agni, at the third pressing... is the verse for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
ŚŚS 8.2.3: "He has approached here"—this is the *unnīyamānasūkta* (the hymn recited while the soma is being ladled out).
ŚŚS 8.2.4: "Let the Hotṛ worship Indra at the third pressing"—this is the *praiṣa* (the call for the offering).
ŚŚS 8.2.5: "O Indra, with the Ṛbhus who possess strength"—with these words he performs the *yajati* (the formal sacrifice).
ŚŚS 8.2.6: "O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed [juice]"—thus the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 8.2.7: "And Indra [drinks] the Soma"—thus the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
ŚŚS 8.2.8: "May they bring you hither"—thus the Potṛ.
ŚŚS 8.2.9: "As if at home," says the Neṣṭṛ.
ŚŚS 8.2.10: "O Indra and Viṣṇu, drink," says the Acchāvāka.
ŚŚS 8.2.11: "This hymn," says the Āgnīdhra.
ŚŚS 8.2.12: The rest is the same as the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana).

ŚŚS 8.2.13: Having invoked the *iḷā* and consumed the portions set forth (*prasthita*), they cast down three balls (*piṇḍa*) each to the south from the *nārāśaṃsa* vessels—those containing the *puroḍāśa* mixed with the parched grain (*parivāpa*)—according to their respective goblets (*camasa*), saying for each ball: "O Fathers, rejoice here; O Fathers, come to your respective portions. ŚŚS 8.3.1: [The Adhvaryu] is addressed with the words, "To the god Savitṛ... and so on.
ŚŚS 8.3.2: "The god has come" is the *puronuvākyā*.
ŚŚS 8.3.3: "Let the Hotṛ worship the god Savitṛ" is the *praiṣa*.
ŚŚS 8.3.4: "The domestic god Savitṛ, the most excellent, bestowing treasure upon the fathers in their lifespan."
"Let him drink the Soma; the sacrifices have gladdened him; even Parijman rejoices in his ordinance. Thus he recites the offering verse.
"O Adhvaryu, śośoṃsāvaḥ!"—this is the call at the beginning of the *śastra* at the third pressing when there is an *uktha*.
At the morning pressing, it occurs within the *śastra*.
ŚŚS 8.3.7: And [this applies] from the *ṣoḍaśin* onwards.
ŚŚS 8.3.8: The two triplets, "tat savitur vṛṇīmahe" and "adyā no deva savitaḥ," are the introductory (*pratipad*) and the following (*anucara*) verses for the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra].
ŚŚS 8.3.9: "abhūd deva" is the verse dedicated to Savitṛ (*sāvitra*).

ŚŚS 8.3.10: "With one and with ten, O self-existent one; with two and with twenty for our sacrifice; with three and with thirty yoked teams you carry [the oblation], O Vāyu—unharness them here. ŚŚS 8.3.11:
"To Heaven and Earth, who increase the *ṛta* through sacrifices..."—this is the hymn to Heaven and Earth (*dyāvāpṛthivīya*).
ŚŚS 8.3.12: In this [section], the response (*pratigara*) contains the word *mad*.
ŚŚS 8.3.13: "surūpakṛtnu" is a single verse.
ŚŚS 8.3.14: "takṣan ratham" is the Ārbhava [laud].
ŚŚS 8.3.15: "This Vena, from whom the mother [is born], even so the father"—these are the *ekapātinī* verses.
ŚŚS 8.3.16: Having recited the *nivid* after the last verse of the *vaiśvadeva* hymn, namely "ā no bhadraḥ.
ŚŚS 8.3.17: The final verse is the *paridhānīyā*.
ŚŚS 8.3.18: A third time, he recites by quarters and twice by half-verses.
ŚŚS 8.3.19: Having murmured the *ukthavīrya*, he performs the *yajati* sacrifice with the verse, "O All-Gods, hear this.
ŚŚS 8.4.1: Being addressed with "Recite the offering for the ghee," he performs the silent (*upāṃśu*) sacrifice with the verse, "The ghee has been sprinkled."
When addressed with "Sacrifice for the Soma," he recites: "O Soma, [be] with the fathers. When addressed with "Sacrifice for the ghee," [he recites]:
"O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling."
"O thou whose source is ghee, drink [the ghee]; further, further promote the lord of the sacrifice"—with these words he sacrifices in a whisper;
there is an option regarding the parījyā offering.
ŚŚS 8.4.5: Having looked at the *saumya* [oblation], the Hotṛ touches the clarified butter with his fingers.
ŚŚS 8.4.6: With the formula, "Thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye," he rubs his two eyes. ŚŚS 8.5.1:
Being addressed by the Agnīdh, "Recite the offering prayer for the Pātnīvata," he recites the offering prayer in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) with the verse, "With these, O Agni, on the same chariot..."
ŚŚS 8.5.2: Without consuming [the draught], having taken the cup, he enters the *sadas* by the eastern door.
ŚŚS 8.5.3: Having sat down close to the *neṣṭṛ* from the north, or ŚŚS 8.5.4: or upon his lap.
Having said, "O Neṣṭṛ,
invite [us]," and having consumed [the portion] and sipped water,
he returns by the way he came.
ŚŚS 8.6.1: The *yajñāyajñīya* is the stotra for the *āgnimāruta* [śastra].
ŚŚS 8.6.2: "To Vaiśvānara of broad radiance" (*vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase*) is the *vaiśvānarīya*.
ŚŚS 8.6.3: "Come to us, O Father" (*ā te pitaḥ*) is a single verse.
"Pratvakṣasaḥ" is for the Maruts.
"Yajñā-yajñā vo agnaye" and "Devo vo draviṇodāḥ" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas* for the *yajñāyajñīya*.
"Pratavyasīm" is for the *jātavedasīya*.
ŚŚS 8.6.7: The three verses beginning with *āpo hi ṣṭha*.
ŚŚS 8.6.8: One verse beginning with *uta no ahiḥ budhnyaḥ śṛṇotu*.
ŚŚS 8.6.9: Two verses beginning with *devānām patnīḥ*.
ŚŚS 8.6.10: "rākām aham" and so forth—these two [verses].
ŚŚS 8.6.11: "avidad dakṣam"—these three *akṣarapaṅkti* verses. ŚŚS 8.6.12: "ud īratām" and so forth—these three verses addressed to the ancestors (*paitrya*).
ŚŚS 8.6.13: "imaṃ yama mātali kavyair aṅgirobhiḥ"—this is the [sūkta] addressed to Yama.
ŚŚS 8.6.14: There are three verses beginning with *svāduṣkiliya*.
ŚŚS 8.6.15: In these, the response (*pratigara*) contains the word *mad*.
ŚŚS 8.6.16: *yayor ojasā*, *viṣṇor nu kam*, and *tantum tanvan* are the *ekapātinī* verses.
ŚŚS 8.6.17: Having recited *evā na indro maghavā* as the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) and having murmured the *ukthavīrya*, he performs the offering with *agne marudbhiḥ śubhayadbhiḥ*.
ŚŚS 8.7.1: The first *nivid* belongs to the *marutvatīya* śastra.
ŚŚS 8.7.2: The second [verse] belongs to the Niṣkevalya;
ŚŚS 8.7.3: Those beginning with the third belong to the Vaiśvadeva and Āgnimāruta; ŚŚS 8.7.4:
The last [verse] belongs to the Ṣoḍaśin.
ŚŚS 8.7.5: There are as many *nivid*s as there are *sūkta*s.
ŚŚS 8.7.6: Before each *sūkta*, there is an *āhāva*. ŚŚS 8.7.7: And there is a *nivid* for each *nivid*.
And for each [verse] that falls alone;
and for the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*);
and for the introductory verse (*pratipad*) and the following verse (*anucara*) in the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra].
ŚŚS 8.7.11: [The rule applies] to the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses of the *āgnimāruta* laud; ŚŚS 8.7.12:
to the *āpo hi ṣṭhā* verses;
ŚŚS 8.7.13: to the verses dedicated to the wives of the gods (*devānām patnī*).
And of the *rākā* verses;
of the *akṣarapaṅkti* meters;
and of those belonging to the ancestors (*paitrī*).
ŚŚS 8.7.17: [The stotras] of the Yāmyas;
ŚŚS 8.7.18: and those of the Svāduṣkilīyas;
ŚŚS 8.7.19: the Vaiśvadeva śastra is recited with the *viyat* (unfilled) verses.

ŚŚS 8.7.20: Having omitted the *āpo hi ṣṭhā* verses immediately preceding the *āgnimāruta* [śastra], ŚŚS 8.7.21: having set down the Soma cups in the waters and performed the animal sacrifice rites beginning with the *anuyāja* offerings and ending with the *śamyu*, they proceed with the *hāriyojana* cup.
ŚŚS 8.8.1: "tiṣṭhā su kam" is the *puronuvākyā*.
ŚŚS 8.8.2: "O Indra, eat the roasted grains with the Soma-juices" is the *praiṣa* (direction).
ŚŚS 8.8.3: "I yoke you" is the *yājyā* (offering verse).
ŚŚS 8.8.4: "O Agni, partake of the roasted grains with the Soma-juices" is the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*.
"Of Soma, O Agni," or "Of Soma, O Agni.

Having consumed the *prāṇabhakṣa* (breath-consumptions) with the formula: "O divine Soma, who art washed in the waters, of thee who art praised by men, lauded by hymns, recited with *ukthas*, and offered with *yajus*-formulas—of that portion which is the gain of horses, the gain of cattle, of thee who art invited, I, being invited, partake," they distribute the parched grains (*dhānās*).

ŚŚS 8.8.7: The *hotṛ* should desire to obtain the most abundant [portion]. ŚŚS 8.8.9: Having looked at the *dhiṣṇya* hearths with the verse, "As you have come here, O Vasus," they proceed north of the *āgnīdhrīya* toward the *āhavanīya*.

ŚŚS 8.8.10: At the *āgnīdhrīya*, they offer expiatory oblations (*prāyaścittāhutīḥ*) with the formulas: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! O Agni, may you be our nearest; O Agni, may you be ours; that [be] for Varuṇa; O Mitra and Varuṇa."
"Fill us with offspring and cattle until the full moon," he says; having scattered parched grains upon the edge of the ashes of the Āhavanīya fire, they place five wood-shavings each.

"Thou art the expiation for sin committed against oneself; thou art the expiation for sin committed against men; thou art the expiation for sin committed against the ancestors; thou art the expiation for sin committed against the gods; whatever sin I have committed knowingly and whatever I have committed unknowingly—thou art the expiation for all that. Thus [he says].

Having turned to the left and moved to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, they sit down behind the waters, each according to their cup, having placed the strainers [into them], and perform the ritual action with the formula:
"The waters have united with the waters; the plants with their sap. Let the wealthy ones be mixed with the moving ones; let the honey-sweet ones be mixed with the honey-sweet ones."
"ŚŚS 8.9.3: 'We have been invited together.

ŚŚS 8.9.4: Having consumed the breath-consumptions (*prāṇabhakṣa*) with the formula, 'O divine Soma, of thee who art shaken in the waters, of that portion which finds the mind, which is the gain of horses and the gain of cattle—of thee, being invited, I, invited, partake,' ŚŚS 8.9.5:
he pours them out toward the east or the north with the verse, 'Toward this [Soma] of yours, by whose power...'"
Having consecrated [the water] with the mantra "samudraṃ vaḥ" (ŚŚS 8.9.6),
and having touched his chest with the four verses beginning with "śaṃ no devīḥ" (ŚŚS 8.9.7),
the touching of the vital breaths and the wiping of the mouth are performed in the same manner as before.
ŚŚS 8.9.9: Having turned to the right and consumed curds at the Āgnīdhrīya fire according to the procedure for consuming curds;
ŚŚS 8.9.10: Having completed the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings and once the Samiṣṭayajus oblations have been offered, he proceeds to the Avabhṛtha bath.
ŚŚS 8.10.1a: "May my sensory power return to me; may my self, wealth, and sacred knowledge return."
"Furthermore, let the fires of the *dhiṣṇyas* remain here in their respective places," [he says].

Having thus looked at the *dhiṣṇya* fires, the sacrificer—or, alternatively, the officiating priests—should look at them either at this point or when the *anūbandhyā* sacrifice has been completed, reciting:
"Both the young sages, who bestow truth through the law of truth, lords of the law of truth—we dissolve our bonds of friendship. Thus.
Chanting "For broad indeed is the King," they proceed;
all of them reach the *nidhana* of the *sāman*.
Having placed their foot in the water while reciting, "Homage to Varuṇa! The noose of Varuṇa is not cast," they conclude.
ŚŚS 8.11.1: The Vāruṇī sacrifice. ŚŚS 8.11.2:
It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice. ŚŚS 8.11.3:
The two verses containing the word *ap* (water)—namely, "O Agni, in the waters" and "O Soma, in the waters"—are used [as the invitatory and offering verses].
Standing, he performs the sacrifice. [He recites:

"O Varuṇa, lift up [the highest bond]; away from us, O Varuṇa, let thy wrath depart. "As such, O Agni, be our nearest; thou, O Agni, knowing [the way], [be our nearest] of Varuṇa"—with these words, he addresses Agni and Varuṇa.
He does not recite the *nigada*;
or he may recite it.
He performs the *prayāja* and *anuyāja* offerings excluding the *barhis*.
ŚŚS 8.11.10: [The sacrifice] begins with the *prayāja*s and ends with the *anuyāja*s. ŚŚS 8.11.11: Or it may end with the *sviṣṭakṛt*.
ŚŚS 8.11.12: Or, omitting the two *ājyabhāga*s and the *anuyāja*s.

"By that [power] with which you two created women, by which you touched the *surā*, by which you consecrated the dice, by which you [consecrated] this great earth—O Aśvins, with that glory of yours, consecrate me!
Thus the Hotṛ sprinkles himself.
"With auspicious eyes, I, a mortal, go toward my home. ŚŚS 8.11.14.
Thus the sacrificer approaches.

Having sat down with the formula, "May Pūṣan, even though he possesses a thousand sacrificial fees, sit down here," he places two pieces of fuel on the Āhavanīya fire: the first with the formula, "Thou art the fuel of the gods," and the second silently.
ŚŚS 8.11.16: [The offering] for the wife is performed silently at the Gārhapatya fire.
ŚŚS 8.12.1: The Udayanīyā offering is explained by [the rules of] the Prāyaṇīyā.
ŚŚS 8.12.2: There is an inversion of the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses, with the exception of those for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
He performs the fourth offering to Pathyā Svasti;
the third [offering] is to Savitṛ;
and there is a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa as the Anubandhyā.
ŚŚS 8.12.6: Or [the offering] consists of curdled milk (payasyā).
ŚŚS 8.12.7: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, come to us," "That [is] yours, O Mitra and Varuṇa," "Om, Mitra and Varuṇa"—these are the invitatory verses (puronuvākyās).
ŚŚS 8.12.8: "You two [bestow] garments," "That which is most firm," and "Forth [your] arms"—these are the offering verses (yājyās).
ŚŚS 8.12.10: From the *dīkṣaṇīyā* offering until the conclusion of the *anūbandhyā* sacrifice, he does not make the wife recite over the Veda, nor does he strew [grass] upon it.
ŚŚS 8.12.10: Having made her recite at the *anūbandhyā*, he strews [grass] in front of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth.
ŚŚS 8.12.11a: "Do not harm the waters, do not harm the plants! You are heat; may your heat reach him whom we hate!"
"O King Varuṇa, from every stronghold, release us!
From whatever we have sworn by 'the waters,' by 'the inviolable ones,' or by 'Varuṇa,' from that, O Varuṇa, release us!

Having worshipped with this verse for the *hṛdaya-śūla* (heart-piercing rite), and having touched water with the words, "May the waters and plants be friendly to us," they step out toward the south with the words, "May they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate."
ŚŚS 8.12.12: Or, beginning with the portions of clarified butter (ājyabhāga), there is the curd-mixture (payasyā).
ŚŚS 8.12.13: It is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice (amāvāsyā). ŚŚS 8.12.14:
It concludes with the iḷā-verse, without the nigada-recitation.
ŚŚS 8.13.1: Having moved northward and offered a full oblation with a verse addressed to Viṣṇu, he performs the concluding sacrifice (udavasānīyā).
ŚŚS 8.13.2: It is an offering to Agni.
ŚŚS 8.13.3: It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice.
Furthermore, those [oblations] which are at the re-establishment of the fires belong to the *havis* and the *sviṣṭakṛt*.
(ŚŚS 8.13.4) The sacrifice pertaining to the re-establishment of the fires consists of five potsherds. (ŚŚS 8.13.5) When it has been completed, he offers the evening *agnihotra*. (ŚŚS 8.13.6)

ŚŚS 8.14.1: The morning pressing is performed with a low-pitched voice. ŚŚS 8.14.2: The *prauga* is at a higher pitch than the *ājya*. ŚŚS 8.14.3: The midday pressing is performed with a medium pitch.
ŚŚS 8.14.4: The Niṣkevalya is higher than the Marutvatīya.
ŚŚS 8.14.5: The third pressing is performed with the final [verse].
ŚŚS 8.14.6: The Āgnimāruta is higher than the Vaiśvadeva.
Or he may perform the midday pressing with the highest [tone];
the third pressing with the low tone;
or [the third pressing] with the middle tone.
ŚŚS 8.15.1: From the time he gives the *preṣya* call until its completion, he restrains his speech.
ŚŚS 8.15.2: And from the *āhāva* call until the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*.
ŚŚS 8.15.3: During the *prātar-anuvāka*, the *brahmán* [restrains his speech].
ŚŚS 8.15.4: And having consumed [the portion] until the impulse for the stotra;
ŚŚS 8.15.5: and from the impulse onwards until the secondary vaṣaṭ-call;
ŚŚS 8.15.6: having heard the end of the *atipraiṣa* call, until the carrying away of the *vasatīvarī* waters.

ŚŚS 8.15.7: The oblation for the droplets is performed before the *pavamāna* chants with the verses, "The drop that falls from thee" and "The drop has fallen. ŚŚS 8.15.8: And he follows after those who are moving.
ŚŚS 8.15.9: And so does the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.
ŚŚS 8.15.10: When the fire is being led forward for the fire-altar (agni-citi), he mutters the Apratiratha hymn.
ŚŚS 8.15.11: "To all the quarters, to all the gods on the right, he has gone here.
Drink, O Aśvins, of the honeyed gharma consecrated with Svāhā!"
Thus, following after the Mahāvīra:
"O Aśvins, drink the Gharma that reaches the heart, with your daily aids!
Homage to the weaver of the thread, and to Heaven and Earth!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered:
"The Aśvins have drunk the *gharma*; Heaven and Earth have approved. When the *anu-vaṣaṭ* has been uttered: "May the gifts remain right here."

ŚŚS 8.15.15: That which is not specifically prescribed is the same [as the standard]. Thus ends the Brahman’s ritual duties in the Soma sacrifice. ŚŚS 8.16.1a: May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink of the Soma.
Praised by the Maruts, the host of Maruts,
strengthened by the Maruts, the friend of the Maruts— he whom the gods rejoiced in following.
In the battle for the waters, in the battle against Vṛtra,
in the slaying of Śambara, and in the search for cattle—
[he protected] him who was chanting with secret steps.
In the furthest distance,
he slew Vṛtra and released the waters,
together with the might of the Maruts.
Increasing the primordial sacred words (*brahmāṇi*) with his might, making them unassailable,
he performs service for the gods.
Together with his friends, the Maruts, may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, hear us here; may he drink of the soma here. May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom.
May this Brahman prevail; may this Kṣatra prevail.
May it protect this pressing sacrificer with its wondrous aids, O Wondrous One!
"May he come with his protection, hearing the sacred words.
(ŚŚS 8.16.2) Then follows the *ukthavīrya*:
"The form, the corresponding form, the matching form, the beautiful form—may it be helpful here; for you who hear well, this hymn has been recited for Indra. (ŚŚS 8.16.3)
May the god Indra drink the Soma; he who is the most heroic among those born of one [father], and the strongest among those born of many.
The rider of the bay steeds;
the offspring of Pṛśni;
the wielder of the thunderbolt.
The destroyer of forts; the breaker of forts;
the leader of the waters.
The leader of beings, the destroyer of enemies, far-renowned, the performer of wondrous deeds, and possessed of marvelous power.
May Uśanas Deva be present here;
may Indra, the god, hear us here and drink the Soma here.
"O God, favor this [offering]"—the rest is the same.

ŚŚS 8.17.2: Now follows the *uktha-vīrya* (the power of the *uktha*). ŚŚS 8.17.3: "Thou art the universal ruler; thou art the self-ruler; thou art the far-shining; thou art the king; thou art the overcomer. May we overcome him whom we hate. For thee, who art deaf to [evil], the *uktha* has been recited for Indra. ŚŚS 8.18.1a: "May the god Savitṛ exhilarate himself with Soma."
Golden-handed, fair-tongued, with beautiful arms and lovely fingers; he whose pressings are true three times a day.
She who brought forth the two treasuries of wealth, the two who take delight in the impulse to give birth—
she has brought forth the most excellent gift of Savitṛ.
The milch cow;
the draft-ox that draws the load; the swift racer.
ŚŚS 8.18.1: [He offers] the swift steed.
The victorious one standing upon the chariot;
the wise woman;
the youthful man fit for the assembly.
May the god Savitṛ drive away our supreme affliction, and drive away the one who utters evil.
May he hear us here; may he rejoice here in Soma.
"Forward this [prayer], O God"—the rest is the same.
May Heaven and Earth rejoice in the Soma; may the Father and the Mother, the Cow and the Bull, rejoice.
And Dhanyā and Dhiṣaṇā; and Suretā and Sudughā; and Śambhū and Mayobhū.
Full of vigor and full of milk,
may Heaven and Earth hear this here and be exhilarated by the Soma;
may these two goddesses favor this invocation of the gods with their divine wisdom.
May this sacred power (brahman) prosper; may this ruling power (kṣatra) prosper. May they both protect this pressing sacrificer with their wondrous aids, O Wondrous Ones.

By their deeds they have fair hands;
they are blessed, most wealthy,
and most peaceful.
By their power, they are most powerful; those who fashioned the all-impelling, omniform cow—
they fashioned the cow, and she became omniform.
They woke up, rejoicing together with their wives; they yoked the two bay horses and went toward the gods. After a year, the skillful ones arrived at their share of the sacrifice.
May the Ṛbhus, the gods, hear us here; may they exhilarate themselves here with Soma.
O gods, may you favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought. May this spiritual power (*brahman*) prevail; may this ruling power (*kṣatra*) prevail.
May they protect this sacrificer who presses the soma with their various aids; may they,
being heard, come hither with their protection to our sacred prayers.
May all the gods, the Vaiśvānara deities, great and mighty, rejoice in the Soma.
Those who eat cooked food, who possess guests and offerings, who bring abundance— cook for them, O carriers,
you who have taken your stand upon both heaven and earth.
The waters and the self;
the sacred word (*brahman*) and the ruling power (*kṣatra*);
the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and the altar (*vedi*).
And the sacrifice, and the wide mid-air;
you who have Vāta as your soul and Agni as your messenger,
you who are the three times eleven.
And thirty-three;
and three hundred and three;
and three thousand and three.
So many [are] in the lifting up;
so many in the settling down;
so many are the wives.
So many are the divine powers (gnās),
so many are the adversaries,
and so many are those who bestow gifts.
Therefore, O gods, you are more numerous.
May no god harm you; may I not harm you. I draw forth life.
May all the gods hear this here; may they rejoice here in the soma.
"O gods, this [sacrifice]... etc., is the same [as before]. ŚŚS 8.21.2:
Now follows the *ukthavīrya* (the power of the hymn).

ŚŚS 8.21.3: "Thou art the past; thou art the future; thou art the pervasive; thou art the abundant; thou art Being; thou art the eye; thou art vigor; thou art auspiciousness. For the sake of renown, the hymn has been recited for thee, for Indra, and for the gods."
Agni Vaiśvānara has exhilarated with Soma;
he is the kindler of all the gods,
the eternal divine light.
He who shines for the wise mortals,
gleaming in the former days of heaven,
ageless upon the face of the dawns.
He who shines across the sky and across the earth, and across the vast intermediate space— may he,
the worshipful one, grant protection with his light.
May Agni Vaiśvānara hear us here; may he exhilarate himself here with Soma.
"O God, [favor] this [offering]"—the rest is the same.
(ŚŚS 8.23.1a) May the Maruts, the gods, exhilarate themselves with Soma.
They are well-praising and well-singing; they are hymns and chants, possessing great vital strength;
they are of the nature of the clouds, clothed in rain.
The brilliant ones, sons of Pṛśni, radiant with golden ornaments, powerful,
and eager to grant blessings.
The Maruts, the gods, heroes with unassailable chariots—may they hear us here; may they exhilarate themselves here with Soma.
"O gods, [protect] this..."—the rest is the same.
Agni Jātavedas,
of beautiful countenance and wondrous radiance,
the never-absent master of the house, shall rejoice in the Soma.
Visible even through the darkness,
he who is invoked with offerings of clarified butter,
the one whose armor is thick, and who has spread the sacrifice.
Conquering enemies through dependence, the unconquered one;
O Agni Jātavedas, bestow upon us splendor and power—
let there be praise, let there be praise!
Protect us from distress, O kindler of the flame!
May Agni Jātavedas hear this here; may he rejoice here in the Soma.
"O God, favor this [offering]"—the rest is the same.

Now follows the *uktha-vīrya*: "Thou art splendor; thou art boldness; thou art courageous; thou art impetuous; thou art steadfast; thou art support; thou art sustenance; thou art firm. For the sake of hearing, I have spoken thee; for Indra the *uktha*, for the gods.
"In the exhilaration of this Soma, O singer, may Indra be intoxicated."
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], O singer, Indra slew the serpent;
in the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra slew Vṛtra;
in the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra propped up the sky and spread out the earth.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], O singer, Indra stretched across the mid-air and reached the sun with his celestial [powers].
In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra extended his noble race and struck down the Dāsa race.
In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra caused the waters to swell and quickened those who were sluggish.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra stilled the enraged mountains that were puffing like seers;
in his exhilaration, O singer, Indra set the surge of the waters in motion;
in his exhilaration, O singer, Indra heard [the call] here from the mountain.
"In the exhilaration of this [Soma], O singer, may Indra hear here; here he shall delight in the Soma.

ŚŚS 9.20.32: *hotā yakṣad aśvinā somānām tiroahnānām* is the direction (*praiṣa*).
ŚŚS 9.20.33: Kauṣītaki says that it should be with the *virāj* [metre] alone."
"Or [the verse] beginning with *aśvinā vāyunā*.
ŚŚS 9.21.1: The *bahiṣpavamāna* is in the *trivṛt* stoma.
ŚŚS 9.21.2: And the *saṃdhi-sāman*.
ŚŚS 9.21.3: Five [stotras] beginning with the fifteen-versed;
ŚŚS 9.21.4: And the night [rite];
ŚŚS 9.21.5: Five [stotras] consisting of seventeen verses.
ŚŚS 9.21.6: Five [sets] of twenty-one.
ŚŚS 9.21.7: These are the Jyotis-stomas.
ŚŚS 9.21.8: These same [stomas] belong to the Abhiplava.
ŚŚS 9.22.1: For one who intends to establish the sacred fires but has not yet been initiated, there is a sacrifice (iṣṭi).
ŚŚS 9.22.2: [It is offered] to Agni accompanied by the Brahman, to Agni accompanied by the Kṣatra, and to Agni the sustainer of the Kṣatra.
ŚŚS 9.22.3: It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice (paurṇamāsī-vikāraḥ).
ŚŚS 9.22.4: For Agni accompanied by the *brahman*, [the verses] are "O Brahman, bring [wealth] rich in progeny" and "And the *brahman* for thee, O Jātavedas.
ŚŚS 9.22.5: For the two following [oblations], [the verses] are "Worshipping thee, O Agni, at our sacrifice" and "O Agni, enjoy the oblation with splendor.
ŚŚS 9.22.6: When many [sacrificers] are about to offer, there is the *saṃnivapanīyā* (the rite of collective piling).
For one [sacrificer], there is the Ukhasambharaṇīyā [offering];
ŚŚS 9.23.1: and the animal sacrifice (paśubandha) dedicated to Prajāpati;
ŚŚS 9.23.2: or one dedicated to Vāyu.
ŚŚS 9.23.3: Or [the offering] is for Agni Kāma.
ŚŚS 9.23.4: The five sacrificial animals are the man, the goat, the sheep, the cow, and the horse.
ŚŚS 9.23.5: Or [there may be] a hornless goat.
ŚŚS 9.23.6: Some perform the animal-cake offering for Vāyu at the rite for Prajāpati;
ŚŚS 9.23.7: [they perform] that for Prajāpati at the rite for Vāyu;
ŚŚS 9.23.8: [they perform] that for Vaiśvānara at the rite for Agni.
ŚŚS 9.23.9: For the offering to Prajāpati, the three verses beginning with "hiraṇyagarbha" are the invitatory verses (*puronuvākyā*), and the following ones are the offering verses (*yājyā*).

ŚŚS 9.23.10: [The recitation] is in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). ŚŚS 9.23.11: For the offering to Vāyu, the invitatory verses are "ekayā ca rāye," "nu kivit aṅga," and "pīvoannān"; the offering verse is "pra yābhir yāsi. For the offering to Vāyu, [the invitatory verses are] "pra yābhir yāsi" and "pra vāyum accha."

ŚŚS 9.23.12: “May Vatsa draw your mind hither; for you, O best of Aṅgirases, Agni [is] in the highest abodes”—this is the *puronuvākyā* for the offering to Agni, beginning with “May we today attain you; I praise you. ŚŚS 9.23.13:
When the five [animal sacrifices] are being performed, the animal formulas (*paśu-nigama*) are in the plural, starting from “The earth, the bodies,” and so forth.
ŚŚS 9.23.14: From this point onward, they are in the singular.
The *dīkṣaṇīyā* [offering] consists of three oblations:
one for Agni and Viṣṇu, one for Vaiśvānara, and one for the Ādityas.
"Holding those very Kṣatriyas... (RV 8.51.7).
Or there are five oblations.
The fourth is for Aditi, and the fifth is for Sarasvatī.
Or the Ātithyā consists of five oblations.
The [offerings] for Agni, Indra, Viśve Devas, Bṛhaspati, and Viṣṇu;
reciting softly the verses beginning with "śucim arkaistam śagmāsaḥ," he follows behind.

ŚŚS 9.25.1: When it has been piled and consecrated, [the Adhvaryu] says, "Recite the *agni-uktha*. Having been thus addressed, [the Hotṛ], sitting behind the altar (*citi*), recites the *ājyeya* [laud] silently; he recites it with a silent recitation (*śaṃsa*) without calling for the *śrauṣaṭ*. ŚŚS 9.25.2: Being addressed [by the Adhvaryu] with "For Vaiśvānara," he recites the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) and sacrifices with the offering verse (*yājyā*), or he does so omitting the fore-sacrifices (*prayāja*) and after-sacrifices (*anuyāja*).
ŚŚS 9.26.1: Following the cake-offering (*paśu-puroḍāśa*) of the animal sacrifice to Agni and Soma, there are the oblations (*havīṃṣi*) for the Devasū deities.

To Agni Gṛhapati, to Soma Vanaspati, to Savitṛ Satyaprasava, to Rudra Paśupati, to Bṛhaspati Vācaspati, to Indra Jyeṣṭha, to Mitra Satya, and to Varuṇa Dharmapati. Agni is the Hotṛ, the Lord of the House, the bearer of oblations; Agni, who does not fail, [bears] all the gods. We [invoke] Indra for great wealth, as a wide [space for us].
And the oblations with all the *pṛṣṭha*-stotras.

To Agni of the spring, of the *gāyatrī* metre, of the *trivṛt* stoma, and of the *rathaṃtara* sāman; to Indra of the summer, of the *triṣṭubh* metre, of the *pañcadaśa* stoma, and of the *bṛhat* sāman; to the Viśvedevas of the rainy season, of the *jagatī* metre, of the *saptadaśa* stoma, and of the *vairūpa* sāman; to Mitra and Varuṇa of the autumn, of the *anuṣṭubh* metre, of the *ekaviṃśa* stoma, and of the *vairāja* sāman; to Bṛhaspati of the winter, of the *paṅkti* metre, of the *triṇava* stoma, and of the *śakvara* sāman; to Savitṛ of the cool season, of the *aticchandas* metre, of the *trayastrimśa* stoma, and of the *raivata* sāman; to Anumati; to Agni Vaiśvānara; to Ka; to Aditi, the wife of Viṣṇu.

Praising you, O Agni, [we perform] our sacrifice according to the *ṛta*. O Bṛhaspati, with outstretched arms, be pleased; thus today, free from sin, we offer what is dear to the Father. May Anumati favor our sacrifice today among the gods, and may Agni, the bearer of oblations, be a source of joy for the donor.
"O Anumati, do thou favor us; grant us prosperity and bring us well-being. Impel us toward wisdom and skill, and prolong our lives.
Thus [it is said]. In the ritual procedure for animal sacrifice (*paśu-tantra*), the oblations (*havīṃṣi*) being enjoined do not receive [the formulas known as] *nigamas*.

ŚŚS 9.27.4: Having completed the offering of the omentum (*vapā*) of the *anūbandhyā* cow, they proceed with the animal sacrifice for Tvaṣṭṛ in the low voice (*upāṃśu*) in the wife’s hall (*patnīśālā*).
ŚŚS 9.27.5: They release the animal after the fire has been carried around it (*paryagni*), but they do not complete the sacrifice.
ŚŚS 9.27.6: Or, they complete the sacrifice using clarified butter according to the ritual procedure for an animal sacrifice.
"O Tvaṣṭṛ, may you be auspicious; [offer] the first portion.
Following the oblations to the Devikās comes the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) of the animal sacrifice. [The portions are offered] to Anumati, Kuhū, Rākā, Sinīvālī, and Dhātṛ.
I invoke with a loud call Kuhū at this sacrifice—she who is well-disposed, whose works are wise, and who is easy to invoke.
May she grant us the renown of the ancestors; O Goddess, let us worship you with this oblation.
Kuhū, the consort of the gods and of immortality, shall make our offerings of this oblation acceptable.
May he bestow abundant wealth upon the donor; may he grant increase of riches to the one who knows.
May Dhātṛ grant to the donor a forward-reaching, imperishable life.
May we obtain the favor of the god whose laws are true.
“Dhātṛ rules over progeny and wealth; Dhātṛ has generated this entire world.
Dhātṛ shall give a son to the sacrificer; therefore, offer to him the oblation accompanied by clarified butter.
Thus [it is said]. And there are oblations for the goddesses.
To the waters, to the plants, to the cows, to the dawn, to the night, to the sun, to the day, to the earth, to speech, and to the cow;
"O Waters, you indeed are... (from *Āpo hi ṣṭha*)... from those that are obstructed;
"The plants which were first, all of them... (from *Yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā*).
ŚŚS 9.28.8: O cows, you are not like those horses.
ŚŚS 9.28.9: This noble lady, the true one, has appeared with the true ones.
ŚŚS 9.28.10: Night has shone forth.
Those steeds of yours, O Night, who look upon men, harnessed— may they be ninety-nine,
or eighty-eight, or even seventy-seven.
Your two [steeds] are well-adorned with *kiṃśuka* flowers.
ŚŚS 9.28.12: O Indra, come hither with your bay horses, O friend Viṣṇu! ŚŚS 9.28.13: O Earth, be pleasant; thus [is the offering] for the mountains.
ŚŚS 9.28.14: To the goddess Vāc, when Vāc speaks.
[The offering] to Mātṛrudra, the knower of speech;
the *aveṣṭi* offerings to the quarters;
[and offerings] to Agni, Indra, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, the Viśvedevas, and Viṣṇu.

ŚŚS 9.28.18: When the Udavasānīyā offering has been completed, the Agnicit should not engage in sexual intercourse until he has sacrificed with the curd-mixture (payasyā) dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa; [if he does so] he should perform [the rite again].
ŚŚS 10.1.1: On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, they undergo initiation for the twelve-day sacrifice (dvādaśāha).
ŚŚS 10.1.2: There are twelve days of initiation.
ŚŚS 10.1.3: There are twelve *upasads*. ŚŚS 10.1.4: There are twelve days of the *soma* pressing (*sutyā*). ŚŚS 10.1.5: The *atirātra* is both the first and the last of the *soma* pressings.
ŚŚS_10.1.6: In the middle is the ten-night period.
ŚŚS_10.1.7: The six-day period consisting of the *pṛṣṭha* chants.
ŚŚS_10.1.8: Three *chandoma* days.
The tenth day.
The *yājyā* for the *hāriyojana* offering is "This sacrifice... (*ayaṃ yajñaḥ*).

Without a subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call and even before being prompted, the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, having recited "Go forth, O Maghavan" (*parā yāhi maghavan*), or alternatively "Conquer the setting [sun]" (*jayed astam*), utters the *atipraiṣa* call "O Maghavan, here indeed is the exhilaration" (*iha mada eva maghavan*) starting from the second [day] onwards.

ŚŚS 10.1.12: Or [the *prāyaṇīya* offering] is performed as prescribed in the traditional recension. ŚŚS 10.1.13: On the day before the Soma-pressing, the Āgnīdhra, having sat down behind his own *dhiṣṇya* hearth, says: "O Indra and Agni, I announce this to you both; to all the gods, to the Brāhmaṇas who are worthy of Soma and drinkers of Soma. O Brahman, restrain your speech! ŚŚS 10.1.14: This [formula] is obligatory until the final day [of the sacrifice].
ŚŚS 10.1.15: [The sacrifice] ends with the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.
ŚŚS 10.1.16: There is no recitation of the *āśis* (benedictions).
ŚŚS 10.1.17: And there is no taking up of the names [of the sacrificer].
ŚŚS 10.1.18: At the Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya [offerings], there is a Sārasvata [offering].
ŚŚS 10.1.19: Or it belongs to the Mādhucchandasa [school].
ŚŚS 10.1.20: In collections of days consisting of two nights or more, wherever the Hotṛ should recite the Āśvina [śastra], there the Maitrāvaruṇa should recite the Prātar-anuvāka.
ŚŚS 10.2.1: The first [day] of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*) is the Agniṣṭoma, characterized by the *trivṛt* stoma and the *rathantara* as its *pṛṣṭha*.
ŚŚS 10.2.2: When the *stomas* are expanded (*vyūḍha*), the *ājya-śastra* is "upa prayanto adhvaram"; when they are contracted (*samūḍha*), it is "pra vo devāya".
ŚŚS 10.2.3: The *prauga-śastra* belongs to Mādhucchandas.
"May Indra come for our aid"—this is the *marutvatīya* [śastra].
"Indra from afar comes to us"—this is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
"O Agni, full of splendor, you are full of splendor among the gods; may I be full of splendor among men"—with these words, he consumes the *atigrāhya* cup.
ŚŚS 10.2.7: “yuñjate mana iha iha vo hayo na vidvān” (RV 6.9.1), or omitting the last [verse], is the modification for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.2.8: The *pañcajanīyā* verse is the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) for the Vaiśvadeva in all cases.
ŚŚS 10.2.9: “pra śardhāya” (RV 5.54.1) is used for the Āgnimāruta [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.2.10: Thereafter, seven [days] are Ukthya sacrifices.
ŚŚS 10.2.11: The fourth [day] ends with the Ṣoḍaśin.
ŚŚS 10.3.1: The second [day] has the Pañcadaśa-stoma and the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha.
ŚŚS 10.3.2: "We choose Agni as the messenger"—this is the *ājya* [śastra] when the [stomas] are expanded (*vyūḷha*).
ŚŚS 10.3.3: "For you indeed are like a master of the house"—this is used when they are contracted (*samūḷha*), everywhere except for omitting the last verse.
ŚŚS 10.3.4: The *prauga* belongs to Gṛtsamada.

ŚŚS 10.3.5: "O Vāyu, those thousand [of yours]"—these two [verses]; "The sharp Soma juices, come hither"—this one; "Of the *śukra* [cup], the first"—this one; "Both gods who touch the sky"—these two; "This [is for you], O Mitra and Varuṇa"—these four *ṛcas*; and "May Sarasvatī be ours, the formidable"—these are the *prauga-ṛcas*. ŚŚS 10.3.6: "Of Viśvānara, O Indra," and "Thou art the Soma-drinker"—these are the *pratipad* and the *anucara* of the *marutvatīya* [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.3.7: "Arise, O Brahmanaspati"—this is the *brāhmaṇaspatya* *pragātha*.

ŚŚS 10.3.8: "O Indra, drinker of Soma, [drink] the Soma"—with these words, he recites the Marutvatīya [śastra]. ŚŚS 10.3.9: "That aid of yours..."—with these words, he recites the Niṣkevalya [śastra]. ŚŚS 10.3.10: "O powerful Indra, you are powerful among the gods; may I become powerful among men"—with these words, he consumes the *atigrāhya* cup.
ŚŚS 10.3.11: *viśvo devasya* is the opening verse (*pratipad*) for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.3.12: *asya hi svayaśastaram* is the subsequent [verse] (*uttara*).
ŚŚS 10.3.13: *ā viśvadevam* is the attendant verse (*anucara*).
ŚŚS 10.3.14: For that deity of yours, for heaven and earth, for the sacrifice—this is the modification in the Vaiśvadeva [section].
ŚŚS 10.3.15: Of the nourishing bull, for the bull, for the host, now indeed, born of strength—this is [the modification] in the Āgnimāruta [section].
ŚŚS 10.4.1: The third [pressing] has the seventeenfold *stoma* and the *vairūpa* as its *pṛṣṭha*.
ŚŚS 10.4.2: "Harness, O God, those who best invite the gods"—this is the *ājya* [śastra] when the [stomas] have been expanded (*vyūḍha*).
ŚŚS 10.4.3: "O Agni, you [bring] the Vasus"—this is used when they have been contracted (*samūḍha*), everywhere except for omitting the last verse.
ŚŚS 10.4.4: The *prauga* consists of verses in the *auṣṇiha* meter belonging to Atri.

ŚŚS 10.4.5: “O Vāyu, come for the feast,” is one [verse]; “O Vāyu, come as a bringer of auspiciousness,” are two; “O Indra and Vāyu, of these pressed juices,” are two; “This Soma, pressed in the vessels,” is one; “O Mitra, Varuṇa, Aśvins, come hither; come with the stones, in harmony with all the gods, and also to us, O beloved ones”—these are the *prauga* triplets. ŚŚS 10.4.6: “Him indeed, him indeed” and “Indra’s Somas” are the opening verse (*pratipad*) and the following verse (*anucara*) of the *marutvatīya* śastra. “Indra’s Somas” are the opening verse and the following verse of the *marutvatīya* śastra.
ŚŚS 10.4.7: "May Brahmanaspati advance" is the *pragātha* dedicated to Brahmanaspati.
ŚŚS 10.4.8: "Aryaman [is] threefold" is the *marutvatīya*.
ŚŚS 10.4.9: "O Indra, as much as the two heavens," "O Indra," and "O Indra, for as long as" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas* of the *vairūpa* [stotra].
ŚŚS 10.4.10: *indra tri-dhātu* is the *sāmapragātha*.
ŚŚS 10.4.11: *aham bhuvam yo jātaḥ* is the *niṣkevalya*.
ŚŚS 10.4.12: He consumes the *atigrāhya* cup with the formula: "O radiant Sūrya, you are radiant among the gods; may I be radiant among men."
ŚŚS 10.4.13: *abhi tvā deva* is the *anucara*.
ŚŚS 10.4.14: The two triplets *ud u sya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā*, *ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām*, and *anaśvo jātaḥ parāvataḥ* constitute the modification for the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.4.15: *vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām*, *dhārāvarāḥ*, *tvam agne prathamaḥ*, and *aṅgirā ṛṣiḥ* are used in the *āgnimāruta* [śastra].
The fourth [day] has the twenty-one-fold stoma and the Vairāja as its *pṛṣṭha* chant.
For the expanded (*vyūḷha*) form, the *ājya* chant is "āgnim na svavṛktibhiḥ"; for the contracted (*samūḷha*) form, it is "agnim naro".
The *praüga* chant is in the *ānuṣṭubh* meter.

ŚŚS 10.5.4: "O Vāyu, the bright one is offered to you," is one verse; "For the invocations [are distinct]," are two verses; "O Indra and Vāyu, of these Soma-draughts," "He who knows us with all aids," "Toward you [flow] the songs," and "Offspring," is one verse; "For you indeed are [the protectors]," are two verses; and "This [cow] has given"—these are the *prauga* triplets. ŚŚS 10.5.5: "Forward for us, O Goddess," is used when [the *dhur* verses] are combined. ŚŚS 10.5.6: "Thee, with sacrifices," is the introductory verse (*pratipad*) of the *marutvatīya* litany.
ŚŚS 10.5.7: Those [verses] which are the first of the three-day period are the subsequent [verses] of the following [day], together with the one addressed to Brahmaṇaspati.
ŚŚS 10.5.8: "Hear the call, O Indra," "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts," and "Now this wondrous one"—these two triplets constitute the Marutvatīya [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.5.9: "Drink the Soma, O Indra," and "May it exhilarate you, O Indra"—these are the stotriya and anurūpa of the Vairāja [stotra], performed with the nyūṅkha insertion.
ŚŚS 10.5.10: When the second and seventh syllables of the middle *pāda* have "dvi" preceding them and "dvi" following them, it is *ānuṣṭubha*.
ŚŚS 10.5.12: When the twelfth syllable is long twelve times, with three short syllables between each pair, it is *vairāja*.
ŚŚS 10.5.13: [The phrase] "yam to suṣāva."
ŚŚS 10.5.14: For the second and fourth syllables of the *pratigara* of the *ānuṣṭubha*, there is the *pratinyūṅkha*.
ŚŚS 10.5.15: In the second [syllable], it is the *vairāja*.
ŚŚS 10.5.17: "Otho modaiva."

ŚŚS 10.5.18: *indram id devatātaye* is the *sāmapragātha*. ŚŚS 10.5.19: For the first two of the three verses beginning with *tubhyam id etat*, there is the *nyūṅkha* insertion. ŚŚS 10.5.20: *kuha śrutaḥ yudhmasya te*, *tyam u vaḥ satrāsāham*, and [the next] three [verses] constitute the *niṣkevalya* hymn.
ŚŚS 10.5.21: From the second day onwards, [the procedure begins with] the *pratipad* (opening verse).
