ŚŚS 10.5.22: "Hiraṇyapāṇim" is the *anucara* (sequel).
ŚŚS 10.5.23: In the *vaiśvadeva* [section], the modification (*vikāra*) consists of: "Ā devo yātu savitā suratnaḥ," "pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī namobhiḥ," "pra ṛbhubhyaḥ," and "pra śukre etu devi."
ŚŚS 10.5.24: "pra saṃrājaḥ ka īm vyaktā huve vaḥ sudyotmānam" is used in the Āgnimāruta [laud].

ŚŚS 10.6.1: The fifth [day] has the Triṇava Stoma and the Śākvara Pṛṣṭha. ŚŚS 10.6.2: In the expanded (vyūḷha) form, the Ājya [laud] consists of the nine verses beginning with "imam ū ṣu"; in the contracted (samūḷha) form, it consists of the verses beginning with "agnim tam manye."
ŚŚS 10.6.3: Of that [first verse], having separated word by word for the first [foot], and having separated two [words] for the second, he utters the *praṇava* with one [syllable].
ŚŚS 10.6.4: The subsequent [verses] are in the *paṅkti* metre. ŚŚS 10.6.5: The *prauga-śastra* is composed in the *bṛhatī* metre.

ŚŚS 10.6.6: "ā no yajñaṃ divispṛśam" (two verses), "ā no vāyo" (one verse), "āvām sahasram" (three verses), "ṛdhag itthā" (two verses), "pra mitrāya" (one verse), and "imā u vām diviṣṭayaḥ," "ā no viśvā suhavyaḥ," "devam-devam vo avase," and "devam-devam iyam adadāt"—these are the *tṛcas* for the *prauga-śastra*.
ŚŚS 10.6.7: "uta syā naḥ sarasvatī" and "ghorā" [are used] when [the *sūktas*] are combined (*samūḷha*). ŚŚS 10.6.8: "yat pāñcajanyayā" is the opening verse (*pratipad*) of the *marutvatīya-śastra*.
ŚŚS 10.6.9: “*Itthā hi some avitā asi marutvān indra vṛṣabha ayam ha yena*”—these three [verses] constitute the Marutvatīya [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.6.10: The *stotriya* consists of the verses known as the Mahānāmnīs.
ŚŚS 10.6.11: Just as there are three *anuṣṭubh* verses, so too there is one [verse] for each [of the others].

ŚŚS 10.6.12: Of the *uttamā* [verse], the *paṅkti* is the best. ŚŚS 10.6.13: And in the latter half [of the verse], there are five feet; they call this the *purīṣa*, and it is the recitation of the *nivid*. ŚŚS 10.6.14:

The three triplets beginning with "praty asmai pipīṣate," "yo rayivo rayintamaḥ," and "tyam u vo aprahaṇam"; and the tenth [verse] beginning with "asmā asmā" and "evā hy asi vīrayuḥ"—this is the *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 10.6.15: *yad indra nāhuṣīṣu eti sāma pragāthaḥ* (That Sāman which goes among the Nāhuṣa women, O Indra).

ŚŚS 10.6.16: *indro madāya pra idam brahma abhūḥ ekaḥ tam indram vājayāmasi* (Indra for the sake of intoxication; you alone have become this prayer; we strengthen that Indra)—these three [verses] constitute the Niṣkevalya. ŚŚS 10.6.17: *tat savitur vareṇyam* (That desirable [splendor] of Savitṛ) is the Anucara.

ŚŚS 10.6.18: “ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā damūnāḥ” (three verses), “mahī dyāvāpṛthivī” (four verses), and “ṛbhuḥ vibhvā ko nu vām mitrāvaruṇau pra śantamaḥ”—this is the modification for the Vaiśvadeva [parvan].
ŚŚS 10.6.19: “haviṣ pāntam vapuḥ nv agniḥ hotā gṛhapatiḥ” (three verses)—this is for the Āgnimāruta [parvan].
ŚŚS 10.6.20: “mūrdhānam,” “ā rudrāsaḥ,” and “imam ū ṣv” (nine verses)—this is when the [parvans] are combined.
The sixth [day] has the thirty-three-fold *stoma* and the *Raivata* as its *pṛṣṭha*.
(ŚŚS 10.7.1) They sacrifice by joining the verses of Parucchepa with the regular *yājyā*s.
(ŚŚS 10.7.2) "Come to you with speed" and "May our prayers come to you both" are the two *puronuvākyā*s for the cup for Indra and Vāyu. (ŚŚS 10.7.3)
ŚŚS 10.7.4: *stīrṇam barhir ā vām ratha* is the *yājyā*.

ŚŚS 10.7.5: *suṣuma* is the *puronuvākyā* for the Maitrāvaruṇa, and the following verse is the *yājyā*. ŚŚS 10.7.6: *yuvām stomaiḥ* is the *puronuvākyā* for the Āśvina, and the following verse is the *yājyā*.

ŚŚS 10.7.7: *vṛṣann indra*, *tām vām dhenum*, *viśveṣu hi tvā mo ṣu vaḥ*, *asmad ā yan naḥ patnīḥ*, *tā no rāsan*—these are for the Neṣṭṛ; they are a *dvipadā* and a *triṣṭubh*. With *agnim hotāram dadhyaṅ ha*, they sacrifice at the morning pressing for those who have set out. ŚŚS 10.7.8: From the two hymns beginning with *tubhyaṃ hinvāna*, they recite one verse from each after the *ṛtu-praiṣas*.
ŚŚS 10.7.9: The Adhvaryu and the Gṛhapati sacrifice themselves.

ŚŚS 10.7.11: “Drink the pressed Soma, O Indra; for Dyaus [is] for Indra; by you, O Maghavan, may we drink; protect us, O Indra; now indeed thus [is] your greatness, O Indra; the one pressing [the juice] wins [you],” this is the modification at the midday pressing. ŚŚS 10.7.12: “And the Mother from the high heaven,” this is the Neṣṭṛ’s [verse] at the third pressing.
ŚŚS 10.7.13: They sacrifice without drawing breath.
ŚŚS 10.7.14: Or [the *prastāva*] is performed with the verses belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhikī*).
ŚŚS 10.8.1: "This one has been born" (*ayaṃ jāyata*) is the *ājya* [śastra]. ŚŚS 10.8.2:
The *prauga* [śastra] consists of verses in the *aticchandas* metre.

ŚŚS 10.8.3: *stīrṇam barhiḥ*, *ā vām rathaḥ*, *ayaṃ mitrāya yuvām stomair vṛṣan indra*—these are the single [verses]; *ava mahān indraḥ*—these are two; *o ṣu na agne*, *iyam adadāt*—these are the *prauga* triplets.
ŚŚS 10.8.4: *uta naḥ priyaḥ* is used when [the verses] are confused. ŚŚS 10.8.5: *sa pūrvyaḥ* is the introductory verse (*pratipad*) for the *marutvatīya* litany.
ŚŚS 10.8.6: "The chariot which you [have]... and "He who is the bull, accompanied by the Maruts, O bountiful Indra..."—these three verses constitute the *marutvatīya* [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.8.7: "The wealthy ones for us," "Of the wealthy one indeed," and "O wealthy one"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses of the *raivata* [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.8.8: "Not at all another... is the *sāmagātha*.
"O Indra, come hither; indeed, come toward this [sacrifice]; come toward us with your two bay horses"—these three verses constitute the *niṣkevalya* hymn.
"Toward that god"—this is the introductory verse (*pratipad*) of the *vaiśvadeva* hymn.

Of this [verse], having divided it with a sixteen-syllable [pāda], having uttered the *praṇava* with an eighteen-syllable [pāda], having paused with a fifteen-syllable [pāda], [and then] with a fifteen-syllable [pāda].
ŚŚS 10.8.12: For this [hymn], the verses beginning with *asya hi sva-yaśastaram* follow.

ŚŚS 10.8.13: The *anucara* (sequel) belongs to the third day. ŚŚS 10.8.14: Having recited the verses *ud u sya devaḥ savitā*, *katara pūrvā*, *kim u śreṣṭham*, and *idam itthā*, and having set aside the last verse, one recites *ye yajñena*; then one recites the remaining verses. This is the modification (*vikāra*) in the Vaiśvadeva section.
ŚŚS 10.8.15: "The day is black" and "O you who are ever-worshipping, this hymn"—these [verses] are used in the Āgnimāruta [śastra].

ŚŚS 10.8.16: From the middle three-day period, he omits the last *ṛc*s of the *niṣkevalya* and *marutvatīya* [śastras], having previously combined them. ŚŚS 10.8.17: And at the end of the *vaiśvadeva* [śastras], he performs the three verses beginning with "May [Agni] measure out well-being for us."
ŚŚS 10.8.18: "Tatam ma" is the Ārbhava [śastra] of the fourth day. ŚŚS 10.8.19: "Pra yantu vājāḥ"—these three [verses] are at the end of the Māruta [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.8.20: "Vasum na citramahasam" is the Jātavedasīya [śastra].

ŚŚS 10.8.21: For one who has been asked about the *parokṣapṛṣṭha*, the *bṛhadrathantarapṛṣṭha*, the *upāṅknyapṛṣṭha*, the *āparkyapṛṣṭha*, the *tanūpṛṣṭha*, and the *chandoruṭstoma*, the *stotriyas*, *anurūpas*, and *sāmapragāthas* are determined according to the authority of the *chandogas*.
ŚŚS 10.8.22: Everything else is the same as in the *samūḷha* [rite]. ŚŚS 10.8.23: Likewise in the *viśvajit*.
The seventh [day] has the twenty-four-fold hymn-form (*stoma*), the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, and both *sāmans*.
"pra vaḥ śukrāya" is the *ājya-śastra*;
the *prauga-śastra* is in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
ŚŚS 10.9.4: *pra vīrayā te satyena ud vām cakṣur ā gomatā no deva pra vo yajñeṣu pra codasā*—these are the *prauga* triplets.

ŚŚS 10.9.5: Those which are the opening (*pratipad*) and following (*anucara*) verses of the first three-day period (*tryaha*), together with those addressed to Bṛhaspati (*brāhmaṇaspatya*), are used in the *chandoma* days, in the *svarasāman* days, and in the *abhiplava* period.
ŚŚS 10.9.6: [These apply] from the very first day of the *chandomika* first [three-day] period.
From the second [day] of the second [abhiplava],
from the third of the third;
thus for the preceding three-day period consisting of abhiplavas.
ŚŚS 10.9.10: Likewise for the subsequent [stotra].
ŚŚS 10.9.11: Likewise for the *svara-sāmans*. ŚŚS 10.9.12: "With what splendor? (*kayā śubhā*) and "That well-guided one" (*tyam sumeṣam*): these constitute the *marutvatīya* [śastra].

ŚŚS 10.9.13: One should recite the *niṣkevalya* [śastra] with the hymn beginning, "Praise him, that ram... (abhi tyam meṣam). ŚŚS 10.9.14: One should not recite the *yoni* verse of the *Kaṇvarathantara*.

ŚŚS 10.9.15: Those which are the *pratipad* and *anucara* verses of the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra] on the first two days [of the *daśarātra*] are used in the *chandoma* days and the *abhiplava* [six-day period].

ŚŚS 10.9.16: *tat savitur vareṇyam*, *pretāṃ yajñasya ayam devāya*, these three ṛcs; *ṛjunītī*, five [verses]; *yāhi vanasā saha*, *omāsaś carṣaṇidhṛtaḥ*, these three—these are the modifications for the Vaiśvadeva.
ŚŚS 10.9.17a: *vaiśvānaro na ūtaye*, *vaiśvānaro na ā gamad imaṃ yajñaṃ sajūr upa*.
Agni, with the vehicle of the hymn—
Vaiśvānara has generated the praise and the sacrifice of the Aṅgirases;
he has brought to them splendor accompanied by celestial light.
"pra yad vaḥ triṣṭubham" and "arcantas tvā"—these fifteen or nine [verses] are for the Āgnimāruta [laud].
The eighth [laud] has the Catuścatvāriṃśa Stoma and the Rathantara Pṛṣṭha. "agnim vo devam" is the Ājya [Stotra].
ŚŚS 10.10.3: The *prauga* is in the *triṣṭubh* metre.

ŚŚS 10.10.4: The *prauga* triplets are: *kuvid aṅga*, *ā vāyo bhūṣa* (one verse), *yāvattaraḥ*, *prati vām sūra udite*, *apa svasuḥ*, *ayaṃ somaḥ*, *pra brahmāṇi*, and *uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇā*. ŚŚS 10.10.5:
*mahān indro nṛvad*, *imā u tvā purutamasya*, *kva sya vīraḥ*—in all cases, omitting the last four verses; then *mahaś cit tam asya dyāvāpṛthivī* constitutes the *marutvatīya* śastra.
ŚŚS 10.10.6: “Thou art great, O Indra; for thou, O Indra, art great,” “This thy praise which is without precedent,” and “This prayer of thine”—these constitute the Niṣkevalya hymn.

ŚŚS 10.10.7: “Hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye” (four verses), “Mahī dyauḥ” and “Yuvānā pitarā” (two triplets), and “Devānām id imam nu kam,” “Viśve devā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ” (three verses)—this is the modification for the Vaiśvadeva litany.
ŚŚS 10.10.8: “Vaiśvānaraḥ ajījanat,” “Agnir no navyasīm matim.”
Increasing through patience and through might,
O purifying Agni Vaiśvānara, shine as a bull with radiant splendor,
being invoked by the Jamadagnis.
"Ṛtāvānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ kad dha nūnaṃ kadha priyo dūtaṃ vo viśvavedasam"—this is for the Agnimāruta [laud].
It has the forty-eight-fold stoma (aṣṭācatvāriṃśastoma) and the Bṛhat-sāman as its *pṛṣṭha*, and it is the ninth [day].
"Aganma mahā somasya mā tavasam"—this is the *ājya* [stotra].
ŚŚS 10.11.3: Or [the *praüga*] may be as before.
ŚŚS 10.11.4: The *praüga* consists of *triṣṭubh* verses.

ŚŚS 10.11.5: The first, third, and last [verses], the second and fourth, and [the verses] beginning with "Come, O Vāyu, be present" (*ā vāyo bhūṣa*), "Like swift horses for glory" (*arvanto na śravase*), "Dwelling in heaven, possessing all boons" (*divi kṣayantā viśvavārāḥ*), "The men [invoke] Indra" (*indram naraḥ*), "Agni stands upright" (*ūrdhvo agniḥ*), and "With the flood" (*pra kṣodasā*)—these are the *triads* of the *praüga*.
ŚŚS 10.11.6: *try aryamā indro rathāya tiṣṭha harī gāyat sāma pra mandine*—this is the Marutvatīya [stotra].
ŚŚS 10.11.7: *ā satyo yātvasmā id u ya indra tat ta indriyam aham bhuvam viśvajitaḥ*—this is the Niṣkevalya [stotra].

*Abhi tvā deva*, *pra vām mahi dyāvā*, these two triplets; *indra iṣaḥ* as one verse; *te no ratnāni* as two verses; the five hymns beginning with *agnir ukthe* belonging to Manu, excluding the penultimate verse of the hymn *ye triṃśati*; *na hi vo asty arbhakaḥ* as one verse; *aśarmā* as four verses; or *babhruḥ ekaḥ* as one; the hymn *viśve devāsa ā gata* in three verses, which belongs to Bhāradvāja—this is the modification for the Vaiśvadeva [offering]. *Divi pṛṣṭhe arocata agnir vaiśvānaro bṛhan.* (Agni Vaiśvānara, the great, has shone upon the back of heaven.)
With light he drives away the darkness;
he has ordained everything, and as the self-controlled one, he sends forth the seasons,
promoting the growth of the sacrifice.
"Agni in the highest abodes," "O Maruts, he whose Agni is the Hotṛ-priest and domestic chaplain"—these [verses] are used in the Āgnimāruta śastra.

Regarding the first three-day period (tryaha), those which are the morning and third pressings (savana) are employed in the combined (samūḷha) Chandomas. Furthermore, in the Niṣkevalya and Marutvatīya śastras, one omits the verses in the Jagatī meter.
ŚŚS 10.11.12: After [the hymn] "sa yo vṛṣā," one should recite fifteen [verses] beginning with "kayā śubhīyāt.
ŚŚS 10.11.13: After [the hymn] "yo jāta," one should recite that which begins with "tam u ṣṭuhīyāt.
ŚŚS 10.11.14: When the Bṛhat and Rathantara are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras, all [the stotriya verses] consist of two sūktas each.
The tenth day has the twenty-fourfold hymn-form (*stoma*) and is characterized by the absence of dispute (*avivākya*).
The *agniṣṭoma-sāman* is the thirty-threefold. The *mānasa* chant consists of three verses.
In the womb of the Vāmadevya, the Rathantara is the *pṛṣṭha* chant.
(ŚŚS 10.12.5) In case of lack of inspiration, another [verse] is used for private recitation (*svādhyāya*).
(ŚŚS 10.12.6) Having extracted the *ānuṣṭubha* verses from the other meters, one completes a thousand [verses] in the *ānuṣṭubha* meter for the fifteen-fold [stoma] at one *savanīya* sacrifice.
ŚŚS 10.12.7: There are thirty-two *gāyatrī* verses.
ŚŚS 10.12.8: In place of the *anuṣṭubh*s, one should recite the three-verse hymns beginning with "agnim naro dhiṣaṇāsu praśastam" and "prati syā sūnaryā śubhrā.
ŚŚS 10.12.9: There are twenty-four *triṣṭubh* verses.
Likewise, there are *jagatī* verses;
fifteen *pragāthas*;
and fifteen *auṣṇiha* triplets (*tṛcas*).
And [the verses] are in the *pāṅkta* meter. The morning litany (*prātar-anuvāka*) consists of *anuṣṭubh* verses in the one hundred and fifteenth [recitation].
Having extracted the third and fourth [verses] of the *stokyās*, there are two [verses] beginning with "abhi pravanta."
ŚŚS 10.12.16: "acchā naḥ śīraśociṣam" and the three verses beginning with "acchā vo agnim avase" take the place of those [verses].
ŚŚS 10.12.17: "prati śrutāya" and the three verses beginning with "praty asmai pipīṣate" take the place of those [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.1: "agne tam adya" is the *ājya* [verse].
In its first [verse], having divided it with a five-syllable word and having paused after two five-syllable words, he pronounces the *praṇava* with the remaining two.
The *prauga-śastra* belongs to Mādhucchandas. There are twenty-two *gāyatrī* verses.

ŚŚS 10.13.5: "mṛjāno vāre pavamāno avyaye"—this is the *grāvastuta* [verse], to be used according to one's preference. ŚŚS 10.13.6: "uttiṣṭhann ojasā" is a single verse; it takes the place of the verse beginning with "uttiṣṭhata ava paśyata. ŚŚS 10.13.7: The *trikadrukīyā* verses are the introductory hymn (*pratipad*) for the *marutvatīya* litany.
Of that [verse], having divided it with sixteen syllables, having chanted forward with sixteen syllables, having concluded with sixteen syllables, [and] with sixteen syllables; ŚŚS 10.13.9:
"tuviśuṣma" and so on are the two subsequent [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.10: From the hymn beginning "bṛhad indrāya," he recites the two preceding *pragāthas* together with the verse containing the word "pinvanti. This is the *marutvatīya* [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.13.11: Having recited the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses of the Vāmadevya, one recites the *dhyāyyā*, followed by the *rāthaṃtara-pragātha* and the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 10.13.12: "O friends, let us receive instruction" (*sakhāya ā śiṣāmahi*)—these are nine [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.13: And "Upon the poles for him, the thunderbolt" (*ā dhūrṣu asmai vajram ekaḥ*)—this is a two-footed verse.
And [the hymn] of Hairaṇyastūpa;
before the Hairaṇyastūpa [hymn], he recites with a *pragātha*.
Thus ends the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
ŚŚS 10.13.17: From the sixth [verse], the *pratipad* and its *anucara* belong to the Vaiśvadeva [parvan].
ŚŚS 10.13.18: Before the *ā no bhadra* hymn, the *pra śukriya* is the modification in the Vaiśvadeva. ŚŚS 10.13.19:
Having omitted the verse beginning with "uru viṣṇo," he performs the sacrifice with the verse beginning with "bhavā mitra."
ŚŚS 10.13.20: *agnim naraḥ* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the *agniṣṭomasāman*.
ŚŚS 10.13.21: *āyam gauḥ* and *mahī dyauḥ* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
ŚŚS 10.13.22: *tam pratnathā* consists of thirteen [verses].
Having recited "The sacrifice has come into being," he performs the *paridhāna* (concluding verse).
He offers the oblation with the words "O Prajāpati.
The call for the *uktha* verses is explained [as follows].
Thus ends the section on the *atiriktoktha* when the ritual is confused.

Having concluded before the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, having offered in the *gārhapatya* fire, and having entered the *sadas* by the eastern door, he sits down behind his own *dhiṣṇya* altar. Having performed the *mānasa-stotra*, he recites the *sārparājñī* verses beginning with "āyam gauḥ," while the others chant them in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) without the *praṇava*.
When the Hotṛ announces, "Oṃ, Hotṛ! So be it, O Hotṛ! he responds with the appropriate *anugraha* (response).
Prajāpati desired: "May I become many; may I procreate; may I pervade this entire Veda—whatever exists here, whether gods, humans, or anything else.
He perceived this sacrificial rite, the Agnihotra, as the Daśahotṛ.
Having said this aloud, he then [recited] in a whisper.
Intelligence is the sacrificial ladle;
thought is the clarified butter;
speech is the altar.
The sacrificial grass has been spread; Agni is the conscious one;
the Agnīdhra has performed his duty with discernment.
Vācaspati is the Hotṛ;
the mind is the Upavaktṛ;
the breath is the oblation.
The Sāman-chanters are the Adhvaryus; thus [are] the Hotṛ-priests. Now follows the cup-offering (graha).
"O Lord of Speech, whose name is the heart's ordainer!
The Lord of Speech has drunk the Soma; bestow manly vigor upon us!
Thus [he recites] in a whisper.
Through that, Prajāpati generated these three: gods, humans, and asuras. Indeed, for those among whom there is such a Hotṛ who knows this, that Hotṛ is propagated with offspring and cattle.
The sacrificers of those for whom one becomes the Hotṛ, knowing thus, are multiplied with offspring and cattle. Those two classes indeed followed [the path]: the gods and humans;
the Asuras, however, turned away from him. He desired: "May a hero be born to me, by whom I may overcome these Asuras."
He perceived this sacrificial rite of the Caturhotṛ as the New and Full Moon sacrifices.
Having said this, he then [recites] in a low voice:
"The Earth is the Hotṛ."
The sky is the *adhvaryu*; Tvaṣṭṛ is the *agnīdh*; Mitra is the *upavaktṛ*.
Thus say the Hotṛ priests.
Now follows the cup-offering:
"O Lord of Speech, with the most powerful vigor of speech, you draw [the offering] forth."
O Lord of the sacrifice, you prepare wealth and heroic vigor.
Let the Lord of Speech drink the Soma. May he generate Indra for the sake of sensory power; Svāhā!
Thus in a whisper.
By means of that, Prajāpati generated Indra the hero; from that, he overcame those Asuras.
This is true for those whose Hotṛ priest is one who knows thus.
A hero is indeed born to that Hotṛ;
heroes are born to those sacrificers.
That Hotṛ indeed overcomes his hateful rival.
"The sacrificers become the conquerors of their hateful rivals, those for whom there is a Hotṛ priest who knows thus.
[When the Hotṛ is about to recite the Pañcahotṛ formula, he says: "O Adhvaryu!
[The deities did not stand above that Indra, for his preeminence and excellence.]
He perceived this Pañcahotṛ sacrifice-rite, the Cāturmāsyas.
Having said this, he then [recites] in a low voice:
"Agni is the Hotṛ; the Aśvins are the Adhvaryus."
Rudra is the Āgnīdh;
Bṛhaspati is the Upavaktṛ;
these are the Hotṛs.
Now follows the *graha* (libation):
"O Lord of Speech, with unimpaired speech, with an unimpaired ladle,
do thou, O God, increase the office of the Hotṛ in heaven."
Thus [he recites] in a whisper.
Then indeed, the deities stood aside for Indra, on account of his seniority and preeminence.
This is so for those whose Hotṛ-priest is one who knows thus.
"Verily, they stand for that *hotṛ* priest for their own preeminence; they stand for those sacrificers for their own preeminence, for whom there is a *hotṛ* who knows thus.
ŚŚS 10.17.2: He desired, "May I be an eater of food, a lord of food.
He perceived this sacrificial rite, the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ*, as the animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*).
Having spoken thus, he then [recites] in a low voice:
"The sun is your eye;
the wind is your breath."
The intermediate space is the self;
the sacrifice is the limbs;
the sky is the back.
"The earth is the body," say the Hotṛ priests.
Now follows the drawing of the cup (graha).
"Let Soma drink of Soma; let the bright one drink of the bright.
These Soma-libations have been cooked for you, O Indra, Vātāpin, who hears our invocation.
Thus [he recites] in a whisper.
From that, he indeed became an eater of food and a lord of food. For those for whom one who knows thus becomes the Hotṛ,
that Hotṛ indeed becomes an eater of food and a lord of food.
"Those sacrificers for whom there is a Hotṛ priest who knows thus become eaters of food and lords of food.
Those gods desired, "May we be established in the established worlds.
They perceived this sacrificial rite of the Seven Hotṛs, the Soma sacrifice.
Having spoken thus, he then [recites] in a whisper:
"The Mahāhavis is the Hotṛ;
the Satyahavis is the Adhvaryu."
The Acittapāja is the Agnīdh; the Acittamanas is the Upavaktṛ;
the Anādhṛṣya and Apratidhṛṣya are the two Abhigars.
"Ayāsya shall be the Udgātṛ"—
thus say the Hotṛs.
Now follows the cup-drawing (graha).
O Lord of Speech, O Ordainer, O Name! We worship your name. May you be the ordainer of our names.
Let not the thread of the gods be severed, nor that of men.
"In harmony with Heaven and Earth, invited, drink of the Soma, Svāhā!
(Thus [he recites] in a whisper.
Thereupon, indeed, it was prepared for them.
Those gods were established in established worlds;
even today they are established in established [worlds].
This is so for those whose Hotṛ priest is one who knows thus.
Prosperity and security indeed attend that Hotṛ;
prosperity and security attend those sacrificers.
That Hotṛ attains the heavenly world and is firmly established in this world.
"The sacrificers attain the heavenly world and are firmly established in this world, for those whose Hotṛ-priest becomes one who knows thus. Then he speaks of the body:

"O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ-priest becomes one who knows the body of Prajāpati as the eater of food—verily, that Hotṛ-priest becomes an eater of food, and those sacrificers become eaters of food."

"O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ becomes one who knows Prajāpati’s body as 'Annapatnī' (the consort of food)—that Hotṛ indeed becomes the Lord of Food (annapati), and those sacrificers become Lords of Food.
"O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ becomes one who knows Prajāpati’s auspicious body (bhadrā tanūḥ)—good fortune indeed comes to that Hotṛ, and good fortune comes to those sacrificers."

ŚŚS 10.19.2c: O Adhvaryu, for those whose Hotṛ is one who knows the auspicious body of Prajāpati, it indeed becomes auspicious for that Hotṛ, and it becomes auspicious for those sacrificers. ŚŚS 10.19.2d:
O Adhvaryu, for those whose Hotṛ is one who knows the non-abiding body of Prajāpati, that Hotṛ indeed becomes non-abiding, and those sacrificers become non-abiding.

ŚŚS 10.19.2e: O Adhvaryu, for those whose Hotṛ, knowing the fearless body of Prajāpati, becomes the Hotṛ, there is indeed fearlessness for that Hotṛ; there is fearlessness for those sacrificers. ŚŚS 10.19.2f: O Adhvaryu, or for those whose Hotṛ, not knowing the unattained body of Prajāpati, becomes the Hotṛ, that Hotṛ is indeed unattained; those sacrificers become unattained.

ŚŚS 10.19.2g: O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the unattainable body of Prajāpati, becomes the Hotṛ—he indeed becomes an unattainable Hotṛ; those sacrificers become unattainable. ŚŚS 10.19.2h:
O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the unassailable body of Prajāpati, becomes the Hotṛ—he indeed becomes an unassailable Hotṛ; those sacrificers become unassailable.

ŚŚS 10.19.2i: O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the inviolable body of Prajāpati, performs the office—he indeed becomes an invincible Hotṛ, and those sacrificers become invincible. ŚŚS 10.19.2j:
O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the unprecedented body of Prajāpati, performs the office—for that Hotṛ no other is prior, nor for those sacrificers are any others prior.

ŚŚS 10.19.2k: "O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the body of Prajāpati, becomes one who is without a rival—those Hotṛs indeed become without rivals, and those sacrificers become without rivals for whom such a Hotṛ is present.
ŚŚS 10.20.1: From this [verse] follows the recitation concerning the Gṛhapati (Householder).
ŚŚS 10.20.2a: "O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Gṛhapati, knowing the Gṛhapati, becomes the Gṛhapati—he indeed prospers as Gṛhapati, and those sacrificers prosper."

ŚŚS 10.20.2b: "O Adhvaryu, those for whom a Gṛhapati who knows thus becomes one whose evil has been struck away—for he, as Gṛhapati, indeed strikes away their evil; those sacrificers for whom a Gṛhapati who knows thus becomes one strike away their evil.
ŚŚS 10.21.1: He sacrifices with the formula "O Prajāpati" mentally.
ŚŚS 10.21.2: He utters the *vaṣaṭ* call mentally.
He performs the *anuvaṣaṭkāra* with the mind;
the consumption [of the soma] is with the mind;
the touching of the chest is with the mind.
ŚŚS 10.21.6: Seated in front of the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, they touch an *audumbara* branch.
ŚŚS 10.21.7: Those who do not pass beyond [the hearths] should hold on to branches of the *palāśa* tree.
ŚŚS 10.21.8: The *hotṛ* should place his two hands at the top [of the branch].
"May I be the best," [he thinks].
Having closed the doors of the *sadas* and the hall, the *adhvaryu* restrains his speech.
Holding his speech in check and closing his eyes, he remains seated until the appearance of the stars.
ŚŚS 10.21.11: While the stars are visible, they cast their gaze upon the *mārjālīya* area with the formula, "That is the eye among the stars.
ŚŚS 10.21.12: Having reached the *nidhana* of all the *sāmans*, they crawl beneath the axle of the northern *havirdhāna* cart.
ŚŚS 10.21.13: Or rather, they crawl along the north side of the northern [cart].

ŚŚS 10.21.14: Having murmured the verse, "O Indra and Parvata, you two... at the time of the axle-ritual, they sit down in front of the two *havirdhāna* carts and meditate upon their desires—whatever desires they may have.

ŚŚS 10.21.15: Those who have many desires should murmur these sacred utterances (*vyāhṛti*): "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. ŚŚS 10.21.16: Having stepped out toward the east and north, they call out to Speech: "May Speech come! May Speech approach! May Speech come to me! Thus they say.
ŚŚS 10.21.17: Having uttered the introductory formula of the *subrahmaṇyā* three times in a low voice (*upāṃśu*), they release their speech.
ŚŚS 10.21.18: At this point, the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*) is concluded.
ŚŚS 10.21.19: It is a statement regarding the time; it is indeed a statement regarding the time.
ŚŚS 11.1.1: The twelve-day sacrifice has been explained as the archetype for both *sattra* and *ahīna* rites.
ŚŚS 11.1.2: Modification is characterized by specific scriptural injunctions.
ŚŚS 11.1.3: The *ahīna* sacrifices begin with the two-night rite and extend up to the twelve-day sacrifice.

ŚŚS 11.1.4: The sacrificial sessions (*satra*) begin with those lasting twelve days. ŚŚS 11.1.5: In the *ahīna* sacrifices, the introductory day (*prāyaṇīya*) does not exist. ŚŚS 11.1.6: And the ritual rules (*dharma*) of the *satra* apply [to them].

ŚŚS 11.2.1: The day characterized by the twenty-four-fold stoma, with the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha* chant and both *sāmans*, whether it be an *agniṣṭoma* or an *ukthya*, is called the "Twenty-fourth Day" (*caturviṃśamahaḥ*).
ŚŚS 11.2.2: The *ājya* [stotra] is "The Hotṛ has been born" (*hotā ajaniṣṭa*).
ŚŚS 11.2.3: The *prauga* [śastra] belongs to Mādhucchandas.
ŚŚS 11.2.4: *Kayā śubhīyam* is the *marutvatīya* [śastra].

ŚŚS 11.2.5: Having recited the preceding verses beginning with *anuttamā te*, which serve as the concluding verses (*paridhānīya*), at the point where the *nivit* is inserted therein, ŚŚS 11.2.6: *Tad id āsīyam* is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].

ŚŚS 11.2.7: From the second [verse], the Sāvitra and Dyāvāpṛthivīya [are taken]. ŚŚS 11.2.8: And the Vaiśvadeva and Māruta [are taken] from the second. ŚŚS 11.2.9: The Ārbhava [is taken] from the sixth.
ŚŚS 11.2.10: The Vaiśvānarīya [sāman] is from the third [stotra].
ŚŚS 11.2.11: "By the sacrifice he prospers"—this is the Jātavedasīya.
ŚŚS 11.2.12: The Sāman is the Antarukthya.

Having recited the *ukthya* stotriyas together with the stotriya of the *yajñāyajñīya*, and the *anurūpa*s together with the *anurūpa*, and having recited [the verses] beginning with "O Agni, drink with the Maruts who sing praises; rejoice with Indra and Varuṇa; with Indra and Bṛhaspati; with Indra and Viṣṇu; in harmony," he performs the *paridhāna*.
ŚŚS 11.2.14: When there is an *ukthya* following another *graha*, one should sacrifice with this recited [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.3.1: In the *ekatrika* rite, the *śastra* is arranged according to triplets (*tṛca*).
ŚŚS 11.3.2: Having recited the *stotriyas* according to how they were chanted, or having recited the triplets.
Having recited the stotriya, the anurūpas, and the sāmamagāthas,
the hotrakas recite the final triplets of the paryāsa hymns;
the hotṛ recites those [verses] for which the *nivid* has been inserted.
ŚŚS 11.3.4: Everything else is according to the original form (*prakṛti*).
ŚŚS 11.4.1: The Abhiplava six-day period is a modification of the Pṛṣṭhya [six-day period].
ŚŚS 11.4.2: Those Ājya-stotras which belong to the first three-day period are used for the preceding Abhiplavas.
ŚŚS 11.4.3: There is an exchange of the *rathantara* and the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha* chants.
ŚŚS 11.4.4: The *jyotis-agniṣṭoma* is both first and last.
ŚŚS 11.4.5: The four *ukthya* sacrifices are in the middle.
ŚŚS 11.4.6: The *gāyatrī* is the second and the fourth;
ŚŚS 11.4.7: The *āyuṣmatī* is the third and the fifth;
ŚŚS 11.4.8: "Indro rathāya" is the *marutvatīya*.
ŚŚS 11.4.9: "Come hither, O steed" (ā yāhy arvāṅ) is the Niṣkevalya hymn. ŚŚS 11.4.10: "How [shall we praise] the gods? (kathā devānām) is the Vaiśvadeva hymn.
ŚŚS 11.4.11: And also in the fifth [day].
ŚŚS 11.4.12: [The hymn] for the Maruts is from the *ekāha* [sacrifice].
ŚŚS 11.4.13: "Come hither, O Hotṛ" (*ehi pra hotā*) is the verse addressed to Jātavedas.
ŚŚS 11.4.14: Everything else is the same as on the first day.
ŚŚS 11.5.1: "imām u tvā" is the second [stotra] for the Maruts (marutvatīya). ŚŚS 11.5.2: "suta it tvā nimitla" is the Niṣkevalya [stotra].
ŚŚS 11.5.3: From the one-day sacrifice (ekāha), the Sāvitra [stotra is taken].
ŚŚS 11.5.4: "tataṃ ma" is the Ārbhava [Stotra].
ŚŚS 11.5.5: And also in the fifth [turn].
ŚŚS 11.5.6: "devān huve" is the Vaiśvadeva [Stotra].
ŚŚS 11.5.7: [The *praüga*] for the twenty-four-fold [stoma] is that dedicated to Jātavedas.
ŚŚS 11.5.8: The rest is the same as on the second day.
ŚŚS 11.6.1: On the third day, the *praüga* belongs to Viśvamanas and consists of verses in the *uṣṇih* meter.
ŚŚS 11.6.2: *vāyo yāhi śivā vām sahasram tā vām viśvasyā vām vāhiṣṭhaḥ sakhāya ā śiṣāmahe uta no devy aditir uta naḥ priya iti* are the *prauga* triplets.
ŚŚS 11.6.3: *tiṣṭhā harī iti* is the *marutvatīya*.
ŚŚS 11.6.4: For the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*), [the *marutvatīya*] is the *niṣkevalya*.
ŚŚS 11.6.5: [The hymn] "ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī" consists of three verses.
ŚŚS 11.6.6: And [it is used] on the sixth day. ŚŚS 11.6.7: From the one-day sacrifice, the Ārbhava and the Vaiśvadeva [laud] are taken.
ŚŚS 11.6.8: "O Agni, the Rudras who follow the cosmic order..."—this is the Āgnimāruta [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.7.1: "The Hotṛ has been born"—this is the Ājya [śastra] for the fourth day. ŚŚS 11.7.2:
The Praüga [śastra] belongs to Medhātithi.

Those [verses] belonging to Gārtsamada are dedicated to Vāyu and to Indra-Vāyu; however, those of Medhātithi are the first ones. "Mitram vayam," "Prātar yujā tvā vahantu," and "Aibhir agne"—these are the triplets.
ŚŚS 11.7.5: Those *sārasvata* hymns which belong to the subsequent three-day period (*tryaha*) when combined (*samūḷha*), those are for the subsequent *ābhiplavika* days.
ŚŚS 11.7.6: The *marutvatīya* [śastra] is from the one-day sacrifice (*ekāha*). ŚŚS 11.7.7: "Ugro jajñe" (The fierce one was born) is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
From the second [verse], the Sāvitra and Dyāvāpṛthivīya [stotras];
from the third, the Ārbhava;
"Agni, Indra" is the Vaiśvadeva.
ŚŚS 11.7.11: Those verses which belong to the Vaiśvānara hymns of each preceding three-day period are used for the succeeding one.
ŚŚS 11.7.12: "pra ye śumbhante janasya gopāḥ" is the Āgnimāruta hymn.
ŚŚS 11.8.1: "agna ojiṣṭham" is the Ājya-śastra of the fifth day, omitting the final verse in every case.
The *praüga* śastra is to be contracted.

The three verses beginning with "Drink first, O Vāyu; you, O God... (*agram piba tava vāyo sa tvam no deva*), followed by the triplets beginning with "Hither to us" (*ā naḥ*), "O Mitra and Varuṇa" (*no mitrāvaruṇā*), "Rich in cattle" (*gomantam*), "From there, O Indra, for us" (*ataś cid indra naḥ*), and "All the Gods, increasers of Truth" (*viśve devā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—these are the triplets.
The *marutvatīya* śastra begins with the verse "Where is that hero? (*kva sya vīraḥ*).
ŚŚS 11.8.5: At this [verse], "etāyām" (RV 10.178.1), the Niṣkevalya hymn is recited.
ŚŚS 11.8.6: From the third [verse] onwards, the Sāvitra and Dyāvāpṛthivīya [hymns] follow.
ŚŚS 11.8.7: With "pra vaḥ sphāraṃ," "kraṃsate," and "citra it śiśoḥ," the Āgnimāruta [section] is performed.

ŚŚS 11.9.1: "O friends, together for you..."—this is the *ājya* [stotra] of the *pṛṣṭha*; in all cases, one should omit the final verse. ŚŚS 11.9.2: The *prauga* [stotra] is to be contracted. ŚŚS 11.9.3: "O Vāyu, come hither with your beautiful chariot, broad-shining," or "When today the sun has risen, against you two, O Sun having risen," or "O you who are dear to many, come to us with your bay horses," or "O All-Gods, come hither"—these are the three triplets belonging to the Bhāradvāja [school].
ŚŚS 11.9.4: "Great is Indra, like a man" is the Marutvatīya [śastra]. ŚŚS 11.9.5: "He who is born" is the Niṣkevalya [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.9.6: From the second [verse], the Sāvitra [śastra] is derived.
ŚŚS 11.9.7: "abudhram u tya" is for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.9.8: "dhārāvarās tvam agne dyubhiḥ" is for the Āgnimāruta [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.9.9: "indra dṛhya" is for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra] on the second Abhiplava of the sixth day.
On the third [day], "uṣāsā naktā" (ŚŚS 11.9.10);
on the fourth, "agnir indra" (ŚŚS 11.9.11);
or alternatively, "śam na indrāgnī" (ŚŚS 11.9.12).
ŚŚS 11.9.13: Or [the first day is] the first in the preceding section, and the second in the subsequent one.
ŚŚS 11.9.14: "From afar" (*parāvata*) is [the *sāman*] on the fifth day.
ŚŚS 11.10.1: The *Abhijit* is an *agniṣṭoma* sacrifice with all *stomas*, having both *sāmans*, and either the *rathantara-pṛṣṭha* or the *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha*.
ŚŚS 11.10.2: "pra vo devāya yad vāhiṣṭham" is the *ājya* [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.10.3: Both the *prauga* [śastras] belong to Mādhucchandasa and Gārtsamada.
ŚŚS 11.10.4: The former *ṛc*-triplets belong to Mādhucchandasa, and the latter ones belong to Gārtsamada.
ŚŚS 11.10.5: Or, for the Gārtsamadas, it is the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.10.6: Or, the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana) is that of the one-day sacrifice (aikāhika).
ŚŚS 11.10.7: After the Marutvatīya [śastra], [the recitation] begins with "O Indra, drink! For thee the juice is pressed for intoxication," which belongs to the one-day sacrifice.
ŚŚS 11.10.8: [The verse] beginning with *yā ta ūtiḥ* is taken from the Niṣkevalya hymn.
ŚŚS 11.10.9: However, when the Bṛhat-sāman is used as the Pṛṣṭha-stotra, [the verses are taken] from the preceding [hymn]. ŚŚS 11.10.10: Or [they may be taken] from a single hymn.
"Drink the Soma; praise him indeed"—with these words, he omits the final verse of the preceding [hymn]. The third pressing belongs to the one-day sacrifice (ekāha).
The Svarasāmans have the seventeenfold stoma. The Rathantara is the *pṛṣṭha* of the first day, the Bṛhat of the second, and the third has both as its *sāman*, with the Rathantara as the *pṛṣṭha*.
According to Kauṣītaki, they have the Svarasāmans as their *pṛṣṭhas*.
The *pavamāna* stotras are performed with the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans];
according to Paiṅgya, they are *agniṣṭoma*s;
according to Kauṣītaki, they are *ukthya*s.
ŚŚS 11.11.7: "With sacrifices, O Agni, [attain] great vigor, the most powerful"—these are the *ājya* verses everywhere, excluding the final ones.
ŚŚS 11.11.8: Those which belong to the first three-day period are the *prauga* hymns.
ŚŚS 11.11.9: "Where is that hero? is the *marutvatīya* for the first *svara-sāman*; "With what splendor? is the *gāyat-sāman* for the second; and "With what [splendor]? is for the third.
Having recited the *sāmapragāthas*, [he recites] the *kadvat-pragāthas*:
"kam navyaḥ" in the first [turn], "kad ū nv asya" in the second, and "imā u tvā purūvaso" in the third; and [the verses] of the *bṛhat* [meter] constitute the womb (*yoni*).

Having omitted the last verse of "yas te sādhiṣṭhaḥ," they sing "arvāk ratham" in the first [turn], "gāyanti tvā apād itaḥ" in the second, and "ud u naś citratama indraṃ viśvāḥ saṃ ca tve jagmuḥ" in the third.

Thus [are the verses] for those whose *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara*. ŚŚS 11.11.14: "When you were born, O unprecedented one" (*yaj jāyathā apūrvya*) is the *stotriya* for those whose *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *Svara-sāmans*. ŚŚS 11.11.15: "O Indra, of wondrous virility" (*yad indra citra mehana*)—these two verses—and "Which, O Indra, are your enjoyments" (*yā indra bhujaḥ*)—this is the third verse of the *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 11.11.16: Or, for the second [verse], one uses "matsy apāyi te mahaḥ";
one makes the first [verse] the third. ŚŚS 11.11.17: "Matsi no vasyaiṣṭaye. (Or: "vasyaiṣṭaye.")
Thus, "dve vayam gha tvā" is the third [verse] of the *anurūpa*;
or alternatively, "praty asmai pipīṣate" is the third of the third [stotra].
One performs the fourth [verse] as the third.

ŚŚS 11.11.19: "Drink this pressed [soma], O Indra"—these two verses; "Who knows him? is the third verse of the *anurūpa*. ŚŚS 11.12.1: From whatever [meter] the *stotriya* is composed in *bṛhatī*, from that same meter the *anurūpa* should be made.
ŚŚS 11.12.2: Having recited the *dhāyyā* and the *kadvat* verses, one should recite the *yoni* of the *rathantara* on the first day, that of the *bṛhat* on the second, and those of both on the third.
ŚŚS 11.12.3: In all cases, the *pūrvā* verses of the *rathantara* [sāman] are used. ŚŚS 11.12.4:

On the first day, they chant the two verses beginning with *yad indra dadhiṣe*; on the second day, the verse beginning with *svaranti tvā*; and on the third day, the verse beginning with *dānā mṛgo na vāraṇaḥ*. ŚŚS 11.12.5:
From the nine verses beginning with *indra tubhyam in maghavan*, three verses each are used daily, along with the *pūrva* hymns.
ŚŚS 11.12.6: Or, having extracted the *ṛcas*, he recites both types of hymns (*sūktas*).
ŚŚS 11.12.7: And [he recites] the *ūhas* in the places where the original melodies (*svarayonis*) occur.
ŚŚS 11.12.8: Or, prior to the *ṛca* in the *anuṣṭubh* meter, he recites it together with a *pragātha*.
ŚŚS 11.12.9: From the first three-day period onwards, the third pressings belong to those [days] that have the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* as their *pṛṣṭha* chants.
ŚŚS 11.12.10: And the opening verses (*pratipad*) belong to those [days] that have the *svara* as their *pṛṣṭha*.
ŚŚS 11.12.11: And [this applies] to those [days] whose *sāman* originates from the *svara* [verse].
ŚŚS 11.12.12: From the third day of the middle [period], having extracted those beginning with the *anucara* that have become confused;
ŚŚS 11.12.13: Having extracted the final hymns of the *vaiśvadeva* [sections] and the triplet "pra vaḥ pāntam raghumanyavaḥ," he performs [the rite] with "tam pratnathā kad itthā.
ŚŚS 11.12.14: Or, on the first [day], [he performs it] with "agann indraḥ."
"pra ye śumbhante" is for the Maruts;
"devān huve" is for the second [offering];
"uṣāsā naktā" is for the third.
The Viṣuvat [day] is an Agniṣṭoma characterized by the twenty-one-fold stoma, the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, or the Mahā-divākīrtya. Having concluded it before the setting of the sun,
the morning litany (prātar-anuvāka) is recited after sunrise.
ŚŚS 11.13.4: Or [he may recite] according to the natural order.
ŚŚS 11.13.5: When the sun has risen, he begins the morning litany (*prātar-anuvāka*) with the verse, "I deem Agni to be my father.
ŚŚS 11.13.6: He should recite either one hundred verses, or one thousand, or two thousand.
ŚŚS 11.13.7: The *āprī* hymn of Vasiṣṭha.
ŚŚS 11.13.8: A solar animal is to be offered at the *savanīya*.

ŚŚS 11.13.9: "The bright [face] of the gods" (*citram devānām*)—these three verses are the invitatory prayers (*puronuvākyā*), and the following one is the offering prayer (*yājyā*) for the solar animal.
In a whisper.
"From the ocean, a wave..."—this is the *ājya* [verse].
The *praüga* is in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
ŚŚS 11.13.13: From the middle *chandoma*, one takes three *ṛc*s—the first and the last.
ŚŚS 11.13.14: From the first [chandoma], one takes three.
ŚŚS 11.13.15: In the *āśvina* [śastra], however, the third [verse] is the *bhānumatī*.
"May the supreme Brahman come from its seat," this is for the Vaiśvadeva [offering].
Or, the morning pressing may consist of the [hymns] belonging to the one-day sacrifice (aikāhika).
Or, its Ājya [stotra] consists of "Forward to your god" and "For you indeed are the lord of the dwelling."
And [the hymn] of Mādhucchandas;
"With what [splendor]? (kayā śubhā), "This one" (tyam sumeṣam), "He was born, O fierce one" (janiṣṭhā ugra)—these constitute the Marutvatīya [stotra].
"As if stretching toward the sun" (śrāyanta iva sūryam) is the stotriya verse in the Bṛhatī meter, which has the Aśva as its source.
ŚŚS 11.13.22: "yad dyāva indra" is the *anurūpa* (responding verse). ŚŚS 11.13.23: Or [it may be] the *mahādivākīrtya*.
ŚŚS 11.13.24: "citram devānām" is the *stotriya* (strophe) of the *mahādivākīrtya*.
And [the verses] following;
"ut sūryo bṛhad arcīṃṣi" is for the third *anurūpa*;
or else, "baṇ mahān" and "ud u tyad darśatam" are the two *pragāthas* serving as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 11.13.28: *vibhrāḍ bṛhat* is the *stotriya*; *vi sūryo madhye* is the *anurūpa*. ŚŚS 11.13.29: Or else, *viśvāhā tvā sumanasaḥ* [is the *anurūpa*].
ŚŚS 11.13.30: *baṇ mahān asi* is the *sāmapragātha*.
ŚŚS 11.13.31: Or [one may recite] "He who truly slays, the far-seeing one. ŚŚS 11.13.32: [One should recite] the *yoni* of the *rathantara* in the *bṛhat* which is its own *yoni*.
ŚŚS 11.13.33: [One should recite] the *yoni* of both in that which is not their own *yoni*.
And also at the Mahādivākīrtya.
If the Sāman-singers should perform these two during the Pavamāna, one should recite them; if they are not being performed, one should not recite them.
"Indraḥ kila" and so forth are the verses for the beginning of the *uktha*; "śaṃ no bhava cakṣasā" is [the verse] for the *mahādivākīrtya* [stotra];
"dyaur na ya indra" is the hymn in its own source, the *bṛhatī*.
ŚŚS 11.14.6: "ya eka id dhavyaḥ" [is used] when the *asvayoni* [sāman] is employed;
ŚŚS 11.14.7: and also in the *mahādivākīrtya*;
ŚŚS 11.14.8: "tam u ṣṭuhi" [is used] when the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* have been extracted.
ŚŚS 11.14.9: *abhi tyam meṣam*.
ŚŚS 11.14.10: Having recited the nine [verses] beginning with *ṛtur janitrī yasya*, one should recite the *nivid* of the *sarvaharit* hymn.
ŚŚS 11.14.11: *ā satyo yātu*.
Having set aside the final verse of the *viśvajit*,
he calls for the response and ascends the *dūrohaṇa*.

He recites [the verse] "The swan dwelling in purity" (*haṃsaḥ śuciṣat*) by quarters, by half-verses, three times by quarters without taking breath, three times by quarters and half-verses, and then by quarters.
Having recited the *uttamā* [verse], [he recites]:
ŚŚS 11.14.16: *eṣa pra pūrvīḥ*;
ŚŚS 11.14.17: *pataṅgam aktam*.
"Urūṃ naḥ";
"iti paiṅgyam";
now follows the Kauṣītaka.
It is the same as up to the *ukthya-mukhīyā* verse.
ŚŚS 11.14.22: The *ṛturjanitrīya* [is used] when the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* have been extracted. ŚŚS 11.14.23: Of that very [sāman], there are eleven [verses] in its own source (*svayoni*).

ŚŚS 11.14.24: Nine [verses] elsewhere. ŚŚS 11.14.25: Having extracted fifteen verses beginning with "Come, O Indra, with thy bay steeds," one recites the Sāvya [hymn]. ŚŚS 11.14.26: Having recited eleven verses of the *vara*, one inserts the *nivid*.
ŚŚS 11.14.27: *abhūr ekaḥ* is in place of *sāvyasya*.
ŚŚS 11.14.28: *tārkṣyaḥ pūrvaḥ pataṅgāt*.
ŚŚS 11.14.29: One hundred and one [verses] for the *niṣkevalya*.
From the first [verse], the Sāvitra;
from the second, the Vyāvāpṛthivīya;
from the sixth, the Ārbhavamāruta.
"Devān huva" is the verse for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].
From the third [verse], the Vaiśvānara [śastra] begins.
"Mūrdhānam" and "mūrdhā divaḥ" are the stotriya and anurūpa verses of the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.
"Seated on the altar"—this is the Jātavedasīya [stotra].
The Svarasāman chants are repeated.
The Viśvajit is an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice characterized by all Stomas, all Pṛṣṭhas, or it may have the Bṛhat as its Pṛṣṭha.
ŚŚS 11.15.2: "agnim naraḥ" is the Ājya [śastra].
ŚŚS 11.15.3: "tvam hi kṣaitavat" is for the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha [stotra].
ŚŚS 11.15.4: The Praüga [śastra] belongs to Mādhucchandas.

The midday pressing belongs to the Caturviṃśa [Stoma]. Having recited the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses of the Vairāja [Sāman], as well as the *pragātha* for the Sarvapṛṣṭha [rite], the *yoni* of the Rathantara, and that of the Bṛhat; from the *anucara* onwards, the third pressing belongs to the Ṣaṣṭha [Stoma].

ŚŚS 11.15.8: *Kathā devānām* is the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra] for the *sātrika* sacrifice when the *bṛhat* is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*. ŚŚS 11.15.9: *Ā no bhadrīya* is [the *vaiśvadeva* śastra] for the one-day (*ekāha*) sacrifice.
ŚŚS 11.15.10: In the *viśvajit* sacrifice where all the *pṛṣṭha-stotras* are employed, the Hotṛ recites the *evayāmarut* hymn before the *māruta* hymn.
The *jagatī* verse is recited with the *nyūṅkha* insertion; or the *paṅkti* verse is recited with the *nyūṅkha*;
or it may be recited without the *nyūṅkha*.
"O Agni, of the sacrifices..."—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
[The following applies] to the *hotraka*s.
The ritual procedure for the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) is as follows.

ŚŚS 12.1.3: *ā no mitrāvaruṇā*, *mitraṃ vayaṃ*, *mitraṃ huve*, *ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā purūruṇā cit*, *prati vāṃ sūra udite*, *pra vo mitrāya*, *yad adya sūra udite*, *pra mitrayos*, *tā naḥ śaktam*—these are the *stotriyas* for the Maitrāvaruṇa cup.

"Come hither; we have pressed [the soma] for Indra; O singers, [sing] for Indra indeed. "For with Indra, Indra [is joined]; [Indra] with Dadhyañc. "Arising with vigor, shatter all [enemies]; [be] the sovereign ruler of the peoples. "We impel that Indra for the prize. "Great is Indra who [rules] by his vigor. "They yoke the bay horse"—these are the verses of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

ŚŚS 12.1.5: *indra-agnī ā gatam sutam; indre agnā namo bṛhat; iyam vām asya manas tā huve yayor idam; indra-agnī yuvām ime; yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijā; iyam vām asya manmanas tā huve yayor idam; indre agnā namo bṛhat*. "Praise him, for they are eternal"—this is [the rule] for the Acchāvāka. ŚŚS 12.2.1: In sequences of days beginning with the two-night sacrifice (*dvi-rātra*), the *anurūpa* verses are the *stotriya* verses for the following day, even when the *stotriyas* are identical.
ŚŚS 12.2.2: Or rather, [the *anurūpa* verses may be] those of the subsequent day.
ŚŚS 12.2.3: They call the final *tṛcas* of the *śastras* "paryāsas" (concluding verses).
ŚŚS 12.2.4: "prati vām sūra udite" is the paryāsa for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 12.2.5: Or, "kāvyebhir adābhya" may be used as the stotriya.
ŚŚS 12.2.6: Or, when the *stotriya* for the following day exists;
ŚŚS 12.2.7: "ud gha it abhi" is for the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*;
ŚŚS 12.2.8: "indra agnī avasā" is for the *acchāvāka*.
ŚŚS 12.2.9: Between the *anurūpa* and the *paryāsa* is the place for the insertion (*āvāpasthāna*).
ŚŚS 12.2.10: They recite the *stoma* with one or two [verses].
ŚŚS 12.2.11: With more [verses] in the case of the *trivṛt*.
ŚŚS 12.2.12: And [these verses are used] in the Viśvajit sacrifice where all the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are employed.
ŚŚS 12.2.13: On the tenth day, [the verse] beginning with *ekayā*.

ŚŚS 12.2.14: The *ekapātinī* verses are: *yuvam dakṣam*, *ā no barhiḥ*, *riśādaso yam rakṣanti*, *kathā rādhāma*, *ṛjunītī naḥ*, *mā kasya adbhutakratū*, *mitro na atyāhitam*, *mahi vo mahatām*, *somasya mirā varuṇā*, *te no santu yujaḥ*, and *pra yo vām mitrāvaruṇā mahitrīṇām*.
ŚŚS 12.2.15: The two triplets beginning with "kāvyebhir adābhyā no gantam" [are for the Maitrāvaruṇa].

ŚŚS 12.2.16: There are forty-seven Gāyatrī verses addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa among the Daśatayas; of these, the Maitrāvaruṇa [recites]. ŚŚS 12.2.17: There are forty-four Gāyatrī verses addressed to Indra; of these, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites].
ŚŚS 12.2.18: Here, "I invoke Indra and Agni, the bountiful slayers of Vṛtra"—this consists of six verses.
ŚŚS 12.2.19: "When the Soma is pressed"—these two [verses].
ŚŚS 12.2.20: "Upon the ears"—this one verse.

"Juṣethām yajñam"—these are seven [verses]. There are forty-six Gāyatrī verses addressed to Indra and Agni found in the ten Maṇḍalas; of these, the Acchāvāka [recites]. In the Viśvajit sacrifice with all the Pṛṣṭhas, [the stotriyas] are taken from the tenth day.

ŚŚS 12.2.24: Having made the stotriyas of the sixth day the *anurūpas*, they recite the *stotriyas* of the other five days. ŚŚS 12.2.25: [They recite them] in reverse order when the stomas are reversed. ŚŚS 12.2.26: [They recite them] in direct order when [the day] has become a one-day (*ekāha*) rite.
They enclose [the sacrifice] with the *paryāsa* hymns.
Regarding the midday libations, there is a modification:
they call the final hymns of the two subsequent libations "paryāsa" hymns.
ŚŚS 12.3.3: The midday [pressings] consist of two *sūktas* each. ŚŚS 12.3.4: The *ukthas* consist of four *sūktas* each.
ŚŚS 12.3.5: "O waters, forward! (*apa prāca*) is always the opening verse (*uktha-mukhīyā*) for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 12.3.6: "śaṃsā mahān yan na indra" is [the first triplet] for the second [day].
ŚŚS 12.3.7: "yudhmasya te kathā mahām" is [the first triplet] for the third [day].
ŚŚS 12.3.8: "pra vo mahe mahivr̥dhe bharadhvam" and "yajāmahe indram" are the two triplets.
ŚŚS 12.3.9: "sadyo hā na indro dūrād ā na āsāt" is for the fourth [day].
ŚŚS 12.3.10: The two triplets beginning with "pro asmā ubhe" and "yad indra" [are used].
ŚŚS 12.3.11: "garbhe nu san" and "kā suṣṭutiḥ" are for the fifth [day].
ŚŚS 12.3.12: "indrāya hi dyauḥ" is a triplet.
ŚŚS 12.3.13: "ā naḥ stuta upa vājebhir ūtyā satyo yātu" is used on the sixth day.
ŚŚS 12.3.14: That is the *ahīna* hymn.
ŚŚS 12.3.15: In the middle three-day period, they call the *tṛcas* "artistic" (*śilpa*).
ŚŚS 12.3.16: Whatever [verse] is other than the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses and the *tṛcas*, that should be understood as being indicated by the general rule (*pradeśa*).
ŚŚS 12.3.17: That which is the *śastra* of the first two days belongs to all [the *tṛcas*] in the first *chandoma*.
ŚŚS 12.3.18: That which [is prescribed] for the third and fifth [verses] should be used in the middle [turn].
ŚŚS 12.3.19: That which [is prescribed] for the fourth and sixth [verses] should be used in the last [turn].
ŚŚS 12.3.20: At the point where the Hotṛ recites the *anīka-sūkta* beginning with "tvam mahān indra tubhyam ha," [the procedure applies].
ŚŚS 12.3.21: *tve ha yat pitaraś cin na indra* (thus) is the twenty-one-verse hymn [to be recited] during the Chandomas, prior to the Paryāsa.
ŚŚS 12.3.22: On the tenth day, the Stotriya and Anurūpa Pragāthas for this [hymn] are *mā cid anyad vi śaṃsata* and *mā bhema mā amiṣma*.
ŚŚS 12.3.23: And the two-footed verse is *ā dhūrṣv asmai*.

ŚŚS 12.4.1: Following the *anurūpa* verse of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, there is a *pragātha* containing a *kadvat* verse, which takes the place of the [verse] belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*).
ŚŚS 12.4.2: And "brahmaṇā te" is the opening verse of the *uktha*.
ŚŚS 12.4.3: "ud u brahmāṇi" is always the concluding verse (*paryāsa*).
ŚŚS 12.4.4: On the third day, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* are "vayam gha tvā" and "ka īm veda. ŚŚS 12.4.5: And [these same two] are used on the first two *chandoma* days.
ŚŚS 12.4.6: However, they are reversed on the middle [day].
ŚŚS 12.4.7: "O Indra, whether from the east, the west, or the north"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 12.4.8: "O Adhvaryus, bring [the offering] for Indra"—this is the eleventh [verse] in the third [turn].
ŚŚS 12.4.9: "Against all hostile armies"—this is the *stotriya*.
"I invoke that Indra; he has been drunk for you—the great one—for this [sacrificer], for this"—this is the *anurūpa* verse.
"When, O Vasu, [will you hear] the hymn? and "He who with his voice [is] in dispute"—these two *ṛc*s [are used].
"He who alone is to be kindled"—this is used on the fourth day.
ŚŚS 12.4.12: *indro madāya made-made hi* and so forth are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 12.4.13: *ā yāhi kṛṇavāma* and *yo na indra abhitaḥ* are two triplets (*tṛcas*). ŚŚS 12.4.14: *yas tigmaśṛṅga* is [the triplet] in the fifth [day].
ŚŚS 12.4.15: *surūpakṛtnu* and [the following] are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
ŚŚS 12.4.16: *tvayā vayam maghavan* is the triplet (*tṛca*).
ŚŚS 12.4.17: *asmā id u pra tavasaḥ* is used on the sixth day.
ŚŚS 12.4.18: That is the *ahīna-sūkta*.
ŚŚS 12.4.19: *śrāyanta iva sūryam* and *śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for the *pragātha* in the final *chandoma*.
ŚŚS 12.4.20: *tvaṃ mahān indra yo ha* takes the place of the *ahīna-sūkta*.
ŚŚS 12.4.21: "Indraṃ stava" (Praise Indra) is [the stotra] in the Chandomas, placed before the Paryāsa.
ŚŚS 12.4.22: On the tenth day, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas* are "ud u tye madhumattamāḥ" and "ud in nv asya ricyate.
ŚŚS 12.4.23: Alternatively, the *stotriya* may be "trikadrukeṣu mahiṣaḥ."
The *anurūpa* is "And I invoke that Indra, the best, for all battles" (viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ).
And the two-footed verse is "Desiring wealth" (rāyas kāmaḥ).

Following the *anurūpa* of the Acchāvāka is the *pragātha* beginning with "kad ū nv asya," containing the word *kad*, which takes the place of the [verse] belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*).

ŚŚS 12.5.2: *uruṃ na* is the introductory verse (*ukthamukhīyā*). ŚŚS 12.5.3: *abhi taṣṭeva* is always the concluding verse (*paryāsa*). ŚŚS 12.5.4: *tvām id ā vayam* and *enam id ā hya* are the two *pragāthas* serving as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 12.5.5: "apūrvyā purutamāni" is [the first verse] for the second [turn].
ŚŚS 12.5.6: "taraṇir it tarobhiḥ" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 12.5.7: "ya ojiṣṭhaḥ" is [the first verse] for the third [turn].
ŚŚS 12.5.8: *yo rājā nakiṣ ṭam* are the two *pragātha* stanzas for the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 12.5.9: *sacāyor indra indra somam imam piba* are the two triplets (*ṛcau*).
ŚŚS 12.5.10: *sam ca tve jagmuḥ* is used at the fourth [turn].
ŚŚS 12.5.11: *svādor itthā hi soma* and *itthā hi soma* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses. ŚŚS 12.5.12: *yac ciddhi satya* and *yat tvaṃ śatakrato* are two triplets (*tṛcas*).
ŚŚS 12.5.13: *kadā bhuvan rathakṣayāṇi* is used on the fifth day.
ŚŚS 12.5.14: "ubhe yad indra" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
ŚŚS 12.5.15: "viduṣ te asya vīryasya" are three verses.
ŚŚS 12.5.16: "śāsad vahniḥ" is used in the sixth [turn].
ŚŚS 12.5.17: That is the *ahīna* hymn.
ŚŚS 12.5.18: "No one [has surpassed him]" (*nakiṣ ṭam*) and "Not thee, O Great One" (*na tvā bṛhant*) are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the first *chandoma*.
ŚŚS 12.5.19: "May he hear both" (*ubhayam śṛṇavat*) is for the middle [day].
ŚŚS 12.5.20: [The hymn] "yata indra bhayāmahe" is at the end.
ŚŚS 12.5.21: All [the verses] are *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 12.5.22: In the *chandome* days, [the hymn] "icchanti tvā" is placed before the *paryāsa*.
ŚŚS 12.5.23: And the *dvipadā* verse beginning with *ayā vājam* [is used] on the tenth day.
ŚŚS 12.5.14: And the [laud] belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*) comes first.
ŚŚS 12.6.1: Between the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya*, there are those containing *kadvat* verses, the *ukthamukhīyās*, the *abhitashṭīya*, and the *bṛhatīkāra* for the *bārhata* [verses].
ŚŚS 12.6.2: Between the *ukthamukhīyā* [verse] and the hymn (*sūkta*) is the place for insertion (*āvāpasthāna*).
ŚŚS 12.6.3: From the *pṛṣṭhya* [six-day period], the hymns [are taken] for the *abhiplava* [six-day period].
ŚŚS 12.6.4: In place of the hymns of the *ahīna* [sacrifices], the hymns of the second day [are used].
ŚŚS 12.6.5: [The *uttara*] belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 12.6.6: From the first three-day period (*tryaha*), [the *uttara*] is used for the *svara-sāman*s.
ŚŚS 12.6.7: At the Caturviṃśa, Abhijit, Viṣuvat, Bṛhatpṛṣṭha, Viśvajit, and Mahāvrata, it is from the sixth [three-day period].
In the Viśvajit sacrifice where all the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are performed:
ŚŚS 12.6.9: For the *mahānāmnī* verses, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* are the *mairāvaruṇa* pragāthas;
ŚŚS 12.6.10: The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites] the *pragātha* containing the *kad* verse for the Vairūpa [stotra].
ŚŚS 12.6.11: The Acchāvāka [recites] the Revatī verses.
ŚŚS 12.6.12: The Maitrāvaruṇa [recites] the Vālakhilyas uninterpolated, six hymns excluding the Indra-nihava, and the Pragātha beginning with "ā no viśve sajoṣasaḥ.
ŚŚS 12.6.13: The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites] the Vṛṣākapi, omitting the Kuntāpa, without the *anyūṅkha* insertion.

ŚŚS 12.6.14: At the place of *dyaur na ya indra* [the *evayāmarut*], the Acchāvāka recites the *viṣṇunyaṅga*. ŚŚS 12.6.15: *abhūr ekaḥ* is the *sāmasūkta* for the Maitrāvaruṇa. ŚŚS 12.6.16: *yo jātaḥ* is for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
ŚŚS 12.6.17: [The verse] "pra ghā nv asya" belongs to the Acchāvāka.
ŚŚS 12.6.18: Having recited the Sāman-hymns and having recited the Ahīna-hymns, they conclude with the hymns belonging to the one-day sacrifice (Ekāha).
ŚŚS 12.6.19: For that which has become a one-day sacrifice, the Paryāsa hymns belonging to the Ekāha come after the Ahīna-hymns.

ŚŚS 12.7.1: While the *uktha* hymns are being performed, having extracted the *Vālakhilyas*, the *Vṛṣākapi*, and the *Viṣṇunyaṅga*, they recite the remaining portions during the midday pressings (*mādhyaṃdina*).
ŚŚS 12.7.2: The *ukthas* are from the sixth day.
ŚŚS 12.7.3: Now, if the third pressing of the sixth day is prescribed for a day that does not have all the *pṛṣṭha* stotras, the *ukthas* are from the second day.
ŚŚS 12.7.4: Following the *parokṣa* [recitation], the counter-arts (*pratiśilpa*) are performed.
ŚŚS 12.7.5: Having extracted the *vālakhilya* verses and recited the *aindra-pragāthas* beginning with "Drink of the flavorful pressed juice" (*pibā sutasya rasinaḥ*), ŚŚS 12.7.6:
having extracted the *vṛṣākapi*, the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin* recites the *aindra-paṅkti* verses beginning with "Indra for exhilaration" (*indro madāya*).

ŚŚS 12.7.7: The Acchāvāka [sings] the Viṣṇunyaṅga [stotra]. ŚŚS 12.7.8: Thus [is it] when the Pṛṣṭha [stotras] are performed indirectly. ŚŚS 12.8.1: Now, regarding the Viśvajit and the Śilpa [stotras].

ŚŚS 12.8.2: Having recited the *pragāthas* of the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*), [the Hotṛ recites] the *Vālakhilyas*, the *Vṛṣākapi*, the *Viṣṇunyaṅga*, and the *Nābhānediṣṭha*, either in their entirety or as *ṛcas*.
ŚŚS 12.8.3: Of the *Vālakhilyas*, he recites four *ṛcas*.
ŚŚS 12.8.4: For the *sāmasūktas*, the *ahīnasūktas*, and the *paryāsa* hymns, the *hotraka*s recite three *ṛcas* each.
Thus ends the modification regarding the *viśvajit* ritual artifice.
[One should recite] the triple-verse sections (*tṛca*) containing the *nivid* formulas,
and the triple-verse section beginning with "yuvor yadi."
ŚŚS 12.8.8: And the hymn beginning with "ye yajñena.
ŚŚS 12.8.9: The triplet beginning with "svasti no mimītām" is the Nivid-insertion point.
ŚŚS 12.8.10: And the triplet beginning with "evayāmarut."
ŚŚS 12.8.11: The morning pressing is according to the *stoma*.

ŚŚS 12.9.1: For the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*), the recitation (*śastra*) is arranged in triplets (*trca*) based on the threefold (*trivṛt*) pattern. ŚŚS 12.9.2: [This applies] to the initial triplets of the *ājya* hymns.
ŚŚS 12.9.3: [The verses] of the Nividdhānas are the last ones.
ŚŚS 12.9.4: One [verse] each from the other Sūktas and from the Śilpas. ŚŚS 12.9.5: But for the sixth [day], the Śilpas are the same as those of the Viśvajit-Śilpa.
ŚŚS 12.9.6: [The stotriya] of the Nābhānediṣṭha [is the same].

ŚŚS 12.9.7: And that of the Evayāmarut [is the same]. ŚŚS 12.9.8: If, during the Gavām Ayana, they should cause the Abhīvarta to follow for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin in the Aindra pragāthas prior to the Viṣuvat, that [verse] upon which they chant is the stotriya; the stotriya of the following day is the anurūpa.
ŚŚS 12.9.9: Or else, [one may recite] with a *ṣaṭpragātha*.
ŚŚS 12.9.10: On the third day, [the verses] are in the *bṛhatī* meter.

ŚŚS 12.9.11: "tam vo dasmam," "tat tvā yāmi," "abhi pra vaḥ," "pra suśrutam," "ā tvā sahasram," "ā mandraiḥ," "indra yo rājā," "nakiṣ ṭam," "na tvā bṛhantaḥ," "tvam indra yaśāḥ," "tvam indra pratūrtiṣu," "pibā sutasya rasinaḥ," and "adhvaryo drāvaya. Or [these are the verses].
At the Viṣuvat [day], the Ādityavrata [is performed].
"citram devānām" are the stotriya and anurūpa;
or alternatively, the Vikarṇa.
ŚŚS 12.9.15: *baṇ mahān*, *ud u tyad darśatam*—these two *pragātha*s are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for Vikarṇa.
ŚŚS 12.9.16: Alternatively, *indra kratum* may be the *stotriya*, and *indra jyeṣṭham* the *anurūpa*.

ŚŚS 12.9.17: The *paurumīḷha*, the *mānava*, the *janitra*, the *bhāradvāja*, the *śyaita*, and the *naudhasa*—these are the positions for the *abhīvarta*; they belong to *indra kratu* and occur after the *viṣuvat*.
ŚŚS 12.10.1: There is a modification regarding the *uktha* hymns.
ŚŚS 12.10.2: Those *jagatī* verses addressed to Indra that follow immediately after the *anurūpa* [strophe] are either the other fixed ones, or—except for the sixth—they are the fixed ones.
ŚŚS 12.10.3: "pra vo vājaḥ" and "pra vaḥ sakhāyaḥ" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 12.10.4: *pra sasrāje bṛhad indrā ko vām varuṇa* is for the Maitrāvaruṇa on the second day.
ŚŚS 12.10.5: *ā vām rājānau* is the *paryāsa* for the third, the fifth, and the middle *chandoma*.
ŚŚS 12.10.6: *purīṣe vām* is for the others.
ŚŚS 12.10.7: *pra maṃhiṣṭhāya gāyata* and *pra so agne* are the two *pragātha*s serving as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
ŚŚS 12.10.8: *dhīrā tv asya* and *indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya* are used on the third day.
ŚŚS 12.10.9: *agnim vo vṛdhantam* and *agnim stomena* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.

ŚŚS 12.10.10: "radat pathaḥ śruṣṭī vām yajñe" is [the first verse] in the fourth [turn]. ŚŚS 12.10.11: "ā te agne idhīmahi," "so agnir yo vasuḥ," and "agnim tam manye" constitute the *stotriya* (the hymn of praise). "ā te agne ṛcā" is the *anurūpa* (the corresponding verse).
"O Indra and Varuṇa, [you two] purify the *praśundhyū* for the sacrifice"—this is [the strophe] in the fifth [day].
"The *dvipadā*s [are used] for all [stotras] in the sixth [day].
"O Agni, you [are our friend]"—this is the *stotriya*.
He performs the fourth [verse] as the third.
"O Agni, be well-kindled" (*agne bhava suṣamiddha*) is the *anurūpa* verse.
And the *Vālakhilya* verses are recited separately.
In the first hymn, he recites by quarters;
in the second, by half-verses;
in the third, by verses.
ŚŚS 12.11.9: One should transpose the last [verse]. ŚŚS 12.11.11: At the conclusion, the former [verse] is first, followed by the *praṇava*.
ŚŚS 12.11.12: Having left aside the last [verse] of the *Tārkṣya* hymn and having called out, one performs the *dūrohaṇa* chant as at the *viṣuvat* day.

There are three verses beginning with "Our fathers were here" (*asmākam atra pitaraḥ ta āsan*).
On the sixth day, there is [the verse] beginning with "O Indra and Varuṇa, you for the sacrifice" (*indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya*).
ŚŚS 12.11.16: "ā te vatsaḥ manaḥ yamat" and "ā agniḥ agāmi" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the first *chandoma*.
ŚŚS 12.11.17: Between the *paryāsa* and the three preceding *aikāhika* [verses], there are five [verses]: "imāni vām bhāgadheyāni" or "yuvām narā paśyamānāsaḥ". ŚŚS 12.11.18:
"pra iṣṭam vaḥ priyo no astu viśpatiḥ" is for the middle [day].

ŚŚS 12.11.20: Alternatively, *ā ghā ye agnim indhate* and *imā abhi pra nonumaḥ*.
ŚŚS 12.11.21: *na hi te kṣatram* is the remainder of the hymn for both.
ŚŚS 12.11.22: "indrā ko vām varuṇa" is for the middle [verse].
ŚŚS 12.11.23: "śruṣṭī vām yajña" is for the last [verse].
ŚŚS 12.11.24: "imā u vām bhṛmayaḥ" constitutes three verses for both.
"Evā hy asi vīrayuḥ" and "evā hy asya sūnṛtā" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
"Yas tastambha" consists of six [verses] for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin on the second day,
placed in the middle of the hymns of the two subsequent *chandoma* days.
ŚŚS 12.12.4: The triplet beginning with "yo adribhit" is used everywhere prior to the *paryāsa*.
ŚŚS 12.12.5: "asteva suprataram" is the *paryāsa* in the third, fifth, and middle *chandoma*s.
ŚŚS 12.12.6: "acchā ma indram" is used in the others.
"ŚŚS 12.12.7: *tam te madam* and *tvām abhi pra gāyata* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* [verses].
ŚŚS 12.12.8: *anarvāṇam vṛṣabham* is used on the third day.
ŚŚS 12.12.9: *udaprutaḥ* is used on the fourth day."

In the first and last [stotras] consisting of meters, and in the sixth [stotra] after the triplets, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses are "Sing the *sāman* for Indra; sing it forth unto him. (ŚŚS 12.12.12)
In the fifth [day] and in the middle *chandoma* of the *yajñāyajñīya*,
the strophe is "imā nu kam" (ŚŚS 12.12.14),
and for the third *anurūpa* in the subsequent [day], it is "ayā vājam" (ŚŚS 12.12.14).

Having recited the *sūkta* beginning with "apa prācaḥ" (ŚŚS 12.13.1), which contains the praise of Sukīrti, Vṛṣākapi, and Paṅktiśaṃsa, he performs the *nyūṅkha* on the second and last syllables of the middle foot.
(ŚŚS 12.13.3) When [the recitation] has ceased, he performs the *pratinyūṅkha*.
(ŚŚS 12.13.7) Having recited that, [he recites] the Kuntāpa.
ŚŚS 12.14.1: Listen to this, O people! Narāśaṃsa shall be praised. We have given sixty thousand and ninety [cattle] to the Kaurama among the Ruśamas.
ŚŚS 12.14.2: He whose draft-camels, twenty in number, are provided with female mates.
The height of the chariot descends, seeking the touch of heaven’s light.
For this purpose, he has offered a hundred gold coins,
ten garlands, three hundred horses, and ten thousand cattle.
The inspired singers, like cattle roaming at will, hasten forth with their hymns.
Their sons are not bound; they sit like unbound cattle.
O singer, bring forth a prayer that finds cattle and finds wealth.
O God, mix this speech for us like an arrow that pierces the unheroic; O singer, sing forth, sing forth like a bird upon a ripe tree!
When lost, the tongue stammers like a razor in the hands of a barber.

Indra awakened the artisan: "Arise, go forth, you who are worn out! Ponder for me, the fierce one; every enemy shall be subject to you. "Here let the cows multiply, here the horses, and here the men!"
Even though Pūṣan has bestowed a thousand-fold sacrificial fees here, he sits down [in his place]:
"O Indra, let these cows not suffer harm; let not their lord suffer harm. O Indra, let no man hostile to them, nor a thief, have power over them."
O Indra, when you plunged into that superhuman battle of the ten kings, Virūpa was left behind for all; he indeed fell under the power of consumption.
O Maghavan, you made the youthful Naṃra, whose eyes were like those of a bull, submissive.
You, Vyāsa, struck down Rauhiṇa; you split asunder the head of Vṛtra.
They spoke to Uccaiḥśravas, the steed of the two bay horses, as he ran at the front: "O horse, bring Indra here for victory, he who wears a beautiful garland."
The Araṅgara speaks aloud, bound in three ways by a triple cord;
he proclaims the *irā* (refreshment) and drives away the *anirā* (want).
O Indra, you have granted protection and the oblation to the Pārāvatas.
You brought wealth to the praising Brahmin Dūrasravas;
O Indra, for the sake of the fleeing, wingless pigeon,
you provided him with much ripe *śyāmāka* grain and *pīlu* fruit.

ŚŚS 12.16.2: From here follow four *pārikṣitī* verses; in their third foot, there is a change of pitch (*vaisvarya*) on the first and fourth syllables. ŚŚS 12.17.1–1: "Of the king who belongs to all people, the god who is above mortals—may the *parikṣits* hear the beautiful praise of Vaiśvānara."
Having exhausted his security and occupied the highest seat,
the Kauravya, building a nest, speaks with his wife:
"Which of these shall I bring to you— curd, stirred-drink, or flowing liquor?"
The wife asks her husband: "In the realm of King Parikṣit, the ripe barley leaps up as if toward the sun, opening a path through the ground.
That person prospers with good fortune in the realm of King Parikṣit."
ŚŚS 12.17.2: He responds in the *vaisvarya* tone with "othā modaiva.
ŚŚS 12.17.3: This is the *etaśapralāpa*; it consists of twenty words; one should recite that as the *nivid*.
ŚŚS 12.18.1: These mares leap forward.
ŚŚS 12.18.2: *pratīpam prātisutvanam*.
ŚŚS 12.18.3: Among them, one is Hariklikā.
ŚŚS 12.18.4: O Hariklikā, what do you desire?
ŚŚS_12.18.5: The virtuous son, made of gold; ŚŚS_12.18.6: Where indeed has he cast him away?
ŚŚS_12.18.7: Where those three *śiṃśapā* trees stand.
ŚŚS 12.18.8: Three vipers are on all sides.
ŚŚS 12.18.9: They sit blowing into a horn. ŚŚS 12.18.10: A gourd has been buried.
He digs a pit;
he tosses it about with a harsh wind;
thinking, "I shall build a nest."
ŚŚS 12.18.14: The fierce one shall strike the stretched [drum]. ŚŚS 12.18.15: One who does not strike shall not strike the unstretched [drum]. ŚŚS 12.18.16: Who among them shall strike the drum?
ŚŚS 12.18.17: He licks; how does he strike?
ŚŚS 12.18.18: Again and again around the enclosure.
ŚŚS 12.18.19: With his hoof, he strikes the fat.
ŚŚS 12.18.20: With the *āyavana* [chant], [it is] the *tedanī*.
ŚŚS 12.19.1: O singer (*jaritar*), the Ādityas brought a horse as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) to the Aṅgirases.
O progenitor (*janitar*), they did not accept it; but, O singer, they did indeed accept it.
O singer, they did not accept it; O singer, they indeed accepted it.
Having departed from the day, they were without discernment; having departed from the sacrifice, they were without a leader.
But the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus praised it: "O Aṅgiras, accept this gift!"
O gods, may you grant this great and wide boon that is most excellent;
may it be in harmony with you, and may it be yours day by day.
Therefore, take hold of it yourselves.
"Moreover, O youngest one, you possess the swiftness of a white horse, and you surpass even those who run on foot;
furthermore, you bear a measure of speed.
Thus [says] Āditya Aṅgirasa.
"Thus says the chanter: 'Othāmo daiva! 'So says the chanter: 'Othāmo daiva!'"—in this way he responds to these [verses].
At the conclusion, the former [response] is preceded by the *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*), and the latter is followed by it.
ŚŚS 12.20.1: There are five arrangements of the directions.

ŚŚS 12.20.1: "He who is fit for the assembly, who is wise, a presser of Soma, a sacrificer, and a protector of men—those gods, O destroyers of enemies, have established him as the eastern quarter together with the sun."
That a son is born to a fortunate man who is steadfast—
that wise man has declared, that Gandharva has spoken as a desirable word.
He who spreads [the seed] among his sisters, he who seeks to harm his friend— [that is the one].

When the eldest is without wisdom, they call that "downward. And when there is a gambler who is not a slave, yet is wealthy and does not give to the priest— of that we have heard it said, "It has indeed gone away from the wise for all time."
And those gods who conquered, and those who yielded;
having gone to heaven like the sun, the Maghavans exult.
From this [arise] six human kalpas.

ŚŚS 12.21.2–1: He whose eyes are unanointed, who is not well-anointed, who has no jewel and no gold, who is no priest yet claims to be the son of a priest—he is a praiser measured only by ritual manuals. ŚŚS 12.21.2–2: But he whose eyes are anointed, who is well-anointed, who possesses fine jewels and fine gold—[he is the true priest].
Subrahmā, the son of Brahmā, is praised in the ritual manuals (kalpas).

And the well without a drinking-place, the pond, the Arevān, and he who is without a gift—these are praised in the ritual manuals. The auspicious maiden who is not to be approached is praised in the ritual manuals.
A well-provided drinking place, a pond, one who is wealthy and a generous giver;
a maiden who is beautiful, well-born, and commensurate with the sacred rites; a discarded queen, and one who is not barren and does not flee from battle.

The swift-horsed *yāmī* chariot, fashioned according to the ritual rules, is for the beloved wife; the *mahiṣī* chariot, together with *svasti*, is for one going to battle. The swift-horsed *yāmī* chariot, fashioned according to the ritual rules, is for the beloved wife.
ŚŚS 12.21.3: From here follow four *pravalhikās* and three *pratīrādhas*; that is the recitation of the *nivid*.
ŚŚS 12.22.1: "Two outstretched rays—man grinds them down.
It is not so, O maiden, as you think, O maiden."
ŚŚS 12.22.2: "Two streams from your mother have turned back from the man;
it is not truly so, O maiden, as you think, O maiden.
ŚŚS 12.22.3: "Having grasped both ears, you draw [the breath] out through the middle."
It is not at all as you think, O maiden; standing, you conceal yourself from her who lies supine. It is not at all as you think, O maiden.
ŚŚS 12.22.5: "In what is smooth, in what is very smooth, you conceal only that which is smooth.
Indeed, O maiden, it is not as you think, O maiden.
ŚŚS 12.22.7: "Whatever is deficient and whatever is excessive, all of that you conceal."
"O maiden, it is certainly not as you think, O maiden.
"Here, in this manner, they have reviled one another—eastward, westward, northward, southward, and crosswise.
Here, in this manner, the Vatsas and Pr̥ṣantas sit facing eastward, westward, northward, southward, and crosswise."
"Here, thus, eastward, westward, northward, and southward, the cooking in the pot dissolves;
here, thus, eastward, westward, northward, and southward, may they be prepared, may they be prepared.
"Bhuk!"—thus it is addressed.
"Śal!"—with this he steps away;
"Phal!"—with this he stands facing [the fire].
He sings the *alābu* verses.
The spotted deer, O Jarita;
the anthill of the ants, O Jarita;
the leaf of the *aśvattha* tree, O Jarita.
"O singer! The dog! "O singer! The leaf-dweller!
"O singer! The cow's hoof!"—having uttered each one of these, he always performs the response (*pratigara*).
ŚŚS 12.23.4: "These gods have prepared themselves; O Adhvaryu, proceed quickly! You indeed possess the true essence of the cows; you move forward. ŚŚS 12.23.5:
When the wife is about to sing, [the Hotṛ] responds to her in this verse: "O singer, *othā modaiva*; O Hotṛ, having performed the rite, *othā modaiva*. Thus he responds.
At the conclusion, the *praṇava* follows the preceding [syllable]. From here on follow the ten *āhanasyā* verses:
"When the gods revealed the lalāmagu who was hidden..."
The woman is indicated by her thigh, just as the eye is the seat of truth.
That which has settled upon her broad, firm thighs—
her two testicles quiver like two small fish in the hoof-print of a cow.
When he struck his testicles with a thick club,
they grew apart like two donkeys in the sand;
the Mahānagnī runs after the running Mahānagna.
"Guard these cows of his; have sexual intercourse with me; [eat] rice porridge.
The Mahānagnī runs around a cock with a wooden pin. "We do not know what beast it is that carries away the testicles with its head."
The Mahānagnī addresses [the animal]: "May the animal be entered by well-being! In this way, may we divide the winnowing-basket after the fruit of the tree!
As the Mahānagnī steps over the mortar, she says: [the same].
Just as they strike you, O Lord of the Forest, so do they strike me.
Truly great and auspicious is the bilva tree; great and auspicious is the udumbara tree.
The great one presses down upon the knee; it is well for the great to be struck.
ŚŚS 12.24.2: [The hymns] "kapṛn naraḥ" and "yad dha prācīḥ," these two;

With the *nyūṅkha* chant, having concluded the other [verses], one should chant the final verse for the sake of continuity.
"I have performed the praise of Dadhikrāvan" is the first [verse].
"The pressed juices, most sweet," "to him who is most generous," and "he who is the breaker of stones; down the drop"—these three triplets are for the sixth [day].
ŚŚS 12.25.3: *tvam na indrā bhara* and *tad indrāva ā bhara* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses. ŚŚS 12.25.4: The entire *pra maṇhiṣṭhīya* hymn is used in the first *chandoma*.

ŚŚS 12.25.6: “O Indra, come to us; here is the most intoxicating of the sweet [soma]” is used in the middle. ŚŚS 12.25.7: “Come now, let us praise Indra, O friends” is used at the end.

Ṛtu is the progenitor;
heaven and earth are his [progenitors];
now, indeed, of Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 12.26.15: *pra vaḥ pāntam andhasaḥ*.
ŚŚS 12.26.16: And [this applies] in the *chandome* chants.
ŚŚS 12.26.17: But in the first [of these], there are three [verses].
ŚŚS 12.26.18: And before the two subsequent *chandoma* days, [one should recite] the triplet beginning with "bhavā mitra.
ŚŚS 12.26.19: On the sixth day, having omitted the final verse of the triplet beginning with "nū martaḥ paro mātrayā," [one should proceed].
ŚŚS 12.26.20: On the first *chandoma*, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* are the two verses beginning with "yad indra citra" and "yad indra te."
"purām bhinduḥ" is [the first verse] in the middle [stotra];
the preceding triplet is the *anurūpa*, while the third [verse] is the first [of the next triplet].
"gāyanti tvā" is [the first verse] in the last [stotra].
ŚŚS 12.27.1: At the twenty-fourth [day], the *śastra* belongs to all [the *chandoma* days] starting from the first.
ŚŚS 12.27.2: That which belongs to the four starting from the second belongs to the four *ābhiplavika* [days].
