ŚŚS 12.27.3: From the third onwards, it applies to the *svarasāman* [days].

ŚŚS 12.27.4: Now, if they should perform the Abhijit, the Viṣuvat, the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, the Viśvajit, and the Mahāvrata day as Ukthya sacrifices, they should perform the Ukthas belonging to the Caturviṃśa day.

ŚŚS 12.27.5: Now, if on the first two days of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava periods they should perform the tenth day as an Ukthya sacrifice, they should perform the Ukthas belonging to the one-day (Aikāhika) sacrifice.
ŚŚS 12.27.6: They should perform the final Ukthya of the Abhiplava period; that which is the third pressing of the second day is [performed as] the third pressing.
ŚŚS 13.1.1: The Chandogas and Adhvaryus are the performers of the preliminary rites.
ŚŚS 13.1.2: If they should perform that which has not been prescribed;
ŚŚS 13.1.4: [This applies] to the stotriya, the chandoma, the day-connection (aharyoga), the modification of the stoma, the pṛṣṭha-stotra, and the concluding rite (saṃsthā).
ŚŚS 13.1.5: If they should transpose a quarter-verse (*pāda*) or a half-verse (*ardharca*), or if they should make it deficient or redundant, one should not heed that.

ŚŚS 13.1.6: One should follow only the transposition of the *ṛc*s themselves. ŚŚS 13.1.7: If a quarter-verse to be chanted with the *nyūṅkha* should be filled by means of a protracted draw-out (*vikarṣa*), one should count it and [apply] a second *nyūṅkha*-verse for it.
ŚŚS 13.1.8: However, after the *svara* [intonation], the consonants belonging to the same *chandoma* [section] shall be elided.

ŚŚS 13.2.1: If the sacrificial animal has been brought forward but dies before it has been dedicated (*anupākṛta*), one should sacrifice another; one should have that other animal prepared by the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*). ŚŚS 13.2.2: [If the animal dies] while it has already been dedicated (*upākṛta*) but is trembling.
"From whatever you cause us to tremble with fear, from that grant us security.
Protect all our cattle; homage to Rudra, the bountiful!
Svāhā!"—with these words he offers the oblation.
ŚŚS 13.2.3: "Out of fear of whom you have bellowed," when it bellows;
ŚŚS 13.2.4: "Out of fear of whom you have fled," when it flees; ŚŚS 13.2.5: "Out of fear of whom you have sat down," when it sits down.
ŚŚS 13.2.6: Because of fear of whom [the victim] was slaughtered;
ŚŚS 13.2.7: If it is lost, dead, or has fled, one should sacrifice another animal of the same form and dedicated to the same deity.
ŚŚS 13.2.8: One should offer the omentum of the dead animal, the sacrificial cake, and the portions of the other animal at the *vaṣaṭ*-calls.
ŚŚS 13.3.1: If the *prayāja* offerings have commenced and [the animal] dies, the sacrifice should be concluded with that very same [animal].
ŚŚS 13.3.2: If the portion cut off (*avadāna*) is lost, spoiled, or mangled, one should substitute clarified butter (*ājya*).
ŚŚS 13.3.3: In the event of the loss of the heart, one should immolate another [animal].
ŚŚS 13.3.4: And if he should desire, "May they meet with affliction and be crushed," he should offer an oblation in the Āgnīdhrīya fire with the verse: *kuvid aṅga yavamanto yavaṃ cid*. ŚŚS 13.3.5:

At the eight-footed barren cow (*vaśā*) to be offered as the *anūbandhyā*, having cooked the embryo, the skin, the omentum-form, and the *phalīkaraṇa* grains along with the *phālīkaraṇa* [grains] and the embryo in the *śāmitra* fire, he should offer them in the *śāmitra* fire itself at the *vaṣaṭ*-calls for the other [portions]. ŚŚS 13.4.1:
If the sacrificial post has grown over and has not been removed, he should sacrifice an animal of many forms to Tvaṣṭṛ.
ŚŚS 13.4.2: “*Piśaṅgarūpaḥ subharo vayodhās*, *tannasturīpamadha poṣayitnu*, *devastvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ*—these are the invitatory verses (*puronuvākyā*).
ŚŚS 13.4.3: “*Pra sū mahe suśaraṇāya prathamabhājam*, *deva tvaṣṭaryad dha cārutvam ānaṭ*—these are the offering verses (*yājyā*).
ŚŚS 13.5.1: When two Soma-pressings (*sutyā*) that are mutually hostile meet on the subject of knowledge (*jñānaviṣaya*), they call that a *saṃsava*.
ŚŚS 13.5.2: Having commenced the morning *prātar-anuvāka*, they should conclude it on the previous day. ŚŚS 13.5.3: They should offer oblations when the fire is well-kindled.
ŚŚS 13.5.4: At the morning pressing (*prātaḥ-savana*), [they offer] with the formula: "To Saṃveśa, to Upaveśa, to the Gāyatrī metre, to Abhibhṛti, svāhā!"
ŚŚS 13.5.5: "For the Triṣṭubh metre," [he says] at the midday pressing. ŚŚS 13.5.6: "For the Jagatī metre," [he says] at the third pressing.
ŚŚS 13.5.7: Desiring the Adhvaryu who has died, the Adhvaryu should offer oblations at the morning pressing with three verses addressed to Prajāpati.
ŚŚS 13.5.8: At the midday pressing, the Hotṛ [should choose] the Hotṛ.
ŚŚS 13.5.9: At the third pressing, the Udgātṛ [should choose] the Udgātṛ. ŚŚS 13.5.10: At each pressing, the Brahman [should choose] the Brahman.
ŚŚS 13.5.11: At each pressing, the sacrificer [should perform the rite] for the sacrificer.
ŚŚS 13.5.12: Desiring all [the priests] to be alive, they should all [perform it] at each pressing.
ŚŚS 13.5.13: They should perform the Bṛhat and Rathantara [sāmans].
The Ābhīka, the Ābhīśava, the Abhinidhana, and the Abhīvarta;
the Kayāśubhīya as the Marutvatīya;
and the Sajanīya as the Niṣkevalya.
ŚŚS 13.5.17: The Vihavya [hymn] belongs to the Vaiśvadeva [offering].
ŚŚS 13.5.18: While they are concluding with the former [sacrificial forms], one should perform the latter form.
ŚŚS 13.5.19: While they are performing the Atirātra, one should perform the Dvirātra.
ŚŚS 13.5.20: For those performing a two-night rite, it is three nights.
ŚŚS 13.5.21: Or, at that conclusion, one should give more sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās).
ŚŚS 13.5.22: Or the flowing waters, the wind, and space disperse.

ŚŚS 13.6.1: If the *soma* that has been purchased is stolen, one should not wait for the [prescribed] time; rather, having procured another [substitute], one should press it. ŚŚS 13.6.2: One should give something to the *soma*-buyer or to the one who brings the *soma*.

ŚŚS 13.6.3: If [the substitute] cannot be obtained, one should press *pūtīka* plants, white-flowered *arjuna* trees, or *kuśa* grass, and mix them with the milk of a cow that has just calved at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), with white curds at the midday pressing (*mādhyandina*), and with curds at the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*).
ŚŚS 13.6.4: Having given one cow as the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) and having emerged from the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*), he should undergo consecration (*dīkṣā*) again.
ŚŚS 13.6.5: Therein, he should give the sacrificial fees for the ritual (*kratu*).
ŚŚS 13.6.6: It is exactly this.
ŚŚS 13.6.7: If [the Soma] is burnt, one should give five cows as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 13.7.1: When the Soma is left over after the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana), ŚŚS 13.7.2: "This Soma is pressed"—this is the stotriya and anurūpa for the Hotṛ.
ŚŚS 13.7.3: One should recite the Stoma with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 13.7.4: The offering verse (yājyā) is one addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 13.7.5: [The verses] "Indram id gāthinaḥ," "Bṛhat," and "Ato devā avantu naḥ" constitute six [verses].
Having clothed [the sacrificer] with the *uttamā* verse, he performs the sacrifice with the verse, "Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu.
Regarding the *mādhyaṃdina* [śastra], when it is exceeded:
"baṇ mahān" and "ud u tyad darśatam" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas*.
ŚŚS 13.8.3: One should recite the *stoma* with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 13.8.4: The *yājyā* verse is one addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 13.9.1: This applies when there is a surplus from the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*).
ŚŚS 13.9.2: *pra tat te adya śipiviṣṭa* and *pra tad viṣṇuḥ* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
ŚŚS 13.9.3: One should recite the *stotra* with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu (*aindrā-vaiṣṇavī*).
ŚŚS 13.9.4: The *yājyā* verse is also addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.
ŚŚS 13.10.1: When there is an *atirikta* [verse] following the *āśvina* [śastra], ŚŚS 13.10.2: one should recite the *stoma* with the *āśvinī* verses;
ŚŚS 13.10.3: the *yājyā* is an *āśvinī*.
ŚŚS 13.10.4: If [the sacrifice] should be interrupted before being fully chanted with the *paryāyas*, they chant for the *hotraka*s using the five *stomas*.
ŚŚS 13.10.5: Having recited the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses, they should recite two *jagatī* verses each for the beginnings of the *ukthas*.
ŚŚS 13.10.6: The *paridhānīyā* verses are fixed (obligatory).
ŚŚS 13.10.7: Or with all the first rounds;
ŚŚS 13.10.8: or for the Hotṛ, the first rounds;
ŚŚS 13.10.9: and for the Maitrāvaruṇa and the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the middle rounds.
ŚŚS 13.10.10: [The verses] for the Acchāvāka are the last ones.
ŚŚS 13.10.11: There are three hundred and sixty [verses] for the Āśvina [śastra].

ŚŚS 13.11.1: If one who has been consecrated (dīkṣita) should die, having cremated him and bound his bones [in a vessel], they should consecrate either a son or a brother and perform the sacrifice together.

ŚŚS 13.11.2: Having pressed the King Soma but not yet drawn the cups, they place a jar of bones on the southern hip of the altar; in that place, they chant the *sārparājñī* verses, proceeding from front to back.
ŚŚS 13.11.3: Or [they chant] in the region of the *mārjālīya* fire-altar.
ŚŚS 13.11.4: They walk three times around the *mārjālīya* in a counter-clockwise direction, striking their left thighs.
The Hotṛ shall recite the Sārparājñī verses.
The Stotra is not measured by a fixed number of verses.
The cups [to be drawn] are those beginning with the one for Indra and Vāyu.
ŚŚS 13.11.8: After a year, they should cause the bones to perform the sacrifice.
ŚŚS 13.11.9: At each stotra, they place a jar containing the bones down [near the altar].
ŚŚS 13.11.10: They pour out the portions for consumption at the Mārjālīya fire.
ŚŚS 13.12.1: When the water-jar has broken, they chant for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with the *vaṣaṭkāra* as the *nidhana*, using the hymn beginning with "The moon fleeing" (*vidhum dadrāṇam*).
ŚŚS 13.12.2: The first triplet of verses is the *anurūpa*.

ŚŚS 13.12.3: When the pressing-stone has broken, they chant for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with the *dyutāna* hymn addressed to the Maruts, beginning with "Fleeing from the snort of Vṛtra" (*vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇāḥ*).
The *uttara* is the *anurūpa*.
One should recite the *stoma* with verses addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu. The *yājyā* is a verse addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.
The Nārāśaṃsa cup has been drawn up again.

O Indra and Agni, satisfy yourselves with what has been offered and what has not been offered, with this Soma that has been offered and not yet offered, and that which has not been offered and has been offered.
He offers with "Svāhā! into the ashes within the enclosing sticks.
When the Nārāśaṃsa cups have been carried near the wind, he should pour out a small portion of whichever cup he may have drawn last, saying, "To Prajāpati, svāhā!
The Adhvaryu should then pour the spoiled Soma into the northern half of the eastern part of the *uparava* pit with four verses addressed to Prajāpati.

Meditating, "The entire Veda is nectar; it is my portion of food," he should consume what has been rained down [into the cup], saying: "Indu has gone to Indra; of that which is drunk by Indra, being invited, I, being invited, partake.
(ŚŚS 13.12.10) When the cup has been brought near, he should offer an oblation with the verse, "Hiraṇyagarbha...
(ŚŚS 13.12.11). And having covered it, he should carry it away. (ŚŚS 13.12.12)
With the three verses beginning "ya ṛte cit," one should consecrate the broken Mahāvīra vessel with the mantra:
"The thirty-three threads which have been stretched out, who partake of this sacrifice with their own inherent power—of those, I join together this break; Svāhā! Let the Gharma go to the gods."
"The milking of the sacrifice has been spread in many places; it has extended across the sky in eight ways.
As such, O Sacrifice, milk forth for me great offspring. May I attain the increase of wealth and a full span of life.
Svāhā!"—with these words he offers two oblations.

ŚŚS 13.13.1: If one who has been consecrated for a *sattra* should depart from it, he should, after distributing the *soma*, sacrifice with the *viśvajit* *atirātra*, which includes all *stomas*, all *pṛṣṭhas*, and has the gift of his entire property (*sarvavedasa*) as the sacrificial fee.
ŚŚS 13.13.2: Or [he may do so] after uttering the *āgūr* formula.

ŚŚS 13.14.1: Those who have established their sacred fires, performed their first sacrifice, and are consecrated, with the householder as the seventeenth, should perform a sacrificial session (*sattra*). [The officiants are: the Hotṛ, Maitrāvaruṇa, Acchāvāka, Grāvastut, Brahman, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Potṛ, Āgnīdhra, Udgātṛ, Prastotṛ, Pratihartṛ, Subrahmaṇya, Adhvaryu, Pratiprasthātṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Unnetṛ.
ŚŚS 13.14.2: [This applies] provided there is no prohibition against performing the priestly functions (*ārtvijya*) simultaneously, unless it is impossible to do so.
ŚŚS 13.14.3: The duties of the sacrificer (*yājamāna*) for all [the priests] follow the sequence of their consecration (*dīkṣā*).
ŚŚS 13.14.4: The principal [priest] should perform the acts for the sake of others. ŚŚS 13.14.5: In case of a conflict between ritual rules (*kalpa*), the common practice of the majority prevails.

ŚŚS 13.14.6: When the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) have been offered, they should return day after day by way of the south, shaking black antelope skins, with the formula: "Here I lead myself as a sacrificial fee toward auspiciousness, fame, the heavenly world, and immortality."
ŚŚS 13.14.7: For the *uktha* [sacrifice], there is the *agniṣṭoma* with a thousand-fold sacrificial fee (*sahasradakṣiṇa*), which serves as the pacifier of the *pṛṣṭha* chants.
ŚŚS 13.14.8: Some maintain that the pacification of the *pṛṣṭha* chants is common to all.
ŚŚS 13.14.9: From the twelve-day sacrifice up to the forty-night sacrifice, these are the *rātrisattras* increasing by one night each; in these, [the *agniṣṭoma*] is obligatory.
ŚŚS 13.14.10: We shall now set forth those twelve days by which [the sacrifice] increases.
ŚŚS 13.15.1: For the purpose of a one-day rite (ekāha), they perform the Mahāvrata.
ŚŚS 13.15.2: Or they perform an Atirātra consisting of all the Stomas.
ŚŚS 13.15.3: Between the *pṛṣṭhya* and the *chandomas*.
ŚŚS 13.15.4: The *go* and *āyus* [stomas] serve the purpose of two days.
ŚŚS 13.15.5: In this injunction, one should understand the second and third [days] as belonging to the *abhiplava* [six-day period].
For the purpose of a three-day period, there are three *ābhiplavika* days;
for the purpose of a four-day period, there are [three] with the *mahāvrata* as the fourth;
for the purpose of a five-day period, there are five.
For the purpose of a six-day rite, there are six;
for the purpose of a seven-day rite, there are those with the Mahāvrata as the seventh.
By this principle, they complete each respective number.
The place for these [stotras] is between the *prāyaṇīya* and the *pṛṣṭhya*.
However, after the tenth day, the place for the *mahāvrata* [is reached].
Now, they exclude these [stotras].
The Abhiplava, the Abhijit, and the Viśvajit are the additional [sacrifices] in the twenty-night rite.
The first twenty-one-night rite consists of an Abhiplava, an Atirātra, and two Abhiplavas.
The latter [twenty-one-night rite] consists of a Pṛṣṭhya, the Svara-sāmans, the Viṣuvat, the reversed Svara-sāmans, the Trayastriṃśa, and the introductory Pṛṣṭhya.
The six-day period with the *pṛṣṭhya* stoma;
the thirty-third day which is undefined (*anirukta*);
the six-day period with the *pṛṣṭhya* stoma, beginning with the thirty-third day.
The *Trivṛt* day is unexpressed (*anirukta*).
They call the *Jyotiṣṭoma-Agniṣṭoma* the "Sessional Course" (*saṃsadām ayana*) consisting of twenty-four nights.

Having performed five *Abhiplava* periods three times, followed by a *Viśvajit* and an *Atirātra*, this is the thirty-three-night rite known as the "Ten-Day Period" (*daśarātra*) within the five-day cycle.

The twenty-fourth [day], the *abhiplava*, the *pṛṣṭhya*, nine days, the *go* and *āyus* [days], the ten-night period (*daśarātra*), and the *mahāvrata*: this constitutes the thirty-seven-night sacrifice.
The twenty-fourth [day], three *abhiplavas*, the *abhijit*, the *svara-sāmans*, the *viṣuvant*, the reversed *svara-sāmans*, and the *viśvajit*.
They call [the sacrifice] beginning with the Abhijit the "Nine-Night" (navarātra).
The Abhiplava, the Go-āyus, the Ten-night (daśarātra), and the Mahāvrata—
these constitute the fifty-night [sacrifice].
It is measured by a year.
Now, regarding the sixty-one-night sacrifice:
on both sides of the nine-night period, there are two periods of sixty nights.

Of those two, the one with the *uttara* (the latter part) reversed is the *śatarātra* sacrifice established by rule. It consists of fourteen *abhiplava* periods; of these, the first is a three-day period (*tryaha*), followed by a ten-day period (*daśarātra*), and the *mahāvrata*.
ŚŚS 13.19.1: The initiation for the seventeen-year cattle-sacrifice (gavāmayana) [takes place];
ŚŚS 13.19.2: or it takes twelve days; ŚŚS 13.19.3: they should undergo initiation one day after the new moon of the month of Taiṣya, or that of Māgha.
For them, the fast-day (upavasatha) occurs on the new moon of Māgha or Phālguna.
Those performing twelve days of initiation (dīkṣā) should undergo initiation four days before the full moon.
For them, the commencement (prasava) takes place on the fifth day of the bright fortnight.
Having performed the *prāyaṇīya* Atirātra and the Caturviṃśa [Stoma], they perform four Abhiplava [six-day periods] with the Pṛṣṭhya [five-day period] as the fifth;
that constitutes one month.
Having thus performed five months in this manner, they perform the Abhiplavas with the Pṛṣṭhya as the fourth.
And for nine nights;
after the Viśvajit, they enter upon the months beginning with the Pṛṣṭhya;
and one should repeat the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava [periods] day by day.
ŚŚS 13.19.13: And the Vaiśvadeva hymns belong to the final Abhiplava periods. ŚŚS 13.19.14: Having reached the Pṛṣṭhya [period], there are three Abhiplavas.
ŚŚS 13.19.15: That constitutes a month.

Having performed the *pṛṣṭhya* [ṣaḍaha] and four *abhiplava* [ṣaḍahas], they proceed for four months in that manner; then they perform three *abhiplavas*, the *āyus* [daśarātra], the *gavya* [daśarātra], the *daśarātra*, the *mahāvrata*, and the *atirātra*. Such is the arrangement of the days of the *gavām ayana*.
The year-long sacrificial sessions (*saṃvatsara-sattra*) have that [ten-day period] as their archetype.
In those sessions, there is a modification except for the ten-day period itself.
In place of the *pṛṣṭhya* [period], there is the *abhiplava*; that is the *abhiplava-ayana*.
ŚŚS 13.20.1: Regarding those who perform the *utsarga* (the ritual of release). ŚŚS 13.20.2: Those days of Soma-pressing that coincide with full-moon days should be omitted.
ŚŚS 13.20.3: Or rather, [they should be omitted] by means of both the New-moon and Full-moon sacrifices.
ŚŚS 13.20.4: Or they should perform the *stoma* with three verses each.
ŚŚS 13.20.5: Or they should omit one verse each from the *stotriyas*.
ŚŚS 13.20.6: [They should do so] for the *śastras*.
And regarding the *yajus* formulas:
those who are omitting a day [of the sacrifice] should perform the animal sacrifice of that day according to the *prājāpatya* rite;
or it may be the animal sacrifice belonging to whichever deity the *savanīya* [oblation] is dedicated.
ŚŚS 13.20.10: There, they bring forward the sacrificial oblations according to the animal sacrifice ritual (paśu-tantra).
ŚŚS 13.20.11: Their procedure is the same as that which is prescribed for those [oblations] being enjoined in the animal sacrifice ritual.
ŚŚS 13.20.12: On the following day, they should perform the stotriya verses as the anurūpas.
ŚŚS 13.20.13: [The procedure] is according to the purpose with the *atipraiṣa* formulas.
ŚŚS 13.20.14: And having risen, they should remain seated for twelve days.
ŚŚS 13.20.15: When both [types of verses] are being released, it is the movement of the assemblies.
In the Ādityas’ journey:
the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* *abhiplava-stomas* are in the first section;
the *pañcadaśa* and *trivṛt* are in the latter.
And the months [of the year] are in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya*.
In the sixth month, having performed three *abhiplava* periods, they enter upon the *pṛṣṭhya* and the nine-night period (*navarātra*).
In the place of the *Abhijit*, there is the *Bṛhaspatisava*.

ŚŚS 13.21.7: The Indra-stoma for the Viśvajit sacrifice. ŚŚS 13.21.8: Having performed the Pṛṣṭhya and the Abhiplava, [one performs] the ten-night period with expanded meters (vyūḷha-chandas). ŚŚS 13.21.9: At the Trivṛt-stoma, it is concluded with the Agniṣṭoma.
And [the days] Udbhid and Balabhid.
Having completed four months with the middle *pṛṣṭhya* periods, they enter the *abhiplava* periods in the middle of the *pṛṣṭhya*s.
[Then follow] the Go and Āyus [days].
And the Chandoma-daśāha;
[this is] in the Aṅgirasām-ayana;
the Trivṛt-abhiplava-stoma.
ŚŚS 13.22.3: They enter upon the months beginning with the *pṛṣṭhya* in the first section. ŚŚS 13.22.4: [They enter upon the months] ending with the *pṛṣṭhya* in the latter [section].
ŚŚS 13.22.5: [The chant is] for longevity, for cattle.
The rest is the same as the Ādityānām ayana.
Regarding the Dṛtivātavator ayana:
[they perform] the Pṛṣṭhya stomas one by one for each month.
The Viṣuvat day is the Mahāvrata.
For those [sacrifices] that turn back, there is one month for each of the Pṛṣṭhya-stomas.
There are Atirātra days on both sides.
ŚŚS 13.23.6: [The *viṣuvat*] is in the middle of the *agniṣṭoma*s.
ŚŚS 13.23.7: The year consists of ten-day periods (*daśarātra*s). ŚŚS 13.23.8: The twelfth [day] is the *viṣuvat* of the *sarpasattra*.
ŚŚS 13.24.1: The Kauṇḍapāyinas’ sacrificial session consists of consecrations lasting for one month.
ŚŚS 13.24.2: Having purchased the King (Soma) and having bound him [to the stake], and having performed the Upasad rites, they perform the Agnihotra for one month.
ŚŚS 13.24.3: They perform the New and Full Moon sacrifices for one month.
ŚŚS 13.24.4: One month for each of the Cāturmāsya festivals.

ŚŚS 13.24.5: One month for each of the five Pṛṣṭhya-stomas beginning with the Trivṛt. ŚŚS 13.24.6: An eighteen-day period, a ten-night period with the Trayastriṃśa stoma, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra.
He who is the *hotṛ* is the *adhvaryu*, he is the *potṛ*.
He who is the *maitrāvaruṇa* is the *brahmán*, he is the *pratihartṛ*. He who is the *udgātṛ* is the *acchāvāka*, he is the *neṣṭṛ*.
He who is the *prastotṛ* is the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*; he is the *grāvastut*. He who is the *pratiprasthātṛ* and he who is the *āgnīdhra* are the *unnetṛ*. The *subrahmaṇya* is the *subrahmaṇya*.
The householder is the householder.
When there is proximity of place and time, one should follow the authority of the primary rite, even if it is not local.
The other rites should be performed according to their respective locations.
They should desist from the *sāṃghātika* [rite] after one day has passed.

This is the *yajñīya* *atipraiṣa* accompanied by the *puronuvākyā*; the forms of the *tāyamāna* are: the *stotriya* for the Hotrakas on the following day, the verses containing the word *ka*, the *ukthamukhīyas*, and the *abhitaṣṭīya*. This is the application of the days for the *gavām ayana* itself.
ŚŚS 13.25.1: There are four months of consecrations (dīkṣā). ŚŚS 13.25.2: There are four upasad days.
ŚŚS 13.25.3: For four [days] they press the Soma.
The first and last months of the Gavāmayana;
the two [sacrifices] with twenty-eight [verses] and the Viṣuvat day—
these they call the "small Tāpaścita."
The consecrations (*dīkṣā*) last for one year;
the attendant rites (*upasad*) last for one year;
they perform [the pressing] for one year.
That is called the *tāpaścita*.
There are initiation rites (*dīkṣā*) for three years;
there are *upasads* for three [years].
ŚŚS 13.27.3: "They press [the Soma] three times.
ŚŚS 13.27.4: Thus is the Mahātāpaścita.
ŚŚS 13.27.5: There is repetition over many years in the case of the Gavamayana.
ŚŚS 13.27.6: Or, having omitted those [days] that are liable to be omitted;
ŚŚS 13.27.7: An Atirātra, a thousand days, an Atirātra—this is Agni’s thousand-fold sacrifice (sahasrasāvin).
ŚŚS 13.28.1: The Gavāmayana is the first year-long rite (saṃvatsara).
Now, [the sacrifice] for the Ādityas;
now, for the Aṅgirases;
[and] for those desiring offspring, the three-year [sacrifice].
By means of each one of the four *pṛṣṭhya* stomas beginning with the *trivṛt*, [one performs] three years each; thus for Prajāpati it is twelve years.
By means of each one of these same [stomas], nine years each for the *śaktyas*; thus for thirty-six years.
By means of each one of these same [stomas], twenty-five years each for the *sādhyas*; thus for a hundred years.
ŚŚS 13.28.8: For each one of these [five], there is a thousand-year sacrifice for the five hundred and fifty Viśvasṛjs.
ŚŚS 13.29.1: The initiation for the Sārasvatas takes place at the confluence of the Sarasvatī.
ŚŚS 13.29.2a: Having purchased the King (Soma), having fastened him, and having performed the Upasad rites.
Having performed the *prāyaṇīya* *atirātra* sacrifice and having offered the *sāmnāyya*, the Adhvaryu throws a *śamyā* (wooden pin) outwards;
having placed the *gārhapatya* fire there, he establishes the *āhavanīya* fire at thirty-six *prakramas* [steps] from that point.
The assembly hall (sadas) is circular like a wheel;
likewise the Āgnīdhra fire-hall;
the sacrificial post (yūpa) has its base shaped like a mortar (ulūkhala).
They do not dig out the *uparava* holes.
They proceed toward that very [new moon] during the waxing fortnight by means of the *āmāvāsya* sacrifice.
For them, on the full moon day, there is the *gaur-ukthya* sacrifice with the *bṛhat-sāman*.
They proceed by means of the full-moon sacrifice toward that very [sacrificial period] whose fortnight is waning.
For them, on the new moon day, there is an *ukthya* sacrifice with the *rathantara* as its *sāman*.
They proceed back against the current by means of the preceding fortnight.
Having offered a pap (caru) dedicated to Aponaptrī,
[he recites] "tad asyānīkam asmin pade" for the offering to Aponaptrī;
[this takes place] at the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī.
They also go to the Sarasvatī.
Among a hundred cows, they release a bull.
When the number reaches a thousand, then there is the rising.
ŚŚS 13.29.18: Or when all [the fires] have been extinguished;
ŚŚS 13.29.19: or when the householder has died;
ŚŚS 13.29.20: or having reached a place where there is a flow of water, they perform an *iṣṭi* sacrifice for Agni Kāma.

ŚŚS 13.29.21: Having given away in that [sacrifice] a mare and a man-cow as sacrificial gifts, they descend into the Yamunā for the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) at Kārapacava. ŚŚS 13.29.22: Thus ends the ritual procedure of Mitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 13.29.23: [The sequence consists of] an Atirātra, the Abhijit and Viśvajit [one-day sacrifices], the Go and Āyus [one-day sacrifices], the two Indra-kukṣis, and an Atirātra.
Thus for Indra and Agni.
Atirātra, Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyuḥ, Viśvajit, Abhijit, the two Indra-kukṣis, and the Atirātra;
thus for Aryaman.
ŚŚS 13.29.27: He should guard the cows of a Brāhmaṇa for one year.
ŚŚS 13.29.28: For one year, he should kindle the fire in a place that is not barren and where there are no thorny shrubs.

ŚŚS 13.29.29: After a year, having enclosed the fires and established them, the sacrificer proceeds along the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī river, offering a cake on eight potsherds to Agni at each throw of the wooden pin (śamyā).
ŚŚS 13.29.30: They descend for the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*) into the Yamunā after it has been thrice-sprinkled.
ŚŚS 13.29.31: Thus is the Dārṣadvata sacrifice.

ŚŚS 13.29.32: An *atirātra* sacrifice, a thousand threefold-day sacrifices (*trivṛt*), a year-long *atirātra*, the thousand-year sacrifice of Prajāpati—this is the thousand-year sacrifice, the thousand-year sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.1.1: In the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*) and the multi-day sacrifices (*ahīna*), there is a modification (*vikāra*) from the archetype (*prakṛti*).
ŚŚS 14.1.2: On whichever day a particular day, a *savana*, or the *hautra* ritual is designated, that [modification] applies to it.
ŚŚS 14.1.3: When there is no specific instruction, the procedure of the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*) is to be followed.
ŚŚS 14.2.1: One desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should sacrifice with the establishment of the sacred fires (*agnyādheya*).
ŚŚS 14.2.2: For that [sacrifice], there are eight stotras at each [of the three daily pressings].
ŚŚS 14.2.3: The *gāyatrī* meter consists of eight syllables.
The Gāyatrī [meter] is splendor and Vedic luster;
the Rathantara [sāman] is the pṛṣṭha [stotra];
the Brahman is the Rathantara.
ŚŚS 14.2.7: The Agniṣṭoma is a sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.2.8: The Agniṣṭoma is indeed Brahman.
ŚŚS 14.2.9: By means of this threefold, perfected Brahman, one attains splendor and the luster of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*).

ŚŚS 14.2.10: The *śastra* is arranged according to the *ṛc* verses. ŚŚS 14.2.11: Or rather, food is threefold—food, drink, and solid edibles—and [this arrangement is] for the attainment of all of that.
ŚŚS 14.2.12: There are twenty-four sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇā*).

ŚŚS 14.2.13: There are twenty-four half-months in a year; [this serves] for the attainment of the year itself. ŚŚS 14.2.14: For that [year], animals are to be seized for the *savanīya* sacrifice, namely: one for Agni Pavamāna, one for Agni Pāvaka, and one for Agni Śuci.
ŚŚS 14.2.15: A barren cow (*vaśā*) is to be seized as the *anūbandhyā*; such is the rule.
ŚŚS 14.2.16: Therefore, when the animals have been thus dedicated, [the sacrificer thinks], "Let me not depart from the *agnyādheya*.
ŚŚS 14.2.17: Following the morning *savanīya* cakes, he offers a cake on eight potsherds (*puroḍāśa*) to Agni Pavamāna. ŚŚS 14.2.18: Following the midday *savanīya* cakes, [he offers] to Agni Pāvaka.
ŚŚS 14.2.19: Following the sacrificial cakes (puroḍāśa) of the third pressing, [he offers] to Agni Śuci.
ŚŚS 14.2.20: The sacrificial cakes of the pressings are indeed a receptacle;
thus, he pours [the oblation] into that very receptacle.

ŚŚS 14.2.21: Now, as for the fact that a barren cow (*vaśā*) is to be offered as the *anūbandhyā* (the animal to be bound after the sacrifice), it is because the establishment of the fire (*agnyādheya*) concludes with Aditi;
ŚŚS 14.2.22: whatever is the conclusion of the fire-establishment, that very conclusion of the sacrifice he thereby effects.
ŚŚS 14.3.1: In this manner, the animals and the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) follow along until the end in the *haviryajña*s and the *soma*sacrifices.
ŚŚS 14.3.2: His weapon [is the hymn].
ŚŚS 14.3.3: The *ājya* [laud] consists of the triplet beginning with "yad vāhiṣṭham. ŚŚS 14.3.4: The *praüga* [laud] belongs to Mādhucchandasa.
ŚŚS 14.3.5: For the *hotraka* priests at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), there are three triplets each for the *stotriya*, the *anurūpa*, and the *paryāsa*.
ŚŚS 14.3.6: The *marutvatīya* [śastra] consists of the triplet beginning with "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the soma here" (*indra marutva iha pāhi somam*).
ŚŚS 14.3.7: The *niṣkevalya* [śastra] consists of the triplet beginning with "Thee, the most manly among men, with songs and hymns" (*nṛṇām u tvā nṛtamaṃ gīrbhir ukthaiḥ*).
ŚŚS 14.3.8: "O Adhvaryu, O hero, for the great [sacrifice], of the pressed juices"—this triplet is the *ukthamukhīya* of the Maitrāvaruṇa.
ŚŚS 14.3.9: The former belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. ŚŚS 14.3.10: The latter belongs to the Acchāvāka.
Of the *paryāsa* hymns, [he recites] the last ones:
"Up has risen this god Savitṛ with his golden [hands]," and "The butter-rich [milk] of the worlds..."
May Indra, together with the Ṛbhus who possess strength,
grant us well-being; may he measure out prosperity for us with his mind through Vaiśvānara.
"May the strengths come forth!
and "Praise with a song the kindled Agni"—these three-verse hymns (*tṛca*) take the place of the *vaiśvadeva*, *āgnimāruta*, and other *sūkta*s.
Under the injunction "the arrangement is by *tṛca*s," this *śastra* is to be understood.
ŚŚS 14.3.14: Or [the rite] may consist of a single-day performance arranged according to the *ṛc*-verses.
ŚŚS 14.3.15: By this, the two *agnihotra* offerings are explained.
ŚŚS 14.3.16: In the first [offering], there is milk dedicated to Agni.
ŚŚS 14.3.17: The offering to Sūrya is on the northern [altar].
ŚŚS 14.3.18: And the animal sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.3.19: A barren cow of such a description is to be designated as the *anubandhyā* (the cow to be bound after the sacrifice) for Prajāpati.
ŚŚS 14.4.1: One who desires splendor should sacrifice with the *punarādheya* (re-establishment of the sacred fires).
ŚŚS 14.4.2: For that [sacrifice], there are five stotras for each [of the three pressings].
ŚŚS 14.4.3: The *paṅkti* meter has five feet.
The sacrifice is indeed fivefold;
[this is] for the attainment of the sacrifice itself.
The *śastra* belongs to the *agniṣṭut*, which is entirely dedicated to Agni.

ŚŚS 14.5.1: The New and Full Moon sacrifices (darśapūrṇamāsa) are for one who desires food. ŚŚS 14.5.2: The Iḍādadha, the Āgrayaṇa, and the Soma sacrifice without the Pravargya rite are [for the same]. ŚŚS 14.5.3: The four Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifices are for one who desires all things.

And there is the Great Sacrifice (mahāyajña). At the conclusion of that [Great Sacrifice], the oblations of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices follow; and the animal sacrifices are offered to the deities of the [respective] Parvan festivals.
ŚŚS 14.5.7: And from the deities of the one-potsherd offerings, there are those to be immolated as supplementary victims (*anubandhya*) of such a kind.
ŚŚS 14.5.8: The sacrifice is the *Atirātra*.
ŚŚS 14.6.1: Prajāpati, desiring offspring, having performed austerity, beheld this sacrificial rite, the *Vaiśvadeva*.
He took it; he sacrificed with it;
having sacrificed with it, he procreated.
One who desires offspring should sacrifice with that [offering].
A beast for the Viśve Devas is to be immolated as a substitute for the Savanīya animal. A barren cow for Heaven and Earth is to be immolated as a substitute for the Anūbandhyā; such is the rule.
The recitation for the *trivṛt* [stoma] is as follows:
either it is arranged according to triplets (*ṛca*) or it is prepared in the standard manner.

Having emerged from the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*) and performed the concluding offering (*udavasānīyā*), the sacrificer remains seated during the *muni-sattra* sacrifice for four months, day after day; in the intervals between sessions, he performs offerings to Agni or to Agni-Viṣṇu.
That itself is the initiation (*dīkṣā*) in that case.
Prajāpati created offspring by means of the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice. Once created, they ate Varuṇa’s barley before they had been born.
Varuṇa bound them with Varuṇa’s nooses. Those creatures, having approached their father Prajāpati, ran to him for refuge, saying:
"Recognize that sacrificial rite by which, having sacrificed, we may be completely released from Varuṇa’s nooses and from all evil."
Then, in the fourth month, Prajāpati beheld this Varuṇapraghāsa, a two-night sacrificial rite (yajñakratu).
He took it up; he sacrificed with it.
Having sacrificed with it, he gratified Varuṇa.
Being well-pleased, Varuṇa released the creatures from the bonds of Varuṇa and from all evil.
Indeed, the offspring of one who, knowing this, performs the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices, is released from the bonds of Varuṇa and from all evil.
There are two Ukthya offerings.

ŚŚS 14.7.3: A victim for Varuṇa is to be sacrificed prior to the Savanīya animal. ŚŚS 14.7.4: One for the Maruts is to be sacrificed subsequently. ŚŚS 14.7.5: A barren cow for Ka is to be sacrificed as the Anūbandhyā; such is the rule.
Those creatures said to Prajāpati, "For what purpose have you created us for our food?
Thereupon, in the fourth month, Prajāpati perceived this sacrificial rite consisting of three nights, the Sākamedha;
he performed it.
With that [sacrifice], he sacrificed. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained food. One who desires food should sacrifice with it.
The Agniṣṭoma, the Ukthya, and the Atirātra [are the forms].
For the first [pressing] of the Savanīya [offering], an animal is to be seized for Agni Anīkavant;
for the second, for the Maruts Sāṃtapanas.
The Māhendra [stotra] is performed on the third day.
A barren cow for Viśvakarman is to be seized as the *anūbandhyā* sacrifice; it is of this kind.
The *śastra* recitation is according to the one-day (*aikāhika*) *pṛṣṭhya* rite.
ŚŚS 14.8.8: Or it is the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma] distributed [over six days].
ŚŚS 14.8.9: Or the litany on the third day belongs to the *viśvajit* sacrifice which has the *bṛhat* as its *pṛṣṭha*.
ŚŚS 14.8.10: And also at the *sautrāmaṇī* sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.8.11: At the Āyuṣkāmayajña and the Mahāyajña;
ŚŚS 14.8.12: At the Vinutti and the Abhibhūti sacrifices;
ŚŚS 14.8.13: At the Svarjit sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.8.14: And [the verses] beginning with "O Indra, O Vajra.
ŚŚS 14.9.1–2: Those creatures said to Prajāpati, "Upon what foundation, pray, have you created us?
Thereupon, Prajāpati perceived this sacrificial rite, the Śunāsīrīya.
He brought it; with it he sacrificed.
Having sacrificed with it, he became firmly established. One who desires a firm foundation should sacrifice with it.

ŚŚS 14.9.2: An animal for Śuna and Sīra is to be immolated as the *upālambhya* of the *savanīya*. ŚŚS 14.9.3: A barren cow for Sūrya is to be immolated as the *anūbandhyā*; such is the rule. ŚŚS 14.9.4: He gives twenty [cows] at the *vaiśvadeva* [offering].
Thirty at the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices;
fifty at the Sākamedha sacrifices;
twenty at the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice.
That is one hundred and twenty.
Or, there are one hundred and twenty days in a season;
thus, he attains that season.
Through the season, [he wins] the year;
and whatever desires are in the year.
At the animal-sacrifices of the Cāturmāsya rites.
On the previous day, the ritual pertaining to the animal sacrifice is performed;
on the following day, the Vaiśvadeva animal sacrifice takes place;
and following the animal cake-offering, the deities of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices are worshipped according to the specific seasonal festival.
ŚŚS 14.10.5: The *sviṣṭakṛt* offering pertaining to the animal sacrifice;
ŚŚS 14.10.6: With the exception of the places for the insertion of the formulas;
ŚŚS 14.10.7: Or, the *vājina* offering according to its proper place.
It concludes with the heart-spit rite.
At the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices, there are offerings to Varuṇa and the Maruts;
they raise the northern sacrificial post.
The Māhendra and Śunāsīrīya [offerings] follow the two subsequent ones. (ŚŚS 14.10.11) The sacrifices proceed according to their respective places.
(ŚŚS 14.10.12) And so does the Pitryā [sacrifice]. (ŚŚS 14.10.13)
ŚŚS 14.10.14: Or, the animals may be assigned according to their respective deities.
ŚŚS 14.10.15: This has been explained in the section on the Ekādaśinī. ŚŚS 14.10.16:
In the Mahāhavis sacrifice, there are the offerings for Ānīkavant, Sāṃtapana, Gṛhamedhīya, Krīlin, and Maitra.
ŚŚS 14.10.17: Or, at every ritual juncture (*parvan*), the sacrifice dedicated to Indra and Agni (*aindrāgna*) is completed.
ŚŚS 14.10.18: Everything else is the same as before.
ŚŚS 14.10.19: Alternatively, even when there is only one juncture and only one animal victim, the oblations (*havīṃṣi*) for Indra and Agni follow in succession.
Having invoked the *iḍā* pertaining to the ancestors;
from the *tryambaka* offering onwards, [the procedure] begins with the *anuyāja*s,
or else it follows the animal sacrifice beginning with the *manotā*.
ŚŚS 14.10.22: All the animal sacrifices have the same sacrificial fees as those belonging to the Soma sacrifices.
ŚŚS 14.10.23: The animal sacrifices [of the Soma rites] have the same sacrificial fees as the animal sacrifices of the Cāturmāsya [seasonal offerings].
ŚŚS 14.11.1: The Pratyavarohaṇīya [offering] is for one who desires firm establishment.
The Jyotiṣṭoma is modified according to one's intention. The Paśubandha is for one who desires cattle.
It has the eleven-fold stoma.
The *triṣṭubh* consists of eleven syllables;
cattle are of the *triṣṭubh* nature;
[this is] for the attainment of cattle itself.
"Drink the Soma, O fierce one, for whom you hasten; we have come, desiring cattle, to Indra"—this is in the *nivid*-insertion.

"The great, upward-directed prize of cattle, being praised, O Indra; we have come, desiring cattle, to Indra"—this is in the praise of the cattle; this is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
Also in the *udbhid*, the *balabhid*, and the *gosava*.
ŚŚS 14.12.1: Now, therefore, follows the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.12.2a: Indra, desiring long life, performed austerities.
Having performed those austerities, he beheld this sacrificial rite, the Sautrāmaṇī.
He took it;
he sacrificed with it.
Having sacrificed with it, he attained long life.
He then spoke this to the aged Bharadvāja:
"By performing this sacrifice, I indeed attained long life; you too should sacrifice with it.
Having sacrificed with it, Bharadvāja attained a full lifespan.
He who knows this and he who sacrifices with this [rite] attain the full span of life.
For him, the Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra;
the sacrifice is the Agniṣṭoma.
ŚŚS 14.12.5: The sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) are according to one's faith.
ŚŚS 14.12.6: In that [rite], there are three stotras consisting of the Trivṛt [stoma]. ŚŚS 14.12.7: There are three [stotras] consisting of the Pañcadaśa [stoma].
Three [stomas] of seventeen;
three of twenty-one— thus,
for the sake of ascending higher and higher.
ŚŚS 14.12.11: "We have heard of long life, reaching further and further. ŚŚS 14.13.1:
For that [sacrifice], a reddish goat for the Aśvins and a ewe for Sarasvatī are to be seized as the animal victims of the *savanīya* offering.
ŚŚS 14.13.2: A barren cow (*vaśā*) is to be seized as the *anūbandhyā* victim for Indra Sutrāman; it is of this same kind.
ŚŚS 14.13.3: When the animals have been thus assigned, they proceed with the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.13.4: Following the morning *puroḍāśa* offerings, having kindled the fire on the outside, they perform the ritual with *surā* and *soma*.
ŚŚS 14.13.5: Following the third-pressing *puroḍāśa* offerings, he offers a *puroḍāśa* cake on twelve potsherds dedicated to Savitṛ.
The sacrificial cakes (puroḍāśas) for the Soma-pressings are indeed a sowing; thus he sows in that very place of sowing.
Now, as for the fact that a barren cow (vaśā) is to be seized as the Anūbandhyā for Indra Sutrāman: the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice is completed in accordance with Indra Sutrāman.
Whatever is the completion of the Sautrāmaṇī, that very thing he effects as the completion of the sacrifice.
Some perform this as an Atirātra sacrifice;
it has the twenty-one-fold stoma, the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, and both Sāmans.
Its ritual recitation (śastra) is the same as that of the Viśvajit sacrifice which has the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha.
ŚŚS 14.13.14: Here the *haviryajñas* and *soma* sacrifices are concluded.
ŚŚS 14.14.1: The gods, desiring cattle, having observed a vow for four months, perceived this *udbhid* sacrificial rite (*yajñakratu*).
By means of it, they obtained cattle.
One who desires cattle should sacrifice with that [rite].
Having sacrificed with the Udbhid, if he should think, "Cattle have not come to me for a long time," he should observe the vow for four months and then sacrifice with the Balabhid;
verily, cattle quickly come to him.
ŚŚS 14.15.1: One who desires cattle should sacrifice with the Go-sava.
ŚŚS 14.15.2: It is performed with the thirty-six-fold hymn-form (ṣaṭtriṃśat-stoma).
ŚŚS 14.15.3: The Bṛhatī meter consists of thirty-six syllables.
The cattle belong to the Bṛhatī meters;
it is for the attainment of cattle.
Thirty-six thousand cows are the sacrificial fee for the Gosava.
ŚŚS 14.15.7: Or ten thousand [times].
ŚŚS 14.15.8: The Ukthya sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.16.1: One desiring splendor should sacrifice with the Ṛtapeya.

There are twelve initiation days (*dīkṣā*) and twelve fasting days (*upasada*). He should consume as his fast-food (*vrata*) ghee measured by the middle joint of the thumb using a cup made of *udumbara* wood. On the odd-numbered initiation days, he should eat rice cooked with milk.
ŚŚS 14.16.5: A Soma-cup [is the sacrificial fee] for the Soma pressed on the right.
ŚŚS 14.16.8: Reciting "Ṛta is truth," they should consume [the draught].
ŚŚS 14.16.9: At the insertion of the *nivid*, [they recite]: "Thou hast been born fierce for victorious power; how has he, the great one, grown? Whose [is he]? Of which Hotṛ?"

"From the truth of the one who rejoices in the truth, offspring [arise]; for from the truth there are many strengthening powers"—this verse contains the word *ṛta* (truth) and is thus the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
Prajāpati, desiring to attain this world, performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite (*yajñakratu*): "bhūḥ. By performing it with that, he attained this world.
One desiring this world should sacrifice with this [rite].
Prajāpati, desiring the intermediate world (antarikṣaloka), performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite, *Bhuvaḥ*. Having sacrificed with it, he attained the intermediate world.
Desiring the world of the intermediate space (*antarikṣaloka*), one should sacrifice with this [rite].
Prajāpati, desiring that world beyond, performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite, the *Svar*. Having sacrificed with it, he attained that world beyond.
Desiring that world, one should sacrifice with this [rite].
The sacrificial fee consists of twenty-one white horses.
This is the Vaiṣuvata day.
Sūrya, desiring splendor, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite, the Śukrastoma. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained splendor.
One who desires splendor should sacrifice with it.
ŚŚS 14.20.2: Twenty-one white horses are the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 14.20.3: This is the Vaiṣuvata day.
ŚŚS 14.21.1: The Tīvrasava [rite] is for one who desires to become preeminent through offspring and cattle.
"O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, this Soma is sharp and exceedingly strong; drink of it for the slaying of Vṛtra!
Sharpening your thunderbolt, fill your belly with the invincible, bull-like, and impetuous Indra!
Thus [is recited] before the insertion of the Nivid in the Marutvatīya hymn.
ŚŚS 14.21.3: *tīvrasya abhivayasaḥ* is used in the *niṣkevalya* [laud].
ŚŚS 14.22.1: *jyotiḥ* is the *sūtasava*. ŚŚS 14.22.2: *goḥ* is the *sthapatisava*.
ŚŚS 14.22.3: The Āyus, Grāmaṇīs, and Savas.
ŚŚS 14.22.4: The Saṃdaṃśas, Anustomas, Iṣuvajras, Śyenājiras, Mṛtyvantakas, Kṣurapavis, Śīrṣacchits, and the Mahāśyena are for the purpose of malevolent magic (abhicaraṇīya).
ŚŚS 14.22.5: In the placement of the *nivid* for the *Manyu-sūkta*, it is determined by its characteristic marks.
ŚŚS 14.22.6: Whatever *pṛṣṭha-stotra* they might perform as an act of sorcery, that same *pṛṣṭha-stotra* becomes the natural one for the one being subjected to sorcery.
ŚŚS 14.22.7: In the *iṣu-śastra*, the *Bṛhat* is the *brahmasāman*.
In the others, there is the *abhīvarta* [chant]. (ŚŚS 14.22.8) It becomes covered with peaks and mats. (ŚŚS 14.22.9) Bows lie prostrate. (ŚŚS 14.22.10)
ŚŚS 14.22.11: [They go] to the Āgnīdhra fire-altar with arrows.
ŚŚS 14.22.12: They lie down upon mats made of *dhāvana* grass.
ŚŚS 14.22.13: The sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is made of *śara* reeds.
ŚŚS 14.22.14: The fuel and the enclosing sticks are [made of] *bādhaka* wood.
ŚŚS 14.22.15: The sacrificial post is made of *vaibhīdaka* wood.
ŚŚS 14.22.16: The clarified butter is from cows that have been afflicted with disease.

ŚŚS 14.22.17: The pressing-skin is made from the hide of a cow that has been slaughtered as a funeral cow (anustaraṇī). ŚŚS 14.22.18: The two pressing-boards are placed upon the funeral pyre. ŚŚS 14.22.19: The waters that have flowed together into the funeral pit—they mix those with the *vasatīvarī* waters.
ŚŚS 14.22.20: With their joints smeared with poison, their bows strung, and their turbans stained red, they should go forth with swords girded.

ŚŚS 14.22.21: No one at all shall be able to master him; he shall live for twelve years. ŚŚS 14.22.22: No one at all can strike him down who practices counter-spells against those [enemies] by means of these [rites].
For one who desires to drive away the evil of the assembly hall and those who hate him,
the penultimate verses of the *śastra*s are omitted.
For one desiring offspring and desiring cattle, the *upasad* verses are used.
And the secondary penultimate verses (*upottamā*) arise as the *śastra* recitations.
The gods and the asuras contended with one another.
Those gods ran to Bṛhaspati, their domestic priest, saying: "Come to that sacrificial rite (*yajñakratu*) by means of which, having sacrificed, we may overcome the asuras."
He perceived this bull-sacrifice (*ṛṣabha-yajña-kratu*);
having sacrificed with it, he overcame the Asuras. Desiring to overcome his hateful rivals, one should sacrifice with it.

For the fifteen-fold *stoma*, the midday *pavamāna* is seventeen-fold; that is its form as a bull (*ṛṣabha*). At the insertion of the *nivid*, [the verses] are: "Drink the Soma, O fierce one, for whom you are the piercer; praise him who is powerful through his overwhelming might";
and "He who is the long-lipped bull, the bull of prayers—strengthen the bull of the people with your songs. Thus, it possesses the form of a bull, which is the characteristic form of this day.
Sūrya, desiring splendor, performed penance and beheld this sacrificial rite, the Vyomāna. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained splendor.
One who desires splendor should sacrifice with it.
For the seventeen-fold *stoma*, the *ārbhava-pavamāna* chant has the twenty-one-fold [stoma].
This one who shines yonder is indeed the twenty-one-fold; thus he endows him with his own form.
"O Indra, I shall praise you, the most ancient one"—these are the *nivid* insertions.

"By means of the sun he has made it known; that sun [has encompassed] wide expanses"—this is the *sūrya*-formula used when there is an utterance concerning the sun, and it is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
Vasiṣṭha, desiring food, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite, the *Virāj*.
Having sacrificed with it, he obtained food.
One who desires food and other such things should sacrifice with this [rite].
The first two Pavamāna-stotras have fifteen verses; the others have three.
It attains the Virāj metre.
"Śrī, Virāj, food, and that which is eaten"—this is for the attainment of *śrī*, *virāj*, food, and that which is eaten.

"O Indra, even from the great [host], you... and "O Indra, you who are king, and those gods..."—these are the *akṣaravairāja* verses used as the *nivid*-insertion; this is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
Indra, desiring self-sovereignty (*svārājya*), performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite, the Svarāja.
By means of that [sacrifice], having sacrificed, one attains self-sovereignty (*svārājya*).
One who desires self-sovereignty should sacrifice with that.
The first two *pavamāna* lauds consist of seventeen verses; the others consist of three verses each.
Those four stotriyas exceed the virāj;
through them one attains sovereignty (svārājya),
as well as the virāj consisting of syllables.
Uśanas Kāvya was the domestic priest of the Asuras.
Having eaten the food of the gods, he became distressed. He reflected:
"How indeed might I perform that sacrificial rite by which, having sacrificed, I might strike away evil?
He beheld this Uśanas-stoma sacrifice;
having sacrificed with it, he struck away evil.
One desiring to drive away evil should perform this sacrifice;
so too one afflicted with a disease of the stomach.
The morning pressing consists of the *trivṛt* stoma.
The *trivṛt* is indeed Brahman.
By means of that *trivṛt*—that is, by means of Brahman—they struck away evil from the front.
The midday [pressing] has a fringe.
That is the Virāj.
By means of the Virāj itself, he thus struck away evil from the middle.
The third pressing is the Trivṛt.
The *trivṛt* is indeed Brahman.
By means of that very *trivṛt*—that is, by means of Brahman—they struck away evil from above.
At the two *nivid*-insertions, [the verses] are "Tryaryamā" and "dyaur na ya indra."
ŚŚS 14.27.13: "When Uśanas came with thousands, bestowing gifts upon Uśanas Kāvya"—this is the *uśanavatī* [verse], which is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
ŚŚS 14.28.1: He reflected: "Having struck away evil, how indeed might I perform that sacrificial rite (*yajñakratu*) by means of which, having sacrificed, I might obtain food?"
He saw this sacrificial rite, the Uśanas-stoma, as the subsequent [offering]. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained food. One who desires food should sacrifice with it.
The morning pressing consists of the Trivṛt stoma;
the Trivṛt is indeed the Brahman;
the midday pressing has a fringe.
The Virāj is food to be eaten;
the Trivṛt is the third pressing;
the Trivṛt is indeed the Brahman.
ŚŚS 14.28.8: By means of that very threefold Brahman, they enclosed the food on both sides and placed it within themselves.
ŚŚS 14.28.9: In the same way, the sacrificer now encloses the food on both sides by means of that very threefold Brahman and places it within himself.
ŚŚS 14.28.10: And [the verses] contain the word "uśan."
And thus, for one desiring food and other provisions, there is this various stoma;
and also the *akṣaravairāja* [stoma].
A thousand [cows] with a hundred horses is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
"Indra and Agni, indeed, were disputing among the gods as to who was superior.
The gods said:
'If these two continue to dispute in this manner, the Asuras will overcome us.'"
"Let us learn that sacrificial rite by which we may bring these two into harmony.
They perceived this sacrificial rite, the "nest" (kulāya) of Indra and Agni;
with it, they brought them into harmony.
ŚŚS 14.29.2: By means of this, a Brāhmaṇa and a Kṣatriya should perform the sacrifice together, whichever one he is about to appoint as the Purohita.
14.29.3: Thus, the two bodies of the Brahman and the Kṣatra unite with one another.
14.29.4: The Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa are the two Stomas.
Agni is indeed the *trivṛt*, Indra is the *pañcadaśa*.
Thus, Indra and Agni joined their two bodies together.
"Mount thy two bay steeds; praise him"—this is the insertion for the *nividdhāna*.

"O Indra, drink the Soma with the tongue of Agni; like Agni, [drink] the dry forest, O Indra, with your weapon"—this verse addressed to Indra contains the word "Agni," which is a characteristic form of this day.
Now, Mitra and Varuṇa desired sovereignty (*vairājya*); one of them desired self-rule (*svārājya*).
They perceived this sacrificial rite, the *Virāṭ-svarāj*.
Having sacrificed with that, one obtains the sovereignty of others (*vairājya*), while the other obtains self-sovereignty (*svārājya*).
Also [the sacrifice] with the *akṣara-vairāja* [stomas].
The *jyeṣṭha-stoma* is for one of junior lineage who desires seniority.
The Bahiṣpavamāna consists of seventeen verses. This is indeed the eldest of the Stomas;
he thus yokes it at the beginning of the sacrifice.

"Thou hast been born fierce for the sake of the thousandfold victor; let us offer a beautiful hymn to you, the most excellent among the virtuous"—this is the *jyeṣṭha-abhivyāhāra* (mentioning the eldest) in the placement of the *Nivid*, and it is the characteristic form of this day.
The gods and the Asuras contended.
Those gods ran to Bṛhaspati as their domestic priest (*purohita*).
"Learn that sacrificial rite by which, having sacrificed with it, the Asuras did not follow after [the gods].
He perceived this Durāśa sacrifice;
having sacrificed with it, the Asuras did not follow after [the gods].
Then indeed the gods prospered and the Asuras were defeated.
He who knows this prospers by himself, and his enemy is defeated.
On the afternoon of the dark fortnight, the Saura sacrifice is performed in the forenoon.
ŚŚS 14.32.3: [The verse] "cāndramasī sāyam" (the lunar one in the evening).
ŚŚS 14.32.4: [The verse] "vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ navo navaḥ" (the moon as it wanes, ever new).
ŚŚS 14.32.5: A golden [vessel] with a hundred folds is the sacrificial fee for the first [offering].
The *rājata* [stotra] is in the north;
the *bhāradvāja-pṛṣṭha* [is performed];
likewise, the *sūkta*.
ŚŚS 14.32.9: After each hymn has been recited, he gives thirty oxen, each possessing the strength of a hundred.
ŚŚS 14.32.10: Or as much gold as the sacrificer may desire.
ŚŚS 14.33.1: Indra, desiring honor, performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite, the *apaciti*.
By means of that, having sacrificed, one obtains honor;
therefore, one who desires honor should sacrifice with it.
The first two Pavamāna lauds consist of twenty-four verses each.
The *ājya* stotras consist of the *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* stomas; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of the *saptadaśa* and *ekaviṃśa* stomas;
and the *ārbhava-pavamāna* consists of the *triṇava* stoma.
The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the twenty-first.
Its morning pressing concludes with a Gāyatrī verse;
for the Vasus are associated with the Gāyatrī metre.
Through that, Indra obtained honor among the Vasus;
the Brāhmaṇas are of the Gāyatrī metre.
Through that, he obtains honor among the Brāhmaṇas.
The midday pressing belongs to the *triṣṭubh* meter;
the Rudras belong to the *triṣṭubh* meter. Through this, Indra obtained honor among the Rudras.
The *triṣṭubh* metre belongs to the Kṣatriyas; by means of it, he obtains honor among the Kṣatriyas. The *jagatī* is the third pressing.
The Jagatī metre belongs to the Ādityas;
through it, Indra attained honor among the Ādityas.
The Jagatī metre belongs to the Viś.
By that, he attains honor among the people.
He recites with speech, he praises with speech, he sacrifices with speech.
Speech is the *anuṣṭubh*.
The *anuṣṭubh* metre belongs to the Viśvedevas;
through it, Indra attained honor among the Viśvedevas.
The *anuṣṭubh* metre belongs to the Śūdras.
By means of this, he receives honor among the *śūdras*.

(ŚŚS 14.33.20) A horse-chariot, armor of khadira-wood, tiger-skin covering, a quiver of bear-skin, a bow-case of leopard-skin, and a dark-brown horse are the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). (ŚŚS 14.33.21) [The intention is: "May I obtain honor through a form that is itself honored."
"O Indra, drink the Soma; O Lord of Soma, praise Indra"—this is used in the insertion of the *nivid* during the invocation of Indra.
This is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
Sūrya, desiring brilliance, performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite (*yajñakratu*), namely, brilliance.
By performing this sacrifice, one obtains brilliance;
therefore, one who desires brilliance should perform it.
The sacrificial fee consists of a horse-chariot, a bronze breastplate, and a white horse.
"May I attain brilliance through a brilliant form"—
this is said during the recitation of the *sūrya* [verse] at the placement of the *nivid*;
this is the characteristic form of this day.
Varuṇa, desiring rain, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite as a means for rain.
Having sacrificed with it, he obtained rain.
One who desires rain should sacrifice with it.
"Upward your eye, O Varuṇa, well-beheld; O Indra and Varuṇa, you two for the sacrifice..."—this is used when the *nivid* is placed during the recitation concerning Indra and Varuṇa.
This is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
"Bhānumatī," desiring splendor, having performed austerity, saw this sacrificial rite, the Āditya.
By means of that [sacrifice], having sacrificed, one obtains splendor;

therefore, one who desires splendor should sacrifice with it. Regarding the placement of the *nivid* during the recitation concerning the Ādityas, [the verse] beginning with "The sun which Svarbhānu... is used.
That is the form of this day:
Indra and Viṣṇu, desiring heaven, performed austerity and beheld this sacrificial rite leading to heaven.
Having sacrificed with it, they attained heaven.
"Therefore, one who desires heaven should sacrifice.
[This applies] during the recitation of the *indra-abhivyāhāra* at the placement of the *nivid*;
that is the characteristic form of this day.
The gods and the asuras contended with one another.
Those gods ran to Bṛhaspati for assistance,
saying, "Come, find out those two sacrificial rites by which, having sacrificed, we may overcome the asuras through victory."
He saw these two sacrificial rites, Vinutti and Abhibhūti.
By means of Vinutti he overcame the Vinuttis, and by means of Abhibhūti he overcame the Abhibhūtis.
Of that Vinutti, there are six upward Pṛṣṭhya stomas and six downward, turning-back stomas directed in all directions.
"Having become turned in all directions, they drive away [the enemies]"—
this is the form of the *vinutta*.
Now, for the *abhibhūti*, there are six upward *pṛṣṭhya* stomas and six downward stomas that are turned toward one another.
"Having become well-aligned, they overcome," it is said. That is the form of the overcoming. That which belongs to the Viśvajit with the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha is their *śastra*.
ŚŚS 14.39.1: For one desiring food and other enjoyments, [the sacrifice] is performed with the *rāśimarāya* verses.
ŚŚS 14.39.2: The two final *chandoma* days are taken from the *samūḷha* arrangement.
ŚŚS 14.39.3: He gives a thousand cows as the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) for the women.
For men, [the rites] are subsequent;
the *tantra* consists of the initiation (*dīkṣā*) and the *upasads*;
likewise the *udayanīyā*.
ŚŚS 14.39.7: Or, two twin brothers born of successive pregnancies may perform the sacrifice together.
ŚŚS 14.39.8: [The *vighana* hymn is used] for one who desires to strike away evil and those who hate him.
ŚŚS 14.39.9: [The *kayāśubhīya* and *tadidāsīya* are used] as the insertion (*nivid-dhāna*).
[This is] for one who desires to strike down his rival and hates him. The Ādityas and the Aṅgirases once vied with one another:
"We shall first go to the heavenly world," said the Ādityas; "We [shall]," said the Aṅgirases.
Those Aṅgirases said to the Ādityas, "Tomorrow is our Soma-pressing; officiate for us.
Now, Agni was their messenger.
Then the Ādityas said:
"If these [others] perform the sacrifice first, they will go to the heavenly world first;
the Asuras will then overcome us."
"Let us recognize that sacrificial rite by which our ancestors sacrificed.
They perceived this sacrificial rite of the *sādyaskra* type;
having sacrificed with it, the ancestors went to the heavenly world.
Therefore, one who desires heaven should sacrifice.
The *stoma* is the *trivṛt*;
the *pṛṣṭha* is the *rathantara*.
The *śastra* is arranged according to three *ṛc*s;
the sacrifice is the *agniṣṭoma*;
the sacrificial altar is as wide as two *yava*s.
The northern altar (uttaravedi) is made from a threshing floor of barley;
the sacrificial post (yūpa) is made from the pole of a plow; and the ring at the top of the post (caṣāla) is made from a bundle of barley stalks.
The *vasatīvarī* waters are brought from the family of one who has performed a sacrifice.
They are carried in leather bags with curds.
Then, they proceed with the clarified butter that rises from them.
The announcer of the Soma is one who possesses a horse-chariot;
at the very least, he must have a chariot yoked;
the sacrificial fee is a horse.
ŚŚS 14.40.16: The initiation ceremony (*dīkṣaṇīyā*) takes place in the forenoon.
ŚŚS 14.40.17: The ritual actions proceed in rapid succession.
ŚŚS 14.40.18: The *pravargya* rite is omitted because its purpose has been fulfilled.
There are three subsequent *upasads*. There is a *puroḍāśa* cake for Agni and Soma. At the time of the *savanīya*, the animal sacrifices share the same ritual framework (*samānatanttra*).
ŚŚS 14.40.22: [One should perform] the offering of the barren cow for the Aśvins in place of the *anūbandhyā* cow.
ŚŚS 14.40.23: Or one may sacrifice with the curd-mixture (*payasyā*) dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.
ŚŚS 14.40.24: Moreover, they sought to follow what had been previously undertaken.
This is the same procedure for the subsequent [sacrifice]. The *stomas*, however, are otherwise:
the *pavamāna* chants consist of eighteen verses, while the others consist of nine.
This very Ukthya has been brought back.
It is for the attainment of both that desire which exists in the Agniṣṭoma and that which exists in the Ukthya. [The verses are:
"The smoke of the cows," and "The fertile field."
ŚŚS_14.41.7: The smoke from the cow-dung fire is free from impurities.
ŚŚS_14.41.8: A bundle of cow-dung smoke serves as the sacrificial post-ring.
ŚŚS_14.41.9: The water in the pot is the *vasatīvarī* water.
The horse is the proclaimer of the Soma;
it ends with the *traipada* [verse];
a mare is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
This same procedure applies to the subsequent [sacrifice].
However, the *stomas* are different:
the *pavamāna* lauds are twenty-four-fold (*caturviṃśa*), while the others are threefold (*trivṛt*).
This Vājapeya has been thus restored.
It is for the attainment of both that which is desired in the Ṣoḍaśin and that which is in the Vājapeya.
If an enemy or rival should perform a sacrifice imitating this one, he should perform it as a counter-sacrifice.
If there is a performance of the *parikriyā* and the *utkriyā*:
one desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should sacrifice with one set of three, another set of three, and one [additional] *ekā*.
Regarding the first [of these], the stotras are performed in one [verse] and in three [verses].
ŚŚS 14.42.9: "In three [verses], in one"—this refers to the subsequent [stotra].
ŚŚS 14.42.10: These are twenty-four stotriya verses.
ŚŚS 14.42.11: The gāyatrī consists of twenty-four syllables.
The Gāyatrī is splendor and Vedic luster; through these two, one obtains splendor and Vedic luster. The two *śastra* recitations are composed of triplets (*ṛca*).
The Abhijit [sacrifice] is for one who desires to conquer;
the Viśvajit is for one who desires to conquer the universe; and both of these conclude with three ritual terminations (trisamstha).

Having become Agniṣṭomas, they established themselves in each other; having become Ukthyas, they established themselves in each other; having become Atirātras, they established themselves in each other.
Indra, desiring to conquer men, performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite, the Nṛjit.
Having sacrificed with it, he conquered men. Desiring to conquer men, one should sacrifice with it.

Indra, desiring to conquer in battle, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite, the Pṛtanājitt. Having sacrificed with it, he conquered in battle. Desiring to conquer in battle, one should sacrifice with it.
Indra, desiring to win the *satrājit* (the all-conquering prize), performed austerities and perceived this sacrificial rite, the *satrājit*.
Having sacrificed with it, he won the *satrājit*. Desiring to win the *satrājit*, one should sacrifice with it.
ŚŚS 14.45.2: At midday, on the first three days, the Nivid-formulas are inserted.
ŚŚS 14.46.1: Indra, desiring to win wealth, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite, the Dhanajit (the Wealth-Winner).
Having sacrificed with it, he won wealth.
Desiring to win wealth, he should perform sacrifice.
[It is] the Caturviṃśa day.
Indra, desiring to win the celestial realm (*svar*), having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite, the Svarjita.
Having sacrificed with it, he won the heavenly world;
therefore, one who desires to win the heavenly world should sacrifice with it.
Indeed, this Svarjit sacrifice is like a sacrifice that has fallen into disuse.
Indra, desiring to conquer all, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite, the All-Conquering.
Having sacrificed with it, he conquered all. Desiring to conquer all, one should sacrifice with it.
The day of the Mahāvrata.
Indra, desiring to conquer all, performed austerities and beheld this sacrificial rite as one that brings victory. Having sacrificed with it, he conquered all.
One who desires to conquer everything should sacrifice with this [sāman].
At the insertion of the *nivid*, [the verses] "Thou hast been born fierce for victorious power; praise him who is of overwhelming might" (RV 10.73.1–2) are used.

From the verse containing the word *dhān* (support), [the words] "The embryos have emerged from the nearness; you have boldly brought forth the one of great strength" (RV 5.45.6) constitute the *udvatī*; that is the characteristic form of this day.
Indra, indeed, slew the three-headed son of Tvaṣṭṛ;
he delivered the Aruṇmukha Yatis to the hyenas.
All beings cried out against him.
He moved as if from the very side of the gods.
Those gods said,
"If he continues to move in this manner, the Asuras will overcome us."
"Let us recognize that sacrificial rite by which we may summon him.
They perceived this Upāṃśu sacrificial rite;
with it, they summoned him.
Restrained by that [rite], the king should perform the sacrifice when he desires to conquer his kingdom;
indeed, he surely attains it.

"O Hero, these invocations of the most frequent singer call upon you as the one to be invoked, you who alone are to be invoked by the people"—with this verse, which contains the word "invocation," the *Nivid* is placed in the two *Nivid*-positions.
That is the form of this day. They reviled him because he was not born on an auspicious day, or because of his sin, or because of misfortune.
He offered all the pressings to Agni.
Agni burnt away all his state of being born base-born and all evil misfortune.
Therefore, whoever is born base-born, or whom evil speech addresses, should sacrifice with the Agniṣṭut.
For him who knows this and who sacrifices with it, Agni burns away all state of being born base-born and all evil misfortune.
One who desires spiritual luster (brahmavarcasa) should perform [the sacrifice] with the Trivṛt-stoma or the Triṣṭoma;
one who desires firm standing (pratiṣṭhā) should perform it with the Catuṣṭoma.
From the morning litany (prātar-anuvāka) until the Hāriyojana cup, everything belongs to Agni.
ŚŚS 14.51.5: There is modification according to the sense.
ŚŚS 14.51.6: There is substitution based on a specific statement. ŚŚS 14.51.7: "I deem Agni to be my father"—this is the introductory verse (*pratipad*) of the morning litany (*prātar-anuvāka*).
ŚŚS 14.51.8: One who desires the *liṅga* should utter the word "Agni" during the latter two sacrifices.
ŚŚS 14.51.9: Having extracted [the verse] beginning with "pra devatrā," he recites fourteen [verses] beginning with "somasya mā.
ŚŚS 14.51.10: [He recites] "tam oṣadhīḥ" while the [soma] is being poured down.
ŚŚS 14.51.11: Having omitted "aurvabhṛguvat" and the three verses beginning with "ambayaḥ," [one proceeds].
ŚŚS 14.51.12: "upaprayantaḥ trīṇi śatā" is the first and the last of the verses for the churning of the fire (agnimanthanīyāḥ).
ŚŚS 14.51.13: "agne juṣasva no haviḥ" is the first, fourth, and fifth of the verses for the Soma-offerings (savanīyāḥ).
ŚŚS 14.51.14: "dūtam vo viśvavedasam" is for the offerings to the dual deities.
ŚŚS 14.52.1: "agnim īḷe purohitam" is for those being lifted up. ŚŚS 14.52.2: "agnim dūtam" is for the seven *prasthita* offerings.
ŚŚS 14.52.3: The four following [verses] take the place of the Acchāvāka’s hymn.
ŚŚS 14.52.4: *agne divaḥ* is the offering verse (*yājyā*) for the clarified butter (*ājya*). ŚŚS 14.52.5:
*upa tvā jāmayaḥ*, *ebhir agne*, *kas te jāmiḥ*, *na yor upabdiḥ*, *agnir vṛtrāṇi*, *agne sutasya*, and *agne dhṛtavratāya*—these are the triplets for the *prauga* recitation.
He recites the verse, "O Agni, with all the Agnis...
He recites the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest: "Who is your kinsman? and "By what [means], O Agni Aṅgiras?
However, at the midday pressing, these two are reversed.
"Agner vṛtrāṇi" is for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin;
"Agnir mūrdhā" is for the Acchāvāka;
"Arcantas tvā" is for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
The *uttara* (supplementary verses) belong to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin;
"O Agni, for the one whose vows are firm" (*agne dhṛtavratāya*)—these six [verses] belong to the Acchāvāka;
they sacrifice with the final [verses].
ŚŚS 14.53.1: [The verse] "Agni, your god... is [recited] over those [cups] being lifted up.
ŚŚS 14.53.2: [The verse] "Forward for your bright one... is [recited] over the seven [cups] that have been set down.
ŚŚS 14.53.3: [The verse] "In the higher [region]... is [recited] over the Marutvatīya cup.
"viśo-viśo vas tvam agne yajñānām" and "iti" are the *pratipad* and *anucara* of the Marutvatīya [śastra].
"agna ā yāhy agnibhiḥ" and "pra vo yahvam" are the two *pragāthas*.
"agnim na mā mathitam" and "tvam agne prathama aṅgirā ṛṣiḥ" are for the *ekapātinīs*.
"O Agni, may he dwell with us... (ŚŚS 14.53.7) is the locus for the *nivid*.
"The last [verse] is the *yājyā*" (ŚŚS 14.53.8).
"Protect us, O Agni, with one [help]... and "Drive away from us, O Agni, the *rakṣas*... (ŚŚS 14.54.1)—these two *pragāthas* are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* of the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
"O Agni, [bring] the oblation-bearing [goddess] for you"—this is the *dhāyyā* verse.
"With this [song], [sing] to your Agni"—this is the *pragātha*.
"As the Hotṛ-priest [knows]"—this is the place for the *nivid* insertion.
"O men, [worship] Agni"—this is the *yājyā*.
"Agni, Agni, your unassailable one," and "O singer, O Agni"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas* for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
"Toward him, the fiercely glowing one"—this is for the Acchāvāka.
ŚŚS 14.55.3: *agne vivasvat*, *tvam agne gṛhapatiḥ*, and *tvam it saprathāḥ*—these are the *pragāthas* in their respective order.
ŚŚS 14.55.4: And the hymns begin with *yajasva hotar*. ŚŚS 14.55.5: They sacrifice with the final verses.
"Aganma mahā—" is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) for the Āditya cup; the following verse is the offering verse (*yājyā*).
"Ūrdhvam ū ṣu ṇo adhvarasya hotar" is used for the nine cups being drawn.
The two subsequent verses are for the Hāriyojana cup.
"O Agni, those who seek the Truth... (ŚŚS 14.56.4) is for the seven *prasthita* offerings.
"The Hotṛ goes forth... (ŚŚS 14.56.5) is the *puronuvākyā* for the Sāvitra cup, and the following verse is the *yājyā*.
"This [is] for thee, the new one... and "Like a horse, not thee... (ŚŚS 14.56.6) are the introductory and subsequent verses (*pratipad* and *anucara*) for the Vaiśvadeva offering.
"O Agni, you are the giver of wealth"—these three [verses] belong to the Sāvitra [offering];
the next three belong to the Ārbhava;
and four belong to the Dyāvāpṛthivīya.

ŚŚS 14.56.10: Six [verses] from the beginning belong to the Vaiśvadeva. ŚŚS 14.56.11: "abodhi jāraḥ" belongs to the verse addressed to Vāyu. ŚŚS 14.56.12: "juṣasva saprathastamam" belongs to the verse for Surūpakṛtnu.
"Samiddho agnir divi" (ŚŚS 14.56.13) consists of three verses for the *ekapātinī* [offering]. "Tad adya vācaḥ" (ŚŚS 14.56.14) consists of five verses for the *janīyā* [offering].
"Yajñena vardhata" (ŚŚS 14.56.15) is the *yājyā*.
"Abhipravanta" is for the ghee;
"Uttarā" is for the Soma offering;
"Ā vo rājānam" is for the verses dedicated to Rudra.
"Like a Vasu, of wondrous majesty"—this is for the Marut [laud].
"May our sacrifice reach to heaven; O Vāyu, come to us"—these are the *pragāthas* serving as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
Or they may be the regular ones.
ŚŚS 14.57.7: "apsv agne" [and the following] are for the verses beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭha.
ŚŚS 14.57.8: "tam devā budhne" are for the Vaiśvadeva verses.
ŚŚS 14.57.9: "imam ū ṣu vo atithim uṣarbudham" and the four [verses following it] are for the wives of the gods and for Rākā.
ŚŚS 14.57.10: "I invoke for you the one of fair splendor" (*huve vaḥ sudyotmānam*)—these three [verses] are of the *akṣarapaṅkti* meter.
ŚŚS 14.57.11: "The three-headed one" (*trimūrdhānam*)—these three [verses] are of the *paitrī* (paternal) class.
ŚŚS 14.57.12: "How, O Agni, do your purifying flames... (*kathā te agne śucayanta āyoḥ*)—these three [verses] are of the *yāmī* (relating to Yama) class.
ŚŚS 14.57.13: "mathīd yad īm" and the two following verses are from the *svāduṣkilīya* hymns.
ŚŚS 14.57.14: In the case of the latter two [hymns], the [next] two [verses] are used.
ŚŚS 14.57.15: "evāgnir gotamebhiḥ" is the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*).
ŚŚS 14.57.16: When the planets remain unaltered, [the verses] "tiṣṭhā harī" and "tam u stuhi" are used as the Nivid-insertion points.
ŚŚS 14.57.17: An ox or gold is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
ŚŚS 14.57.18: For this is the form belonging to Agni.
And having risen, there is the Agniṣṭoma.
Indeed, he who sacrifices with the Agniṣṭut is severed from all the deities.
Indra, desiring strength, performed penance and saw this sacrificial rite, the Indrastuta.
By means of that, one obtains strength;
therefore, one who desires strength should sacrifice with it.
In the recitation of the *nivid* during the invocation of Indra, that constitutes the characteristic form of this day.
Sūrya, desiring splendor (*tejas*), performed austerity and beheld this sacrificial rite, the Sūryastuta. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained splendor.
One who desires splendor should sacrifice with it.
ŚŚS 14.59.2: The mention of the sun and the insertion of the *nivid*—this is the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.
ŚŚS 14.60.1: All the gods (*viśve devāḥ*), desiring offspring, performed austerity and beheld this sacrificial rite, the *stotra* for the Viśvedevas.
Having sacrificed with it, they procreated.
One who desires offspring should sacrifice with this [offering].
At the insertion of the *nivid*, one recites: "O Indra, these [songs] of the most frequent [worshipper], the exhilaration of the bull...

and "For furtherance, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Indra... and "May Mitra and Varuṇa here, and Pūṣan..."—this is the invocation to the Viśvedevas, which constitutes the characteristic form (*rūpa*) of this day.

Gotama, desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*), performed austerities and saw this sacrificial rite, the *Gotama* sacrifice characterized by the fourfold increasing *stoma*. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained spiritual luster. One who desires spiritual luster should sacrifice with it.
The *bahiṣpavamāna* [stotra] is performed on four [verses];
the *ājya* [stotras] are performed on eight [verses] each;
the *mādhyandina-pavamāna* is performed on twelve [verses].
The *pṛṣṭha* stotras consist of twenty-six verses each;
the *ārbhava-pavamāna* consists of twenty verses;
and the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* consists of twenty-four verses.
ŚŚS 14.61.8: The *sāman* is the *antar-ukthya*.
ŚŚS 14.62.1: The *pañca-śāradīya*. ŚŚS 14.62.2:
In the beginning, the Maruts were those who did not share in the drinking of Soma.

Where the Maruts exhilarated Indra, there Indra shared with them a share in the drinking of Soma. He who has not yet partaken of the Soma-drinking, or he who desires union (*sāyujya*) and residence in the same world (*salokatā*) as the Maruts, should sacrifice with this [rite].
Five bulls, sprinkled for the Maruts, wander for five autumns.
They are to be seized for the *savanīya* [animal sacrifice].
